pro.note: Drafts, results, durations, map variants, MVPs and VOD links from Liquipedia playoff pages, fetched November 11, 2026. Heroes are shown in the order Liquipedia lists them; this app does not assign lanes to pro picks.

Hirara.short: The most banned hero in high-rank ranked and the most picked hero of the MPL PH playoffs
Hirara.body:
## Why she is meta
In the official rankings for Mythical Glory+ over the past 7 days, Hirara is banned in 86.70% of games, the highest ban rate of any hero, with a 49.65% win rate when she gets through. In the MPL Philippines Season 18 playoffs she was picked 26 times (15 wins) and banned 7 times across 38 games, so she was in 33 of 38 drafts. In the MPL Indonesia Season 18 playoffs she was picked 19 times (10 wins) and banned 8 times across 41 games.
Her two-skill energy kit lets a good player clear, gank and fight with almost no downtime, which is why players ban her rather than face her. Her win rate near 50% says she is strong in the right hands, not unbeatable.
## How to answer her
The official counter list in Mythical Glory+ is Yin, Thamuz, Lolita, X.Borg and Hanzo. If you cannot ban her, pick a jungler who can contest her early camps and keep vision on her side of the map.

Masha.short: Second-highest ban rate in Mythical Glory+, with a 62.20% win rate when picked
Masha.body:
## Why she is meta
Mythical Glory+, past 7 days: banned in 74.62% of games, picked in 0.78%, and winning 62.20% of those games, the highest win rate among the most-banned heroes. In the MPL PH Season 18 playoffs she was picked 7 times (4 wins) and banned 31 times: she was in every one of the 38 drafts. In MPL ID Season 18 playoffs: 14 picks (10 wins) and 27 bans in 41 games.
Three HP bars give her a margin for error in dives that other fighters do not have, and her damage grows as she loses health, so trading with her is rarely even.
## How to answer her
Official counters: Lesley, Eudora, Dyrroth, Aamon and Gloo. Burst and anti-heal, kept for her last bar, work better than long trades.

Marcel.short: Banned in 71.55% of Mythical Glory+ games and a staple of pro drafts
Marcel.body:
## Why he is meta
Mythical Glory+, past 7 days: banned in 71.55% of games, picked in 0.43%, 57.36% win rate. MPL PH S18 playoffs: 16 picks (10 wins) and 17 bans in 38 games. MPL ID S18 playoffs: 6 picks (4 wins) and 30 bans in 41 games.
His freeze gives his team a guaranteed window to land follow-up damage, which is valuable in both coordinated pro play and solo-queue skirmishes.
## How to answer him
Official counters: Atlas, Chip, Sun, Joy and Valentina. Spread out so his control catches fewer heroes.

Obsidia.short: The most picked of the high-ban heroes in Mythical Glory+
Obsidia.body:
## Why she is meta
Mythical Glory+, past 7 days: picked in 2.72% of games (more than any other hero in this list), banned in 61.42%, 52.89% win rate. In pro play she is less dominant: MPL PH S18 playoffs 8 picks (3 wins) and 11 bans; MPL ID S18 playoffs 8 picks (2 wins) and 5 bans.
Her ultimate tethers a target and stops displacement skills, which punishes the dash-heavy junglers common in ranked. In organized pro play, where teams protect against her engage, her results were weaker.
## How to answer her
Official counters: Helcurt, Benedetta, Yin, Aldous and Hanzo. Catch her before she stores Bone Shards.

Belerick.short: Ranked ban target whose thorns punish focus fire
Belerick.body:
## Why he is meta
Mythical Glory+, past 7 days: picked in 1.87%, banned in 57.92%, 49.89% win rate. MPL PH S18 playoffs: 6 picks (4 wins), never banned. MPL ID S18 playoffs: 7 picks (5 wins), 6 bans.
His passive damage when hit and taunt make him a hard target for basic-attack carries, which is why ranked players ban him.
## How to answer him
Official counters: Obsidia, Miya, Minsitthar, Zhask and Valentina.

Lukas.short: Sustain fighter banned in about half of Mythical Glory+ games
Lukas.body:
## Why he is meta
Mythical Glory+, past 7 days: picked in 1.19%, banned in 52.22%, 52.61% win rate. In the MPL PH S18 playoffs he was picked 3 times (1 win) and banned 3 times; he did not appear in the MPL ID S18 playoff stats.
Each hero hit from his main combo heals him, so he wins long trades in ranked. In pro play the strongest fighters (Masha, Freya, Paquito) took priority over him.
## How to answer him
Official counters: Ling, Natalia, Zilong, Fanny and Harith. Kite him and bring anti-heal.

Aulus.short: Banned in half of high-rank games and the most picked fighter of the MPL PH playoffs
Aulus.body:
## Why he is meta
Mythical Glory+, past 7 days: picked in 1.19%, banned in 52.19%, 53.76% win rate. MPL PH S18 playoffs: 20 picks (12 wins) and 8 bans. MPL ID S18 playoffs: 18 picks (7 wins) and 10 bans.
His Charge can turn into control immunity, and his ultimate is a wide teamfight slash with damage reduction. In the PH playoffs he was frequently drafted with Marcel (7 games together, 5 wins).
## How to answer him
Official counters: Gloo, Tigreal, Minsitthar, Natalia and Ruby. Control him in the first 2 seconds of Charge, before he becomes Enraged.

Eudora.short: Burst mage with a targeted stun, banned in over 40% of Mythical Glory+ games
Eudora.body:
## Why she is meta
Mythical Glory+, past 7 days: picked in 1.93%, banned in 41.50%, 50.57% win rate. Low pro presence: MPL PH S18 playoffs 4 picks (1 win) and 6 bans; MPL ID S18 playoffs 2 picks (2 wins) and 3 bans.
A point-and-click stun that spreads to marked enemies and high burst make her one of the most reliable ranked mages; pro teams can protect their carries better, which lowers her value there.
## How to answer her
Official counters: Zilong, Floryn, Marcel, Helcurt and Aldous.

Gloo.short: Tank with a damage-transfer ultimate, strong in Indonesia's playoffs
Gloo.body:
## Why he is meta
Mythical Glory+, past 7 days: picked in 1.03%, banned in 39.83%, 52.61% win rate. MPL ID S18 playoffs: 13 picks with 10 wins and 6 bans. MPL PH S18 playoffs: 2 picks (0 wins) and 1 ban, so the two regions valued him very differently.
## How to answer him
Official counters: Aamon, Jawhead, Johnson, Karina and Chang'e. Kill him before he builds full Sticky stacks.

Carmilla.short: Roam support whose linked curse spreads control
Carmilla.body:
## Why she is meta
Mythical Glory+, past 7 days: picked in 1.75%, banned in 38.24%, 52.70% win rate. MPL PH S18 playoffs: 4 picks (0 wins) and 8 bans. MPL ID S18 playoffs: 9 picks (4 wins) and 5 bans.
Her ultimate links enemies so control and damage on one spreads to the others, which rewards grouped fights.
## How to answer her
Official counters: Popol and Kupa, Chip, Estes, Minotaur and Cyclops. Move apart to break the link.

Sun.short: Clone fighter banned in over a third of Mythical Glory+ games, absent from pro playoffs
Sun.body:
## Why he is meta
Mythical Glory+, past 7 days: picked in 1.69%, banned in 36.03%, 52.69% win rate. He does not appear in the MPL PH or MPL ID Season 18 playoff stats.
Armor shred from every clone hit plus fast pushing make him a solo-queue threat; in coordinated play, area damage and control on Sun answer him.
## How to answer him
Official counters: Jawhead, Harley, Hanzo, Diggie and Layla.

Paquito.short: Pro priority fighter with modest ranked ban rates
Paquito.body:
## Why he is meta
MPL PH S18 playoffs: 10 picks (6 wins) and 23 bans in 38 games. MPL ID S18 playoffs: 15 picks (6 wins) and 21 bans in 41 games. In ranked Mythical Glory+, past 7 days, he is picked in 1.58% and banned in 16.07% of games, with a 49.97% win rate.
The gap is typical of heroes whose strength depends on precise cooldown management: pro players get more out of the enhanced-skill cycle.
## How to answer him
Official counters: Natalia, X.Borg, Karina, Helcurt and Aldous.

Freya.short: Banned or picked in every MPL PH playoff game, but rarely banned in ranked
Freya.body:
## Why she is meta
MPL PH S18 playoffs: 7 picks (6 wins) and 31 bans, present in all 38 games. MPL ID S18 playoffs: 20 picks (11 wins) and 20 bans in 41 games. In ranked Mythical Glory+, past 7 days, she is banned in only 1.25% of games, with a 50.39% win rate.
Her ultimate's control immunity is worth the most when the enemy draft is built around coordinated control, which is far more common in pro play than in solo queue.
## How to answer her
Official counters: Yve, Lolita, Sun, X.Borg and Masha.

Atlas.short: The pro tank of the season: 36 of 38 PH playoff drafts
Atlas.body:
## Why he is meta
MPL PH S18 playoffs: 13 picks (9 wins) and 23 bans. MPL ID S18 playoffs: 23 picks (9 wins) and 13 bans. In ranked Mythical Glory+, past 7 days, he is picked in 1.26% and banned in 11.02% of games, 50.65% win rate.
His chained ultimate is the clearest teamfight-winning tool in coordinated play. In the PH grand final, Aurora Gaming PH drafted him in five of six games.
## How to answer him
Official counters: Popol and Kupa, Eudora, Lolita, Ixia and Aamon. Keep a suppression ready, since only suppression stops his channel.

Kalea.short: Pro roam pick, banned 32 times in Indonesia's playoffs
Kalea.body:
## Why she is meta
MPL PH S18 playoffs: 22 picks (8 wins) and 13 bans. MPL ID S18 playoffs: 9 picks (6 wins) and 32 bans in 41 games. Ranked Mythical Glory+, past 7 days: 1.07% pick, 11.83% ban, 51.00% win rate.
## How to answer her
Official counters: Lolita, Yve, Fanny, Helcurt and Arlott.

Esmeralda.short: Pro ban target with a below-average ranked win rate
Esmeralda.body:
## Why she is meta
MPL PH S18 playoffs: 7 picks (4 wins) and 26 bans. MPL ID S18 playoffs: 7 picks (2 wins) and 28 bans. Ranked Mythical Glory+, past 7 days: 0.92% pick, 1.22% ban and a 45.94% win rate, the lowest in this list.
Shield-stealing sustain is strongest against coordinated shield and control drafts; in solo queue, she is easier to kite and burst.
## How to answer her
Official counters: Lolita, Mathilda, Marcel, Diggie and Yin.

proanalysis.title: Grand final: Aurora wins four short games around Atlas
proanalysis.sub: Team Falcons PH 2-4 Aurora Gaming PH, October 25, 2026
proanalysis.body:
## The result
Aurora Gaming PH beat Team Falcons PH 4-2 in the MPL Philippines Season 18 grand final. The series MVP listed on Liquipedia is Domeng. Aurora won games 1, 4, 5 and 6; Falcons won games 2 and 3.
!! How this breakdown was built: drafts, winners, game lengths and MVP come from Liquipedia; kills, deaths, assists, gold and items per player come from MLBBHub's match page. Pick order, ban order, lanes, objective timings and fight-by-fight play were not in these sources, and no VOD or caster commentary was checked, so nothing here describes a specific fight. Lines marked "Our reading" are our interpretation of the numbers.
## Game 1: Aurora, 14:24
- Aurora: Arlott (Nathzz 2/3/7), Suyou (Koyl 3/1/7), Zhuxin (Yue 6/1/7), Chou (Domeng 3/1/2), Atlas (Light 0/1/11).
- Falcons: Alice (Flap 0/4/4), Hirara (Kyle 3/3/2), Eudora (Hadji 1/3/5), Cici (SuperMarco 3/1/3), Marcel (Owgwen 0/3/7).
- Bans: Masha, Paquito, Freya, Barats, Hylos, Esmeralda, Kalea, Kimmy, Yu Zhong, Obsidia.
- Kills 14 to 7 and end-of-game gold 48.0k to 40.0k for Aurora. Yue's Zhuxin led the game with 6 kills and 1 death.
!! Our reading: Aurora's draft stacked control. Atlas's Fatal Links drags the heroes it hits toward him, Zhuxin's capture pulls a hero airborne and throws them, and Chou's kick moves a target. Light's 11 assists on Atlas, with 0 kills, fit a game decided by engages.
## Game 2: Falcons, 13:24
- Falcons: Esmeralda (Flap 1/3/11), Saber (Kyle 3/2/5), Zhuxin (Hadji 6/1/7), Claude (SuperMarco 3/0/7), Kalea (Owgwen 0/3/11).
- Aurora: Atlas (Nathzz 0/4/8), Nolan (Koyl 0/3/7), Zetian (Yue 1/2/8), Kimmy (Domeng 7/1/0), Belerick (Light 1/3/6).
- Bans: Freya, Masha, Hirara, Dyrroth, Barats, Paquito, Chou, Marcel, Cici, Harith.
- Kills 13 to 9 and gold 43.7k to 37.9k for Falcons. Falcons took Zhuxin this time, and Hadji went 6/1/7 on her, the same line Yue had in game 1.
- MLBBHub lists Nathzz on Atlas and Light on Belerick in this game.
!! Our reading: Koyl's Nolan finished with 0 kills and 3 deaths, his only game of the series without a kill. With Zhuxin on the other side and Chou banned, Aurora lost two of the three control tools that won game 1.
## Game 3: Falcons, 20:41
- Falcons: Hylos (Flap 1/2/9), Hirara (Kyle 4/1/8), Pharsa (Hadji 2/2/9), Cici (SuperMarco 6/1/8), Marcel (Owgwen 1/1/10).
- Aurora: Barats (Nathzz 1/2/3), Suyou (Koyl 2/4/3), Zhuxin (Yue 1/2/3), Chou (Domeng 2/2/1), Atlas (Light 1/4/5).
- Bans: Esmeralda, Kalea, Nolan, Harith, Kimmy, Masha, Paquito, Freya, Lylia, Zetian.
- The longest game of the series. Only 21 kills in total (14 for Falcons, 7 for Aurora), and gold ended close: 62.6k to 59.7k. Kyle's Hirara had the most gold on the map, 16.4k.
!! Our reading: Aurora ran almost the game 1 draft again (Suyou, Zhuxin, Chou, Atlas) with Barats for Arlott, and the game went long with few kills. Falcons answered with Hirara through the draft and a sturdier front (Hylos, Marcel); the low kill count suggests neither side's engage found picks for a long time.
## Game 4: Aurora, 10:23
- Aurora: Barats (Nathzz 3/0/6), Suyou (Koyl 2/1/7), Estes (Yue 0/0/9), Kimmy (Domeng 6/0/5), Masha (Light 0/1/3).
- Falcons: Cici (Flap 0/3/2), Hirara (Kyle 1/2/1), Rafaela (Hadji 0/3/1), Claude (SuperMarco 0/0/2), Kalea (Owgwen 1/3/1).
- Bans: Paquito, Esmeralda, Atlas, Chou, Carmilla, Freya, Zhuxin, Nolan, Lylia, Zetian.
- The shortest game of the series. Kills 11 to 2 and gold 37.7k to 28.3k. Aurora's five players died 2 times in total.
- With Atlas banned, Light played Masha, the only game in which Masha got through the draft in this series.
!! Our reading: with Atlas, Chou and Zhuxin all banned, Aurora switched to a healer (Estes's ultimate heals allies over 8 seconds) and Masha. It shows they had a second plan ready when their main control heroes were taken.
## Game 5: Aurora, 12:42
- Aurora: Atlas (Nathzz 0/4/16), Hirara (Koyl 10/3/8), Yve (Yue 1/4/16), Chou (Domeng 9/1/10), Estes (Light 1/5/16).

- Bans: Masha, Freya, Marcel, Kalea, Saber, Esmeralda, Kimmy, Barats, Yu Zhong, Cici.
- The bloodiest game: 38 kills (21 for Aurora, 17 for Falcons), yet gold was the closest of the series, 40.2k to 38.7k. Koyl's Hirara had 10 kills and Domeng's Chou 9 kills with 1 death.
!! Our reading: this was an even, fight-heavy game decided by Aurora's two carries staying alive (Domeng died once). Falcons had Paquito and Aulus through the draft, two of the most contested fighters of the season, and still lost the fights.
## Game 6: Aurora, 11:41
- Aurora: Barats (Nathzz 0/2/9), Suyou (Koyl 4/0/7), Zhuxin (Yue 2/0/9), Clint (Domeng 9/0/3), Atlas (Light 0/0/7).
- Falcons: Kalea (Flap 0/5/1), Hirara (Kyle 0/3/2), Kimmy (Hadji 2/2/0), Miya (SuperMarco 0/2/0), Marcel (Owgwen 0/3/2).
- Bans: Esmeralda, Paquito, Chou, Cici, Harith, Freya, Masha, Estes, Arlott, Mathilda.
- Kills 15 to 2 and gold 42.7k to 30.7k. Aurora's five players died 2 times in total; Domeng's Clint went 9/0/3.
!! Our reading: back to the core that won game 1 (Suyou, Zhuxin, Atlas) with Barats in front. Falcons' two kills in 11 minutes say the game was over early.
## Across the series
- Freya was banned in all six games. Masha was picked once, by Aurora in game 4 (a win). Paquito, Esmeralda and Hirara were picked or banned in every game.
- Aurora drafted Atlas in five games (1, 2, 3, 5, 6) and won three. MLBBHub lists Light on him in games 1, 3 and 6 and Nathzz in games 2 and 5. Atlas was banned in game 4.
- Suyou: Aurora picked Suyou in games 1, 3, 4 and 6 and won three of those four.
- Zhuxin changed hands: Aurora picked her in games 1, 3 and 6 (two wins), and Falcons in games 2 and 5 (one win).
- Barats: Aurora picked Barats in games 3, 4 and 6 and won games 4 and 6.
- Domeng, the series MVP, finished the six games with 36 kills and 5 deaths across Chou, Kimmy and Clint.
- Aurora's four wins all ended between 10:23 and 14:24. Falcons' two wins took 13:24 and 20:41.
## What a ranked player can take from it
- Have a second plan when your best hero is banned. Aurora lost Atlas, Chou and Zhuxin in game 4 and still won in 10 minutes with a different draft.
- A tank with a team-wide engage, like Atlas, gives a draft a plan. In ranked, pick one only if your team has damage that can follow the pull.
- Deaths matter more than kills for your carry. Domeng averaged under one death a game; staying alive kept Aurora's damage in every fight.

guides.title: How a match is won
guides.sub: The one goal every decision serves
guides.body:
## The goal
Destroy the enemy Base. Everything else in Mobile Legends (kills, gold, buffs, Turtle, Lord) only matters because it helps you get there faster or stops the enemy from getting to yours.
## The map in one picture
The Land of Dawn has three lanes (top, middle, bottom), each guarded by three turrets per team: the Outer Turret, the Inner Turret and the Inhibitor (Base) Turret. Between the lanes sits the jungle, split by a river that runs through the middle of the map. Each team owns the half of the jungle on its side.
- **EXP Lane**: the side lane next to the first Turtle. Usually a Fighter or Tank who wants levels early.
- **Mid Lane**: shortest lane, fastest rotations. Usually a Mage who clears waves and helps both sides.
- **Gold Lane**: the side lane farther from the first Turtle. Usually the Marksman, the hero who needs the most items.
- **Jungle**: a Jungler (Assassin or Fighter, with Retribution) farms creeps and takes objectives.
- **Roam**: a Tank or Support who protects teammates, gives vision and starts fights.
> Kills are a means, not the goal. A team that trades two kills for a turret and a Turtle is usually the team that is winning.
## Why turrets matter so much
A turret is permanent map control. When your Outer Turret falls, that part of the jungle becomes dangerous for your team and safe for theirs. That is why pros convert every won fight into a turret or an objective before anything else.

guides.title: Roles and lanes
guides.sub: Who does what, and what each role needs
guides.body:
## The six roles
- **Tank**: soaks damage, starts fights with crowd control (CC), protects the carry. Needs few items to be useful.
- **Fighter**: durable damage dealer. Wins side lanes and dives backlines.
- **Assassin**: fast, high burst, kills isolated targets. Most Junglers.
- **Mage**: magic damage and control from range. Clears waves fast.
- **Marksman**: sustained physical damage from range. Weak early, carries late.
- **Support**: heals, shields and peels for allies.
Many heroes have two roles (for example Fighter/Assassin), and the in-game lane is what really matters: EXP, Mid, Gold, Jungle or Roam. Every hero page in this app shows both.
## Gold priority
A simple way to think about who gets resources: Jungler and Gold Laner first, then Mid and EXP, then Roamer. The Roamer buys a Roaming item that shares gold with the team, and the team plays to make the carries strong.
## Damage types
Physical damage is reduced by Physical Defense; magic damage by Magic Defense; true damage ignores both. Check each hero's damage type on its page before you choose defensive items.

guides.title: Minions, waves and gold
guides.sub: Where your gold actually comes from
guides.body:
## Minion waves
Minions spawn from each Base and walk down all three lanes. Last-hitting them (dealing the killing blow) gives the most gold; if a minion is killed by something else while you are nearby, you get less.
- Per the MLBB Wiki: Lancer minions start at 33 gold, Infantry at 65 and Cannon at 100, rising over time.
- Per the MLBB Wiki: on the Gold Lane the Cannon minion gives extra gold for the first 10 waves, and on the EXP Lane the Cannon gives extra EXP for the first 10 waves.
- Patch 2.2.16 slightly reduced how fast minion gold grows over the match.
!! Minion gold numbers come from the MLBB Wiki and can lag behind the latest patch.
## Why waves matter
A wave that reaches an enemy turret makes the turret shoot minions instead of heroes, which is the safest time to hit it. A wave that crashes into your turret is gold you lose. Learning to look at where waves are is the first step from casual to ranked-ready play (see Advanced > Wave management).

guides.title: Jungle creeps and buffs
guides.sub: Every camp and what it gives
guides.body:
## Common creeps
Small camps give gold and EXP and no buff. Per the MLBB Wiki:
- **Lithowanderer**: does not fight back; gives Walkie Grass (bonus movement speed).
- **Horned Lizard**, **Fire Beetle**, **Lava Golem**: standard farm camps. Patch 2.2.16 cut their base gold by 13%.
- **Scavenger Crab** (river): gives a Gold or EXP buff depending on the side.
## Elite creeps (the buffs)
- **Purple Buff** (from the Thunder Fenrir pair): cooldown reduction, lower mana/energy costs, and healing when you kill targets. Mages and skill-reliant Junglers love it.
- **Orange Buff** (from the Molten Fiend): your attacks deal extra true damage and slow. Great for chasing and for Marksmen.
## Retribution
Junglers carry the Retribution spell and a jungle item (Flame, Ice or Bloody Retribution), which upgrades as they farm. It is also the tool that secures Turtle and Lord, so tracking the enemy Jungler's Retribution cooldown is a core skill.

guides.title: Turtle and Lord
guides.sub: The two big objectives and their timers
guides.body:
## Turtle
Per the MLBB Wiki:
- The first Turtle spawns at 2:00, always next to the EXP Lane.
- The next spawn location and timer show up after a Turtle dies.
- No new Turtle appears if the last one dies after 6:00. A Turtle still alive after 8:00 turns into the Lord if it takes no damage for 5 seconds (can be delayed until 9:00).
- Every hero on the killing team gets gold (60, 70, 80 for the first, second, third Turtle) and a large amount of EXP, plus a one-time shield for 120 seconds.
- The hero who lands the last hit also gets an instant heal and a 120-second shield that repairs itself after 5 seconds without taking hero damage, and grants extra damage while it lasts.
## Lord
Per the MLBB Wiki:
- The first Lord appears 2 minutes after the last Turtle is killed.
- Killed between 8:00 and 18:00, it respawns every 180 seconds; after 18:00, every 120 seconds.
- The Lord evolves at the 18-minute mark, and a Lord summoned between 8 and 18 minutes deals 30% of a turret's max HP as true damage with its charge.
- The slain Lord joins the killing team and pushes a lane, enhancing nearby minions.
!! Turtle and Lord rules come from the MLBB Wiki pages, which were current as of their last edit and may lag behind a recent patch.
> Kill the Lord when 2 or 3 enemies are dead, or right after the enemy Jungler used Retribution. Otherwise the Lord fight is a coin flip.

guides.title: Turrets and the Base
guides.sub: How defenses work
guides.body:
## The rules
Per the MLBB Wiki:
- Each team has nine turrets: three per lane.
- Outer Turrets cannot be damaged until 15 seconds after the first minions spawn.
- A turret stays invincible until the turret in front of it in the same lane is destroyed. Destroying a lane's Inhibitor Turret exposes the Base.
- A turret hits one target at a time, and its damage rises the longer it keeps hitting the same target.
## How to take a turret safely
- Push with a minion wave so the turret targets minions.
- Check the minimap: if three or more enemies are missing, back off.
- Never dive a turret for one kill unless you are sure you will survive the shots.

guides.title: Items 101
guides.sub: Building in the right order
guides.body:
## Item categories
The shop has Attack, Magic, Defense, Movement (boots), Jungling and Roaming items. Most heroes build one pair of boots, one Jungling or Roaming item if they jungle or roam, and five or six main items.
## Build order basics
- Buy boots early; upgrade them when you know which defense you need.
- Your first full item should do what your hero needs most: damage for a carry, durability or utility for a tank.
- Complete one item before starting the next; half-built components give less.
- Watch the enemy's fed heroes and adapt with defense (see Items > Counter-building).
## Anti-heal
When an enemy heals a lot, Sea Halberd (physical), Dominance Ice (defense) and Glowing Wand (magic) are the common answers. Each item page in this app shows its exact passive from the MLBB Wiki.

guides.title: Emblems and spells 101
guides.sub: Your pre-match setup
guides.body:
## Emblems
You pick one emblem set before the match. Each set gives fixed attributes, then you choose talents: standard talents and one core talent. The Basic Common set's talents can be used with any set. The Emblems screen in this app lists every set and talent with its current description.
## Battle spells
Each player takes one battle spell. The most common:
- **Flicker**: short blink. The default for heroes who need to dodge or start fights.
- **Retribution**: required for the Jungler.
- **Execute**, **Purify**, **Inspire**, **Vengeance**, **Aegis**, **Petrify**, **Sprint**, **Flameshot**, **Arrival**, **Revitalize**, **Healing**: situational picks covered on each hero guide.
## Quick choices
- Junglers: Retribution, always.
- Marksmen and mages vs heavy crowd control: Purify; otherwise Flicker.
- Fighters in EXP Lane: Flicker, Vengeance or Petrify depending on the matchup.
- Roamers: Flicker for initiation, or Aegis/Revitalize for a protect-the-carry style.

guides.title: Reading the minimap
guides.sub: The habit that separates good players
guides.body:
## Look every few seconds
The minimap shows allied vision, enemy heroes in vision, turret states and objective timers. Glance at it after every wave, every buff and every fight.
## What to look for
- **Missing enemies**: if the enemy Jungler or Roamer has not been seen for a while, assume they are coming to the lane closest to their last position.
- **Where your team is**: never fight in a part of the map where your team cannot reach you in time.
- **Objective timers**: start moving to Turtle or Lord before it spawns, not when it spawns.
- **Waves**: a big wave heading to your turret is a reason to go defend it.

guides.title: Drafting like a coach
guides.sub: Bans, first picks, flex and last-pick counters
guides.body:
## Think in win conditions, not heroes
Before the draft starts, decide how your team wants to win: early skirmishes and snowball, a front-to-back late-game teamfight, split push, or pick-offs. Every pick should push that plan forward or deny the enemy theirs. A draft of five strong heroes with no shared plan loses to a draft of five decent heroes that all want the same fight.
## The priority ladder
- **Ban phase one**: remove the heroes that are strong in any draft. In MPL PH Season 18, Freya was picked or banned in every one of the 172 games, Atlas in 97.67% and Hirara in 96.51% (see Meta). If your opponent has a signature hero, that is the other ban to consider.
- **First pick**: take a hero that is strong and flexible, ideally one that can play two roles or lanes so the enemy cannot plan around it. Avoid first-picking a hero that has an obvious hard counter still open.
- **Middle picks**: complete your win condition (initiation + damage + frontline) and take answers to what the enemy has shown.
- **Last pick**: counter-pick the lane that has the clearest matchup, usually EXP Lane or Mid.
## Flex picks
A flex pick is a hero who can go to two or more lanes. It hides your intention: the enemy cannot counter-pick a lane they cannot read. Many pro drafts in this patch revolve around heroes listed with two lanes on their page (check a hero's Lane line in this app).
## Composition checklist
- At least one reliable initiator or catch tool (hard CC that starts a fight).
- A way to deal both physical and magic damage, so a single defense item does not shut you down.
- Frontline that can survive the first 3 seconds of a fight.
- Wave clear for when you are behind.
- Answers to the enemy's best hero (anti-heal, Purify, peel, or a counter-initiation).
## Solo queue drafting at high ranks
You cannot coordinate five players, so draft to cover what is missing. If no one has picked a frontline by your turn, a tank or tanky fighter is worth more than your best assassin. Ban what you lose to, not what you dislike.
!! The specific ban priorities here are based on MPL PH Season 18 statistics (patches 2.1.95 to 2.2.16a). Ranked priorities on the newest patch may differ.

guides.title: Counter logic
guides.sub: Why a hero beats another, and how to apply it
guides.body:
## Counters come in five kinds
- **Mobility vs control**: dash-heavy heroes (Fanny, Ling, Lancelot) struggle against instant, point-and-click or area control that catches them mid-dash.
- **Sustain vs anti-heal**: heroes who heal through fights (Freya with her ultimate, Esmeralda, Uranus) lose much of their value to anti-heal items.
- **Range vs gap close**: long-range poke loses to heroes who can close distance and survive the poke.
- **Burst vs shields**: burst assassins lose value against shields (Aegis, Valkyrie's Shield against magic burst, Marcel's Platinum Snap).
- **Tankiness vs percentage damage**: high-HP frontlines melt to max-HP and true damage.
## Use the hero's own kit
Every hero page lists the exact skill text from the MLBB Wiki. Read it to find the counter window: a long cooldown on the escape skill, a channel that can be interrupted, a passive that needs stacks. Examples from current kits:
- **Barats**' ultimate is a channel that pulls enemies in; per his kit, he is immune to control during it, but it can be canceled, refunding part of the cooldown. Bait it out before committing.
- **Atlas**' ultimate tethers and then slams; Purify, Flicker and dashes during the tether window break it.
- **Masha** (revamped in 2.2.16) has three HP bars and blocks damage once each time a bar empties. Burst that kills through one bar wastes damage; sustained damage and anti-heal are more efficient.
## Counter the player, too
At Mythical Immortal, the person matters as much as the hero. A one-trick Fanny player gets a ban or a hard-control lineup. A hyper-aggressive Jungler gets an invade-ready lineup that punishes their first rotation.

guides.title: Micro: mechanics that win fights
guides.sub: Positioning, animation canceling and skill timing
guides.body:
## Positioning first
Most deaths at high rank are positioning errors, not mechanics errors. Before every fight, ask: where is the enemy initiator, and am I within their engage range? Marksmen and Mages stand behind their frontline and to the side, so one engage cannot catch two carries.
## Hold your key skill
The best players hold their crowd control or escape until the enemy commits. A stun used at the start of a fight is predictable; a stun saved for the enemy assassin's dive wins the fight.
## Animation and attack canceling
Many heroes can cancel the end of a basic attack animation with movement or a skill. Practice in Practice mode until the timing is automatic. Heroes with enhanced basic attacks (Freya, Kalea, Masha's claw strikes) gain the most from clean attack-skill weaving.
## Target selection
The target you can kill is usually more valuable than the target you want to kill. In teamfights, hit what is in front of you until the backline is reachable safely. Assassins are the exception: their job is the backline, and only after key enemy control is used.
## Cooldown tracking
Track the enemy's ultimates and spells (especially Flicker, Purify, Retribution). The window right after an enemy uses Flicker is the best time to engage on them; Flicker's cooldown is listed in the Spells screen.
## Practice routine
- Ten minutes a day in Practice mode on combos for your top three heroes.
- Rewatch one loss a day from the enemy's point of view and write down one positioning mistake.
- Play a few matches focusing on only one habit (minimap glances, holding a skill) until it sticks.

guides.title: Macro: playing the map
guides.sub: Tempo, rotations and decision-making
guides.body:
## Tempo
Tempo is who forces the other team to react. A team with tempo arrives first at objectives, starts fights on its terms and takes free turrets. You gain tempo by clearing your wave quickly, then moving before the enemy does.
## The three-question loop
After every wave, buff or fight, ask:
- What is the next objective that spawns (Turtle, Lord, a buff)?
- Where are my waves, and which one is about to hit a turret?
- Where is the enemy Jungler?
The answers tell you whether to farm, rotate, set up vision, or push.
## Trading objectives
When the enemy takes an objective you cannot contest, take something else on the opposite side of the map at the same time: a turret, a buff or the other Turtle. Never stand around watching them take it.
## Converting a won fight
After a won fight, check the timer and the map. In order of value: Lord (late game), Inhibitor or Base turrets, Turtle, outer turrets, enemy buffs. Then reset (go back to base) together so you do not get caught one by one.
## Playing from behind
Clear waves under your turret, avoid face-checking bushes, trade objectives on the side away from the enemy, and wait for the enemy to overextend. The comeback bounty rule (Patch 2.2.16 lowered the gold deficit needed for it from 2,000 to 1,500) means the team behind gets more from each kill than before.

guides.title: Rotations by role
guides.sub: Where to be at each minute
guides.body:
## Jungler
- Clear your buffs and the closest camps, then look at the lanes: gank the lane where the enemy is pushed up and has used their escape.
- Plan your path so you finish near the first Turtle when it spawns (2:00) with your laners able to help.
- After the first Turtle, invade the enemy jungle on the side where your team has priority (laners who pushed their waves).
## Roamer
- Help your Jungler secure the first buff, then roam where it helps most: usually the Gold Lane early, Mid for vision.
- Move ahead of objectives: be at the Turtle pit before it spawns, check the bushes on the way.
- Never let your carry walk into unchecked bushes alone.
## Mid
- Clear the wave fast, then rotate to the side where the Turtle or a fight will happen. Return to clear the next wave before it hits your turret.
## EXP and Gold Lane
- Win your lane, push the wave into the enemy turret, then rotate to help at objectives. A side laner who arrives at a Turtle fight with a pushed wave behind them has won two things at once.

guides.title: Objective control
guides.sub: Turtle, Lord and buff setups
guides.body:
## Before the spawn
- Push the two closest lanes so enemy laners must choose between their wave and the objective.
- Clear vision around the pit: check bushes with a tank, not your carry.
- Know where the enemy Jungler is and whether their Retribution is up.
## During the take
- Your Jungler holds Retribution for the last hit; everyone else deals damage and watches for the enemy arrival.
- If the enemy arrives in force, fight first and take the objective after, or abandon it. A lost teamfight costs more than a Turtle.
## Lord timing
The Lord is worth the most when two or three enemies are dead, or when the enemy Jungler is dead or out of position. A Lord taken while all five enemies are alive is a gamble on a single Retribution.
## Buff control
Taking the enemy's Purple or Orange Buff denies their carry and speeds up yours. Only invade when your laners have pushed their waves (lane priority), or you will be collapsed on.

guides.title: Wave management
guides.sub: Push, freeze and slow push
guides.body:
## Three wave states
- **Fast push**: clear the wave as quickly as possible to crash it into the enemy turret. Use before rotating or before an objective.
- **Slow push**: kill only the enemy back-line minions so your wave grows over time. A big slow-pushed wave crashing into a turret forces an enemy to defend it.
- **Freeze**: keep the wave near your own turret by last-hitting only. You farm safely and the enemy must overextend to farm.
## Practical rules
- Before you rotate or recall, push your wave. A wave left at your turret is gold lost.
- Before an objective, push the waves on the side of the objective.
- When you are behind, let the wave come to you and clear under your turret.
- Patch 2.2.16 slightly slowed minion gold growth, so jungle and objective gold are a bigger share than before.

guides.title: Vision and map awareness
guides.sub: Seeing first is winning first
guides.body:
## Where vision comes from
Allied heroes, minions, turrets and some skills reveal the map. There are no buyable wards in MLBB, so vision comes from where your heroes and minions stand and from skills that scout.
## Using bushes
Bushes hide heroes. Control the bushes on the path to the next objective and around your carry. A Roamer who checks bushes first saves the carry from walking into an ambush.
## Reading absence
When an enemy disappears from the minimap, count the seconds. A Jungler gone for several seconds after clearing a camp is most likely moving to the lane nearest that camp.
## Pressure without vision
If you cannot see the enemy Jungler, do not push past the river on the side they were last seen. If you can see them on the opposite side, that is your window to push or invade.

guides.title: Next-level habits
guides.sub: What separates Immortal from top global
guides.body:
## Habits worth copying from pro play
- Every fight starts with a reason: an objective, a pushed wave, or an enemy caught out of position.
- After every win, the team resets together and arrives at the next objective first.
- Flex picks and late-game power picks are drafted to keep options open (see Drafting).
## Personal habits
- Look at the minimap every few seconds, not only when something happens.
- Track enemy Flicker, Purify and Retribution timers out loud or in your head.
- Play to your win condition: a scaling team does not fight at 4 minutes over a Turtle it cannot win.
- Review losses from the enemy's point of view: what did they do that worked?
- Specialize: a small hero pool (two or three per role) played at a very high level beats a large pool played at an average level.
!! Pro and coach quotes are not included yet: each one needs a link to a verifiable interview or broadcast. The insights here are drawn from MPL PH Season 18 statistics and the patch notes.

guides.title: Counter-building: the core idea
guides.sub: Build for the game in front of you
guides.body:
## Read the enemy draft first
Before buying your second item, open the scoreboard and answer three questions:
- Is the enemy damage mostly physical, mostly magic, or mixed?
- Who is the fed or most dangerous enemy?
- Does the enemy rely on healing, shields, attack speed, burst, or crowd control?
Each answer points to a specific item below. All item stats and passives quoted here are from the MLBB Wiki's item data; open any item in the Items screen for the full text.
## The swap rule
Your standard build is a starting point. At high rank, the best players change one or two items every game. A Marksman who keeps building damage against a fed Assassin dies before the damage matters.

guides.title: Against healing and shields
guides.sub: Lifebane items and when to buy them
guides.body:
## The Lifebane family
- **Sea Halberd** (Attack, 2,050 gold): +80 Physical Attack, +20% Attack Speed; dealing damage reduces the target's Shield and HP Regen to 60% for 3 seconds, and deals 8% more damage to heroes with more extra HP.
- **Glowing Wand** (Magic, 2,150 gold): +60 Magic Power, +300 HP; magic damage burns for 1% of the target's Max HP per second and applies the same 60% Shield and HP Regen reduction.
- **Dominance Ice** (Defense, 2,010 gold): +40 Physical and Magic Defense; reduces Shield and HP Regen of nearby enemies within 5 units to 60%, and gains Hybrid Defense for each nearby enemy hero.
## Who to buy it against
Heroes whose kits heal or shield heavily: Freya's ultimate heals per basic attack, Esmeralda converts shields, Uranus regenerates, Kalea heals herself and the lowest-HP ally, Masha's Feral claw strikes recover HP. Check each enemy's skill text on their hero page.
## Who buys it
One player on each damage type is enough. Usually the Marksman or physical Jungler buys Sea Halberd, the Mage buys Glowing Wand, and a Tank or Fighter buys Dominance Ice.

guides.title: Against physical damage
guides.sub: Choosing the right armor
guides.body:
- **Antique Cuirass** (2,170 gold): +920 HP, +40 Physical Defense. Each time you are hit by a skill, the attacker's physical damage drops 6% for 2 seconds, stacking 3 times. Best against skill-based physical heroes (Fighters, Assassins).
- **Blade Armor** (1,910 gold): +80 Physical Defense and 20% crit damage reduction. Reflects part of basic attack damage and slows the attacker. Best against basic-attack Marksmen and crit builds.
- **Chastise Pauldron** (2,100 gold): +900 HP, +40 Physical Defense. Taking damage cuts the attacker's attack speed and attack speed cap to 75% for 2 seconds; heals 20% Max HP when you drop under 30% (60-second cooldown). Best against attack-speed carries like Freya or a hyper-carry Marksman.
- **Dominance Ice**: hybrid defense plus anti-heal, best when you are in the middle of fights.
- **Warrior Boots** and **Tough Boots** are the boot choices against physical and control-heavy lineups; check their passives in the Items screen.

guides.title: Against magic damage
guides.sub: Magic defense choices
guides.body:
- **Valkyrie's Shield** (2,150 gold): +900 HP, +48 Magic Defense. Taking magic damage from hero skills or attacks reduces magic damage taken by 25% for 3 seconds, including the hit that triggers it. Regains the effect 5 seconds after leaving combat. The answer to magic burst.
- **Radiant Armor** (1,880 gold): +950 HP, +40 Magic Defense, +12 HP Regen. Taking magic damage stacks extra Magic Defense up to 6 times. Best against sustained magic damage (damage over time, frequent skills).
- **Cursed Helmet** (1,910 gold): +1,200 HP, +20 Magic Defense, burns nearby enemies and reduces their Hybrid Defense. A tank's damage-and-defense item.

guides.title: Against tanks and high HP
guides.sub: Penetration and percentage damage
guides.body:
- **Malefic Roar** (2,060 gold): +60 Physical Attack, +30% Physical Penetration, plus up to 30% more penetration based on the target's Physical Defense. Buy when the enemy stacks armor.
- **Malefic Gun** (2,120 gold): +40 Physical Attack, +20% Attack Speed, +30% Physical Penetration, +12% basic attack range. A Marksman's penetration option.
- **Demon Hunter Sword** (2,180 gold): basic attacks deal 8% of the target's current HP as extra physical damage and heal you. Shreds high-HP frontlines.
- **Divine Glaive** (1,970 gold): +65 Magic Power, +40% Magic Penetration, scaling with the target's Magic Defense. The Mage's answer to magic defense.
- **Sea Halberd** also deals 8% more damage to heroes with more extra HP than you.

guides.title: Against burst and assassins
guides.sub: Surviving the first combo
guides.body:
- **Immortality** (2,120 gold): +850 HP, +15 Physical Defense; revives you 2.5 seconds after death with 16% Max HP and a shield (210-second cooldown). The late-game insurance item for carries.
- **Queen's Wings** (2,250 gold): +750 HP, +30 Adaptive Attack, 10% Spell Vamp; below 40% HP gain 30% Damage Reduction for 3 seconds and cut skill cooldowns by 2 seconds (60-second cooldown). A Fighter's anti-burst damage item.
- **Rose Gold Meteor** (2,030 gold): +30 Physical Attack, +20% Attack Speed, +10% Lifesteal; below 30% HP gain a shield and a burst of speed (60-second cooldown).
- **Valkyrie's Shield** against magic burst assassins and mages.
- Spells: Aegis or Purify on carries when the enemy has a lot of burst or control.

guides.title: Against attack-speed carries
guides.sub: Freya, Marksmen and on-hit builds
guides.body:
## Why it matters this patch
Freya was the most contested hero of MPL PH Season 18 (100% pick or ban presence). Her ultimate turns her basic attacks into splash damage with healing, and her damage relies on attack speed and on-hit effects.
## The answer set
- **Chastise Pauldron** cuts the attacker's attack speed and cap to 75% for 2 seconds whenever you take damage.
- **Blade Armor** punishes every basic attack with reflected damage and a slow.
- **Sea Halberd** or **Dominance Ice** for the healing.
- Hard crowd control and Petrify on the frontline. Freya's ultimate, per her kit, grants control immunity during its activation, so hold your stun until after she lands.

guides.title: Roaming and jungle items
guides.sub: Choosing your role item
guides.body:
## Jungle
Junglers pick one of three Retribution items:
- **Flame Retribution**, **Ice Retribution** or **Bloody Retribution**. Each upgrades as you farm and changes what your Retribution does to heroes. Open each in the Items screen for its current effect.
## Roaming
The Roamer buys roaming boots and picks one roaming effect: **Active - Conceal**, **Passive - Dire Hit**, **Passive - Encourage**, **Passive - Favor** (as listed in the MLBB Wiki item data). Pick the effect that matches your hero: engage tanks prefer Conceal or Encourage, sustain supports prefer Favor.
!! The exact numbers of jungle and roam items change often between patches; the Items screen shows the wiki text that was current when this data was gathered.

guides.title: Freya
guides.sub: Sustained EXP fighter whose ultimate grants control immunity and turns her into a lifesteal brawler
guides.body:
## Hero Overview
Freya is a physical melee fighter for the EXP lane or jungle. Her kit runs on Sacred Orbs: every basic attack gives one, up to 6, and each orb consumed gives her next basic attack 100% attack speed. Her Valkyrie Slash has no base cooldown but costs 2 orbs, so her pattern is attack, attack, slash, attack, attack, slash. Her ultimate dives with control immunity and 50% damage reduction, then turns her into a Valkyrie for 12 seconds with healing and splash on every basic attack.
She is picked because that ultimate gives her a reliable way into fights against teams with control, and because once she is in, she keeps healing as long as she keeps hitting. She is weak when she cannot hit: kited, kept away, or facing a target with more sustain than her.
## Kit deep-dive
### Power of Einherjar (passive)
Freya gains 1 Sacred Orb per basic attack, up to 6 orbs. Consuming one orb gives her next basic attack 100% attack speed, up to 6 stacks. Orbs recover out of combat. How to use it: orbs are both her attack-speed engine and the currency for Valkyrie Slash. Why it matters: her damage comes from many fast hits, so having orbs going into a fight is the difference between a fast burst and a slow start. Let them recover before you engage.
### Leap of Faith (Skill 1)
Freya leaps to a target area and strikes the ground, gaining a shield and dealing damage while knocking enemies airborne for 0.4 seconds. How to use it: it is her gap-closer, her control and her defense. Leap onto the target when they try to escape, or leap onto a group to knock them up while the shield absorbs damage. Why it matters: the shield and short knock-up let her start a trade on her terms.
### Valkyrie Slash (Skill 2)
Freya charges forward and slashes, dealing damage and slowing enemies by 30% for 0.5 seconds. It has no base cooldown but consumes 2 orbs per cast, and deals 50% damage to creeps. How to use it: it is both a chase tool and damage. Alternate attacks and slashes so orbs keep coming. Why it matters: as long as she keeps hitting, she has slashes, and every slash is a short dash and a slow.
### Valkyrie Descent (Ultimate)
Freya dives to a target area as a Valkyrie with control immunity and 50% damage reduction, dealing damage and a 40% slow to enemies in her path and at the landing point for 2 seconds. On landing, she enters the Valkyrie state for 12 seconds: her basic attacks deal extra damage, recover HP per hit and splash. How to use it: the dive is her engage; the state is her sustained fight. Why it matters: the immunity during the dive lets her land in the middle of the enemy without being stopped, and the 12-second state heals her as long as she keeps attacking.
::curve 3,4,4 | A strong mid game; her late game depends on landing in a fight with the ultimate.
## How the kit fits together
Freya's loop is basic attacks for orbs, orbs for attack speed and slashes, slashes to stay on the target, and the ultimate to enter fights and heal. The leap's shield and knock-up start trades. In the Valkyrie state, every attack heals and splashes, so a Freya who stays on targets is very hard to kill.
What breaks the loop is losing contact. Knockbacks, slows and kiting all stop her from hitting, which stops orbs, slashes and healing. Her ultimate's dive answers this for its duration, but after that she must stay in range on her own.
## Combos
::combo Lane all-in | BA > BA > S1 > S2 > BA > S2 | Build orbs, leap and shield, slash to stay on the target, and alternate attacks and slashes.
Why it works: the first attacks build orbs for slashes. The leap gives a shield and knock-up as the enemy responds. Then attacks and slashes alternate, each slash consuming orbs and slowing the target, so they cannot walk away.
::combo Teamfight entry | ULT > S1 > BA > S2 > BA | Dive in with control immunity, leap onto the backline for the shield and knock-up, and keep attacking for the healing.
Why it works: the dive cannot be stopped, and the slow at the landing point keeps enemies near her. The leap reaches the backline and shields her, and in the Valkyrie state every basic attack heals and splashes.
## Builds and emblems
::build Sustained fighter | Warrior Boots, War Axe, Corrosion Scythe, Brute Force Breastplate, Sea Halberd, Immortality | War Axe and Corrosion Scythe suit a basic-attack fighter with many hits; Brute Force Breastplate stacks quickly with her attack speed; Sea Halberd cuts healing on her targets.
::emblem Custom Fighter Emblem | Firmness, Festival of Blood, Brave Smite | Defense, spell vamp and a heal when her skills hit heroes.
::spells Retribution, Vengeance, Flicker | Retribution in the jungle; Vengeance or Flicker in the EXP lane.
How to choose: Freya wants items that reward many hits and attack speed. Sea Halberd moves up when the enemy has sustain. Vengeance is good in lane against divers; Flicker when you need extra reach for the ultimate.
## Laning
In the EXP lane, Freya wins trades when she has orbs and the enemy steps into leap range. Build orbs on minions before a trade, then leap and alternate attacks and slashes. Back off when orbs run out and let them recover out of combat.
## Teamfights
Use the ultimate to land where enemies stand close together, not on a lone target. Her splash attacks and healing are best in tight spaces, which is why objective pits suit her.
::map objectives | Freya's splash attacks and healing are strongest in tight spaces: fight around Turtle and Lord pits where enemies stand close together.
After landing, attack the nearest target you can stay on and look for the backline with the leap. The control immunity lasts only during the dive, so expect the enemy to use their control once you land.
## Decision-making by game state
When ahead, her healing in the Valkyrie state lets her fight several enemies; dive the backline. When behind, wait for the enemy to use their control and then ultimate. When even, play around objectives where enemies group.
## Advanced techniques
- Orb banking: let orbs recover before engaging so your first slashes are available immediately.
- Slash chases: slashes are short dashes, so alternating attacks and slashes keeps up with fleeing targets.
- Ultimate landing: aim for the spot where enemies will be grouped; the slow on landing keeps them there.
- Leap as escape: after the Valkyrie state, the leap can carry her out of a lost fight.
- State timing: the Valkyrie state lasts 12 seconds. If the fight is not going to happen in that window, do not land yet; a descent wasted on positioning leaves her without healing when the real fight starts.
## Jungle play and the first fights
When Freya jungles, her clear speed depends on orbs. Valkyrie Slash deals only 50% damage to creeps, so do not spam it on camps the way you would on heroes; use basic attacks to build orbs and attack speed, and slash only to reach the next camp or finish a monster. The out-of-combat orb recovery means walking between camps refills her for the next one.
Her first strong moment is the ultimate. Before it, her ganks rely on Leap of Faith's short knock-up and the slows from slashes, which work best on a laner who is already low or slowed by your teammate. After it, she can dive a lane with control immunity during the descent, land with a 40% slow, and keep attacking to heal through turret or enemy damage. That makes her ganks much stronger, but the Valkyrie state lasts 12 seconds and the ultimate has a long cooldown, so a wasted dive means several minutes without her best tool.
## Laning details
In the EXP lane, orb management decides trades. Hit minions to build orbs before the enemy walks up, then start the trade with orbs ready so your first slashes come immediately. When you run low, step back: orbs recover out of combat, and returning with a full set gives you another strong trade. Leap of Faith's shield is best used when the enemy commits their burst, because it absorbs it while you hit back.
## Reading the fight
The question Freya asks in every fight is: can I keep hitting? Look at the enemy team for three things. Knockbacks and pulls stop her from attacking and break her chain. Slows and kiting let a marksman stay out of range. Burst can kill her before her healing catches up. If the enemy has all three ready, wait for them to be used on someone else, then dive. If they have used them, dive immediately, because her healing in the Valkyrie state rewards a long fight and the enemy has nothing left to stop it.
## Situational adjustments
Against heavy anti-heal, prioritize defense over damage so you survive long enough to use the Valkyrie state. Against teams with a lot of knockback, wait for those skills before engaging. Against tanks who rely on control, the ultimate's immunity lets you dive past them.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Tigreal,Franco,Hylos,Johnson | bad=Karrie,Thamuz,Dyrroth,Esmeralda | ally=Estes,Angela,Atlas,Kaja
Why the good matchups are good: Freya beats tanks who rely on control, because her dive ignores it and her sustained healing outlasts their damage.
Why the bad matchups are bad: Karrie's true damage shreds her through sustain; Thamuz and Esmeralda outlast her; Dyrroth bursts her before she can heal.
Why the allies work: Estes and Angela heal her further; Atlas and Kaja group or lock targets for her dive.
Playing against Freya: save control until after her dive ends, buy healing reduction, and kite her during the twelve-second Valkyrie state.
## Common mistakes
- Engaging with no orbs: her slashes and attack speed depend on them.
- Diving a lone target: the ultimate is for groups.
- Stopping attacks in the Valkyrie state: the healing is per hit.
- Using the leap first: save it to follow or escape.

guides.title: Atlas
guides.sub: Mecha tank whose chained ultimate drags a whole team into a pile
guides.body:
## Hero Overview
Atlas is a magic melee tank who roams. He pilots a Mecha Sentry, and his kit lets him leave it, run ahead, and return with a stun. His ultimate, Fatal Links, throws chains around him that damage and slow enemy heroes, and recasting drags them all toward him and slams them down at a chosen location. A good Atlas ultimate pulls several heroes into one pile, which is why he is one of the best teamfight initiators in the game.
He is picked for that ultimate and for his passive frost aura, which freezes enemies who stay near him. He is weak against enemies who spread out, have suppression (which interrupts his channel), or cleanse his control.
## Kit deep-dive
### Frigid Breath (passive)
Each time Atlas casts a skill, he creates Frigid Breath around him for 5 seconds. Enemies who stay in the area over 1.5 seconds are slowed gradually until frozen for 0.5 seconds. He also gains extra physical and magic defense while it is present. How to use it: cast skills often and stand among enemies. Why it matters: the aura punishes enemies who stay near him, which adds control after his engage.
### Annihilate (Skill 1)
Atlas smashes the ground, causing 3 explosions that each deal magic damage. In Ejected State, both Atlas and his Mecha cast Annihilate. How to use it: it is damage and a way to trigger the frost aura. Why it matters: in Ejected State, two sets of explosions double the area.
### Perfect Match (Skill 2)
Atlas ejects, gaining 30% movement speed and slow immunity. The Mecha follows at increasing speed (it can only be controlled by suppression). When they meet, Atlas returns, dealing damage and stunning nearby enemies for 1 second. In Ejected State, they share HP and reduce damage taken by 50%. How to use it: run toward the enemy, and the Mecha arrives behind you for the stun. Why it matters: it is both an engage and a disengage, and the damage reduction makes it safe.
### Fatal Links (Ultimate)
Atlas throws chains around him and channels (only suppression interrupts), damaging enemy heroes hit and slowing them by 40% for 3 seconds. Recasting drags the targets toward him and slams them down at a chosen location. In Ejected State, the Mecha returns immediately, but the stun is replaced by a 40% slow. How to use it: get into the middle of the enemy team, cast, then drag them into your team. Why it matters: it groups enemies for your team's area damage.
::curve 4,5,4 | Useful early for picks, strongest when the enemy groups for objectives, and still decisive late with a single good ultimate.
## How the kit fits together
Atlas engages with Perfect Match: eject, run in, and let the Mecha catch up for the stun. Then he casts Fatal Links, chaining everyone nearby, and drags them into his team. Annihilate and the frost aura add damage and freezes after the drag. Every skill cast refreshes Frigid Breath, so a full combo leaves enemies standing in his aura.
## Combos
::combo Standard engage | S2 > ULT > S1 | Eject toward the group, chain them, drag them into your team as the Mecha arrives.
Why it works: Perfect Match gives speed and slow immunity, letting Atlas reach the group. The chains slow them, and the drag pulls them into your team. Annihilate adds damage and refreshes the frost aura.
::combo Flicker chain | ULT > Flicker > ULT | Throw chains, Flicker while channeling to reposition, then drag them into your team.
Why it works: the channel is not interrupted by Flicker, so throwing chains and then Flickering back toward your team pulls the enemies further into your side.
::combo Lane harass | S1 > BA > S1 | Explosions plus passive aura to slow and freeze.
Why it works: each skill refreshes Frigid Breath, so enemies who stay near you get slowed and frozen. In lane, this means a laner who trades with your partner while standing near you will be slowed after 1.5 seconds and then frozen for 0.5 seconds, which gives your laner free hits. The explosions also add damage, but the real effect is the aura: it forces the enemy to step away from the wave or accept the freeze.
## Builds and emblems
::build Engage tank | Tough Boots, Dominance Ice, Antique Cuirass, Radiant Armor, Oracle, Immortality | Dominance Ice for grouped fights and anti-heal, Antique Cuirass and Radiant Armor against physical and magic damage, Oracle for shields and healing, Immortality to survive after the engage.
::emblem Custom Tank Emblem | Vitality, Tenacity, Concussive Blast | HP, more defense when low, and extra damage on basic attacks.
::spells Flicker | Flicker is the standard; it gives extra range to the chains.
How to choose: Atlas needs to survive after his engage, so defense comes first. Dominance Ice is strong because he is always among grouped enemies.
## Roaming and early game
Atlas roams between the gold lane and mid, setting up kills with Perfect Match.
::map roam | Move between gold lane and mid, setting up kills with Perfect Match.
Early, his stun and frost aura help laners get kills. Once he has his ultimate, he becomes the main initiator for objectives.
## Perfect Match in depth
Perfect Match is more flexible than it looks. When Atlas ejects, he moves 30% faster and is immune to slows, and the Mecha follows at increasing speed. While ejected, he and the Mecha share one HP bar and take 50% less damage. When they meet, he returns and stuns nearby enemies for 1 second. This has three uses. As an engage, you run into the enemy and the Mecha arrives behind you, stunning whoever is near you. As a chase, you run after a fleeing target and the Mecha's speed catches you up for the stun. As a disengage, you run away from danger with slow immunity and halved damage, and the Mecha's arrival stuns anyone chasing you.
The only thing that controls the Mecha is suppression. That means the enemy's suppression skills are your biggest threat: they can stop the Mecha from reaching you, which leaves you in the enemy team without a stun.
## Reading the engage
The ultimate's value depends entirely on how many heroes it catches and where you drag them. Before you engage, check three things. First, how many enemies are close enough to the chains? Two is acceptable, three or more is excellent, one is usually a waste. Second, is your team ready? A drag into empty space just puts you in the middle of the enemy with no help. Your damage dealers must be close enough to hit the pile when it lands. Third, do the enemies have suppression? Suppression interrupts the channel and stops the drag, so wait for it to be used or for that hero to be away.
When the chains are worth it, commit fully: Perfect Match or Flicker in, chains, drag, Annihilate, and stay among the pile so the frost aura keeps freezing them.
## Using the drag location
The recast of Fatal Links lets you choose where the enemies land. That choice is as important as the chains themselves. Drag them toward your damage dealers, under your turret, into a narrow path, or away from their own backline so their carries are separated from their tanks. Avoid dragging them into open space far from your team, because then your team must walk to the pile and the enemies have time to recover.
## Teamfights
Atlas's teamfight is about the ultimate. Look for the moment enemies are grouped: around a Turtle or Lord, in a narrow jungle path, or chasing your team. Use Perfect Match or Flicker to get into the middle of them, cast the chains, and drag them into your team. Your team must be ready with area damage.
## Decision-making by game state
When ahead, look for engages around objectives. When behind, wait for enemies to group near your turrets, then drag them into your team. When even, hold the ultimate for the first big enemy engage or objective fight.
## Advanced techniques
- Ejected State: Perfect Match makes Atlas immune to slows and halves damage taken; use it to run into the enemy team safely.
- Flicker chain: Flicker during the channel to drag enemies further toward your team.
- Aura control: stay among enemies after the drag; the frost aura freezes enemies who stay near you.
- Suppression awareness: only suppression interrupts the channel; know which enemies have it, and engage when they are dead, far away, or have just used it.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Ling,Lancelot,Fanny,Gusion | bad=Popol and Kupa,Eudora,Lolita,Ixia,Aamon | ally=Pharsa,Eudora,Odette,Yve
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+; the good and ally lists are assessments from his kit (area damage combos and mobile heroes he can lock).
Why the good matchups are good (assessment): Ling, Lancelot, Fanny and Gusion rely on dashes to reach targets, and a chain that catches them mid-dash, followed by a drag into your team, punishes their entry hard. They also tend to dive into the middle of fights, where the chains land.
Why the bad matchups are bad (assessment): Popol and Kupa, Lolita and Aamon have ways to deny or punish his engage, Eudora bursts him or his targets after the drag, and Ixia punishes grouped fights from range.
Why the allies work: Pharsa, Eudora, Odette and Yve deal area damage to the pile he creates.
Playing against Atlas: spread out, keep a suppression or a cleanse ready, and do not group in tight spots when he has his ultimate.
## Common mistakes
- Ultimate on one target: it is for groups.
- Dragging into nothing: drag only when your team is ready.
- Forgetting the aura: cast skills often to keep Frigid Breath active.
- Ejecting into suppression: suppression interrupts the Mecha and the channel.

guides.title: Hirara
guides.sub: Two-skill jungle assassin who wins by sequencing energy, not by spamming buttons
guides.body:
## Hero Overview
Hirara is a physical melee assassin built for the jungle, and her kit is unlike almost anyone else's: she has only two base skills, **Meisen-e** (up to two joystick dashes) and **Kaerazu** (a fan-shaped strike followed by a delayed second hit at the target spot). Her passive lets you drag one skill onto the other to cast an enhanced combo version, and each combo cast spends one of her two Crimson Energy charges. That is the whole kit. There is no ultimate to wait for, which is exactly why she is picked: she is a complete threat from her first clear instead of from level 4.
The way to understand Hirara is as a budget. At full strength you own two dashes from Meisen-e, one Kaerazu, and two combo casts. Every engagement is a question of how you spend that budget, and the single biggest difference between a weak and a strong Hirara is whether there is anything left in the budget when the enemy answers. Energy refills on the same timer as Meisen-e, and spending energy interrupts the refill, so chaining casts carelessly does not just empty you, it also delays when you are dangerous again.
The price for her early power is written into her passive: she deals only 30% plus 4% per hero level of her damage to minions. At level 1 that is a third of her damage; even late it is well short of full. She cannot rescue a lost lane by shoving waves, and she is a poor tower-pusher on her own. Her value comes from kills, objectives and the map pressure created by the threat of both. Draft her when your team has a frontline to fight behind and lanes that can hold themselves.
## Kit deep-dive: the what, how and why of each piece
### Twin Fans: Ukifune (passive)
What it does: drag Meisen-e onto Kaerazu to cast **Infernal Torrent**, or drag Kaerazu onto Meisen-e to cast **Falling Maple**. Each costs one Crimson Energy, and she holds two. How to use it: think of energy as your real cooldown and of the base skills as filler between energy casts. Why it matters: combo casts hold all of her control (the immobilize) and all of her defence (the untargetable window). If you spend both charges on damage, you have spent your only escape and your only lock too.
A useful habit is to say your state to yourself before every fight: "two energy, dash up" means you can engage and still leave; "one energy, no dash" means you can finish a target but not survive a counter-engage; "no energy" means you are a melee hero with a short-range poke and should not be in front of anyone.
### Meisen-e (Skill 1)
Two joystick dashes, the first in your facing direction, each dealing damage to enemies it passes through. The first dash is commitment; the second is information. Because the first always goes where you face, line up your approach so that facing direction already points through the target and out the far side; that way the first dash puts you behind them and cuts their retreat. The second dash is the most valuable button you own. It can extend a chase, reposition for a Kaerazu angle, carry you out of a fight, or end Falling Maple early. Holding it until the enemy has committed their crowd control is the habit that keeps Hirara alive.
### Kaerazu (Skill 2)
A fan-shaped hit in front of you, then a second hit at the target location after a short delay that deals twice the first hit. The delayed hit is the real damage, and it is placed, not aimed at a body. Against a moving enemy, put it where they will be when it lands; against an enemy who is held by Infernal Torrent, put it on top of them and it cannot miss. In the jungle, stack the monsters together and place the delayed hit where it covers the whole group: this is what makes her clear speed respectable despite having so few buttons.
### Infernal Torrent (Meisen-e enhanced)
After the first dash, Hirara spins, dealing 2.5 times Kaerazu's base damage and immobilizing enemies for 0.8 seconds. This is your lock and your setup. An immobilize stops movement, so it is what makes the delayed hit of Kaerazu reliable. The window is short, so the follow-up must already be on its way when the spin lands: cast Kaerazu immediately, or have a teammate's skill in flight. A common mistake is to spin and then think; by the time you decide, the target is free.
### Falling Maple (Kaerazu enhanced)
Hirara becomes untargetable and immobilized for up to one second; after 0.6 seconds she deals three times Kaerazu's base damage, and she can cast the second Meisen-e dash to end the state early. Read that carefully: it is both her largest single hit and her defensive button. Untargetable means a point-and-click skill or a projectile aimed at you as you enter the state does not find you. But you are also immobilized, so you are standing still in a known spot. If the enemy has area damage that will still be on the ground when you come out, you take it. That is why the option to leave early with the second dash matters: cast Falling Maple as the enemy commits, let the hit land, and dash out in the same motion.
::curve 4,4,3 | Strong from the first clears because her damage comes from skills and combos, not from an ultimate. She falls off if fights become long and tank-heavy.
## How the kit fits together
Every Hirara fight follows the same three beats: approach, lock, and either finish or leave. The approach uses the first Meisen-e dash or simple walking through brush. The lock is Infernal Torrent. The finish is Kaerazu or Falling Maple; the leave is the second dash, ideally out of Falling Maple. If you count the resources, a full engage that locks, bursts and leaves uses both energy charges and both dashes, which is why her fights are short and why the wait between them is long. You do not fight twice in ten seconds with Hirara; you fight once, well, and then you are a threat again when Meisen-e and energy come back.
The practical consequence is target choice. Her full budget kills one squishy hero who is away from help. It does not kill a tank, and it does not kill a carry standing behind two teammates with crowd control ready. Before you commit, ask: if I spend everything on this target, does it die, and can the enemy reach me before my second dash is back? If the answer to either is no, wait.
## Combos
::combo Pick-off | S1 > [Infernal Torrent] > S2 > BA | Dash in, spin to immobilize, then Kaerazu so the delayed hit lands during the immobilize. Ends with one energy left for an escape.
Why this order works: the plain first dash closes distance without spending energy, so the spin from Infernal Torrent is the only charge you use. Kaerazu is cast while the target is immobilized, which is the only time its delayed hit is guaranteed. You finish with a basic attack, and you still hold one energy for Falling Maple if someone turns on you. Use it on the lone marksman or mage farming a side lane.
::combo Burst through a skill | [Infernal Torrent] > [Falling Maple] > S1 | Spend both energies: lock, then go untargetable as the enemy answers, and use the remaining dash to exit or chase.
Why this order works: Infernal Torrent locks the target, and the enemy's natural reaction is to hit back with their control. Falling Maple goes untargetable in that exact moment, so their answer misses while your largest hit lands. The second dash then decides the fight's ending: chase if they are low and alone, leave if help is arriving. This combo uses everything, so only take it when the kill is certain or when it wins an objective.
::combo Dodge-first | S2 > [Falling Maple] > S1 | Into a target that is about to cast a targeted control skill: poke with Kaerazu, become untargetable as they cast, then dash out of Falling Maple to finish.
Why this order works: against heroes whose main defence is a single targeted skill, the threat of that skill is what stops you from engaging. This combo baits it: poke with Kaerazu to draw the reaction, go untargetable as they cast, and you are now fighting a hero whose answer is on cooldown. It keeps your second energy unused, so the next Infernal Torrent is still in your pocket.
## Builds and emblems
::build Core physical assassin | Tough Boots, Hunter Strike, Blade of Despair, Malefic Roar, Sea Halberd, Immortality | Hunter Strike grants a burst of decaying movement speed after five consecutive hits on the same target, which her dashes and combo hits reach quickly; Blade of Despair amplifies damage on targets already below half HP; Malefic Roar cuts through armor once tanks itemize; Sea Halberd stops sustain heroes; Immortality is the late-game safety slot.
::build Into heavy burst and control | Tough Boots, Hunter Strike, Malefic Roar, Blade of Despair, Queen's Wings, Immortality | Queen's Wings gives 30% damage reduction and two seconds off her cooldowns when she drops below 40% HP, which often buys the second energy charge she needs to escape; Tough Boots cut control and slow duration by 25%.
How to choose: the core build assumes you are the one choosing the fights. When the enemy has several point-and-click stuns or a lot of burst, your problem is not damage but surviving the first second after you commit, and that is what the second build buys. Tough Boots are in both because her whole plan depends on not being held while her dashes are available. Sea Halberd is the slot to bring forward when the enemy has a healer or a sustain fighter; Malefic Roar moves up when their frontline has started buying armor and your full budget no longer kills.
::emblem Custom Assassin Emblem | Rupture, Seasoned Hunter, Killing Spree | Rupture adds penetration for early skirmishes; Seasoned Hunter speeds up Turtle and Lord; Killing Spree's heal and speed after damaging low-HP heroes chains her into the next target.
::spells Retribution | Retribution is required for the jungle. Pick the Retribution upgrade that fits the game: the slowing upgrade (Ice) for chasing, the damage upgrade (Flame) for duels, or the sustain upgrade (Bloody) when you expect long fights.
## Early game: clearing and first moves
Her early clear is about using Kaerazu's delayed hit on stacked monsters and Meisen-e's dash damage through camps. Because she has no ultimate to unlock, the moment she has both skills and both energy charges she can gank, so the first gank window comes earlier than for most junglers. The condition is simple: never gank with less than two energy. One charge for the lock, one for the answer; a gank with one charge is a gank with no escape.
How to choose the lane: look for an enemy laner with no dash and a lane pushed toward your side. Approach from the river or side brush at an angle where the first Meisen-e dash, which travels in your facing direction, crosses the enemy's path back to their turret. If the dash lands behind them, Infernal Torrent holds them in reach of your laner, and the kill comes from two heroes rather than from your budget alone.
::map gank | Approach from the river or behind the side brush so the first dash cuts off the retreat toward their turret.
What to avoid early: chasing an enemy who has a dash of their own, and fighting near a full wave. Minions take little damage from her, so a wave does not just fail to help, it also blocks a lot of her uptime while the enemy's minions keep hitting her. Contest the first Turtle when your laners have priority, and use Retribution timing rather than raw damage to secure it.
## Mid game: turning pressure into objectives
In the mid game, Hirara's threat matters as much as her kills. An enemy marksman who knows Hirara is missing from the map has to farm closer to their turret, which gives your side lanes time and space. Use that: show on one side, then disappear toward the objective on the other. When the enemy roamer and jungler are seen far away, the backline is exposed and the Turtle or a turret is free.
When you are ahead, invade. Her early power and two dashes make her good at catching an enemy jungler in their own camps, especially one who must use skills to clear. When you are behind, stop trying to force duels and play around objectives and vision, entering fights only after the enemy has used their control.
## Late game and teamfights
Hirara is not a front-to-back fighter, and she should almost never be the first hero into a five-versus-five. Her job in a teamfight is to wait on the flank while the frontlines collide and the enemy spends their crowd control on your tank. The signal to enter is when the hero who can stop her (a tank with a point-and-click stun, a support with a heal or cleanse, a mage with a lock) has used that skill. Then she enters on the backline target, in this order: the enemy carry who is out of position, the mage who has used their spells, then anyone already below half HP, where Blade of Despair's bonus applies.
If your team loses the opening, do not try to save it with a solo dive. A Hirara who survives a lost fight still threatens the next one; a Hirara who dies to a five-hero backline just makes the lost fight a bigger loss.
## Advanced techniques
- Energy discipline: a full combo uses both charges. When you know an enemy has a cleanse or an untargetable skill of their own, keep one charge for Falling Maple so you can survive their answer rather than spending everything up front.
- Falling Maple as a dodge: casting it as an enemy commits a targeted skill makes that skill miss you. It does not make you immune to area damage that is already on the ground when the window ends, so exit with the second dash rather than waiting out the full second.
- Facing control: since the first Meisen-e dash goes in your facing direction, walk past the target before you cast so that you dash back through them toward their own team. The spin then catches them between you and your team.
- Refill awareness: energy recovers on Meisen-e's timer and spending it interrupts the recovery. After a fight, avoid spending a charge on monsters; let both energy and Meisen-e come back together so the next engagement starts from a full budget.
- Objective steals: Falling Maple's delayed burst plus Retribution can take a Turtle or Lord at the last moment, and the untargetable window protects you from a single targeted answer while you do it.
## Matchups and how to play against her
::vs good=Pharsa,Lylia,Layla,Miya | bad=Khufra,Chou,Franco,Belerick | ally=Atlas,Tigreal,Masha,Gloo
Why the good matchups are good: Pharsa, Lylia, Layla and Miya rely on distance to survive, and Hirara closes distance twice. Once the first dash and the spin land, a hero without a reliable escape has nothing to do during the immobilize.
Why the bad matchups are bad: Khufra and Chou can interrupt a dash and catch her mid-commit, which breaks her whole sequence. Franco's hook pulls her out of her flank before her team has engaged. Belerick's taunt forces her to walk into his team and also punishes the hits she lands on him. The common thread is control that she cannot dodge with Falling Maple, or control used before she has reached her target.
