Why the allies work: Atlas and Tigreal group enemies and spend the enemy's attention, giving Hirara a clean backline; Masha and Gloo hold the frontline long enough for her to pick her moment.
To play against Hirara: track her energy. After she uses both combos she has no answer, so the moment to turn on her is right after Falling Maple ends. Keep your backline close to a tank, and save a point-and-click control skill for the second Meisen-e dash rather than the first.
## Common mistakes
- Ganking with one energy: you lock the target, but when their jungler or roamer arrives you have nothing.
- Spending Falling Maple for damage when it should be your dodge: if a key enemy control skill is still up, Falling Maple belongs to that skill.
- Trying to push turrets alone: her reduced damage to minions means slow waves and slow turrets; bring a laner.
- Entering a fight first: she has no frontline tools. Wait for the enemy's control to be used.
- Forgetting the facing direction: a first dash in the wrong direction wastes half your mobility before the fight starts.

guides.title: Paquito
guides.sub: Boxer fighter who counts to three and then hits much harder
guides.body:
## Hero Overview
Paquito is a melee physical fighter and assassin for the EXP lane. His passive, **Champ Stance**, triggers after every three skill casts: his next skill is enhanced and ignores current cooldowns, and casting it grants 60% movement speed that decays over 2.5 seconds.
**Heavy Left Punch** deals damage and gives a shield if it hits a hero; enhanced, it hits harder and the shield is increased to 120% (and the two shields stack). **Jab** dashes and jabs, stopping early if he collides with a hero or creep; enhanced, it deals much more damage. His ultimate, **Knockout Strike**, is an elbow that knocks back, then a haymaker that slows by 75% for 1 second as he darts back; enhanced, it is an uppercut that knocks airborne for 0.5 seconds.
Why he is picked: his skills have short cooldowns and the enhanced skill comes often, so he trades and bursts very quickly. His weakness: the enhanced cycle can be disrupted, and he lacks sustained damage against tanky targets.
## Kit deep-dive
### Champ Stance (passive)
Count your casts. The fourth skill is the enhanced one, so plan which skill you want enhanced.
### Heavy Left Punch (Skill 1)
Your poke and shield. Enhanced, it gives a bigger shield for trades.
### Jab (Skill 2)
Your gap closer. It stops on the first hero or creep in its path.
### Knockout Strike (Ultimate)
Your burst. The enhanced version knocks airborne instead of slowing.
::curve 5,4,3 | Very strong early, strong in mid-game skirmishes, and less dominant late against tanky teams.
## Combos
::combo Enhanced ultimate | S1 > S2 > S1 > ULT | Three casts, then the enhanced uppercut.
::combo Enhanced jab | S1 > ULT > S1 > S2 | Three casts, then an enhanced Jab to finish.
## Builds and emblems
::build Burst fighter | Warrior Boots, Hunter Strike, Blade of Despair, Malefic Roar, Queen's Wings, Immortality | Damage and penetration for bursts, plus survival for the late game.
::emblem Custom Fighter Emblem | Firmness, Festival of Blood, Brave Smite | Defense, spell vamp and healing on skill damage.
::spells Petrify, Flicker | Petrify for locks; Flicker for engages.
!! Builds are based on item effects and his kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Trade aggressively with enhanced skills. His short cooldowns let him cycle to an enhanced skill often, so short trades favor him. The best trades start when the enemy laner uses a key skill on the wave: step in, punch for the shield, and finish the cycle before they can answer.
::map lane | Pressure the EXP lane early.
## Mid game and teamfights
Look for picks on squishy heroes. In fights, use enhanced skills on the backline when possible.
## Advanced techniques
- Cast counting: track your casts so the enhanced skill is the one you need. A common pattern is to spend the first three casts on poke and repositioning, then save the enhanced cast for the ultimate when the target is low.
- Shield stacking: the regular and enhanced shields stack for big trades. Enter a trade with a punch that hits, then use the enhanced punch so both shields are up while the enemy answers.
- Jab collision: Jab stops at the first hero or creep, so watch for enemies blocking your path. Keep jungle creeps in mind when chasing through the river: they stop Jab early too.
- Movement after enhanced skills: the 60% movement speed after an enhanced skill decays over 2.5 seconds. Use it to walk out of the enemy's retaliation or to follow a fleeing target.
- Ultimate direction: the normal ultimate ends with Paquito darting backward, which lets you trade and leave. The enhanced uppercut knocks airborne instead, which is better when your team is ready to follow up.
## Draft and team fit
Paquito works best in a team that can follow his early aggression: a jungler who invades and a roamer who rotates to the EXP lane. In the MPL PH S18 playoffs he was picked 10 times (6 wins) and banned 23 times in 38 games; in the MPL ID S18 playoffs he was picked 15 times and banned 21 times in 41 games. In ranked Mythical Glory+ he is banned far less often (16.07% over the past 7 days), so he is usually available. Pick him when the enemy EXP laner is a melee fighter who cannot avoid short trades.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Masha,Freya,Lukas,Sun | bad=Natalia,X.Borg,Karina,Helcurt,Aldous | ally=Estes,Angela,Atlas,Tigreal
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+. The good list is an assessment from his early-game strength against melee fighters.
Playing against Paquito: track his casts; avoid him when he has the enhanced skill ready.
## Situational adjustments
- Against tanky teams: build more penetration.
- Against burst: build more defense.
- When ahead: invade the jungle.
## Practice drills
- Count drill: practice the three-cast cycle until you track it without thinking.
- Jab drill: practice Jab to reach targets past minions.
## Common mistakes
- Wasting enhanced skills.
- Diving without the enhanced skill ready.
- Losing track of the cast count.

guides.title: Marcel
guides.sub: Photographer support whose freeze buys his team two seconds to set up the kill
guides.body:
## Hero Overview
Marcel is a physical melee support whose ultimate, Golden Hour, freezes everyone in an area for 2s except himself and allies who carry his shield. His split soul Clemar automatically snaps photos of nearby enemy heroes, briefly freezing them and dealing true damage equal to 20 + 5% of their max HP, while granting a shield of the same value to Marcel and a nearby ally. His basic attacks deal fixed physical damage, and his extra HP is converted into hybrid defense. In short: he is a durable support who freezes enemies and shields allies just by being near.
He is picked for Golden Hour, one of the most decisive teamfight skills in the game, which can save a carry, reset a fight, or set up a guaranteed combo. He is weak against long-range poke and knockback that keep him from getting close.
## Kit deep-dive
### Platinum Snap (passive)
Marcel's basic attacks deal 50 physical damage, and his extra HP is converted into 1.5% hybrid defense. Clemar automatically snaps photos of nearby enemy heroes, causing a brief Frozen Moment and dealing 20 + 5% of their max HP as true damage, and giving the same value as a shield to Marcel and a nearby ally. Each target has a 12s cooldown. How to use it: just being near enemies triggers it, so walk toward them. Why it matters: the snap's true damage scales with the target's max HP, so it is stronger against tanks, and the shields protect his team. The snap also applies the shield that lets allies move inside Golden Hour.
### Framed Moment (Skill 1)
Clemar focuses on an area around Marcel, slowing enemy heroes by 60%. After 2.5s, he completes the shot, dealing 350 physical damage to enemies inside. How to use it: the slow holds them in the area; the shot lands at the end. Why it matters: when combined with Golden Hour's freeze, enemies cannot leave the area before the shot lands.
### Tracking Shot (Skill 2)
Marcel enters Tracking Haste for 3s, gaining 15% movement speed, rising to 75% when moving toward an enemy hero. Using it again dashes him in a direction, leaving a framing phantom while the Framed Moment area stays at its original location. How to use it: approach fast, then dash to adjust. Why it matters: it gives him the speed to reach enemies and the dash to reposition, and the framing area stays behind when he dashes.
### Golden Hour (Ultimate)
After a short delay, Clemar takes a wide-angle shot of an area for 2s. Inside, Marcel enters Tracking Haste, all other units are frozen and immune to all effects except his, and projectiles are frozen and continue after a delay (targeted projectiles deal 50% damage). Golden Hour resets Platinum Snap's cooldown on each enemy hero. Allies with the Platinum Snap shield can move freely inside. How to use it: decide whether you are saving, resetting or setting up before you cast. Why it matters: a freeze affects everyone, including your team, unless they carry the shield.
::curve 3,4,4 | His impact grows with the size of fights and the availability of Golden Hour.
## How the kit fits together
Marcel's kit revolves around proximity. The passive snaps and shields as he walks among enemies. Tracking Shot gets him close. Framed Moment slows and lands a delayed shot. Golden Hour freezes everything, resets the snap on every enemy hero, and lets shielded allies move. A Marcel who walks into the enemy team snaps every enemy, shields his team, and then freezes them, with his shielded allies able to move freely.
The key detail is the shield: allies who received a Platinum Snap shield can move inside Golden Hour. That means the order in which you snap and freeze decides whether your team can act.
## How Golden Hour actually wins fights
::steps Three uses of Golden Hour | Save: freeze the divers on top of your carry, and the carry walks out of range while they are frozen; Reset: freeze both teams mid-fight when you are losing, so allies with your shield reposition behind the frontline and enemies lose the momentum of their engage; Set up: freeze a group, snap every enemy again (the ultimate resets Platinum Snap on each of them), place Framed Moment so its shot lands as the freeze ends, and have allies stand ready with area skills aimed at where the frozen enemies are standing.
Why this matters: Golden Hour is not just a long stun. Because it freezes everyone without the shield, using it carelessly can freeze your own carry mid-combo. Decide which of the three uses you want before you cast, and make sure the allies who need to move have the shield.
## Combos
::combo Set-up lock | S2 > ULT > S1 | Run in with Tracking Shot, cast Golden Hour, then cast Framed Moment while the enemies are frozen so the 2.5-second shot lands just after the freeze ends.
Why it works: Tracking Shot gets you close quickly. Golden Hour freezes the enemies and resets the snap. Framed Moment cast during the freeze slows them as it ends, and the shot lands while they are still slowed, keeping them in place for your team's damage.
::combo Pick | S2 > S1 > S2 | Close the gap with Tracking Shot, slow with Framed Moment, and recast the dash to stay close so the target cannot leave the area before the shot.
Why it works: Framed Moment's area stays where it was cast when Marcel dashes, so the dash keeps him near the target while the slow holds them in the area until the shot.
## Builds and emblems
::build Roam tank | Tough Boots, Dominance Ice, Fleeting Time, Antique Cuirass, Oracle, Immortality | Fleeting Time cuts Golden Hour's current cooldown by 30% on each kill or assist; Oracle increases the shields he receives by 25%; Dominance Ice reduces enemy shields and healing near him.
::emblem Custom Support Emblem | Agility, Pull Yourself Together, Focusing Mark | Movement speed for roaming, shorter spell and item cooldowns, and extra damage for allies against targets he hits.
::spells Flicker, Vengeance | Flicker can carry him into range for Golden Hour on a group that thinks it is out of reach.
How to choose: Marcel's extra HP becomes hybrid defense, so HP items do double duty. Fleeting Time brings Golden Hour back faster, which is his main value.
## Roaming and early game
Early, Marcel's passive snaps and shields make him strong in skirmishes. Walk with your jungler or a laner, and let snaps and Framed Moment set up kills. Turtle and Lord fights put enemies close together, which is where a wide Golden Hour catches the most of them.
::map objectives | Turtle and Lord fights put enemies close together, which is where a wide Golden Hour catches the most of them.
## Teamfights
In teamfights, walk in early so the passive snaps enemies and shields your team. Then choose your Golden Hour use: save, reset or set up. Most of the time, set up is best when your team has area damage ready; save is best when an enemy diver is on your carry; reset is best when the fight is going badly and your team needs time.
## Decision-making by game state
When ahead, use set-up Golden Hours to take objectives and end the game. When behind, use it as a save or reset to deny enemy picks. When even, hold it for the first big enemy engage.
## Advanced techniques
- Shield first: allies with the snap shield move freely in Golden Hour, so walk near enemies to snap them before you freeze.
- Projectile freeze: projectiles freeze and continue later, and targeted projectiles deal 50% damage.
- Framed Moment in the freeze: cast it during the freeze so its slow begins as the freeze ends.
- Tracking Haste: moving toward enemies gives 75% movement speed; use it to catch targets.
## Reading the enemy draft
Marcel's value depends heavily on what the enemy plays. Against teams built around dives (assassins, fighters with dashes, tanks who engage), Golden Hour is mainly a save: the divers commit, you freeze them on top of your carry, and your carry walks away while they are stuck. Against teams that group up and fight front to back, it is a set-up: a wide freeze catches several heroes, the snap resets on each of them, and your team aims area damage at frozen targets. Against teams that poke from long range, Marcel struggles to get close enough for snaps or a freeze, so he should play around brush, flanks and objectives where the enemy must come to him.
Remember that projectiles freeze too. Enemy skills already in the air when Golden Hour lands pause and continue after a delay, and targeted projectiles deal 50% damage. Your own team's projectiles behave the same way, so a skill fired into the freeze will land when it ends, which can be timed with Framed Moment's shot.
## Situational adjustments
Against long-range poke, avoid walking in alone; wait for your team. Against divers, stay near your carry and hold Golden Hour as a save. Against grouped teams, look for a flank where the freeze catches several heroes.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Fanny,Ling,Lancelot,Gusion | bad=Valir,Pharsa,Lesley,Yve | ally=Pharsa,Claude,Freya,Hirara
Why the good matchups are good: Marcel catches divers who must come close, and his freeze undoes their engage.
Why the bad matchups are bad: Valir's knockback and Pharsa, Lesley and Yve's long-range poke keep him away.
Why the allies work: Pharsa and Claude deal area damage to frozen enemies; Freya and Hirara dive in with follow-up.
Playing against Marcel: spread out so Golden Hour cannot catch many of you, and attack him from range before he gets close enough to snap.
## Common mistakes
- Freezing your own team: allies without the shield are frozen too.
- Casting Golden Hour without a plan: choose save, reset or set up first.
- Walking alone: Marcel needs his team close to follow up.
- Missing the snap shield: walk near enemies first so allies get shields.

guides.title: Barats
guides.sub: Rider and lizard tank whose partner grows with every hit, then swallows an enemy whole
guides.body:
## Hero Overview
Barats is a melee physical tank and fighter for the EXP lane or jungle who fights on the back of his giant lizard, Detona. His passive, **Big Guy**, gives Detona a stack each time either of them damages an enemy with a skill, up to 10 stacks lasting 12 seconds. Each stack makes Detona bigger and adds 4-10 hybrid defense and 5% resilience. At max stacks, Detona's basic attacks become Trample, which hits a circular area, slows by 40% for 0.2 seconds and refreshes the stacks with each hit.
**So-Called Teamwork** has Detona spit oil in a fan for 60-160 physical damage, then Barats ignites it for 120-320; the area grows with Big Guy stacks. **Missile "Expert"** fires two missiles that slow by 40% for 1 second, and their exhaust pushes enemies toward Barats. His ultimate, **Detona's Welcome**, charges forward after a short delay, devours and suppresses the first enemy hit for 1.2 seconds, then spits them out; if they hit an enemy hero or a wall, they explode, and they and nearby enemies take 180-300 more damage and are stunned for 1 second. Barats is immune to control during the charge, and cancelling it refunds 60% of the cooldown. On respawn, Detona starts with 4-10 stacks.
Why he is picked: he becomes a huge, tanky frontliner in long fights, and his ultimate is a suppression that also stuns a second hero if aimed well. In the MPL PH S18 playoffs he was picked 15 times with 11 wins and banned 9 times. His weakness: he needs time in a fight to stack up, and kiting before he reaches 10 stacks keeps him small.
## Kit deep-dive
### Big Guy (passive)
Stacks are everything: defense, resilience and, at 10, the Trample attack. Keep hitting with skills to keep them up.
### So-Called Teamwork (Skill 1)
Your main damage and stack source with a short cooldown. The area grows as Detona grows.
### Missile "Expert" (Skill 2)
A slow plus a pull toward you. Use it to bring enemies into your oil fan.
### Detona's Welcome (Ultimate)
A suppression with a bonus: spit the target into a wall or another enemy hero for an explosion and a 1-second stun.
::curve 3,5,4 | Moderate early, very strong mid game once stacks build quickly, and still a durable frontliner late.
## Combos
::combo Stack up | S2 > S1 > BA > S1 | Missiles pull enemies in, oil and fire, then repeat to reach Trample.
::combo Wall slam | ULT > S1 > S2 | Swallow the target and spit them into a wall for the explosion, then oil and missiles.
::combo Pick into team | S2 > ULT > S1 | Pull with missiles, swallow, spit into your team or into another enemy hero.
## Builds and emblems
::build Durable frontline | Tough Boots, Cursed Helmet, Dominance Ice, Antique Cuirass, Radiant Armor, Immortality | Area damage while standing in fights, anti-heal and both kinds of defense.
::build Fighter damage | Warrior Boots, Hunter Strike, War Axe, Brute Force Breastplate, Queen's Wings, Immortality | More damage when your team needs a fighter more than a tank.
::emblem Custom Tank Emblem | Vitality, Tenacity, Concussive Blast | HP, defense when low, and extra damage on attacks.
::spells Petrify, Retribution | Petrify in the EXP lane; Retribution in the jungle.
!! Builds are based on item effects and his kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Trade with So-Called Teamwork on the wave and the enemy laner together, since every skill hit adds Big Guy stacks. Missile "Expert" pulls the enemy toward you, which makes it a good opener before the oil. Avoid long fights with heroes who outscale you early until you have your ultimate at level 4.
::map lane | Hold the EXP lane and stack Big Guy on the wave and the laner.
## Mid game and teamfights
Barats wants long fights. Walk into the middle of the enemy team, cast skills on as many heroes as possible to reach 10 stacks, and keep Trample going. Save Detona's Welcome for the enemy carry or the hero who threatens your backline. The spit direction matters: into a wall or another enemy hero gives an extra 1-second stun on everyone nearby.
## Advanced techniques
- Wall spits: fights in narrow jungle paths give you more walls to spit targets into.
- Cancel refund: cancelling the channel refunds 60% of the cooldown, so if the target moves away, cancel and try again soon.
- Control immunity: you cannot be controlled during the charge, so it is safe to start into enemy crowd control.
- Respawn stacks: you return with 4-10 stacks, so you are already part of the way to Trample after dying.
## Draft and team fit
In the MPL PH S18 playoffs, Barats was drafted most often with Hirara (8 games together, 5 wins), Kimmy (5 games, 4 wins), Zhuxin and Zetian (4 games each, 3 wins each). In ranked Mythical Glory+, over the past 7 days, he is picked in 0.86% of games with a 51.6% win rate. He works well with mages who have area damage, since his missiles bunch enemies up.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Masha,Freya,Aulus,Paquito | bad=Phoveus,Argus,Silvanna,Alucard,Fredrinn | ally=Hirara,Kimmy,Zhuxin,Zetian
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+. The ally list comes from his most frequent pro partners. The good list is an assessment: melee fighters who have to stand in his growing area.
Playing against Barats: kite him before he reaches max stacks, and avoid standing between him and a wall when his ultimate is up.
## Situational adjustments
- Against magic damage: Radiant Armor earlier.
- Against kiting teams: build movement and wait for your team's engage.
- When ahead: push side lanes, where his stacks let him duel most heroes.
## Practice drills
- Stack drill: count how fast you reach 10 stacks on grouped dummies.
- Spit drill: practice spitting a target into walls.
## Common mistakes
- Using the ultimate without aiming the spit.
- Engaging with no stacks.
- Chasing kiting heroes alone.

guides.title: Uranus
guides.sub: Regenerating tank who gets healthier the more enemies hit him
guides.body:
## Hero Overview
Uranus is a melee magic tank for the EXP lane, famous for being almost impossible to kill in long fights. His passive, **Radiance**, absorbs energy from incoming attacks to regenerate HP every 0.8 seconds; each stack lasts 10 seconds, and at max stacks (20), he regenerates 48-224 HP each tick, scaling with level.
**Ionic Edge** releases two orbiting blades for 155-255 magic damage, slowing by 30% for 2 seconds; each hit marks the target for 6 seconds, and each stack increases the skill's damage by 40%, up to 320%. **Transcendent Ward** charges to a location, damaging enemies along the way and at the target, slowing them by 25% and giving Uranus a 300-750 shield for 4 seconds that explodes for 300-750 magic damage when it ends or breaks. His ultimate, **Consecration**, removes slows, heals 200-400 HP, gives 60% movement speed for 8 seconds (decaying), adds 5-15 Radiance stacks, and increases shields received and HP regen by 20% for 8 seconds.
Why he is picked: he wins long side-lane duels and soaks damage in teamfights. In the MPL PH S18 playoffs he was picked 8 times (3 wins) and banned 12 times; in the MPL ID S18 playoffs, 7 picks (2 wins) and 7 bans. His weakness: low burst, and he is weak against anti-heal and percentage damage.
## Kit deep-dive
### Radiance (passive)
The more he is hit, the more he heals. Stacks build in fights and last 10 seconds.
### Ionic Edge (Skill 1)
Hit the same target with repeated casts to stack up to 320% damage.
### Transcendent Ward (Skill 2)
Engage, shield and a delayed explosion.
### Consecration (Ultimate)
A heal, speed boost and instant Radiance stacks.
::curve 3,4,5 | Moderate early, strong mid and very durable late.
## Combos
::combo Engage | S2 > S1 > BA > S1 | Charge in with the shield, then stack Ionic Edge.
::combo Sustain | ULT > S2 > S1 | Heal and speed up, charge back in.
## Builds and emblems
::build Sustain tank | Tough Boots, Dominance Ice, Antique Cuirass, Radiant Armor, Guardian Helmet, Immortality | Defense and regen; Guardian Helmet adds to his HP regeneration.
::emblem Custom Tank Emblem | Vitality, Tenacity, Concussive Blast | HP and defense.
::spells Petrify, Flicker | Petrify for lane control; Flicker for engages.
!! Builds are based on item effects and his kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Farm safely in the EXP lane and trade with Ionic Edge, stacking it on the enemy laner. Radiance makes you hard to pressure out of lane, so long trades favor you.
::map lane | Hold the EXP lane and outlast your opponent.
## Mid game and teamfights
Uranus is a frontliner who absorbs damage and splits the enemy's attention. Charge into the enemy team with Transcendent Ward, keep Ionic Edge on cooldown, and use Consecration when you need to stay in the fight or reposition. In side lanes, he can push and survive almost any duel.
## Advanced techniques
- Shield explosion: the shield explodes when it breaks or ends, so charge into enemies to make them break it.
- Ionic Edge stacking: repeated casts on the same target build damage.
- Ultimate timing: use it when Radiance stacks are low to instantly gain stacks.
- Slow removal: Consecration removes slows on himself, which makes it an escape against kiting teams as well as a heal.
- Stack upkeep: each Radiance stack lasts 10 seconds, so in a long side-lane duel, staying in combat keeps you at max regeneration.
- Shield boost: the ultimate increases shields received by 20%, which also strengthens the shield from Transcendent Ward if you cast it right after.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Dyrroth,Masha,Lukas,Paquito | bad=Masha,Gatotkaca,Argus,Phoveus,Yi Sun-shin | ally=Pharsa,Eudora,Odette,Yve
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+. Uranus is in the official counter list for Dyrroth, which is the basis of the good list. Note: Masha appears in both lists; treat her as a skill matchup.
Playing against Uranus: anti-heal and percentage damage, and avoid long fights with him. Burst him down when his Radiance stacks are low, and ignore him in teamfights if he is not protecting anyone: he deals little damage compared to the attention he draws.
## Draft and team fit
Uranus suits teams that want a frontline who can also hold a side lane alone. Pro teams in the Philippines banned him 12 times in the MPL PH S18 playoffs, more often than they picked him. In ranked Mythical Glory+, over the past 7 days, he is picked in only 0.3% of games with a 48.26% win rate, so he is rarely seen in solo queue. Pair him with damage dealers who can punish enemies distracted by his sustain.
## Situational adjustments
- Against anti-heal: more HP and focus on shields rather than healing.
- Against burst: more defense, and use the ultimate earlier in fights.
- When ahead: push side lanes and force the enemy to send two heroes to stop you.
- When behind: hold your lane and stay alive; your sustain lets you survive pressure until your team is ready.
## Practice drills
- Stack drill: practice stacking Ionic Edge on the same target.
- Shield drill: charge into a group so the shield explodes on as many enemies as possible.
## Common mistakes
- Fighting without Radiance stacks.
- Using the ultimate before you need the heal.
- Chasing kills instead of soaking damage for your team.

guides.title: Fanny
guides.sub: Cable assassin with the highest skill ceiling in the game
guides.body:
## Hero Overview
Fanny is a melee physical assassin for the jungle, famous for the hardest mechanics in Mobile Legends. She flies around the map on steel cables, and in the right hands she is everywhere at once. Her passive, **Air Superiority**, makes her deal 10%-20% extra damage depending on her flying speed and applies Prey Mark (up to 2 stacks) on each attack; her later skill hits on marked enemy heroes restore 8 energy per stack.
**Tornado Strike** whirls her blades for 275-525 physical damage to nearby enemies. **Steel Cable** shoots a cable that pulls her to the first obstacle hit; she can recast within 2 seconds as long as she has energy, each successive cast costs 2 less energy, and she automatically casts Tornado Strike when she hits an enemy mid-flight. Her ultimate, **Cut Throat**, leaps at a target enemy hero or creep for 400-650 physical damage, increased by 30% for each Prey Mark stack.
Why she is picked: unmatched mobility and burst. Her weakness: energy limits her, she needs walls to fly, and crowd control stops her instantly.
## Kit deep-dive
### Air Superiority (passive)
Flying faster means more damage. Prey Mark stacks feed energy back.
### Tornado Strike (Skill 1)
Short cooldown and auto-cast on cable hits.
### Steel Cable (Skill 2)
Your whole game. Each cable needs an obstacle; chaining cables reduces cost.
### Cut Throat (Ultimate)
A finisher that grows with Prey Mark stacks.
::curve 4,5,3 | Strong early with a blue buff, very strong mid game, and harder late against grouped control.
## Combos
::combo Cable burst | S2 > S2 > S1 > ULT | Two cables to fly through the target, Tornado Strike, then the ultimate with two Prey Marks.
::combo Hit and run | S2 > S1 > S2 | Fly in, strike, fly out.
## Builds and emblems
::build Burst assassin | Tough Boots, Hunter Strike, Blade of Despair, Malefic Roar, Blade of the Heptaseas, Immortality | Burst and penetration with survival.
::emblem Custom Assassin Emblem | Rupture, Seasoned Hunter, Killing Spree | Penetration and healing on kills.
::spells Retribution | Retribution in the jungle.
!! Builds are based on item effects and her kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Take the blue buff early to manage energy. Clear quickly and gank lanes where the enemy has no control.
Fanny's energy is her real cooldown. Every Steel Cable costs energy (each successive cast within 2 seconds costs 2 less), and her passive restores 8 energy per Prey Mark stack when her skills hit marked heroes. In practice, this means she runs out quickly against creeps and gets energy back by fighting heroes. Plan your route so you arrive at a gank with enough energy to cable in, fight and cable out again.
::map jungle | Clear quickly and gank.
## Mid game and teamfights
Wait for the enemy's control to be used, then fly in and burst the backline.
Your targets are the enemy marksman and mage. Fly in along walls, mark them with attacks and Tornado Strike, then finish with Cut Throat, which deals 30% more damage per Prey Mark stack. Leave the same way you came in. Do not stay in the middle of the enemy team: one stun stops your cables and you have no other way out. In grouped late-game fights, flank and pick off whoever is out of position rather than diving into five enemies.
## Advanced techniques
- Cable chaining: each recast costs less energy.
- Prey Mark: two stacks before the ultimate.
- Walls: learn which walls give the best cable angles.
- Auto Tornado Strike: hitting an enemy mid-flight casts Tornado Strike for you as long as you have energy, so flying through a target is both movement and damage.
- Energy on multiple heroes: the passive's energy restoration is reduced if you hit several enemy heroes in a short time, so energy is easiest to sustain in duels.
## Draft and team fit
In the MPL ID S18 playoffs Fanny was banned 26 times in 41 games and picked twice (2 wins). In ranked Mythical Glory+, over the past 7 days, her win rate is 42.8%, a reminder of how hard she is to play well.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Miya,Layla,Eudora,Nana | bad=Granger,Yve,Clint,Gloo,Kimmy | ally=Atlas,Tigreal,Kalea,Angela
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+.
Playing against Fanny: buy control, stay grouped, and invade her blue buff.
## Situational adjustments
- Against heavy control: wait for skills before entering.
- Against tanky teams: Malefic Roar earlier.
- When ahead: invade.
## Practice drills
- Cable drill: practice cable chains in custom games.
- Energy drill: practice managing energy.
## Common mistakes
- Running out of energy mid-fight.
- Entering before control is used.
- Ignoring the blue buff.

guides.title: Nolan
guides.sub: Rift assassin whose low-cooldown dashes cut the jungle into kill zones
guides.body:
## Hero Overview
Nolan is a melee physical assassin for the jungle. His passive, **Dimensional Rift**, leaves a rift with each skill that lasts 5 seconds and slows enemies by 30%. When two rifts touch, they activate, pulling enemies to their center and dealing 220 physical damage after a short delay; each activation that hits a hero or creep gives him 15 energy and heals him 150. Repeated activations on the same enemy deal 40% damage after the first. **Cosmic Leap**: if he neither deals nor takes damage for 5 seconds, his next basic attack dashes to the target and leaves a rift.
**Expansion** cuts a rectangle in front of him and leaves a rift at the first enemy hit. **Gauge** dashes and slashes, leaving a rift. Both have very short cooldowns. His ultimate, **Fracture**, slashes 3 times, leaving 3 rifts and slowing the target by 30% for 0.5 seconds, and activates them as he dashes backward.
Why he is picked: rift combos give him burst, healing and an escape in one rotation, and low cooldowns let him clear and fight constantly. His weakness: he needs to line up rifts precisely.
## Kit deep-dive
### Dimensional Rift (passive)
Two rifts touching activate. Plan the overlap rather than casting skills randomly.
### Expansion (Skill 1)
The rift appears at the first enemy hit, so it can be aimed to overlap a previous rift.
### Gauge (Skill 2)
The dash leaves a rift along its path; use it to connect with a rift from Expansion.
### Fracture (Ultimate)
Three rifts that activate as you dash away, which gives burst and an exit.
::curve 4,5,4 | Strong early clears, very strong mid-game ganks and still a threat late.
## Combos
::combo Rift burst | S1 > S2 > ULT | Expansion leaves a rift, Gauge connects it, then Fracture adds three more and leaves.
::combo Cosmic Leap opener | BA > S1 > S2 | After 5 seconds without damage, the dash attack opens with a rift.
## Builds and emblems
::build Burst assassin | Tough Boots, Hunter Strike, Blade of Despair, Malefic Roar, Blade of the Heptaseas, Immortality | Burst, penetration and survival.
::emblem Custom Assassin Emblem | Rupture, Seasoned Hunter, Killing Spree | Penetration, faster objectives and a heal on low-HP kills.
::spells Retribution | Retribution in the jungle.
!! Builds are based on item effects and his kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Clear fast with rift activations, which heal you and give energy on creeps too. Gank lanes once you have the ultimate.
Each activation that hits a creep gives 15 energy and heals 150, so overlapping rifts on camps keeps you healthy and fueled through the clear. Before a gank, stay out of combat for 5 seconds so Cosmic Leap is ready: your first basic attack becomes a dash that leaves a rift, which is the start of your combo.
::map jungle | Clear quickly and look for ganks once Fracture is ready.
## Mid game and teamfights
Wait for the enemy's control to be used, then enter with Cosmic Leap, burst the backline with rifts, and leave with Fracture's backward dash.
Rift activations pull enemies toward the rift's center, so you can bunch the enemy backline for your team's area skills. The heal on each activation keeps you alive while you are in range of their team. Keep track of which enemy still has crowd control: one stun stops your whole rotation.
## Advanced techniques
- Rift overlap: two rifts touching is what activates them; aim for overlap.
- Damage falloff: repeat activations on one target deal 40% damage, so spread activations across several enemies in teamfights.
- Cosmic Leap reset: staying out of combat for 5 seconds enables the dash attack again.
## Draft and team fit
Nolan is a priority jungler in both pro regions: 18 picks (6 wins) and 10 bans in the MPL PH S18 playoffs, and 20 picks (11 wins) and 15 bans in the MPL ID S18 playoffs. In ranked Mythical Glory+, over the past 7 days, he is picked in 2.21% of games, among the most picked junglers, with a 50.47% win rate. He works best when his team can lock targets for his rift combo, which is why pro teams paired him with control heroes such as Gloo and Atlas.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Miya,Layla,Eudora,Nana | bad=Estes,Baxia,Yve,Zhuxin,Natan | ally=Atlas,Lylia,Cici,Aulus
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+. The ally list comes from his most frequent MPL PH S18 playoff partners: Lylia (7 games together), Cici (6), Atlas (5) and Aulus (4). The good list is an assessment from his kit: immobile backliners cannot escape a rift combo.
Playing against Nolan: stand apart so his rifts do not catch several heroes, and use control to stop his rotations.
## Situational adjustments
- Against tanky teams: Malefic Roar earlier.
- Against heavy control: wait for their skills before entering.
- When ahead: invade the enemy jungle.
## Practice drills
- Overlap drill: practice Expansion then Gauge through the rift.
- Fracture drill: practice the ultimate's backward dash to exit fights.
## Common mistakes
- Casting skills without overlapping rifts.
- Entering fights before control is used.
- Ignoring Cosmic Leap.

guides.title: Selena
guides.sub: The art of turning vision, prediction, and one precise pick into map control
guides.body:
## Hero Overview
Role: Assassin / Mage Primary positions: Mid Lane, Roam Specialty: Initiator / Finisher Difficulty: High
Selena is a pickoff-oriented assassin-mage who thrives on information, positioning, and timing. Her greatest strength is not sustained damage or conventional teamfight presence. It is her ability to make certain areas of the map dangerous for enemies, catch an isolated target with Abyssal Arrow, and convert that opening into a numbers advantage.
She has two forms:
- Elven Form: Ranged abilities, traps, and long-range crowd control.
- Abyssal Form: Close-range damage, mobility, and mark consumption.
Her effectiveness depends on understanding when to switch between these forms and, more importantly, when not to commit.
Selena can be played in Mid Lane or as a Roamer. Mid Selena needs to manage waves and rotate without sacrificing too much farm. Roam Selena focuses more on vision, map pressure, and helping teammates secure picks.
Her biggest weakness is that she does not provide the same reliable area damage and front-to-back teamfight presence as many conventional mages. If your team needs a dependable late-game damage source, Selena may not be the ideal choice.
Her win condition: Create opportunities before the enemy team can organize, punish isolated targets, and convert picks into objectives.
Where she stands right now: in the official rankings for the past 7 days at Mythical Glory and above, Selena has a 1.99% pick rate, a 47.87% win rate and a 6.6% ban rate.
## Kit deep-dive
### Passive: Symbiosis
Selena can switch freely between Elven Form and Abyssal Form.
In Elven Form, her damaging skills apply Abyssal Marks. These marks last 8 seconds and can stack up to two times.
In Abyssal Form, her basic attacks become melee attacks and gain additional magic damage. Her skills deal additional magic damage to enemies carrying Abyssal Marks, consuming one mark stack when the effect triggers.
This is the foundation of Selena's damage cycle.
The important detail is that marks are not simply a damage indicator. They are resources that influence how you use her Abyssal skills.
Practical application:
- Apply marks with Elven skills before committing to close-range combat.
- Pay attention to how many marks remain on your target.
- Use Garotte when consuming a mark can reset its cooldown.
- Avoid wasting your mark-consuming attacks when the target is already escaping or when you cannot safely follow up.
### Elven Skill 1: Abyssal Trap
Selena summons an Abyssal Devil that hides underground and reacts when an enemy approaches.
The trap attaches to an enemy, applies an Abyssal Mark, slows the target, and eventually explodes to damage nearby enemies.
You can have up to three Abyssal Devils active simultaneously, and each can remain on the battlefield for up to 60 seconds. Additional traps affecting the same enemy increase the resulting damage.
But the trap's most important purpose is not necessarily damage.
It gives Selena information and helps control enemy movement.
Practical application:
- Place traps near jungle entrances and river approaches.
- Use them to monitor routes leading toward Turtle or Lord.
- Cover likely enemy rotations rather than placing traps randomly.
- Place traps around brushes your team intends to contest.
- Use them to make an enemy hesitate before entering a contested area.
A trap placed in an irrelevant location contributes very little. A trap placed on a route the enemy must cross can influence the entire next engagement.
### Elven Skill 2: Abyssal Arrow
Selena fires a projectile in a straight line. It stops when it hits an eligible target, dealing magic damage and stunning the target.
The damage and stun duration increase with the distance the arrow travels. The arrow can also pick up Abyssal Traps along its path and apply the trap's effect to the enemy it hits.
Abyssal Arrow is Selena's most recognizable ability, but it is also one of the easiest skills to misuse.
A long-range arrow can produce a devastating stun. However, a shorter and more reliable arrow can be more valuable if your teammates are ready to follow up.
Practical application:
- Aim toward the direction an enemy is moving, not simply their current position.
- Use narrow jungle passages to reduce the enemy's available escape routes.
- Combine the arrow with traps whenever the geometry allows.
- Avoid repeatedly throwing arrows at targets who have already seen your position.
- Save your arrow when an objective fight is about to begin and a pick could decide the contest.
Abyssal Arrow can also reveal the location of an enemy it hits, making it useful for checking dangerous areas and gathering information.
### Ultimate: Primal Darkness (to Abyssal Form)
Selena enters Abyssal Form and receives a brief movement-speed increase. The transformation immediately resets the cooldowns of Soul Eater and Garotte.
This is more than a form-changing ability.
It gives Selena access to her close-range combat tools and allows her to continue a prepared combination.
Practical application:
- Use it after landing a reliable arrow when you are ready to commit.
- Use the movement-speed boost to reposition.
- Remember that it refreshes both Abyssal skills.
- Do not automatically transform just because the ultimate is available.
The transformation should serve a purpose: engage, reposition, or prepare an escape.
### Abyssal Skill 1: Soul Eater
Selena empowers her next basic attack.
The empowered attack dashes toward the target, deals additional magic damage, and grants Selena a shield.
!! The official Soul Eater text describes the empowered Basic Attack, its extra Magic Damage and the shield, but not a dash. The dash is from Jade's draft and is not confirmed by the skill text; check it in Practice Mode.
Soul Eater itself does not reset Garotte. Garotte's cooldown resets when Garotte's own damage triggers an Abyssal Mark.
!! Jade's draft said here that when Soul Eater's damage triggers an Abyssal Mark, Garotte's cooldown resets. The official skill text (MLBB Wiki, checked 11 November 2026) gives that reset only to Garotte's own damage, and Soul Eater's text has no reset, so the line was corrected.
Soul Eater is an important part of Selena's close-range burst. The shield helps her survive the moment of contact, but it does not make her invulnerable.
Practical application:
Use Soul Eater when:
- Your target is already controlled.
- The enemy is isolated.
- Your teammates can follow up.
- You have a clear exit after the attack.
Do not use it to blindly dive into a group of enemies. The shield is a defensive advantage, not permission to ignore positioning.
### Abyssal Skill 2: Garotte
Garotte is a directional dash that damages enemies along its path.
When its damage consumes an Abyssal Mark, its cooldown resets.
This is one of Selena's most important mechanics.
A successful mark-triggering Garotte can allow another dash, giving Selena additional mobility and damage opportunities.
However, the reset does not mean you should always dash forward.
Sometimes the correct decision is to use the refreshed dash to retreat.
Practical application:
- Dash through a marked target when the follow-up is safe.
- Use the reset to reposition if the enemy team begins collapsing.
- Avoid spending both your offensive and defensive mobility options unnecessarily.
- Be conscious of walls and terrain when planning your entry and exit.
### Ultimate: Blessing of the Moon Goddess (to Elven Form)
Selena returns to Elven Form, gains a brief movement-speed increase, and immediately resets the cooldowns of Abyssal Trap and Abyssal Arrow.
This lets her return to ranged control after a close-range engagement.
The reset is particularly useful when you need to establish another trap, threaten another arrow, or disengage from a fight.
Remember: Selena's form changes are part of her cooldown management. They should not be treated as purely offensive abilities.
::curve 3,4,3 | Early: clear waves, establish traps and coordinate rotations. Mid: control jungle entrances, punish isolated enemies and turn picks into objectives (her peak). Late: play around flanks, protect escape routes and punish enemies who separate from their team.
## How the kit fits together
### The Abyssal Mark Cycle
Selena's most important interaction is the relationship between her two forms.
Elven Form applies Abyssal Marks. Abyssal Form consumes those marks through its skills to trigger additional damage.
A practical sequence is:
- Apply an Abyssal Mark with an Elven skill.
- Land Abyssal Arrow or establish another form of control.
- Switch to Abyssal Form.
- Use Soul Eater to close the distance and trigger mark damage.
- Use Garotte to continue or escape, depending on the situation.
Remember that a mark can be consumed by Abyssal skills. Do not assume every skill will receive the bonus simultaneously from the same mark stack.
### Trap and Arrow Interaction
Abyssal Trap and Abyssal Arrow are designed to work together.
When the arrow travels over an Abyssal Trap, it can pick up the trap and apply its effect to the enemy hit.
This makes trap placement especially important.
A trap placed directly along a likely enemy route can improve the value of an arrow. It can also make an enemy think twice before crossing a particular area.
The best Selena players understand that these two skills should not be treated as unrelated abilities.
### Garotte Reset Management
Garotte can reset when it consumes an Abyssal Mark.
This gives Selena an opportunity to chain mobility into her damage sequence.
However, the reset should be evaluated according to the fight's situation.
If the enemy is nearly defeated and isolated, continuing the engagement may be worthwhile.
If the enemy team is approaching, using Garotte to escape may be the better decision.
A successful reset is an opportunity. It is not an obligation to dive deeper.
## Combos
::combo Standard Pickoff | [Abyssal Trap] > [Abyssal Arrow] > ULT > [Soul Eater] > [Garotte] | Selena's basic pickoff sequence: trap the route, arrow through it, switch forms after the stun and finish up close.
Sequence: Abyssal Trap → Abyssal Arrow → Primal Darkness → Soul Eater → Garotte
This is Selena's basic pickoff sequence.
Set up the trap where the target is likely to move. Fire Abyssal Arrow through the trap's location and switch forms after landing the stun.
Use Soul Eater to close the distance, then use Garotte according to the target's remaining health and the surrounding enemy positions.
::combo Fast Close-Range Conversion | [Abyssal Arrow] > ULT > [Soul Eater] > [Garotte] | When the enemy is already within a reliable arrow angle: a dependable stun with immediate follow-up.
Sequence: Abyssal Arrow → Primal Darkness → Soul Eater → Garotte
Use this when an enemy is already within a reliable arrow angle.
You do not always need to prepare a complicated trap setup. A dependable stun with immediate follow-up can be enough.
::combo Objective Area Control | [Abyssal Trap] > [Abyssal Trap] > [Abyssal Arrow] | Traps around the entrances before an objective fight, then hold the arrow to punish the approach.
Sequence: Abyssal Trap placements → Hold Abyssal Arrow → Punish enemy approach
Before an objective fight, establish traps around the entrances your opponents are likely to use.
Do not immediately throw your arrow when an enemy appears.
Sometimes holding the threat is more valuable than taking a low-probability shot.
::combo Defensive Disengagement | ULT > [Garotte] > Flicker | When an enemy dives you: switch forms, reposition, Garotte toward safety, Flicker only if necessary.
Sequence: Form switch → Movement repositioning → Garotte toward safety when available → Flicker if necessary
If an enemy dives you, prioritize survival.
Use your mobility tools to create distance rather than forcing a counterattack.
Do not waste Flicker simply to chase a low-value target when it could save your life in the next engagement.
## Builds and emblems
Selena's itemization should reflect her role and the enemy composition.
There is no single universally correct six-item build. Current community data shows multiple item orders, while curated build recommendations emphasize burst-oriented equipment for Mid Selena. MLBBHub +1
What the pros did: the app has 118 recorded Selena games from MPL Season 18 (46 in Indonesia, 36 in the Philippines, 36 in Malaysia), 55 of them wins. Glowing Wand was in 117 final inventories, Divine Glaive in 67, Wishing Lantern in 62 and Enchanted Talisman in 51. Many games ended with unfinished components such as Magic Shoes or Magic Wand still in the inventory. Every recorded game used the Mage emblem, most often with Inspire, Seasoned Hunter and Lethal Ignition (48 games).
::build Pro build: Sionnn | Arcane Boots, Glowing Wand, Enchanted Talisman, Wishing Lantern, Lightning Truncheon, Divine Glaive | Sionnn (Twisted Minds PH), MPL PH Season 18, 22 August 2026, a win with 11802 gold. Final inventory as recorded by MLBBHub.
!! Pro item lists are the final inventory at the end of the game, shown in slot order, not the order the items were bought.
- Glowing Wand: Scorch burns targets for a share of their Max HP, and Lifebane cuts their shields and HP regen. Pros bought it in almost every game.
- Wishing Lantern: every 900 Magic Damage dealt to an enemy hero summons a Butterfly Goddess that hits for 8% of their Current HP, which suits Selena's burst on one picked-off target.
- Enchanted Talisman: Mana Spring restores 15% of her Max Mana every 10 seconds and Magic Mastery raises her cooldown reduction cap by 5%, so trap and arrow come back sooner.
::build Pro build: Treacky | Immortality, Arcane Boots, Divine Glaive, Enchanted Talisman, Glowing Wand, Wishing Lantern | Treacky (iG), MPL MY Season 18, 11 September 2026, a win from the Mid Lane. Immortality in place of a sixth damage item.
Jade's builds (curated and community templates, not pro builds):
### Build 1 — Mid Lane Pickoff Burst
::build Mid Lane Pickoff Burst | Arcane Boots, Clock of Destiny, Lightning Truncheon, Starlium Scythe, Divine Glaive, Holy Crystal | Jade's curated mid-lane template (MLBBHub).
Curated mid-lane template
- Arcane Boots
- Clock of Destiny
- Lightning Truncheon
- Starlium Scythe
- Divine Glaive
- Holy Crystal
This is a burst-oriented setup intended to make a successful trap-arrow connection more threatening.
Why it works as a template:
- Arcane Boots provide early magic penetration.
- Clock of Destiny offers scaling and additional durability.
- Lightning Truncheon contributes burst potential.
- Starlium Scythe supports Selena's skill-to-basic-attack conversion.
- Divine Glaive helps against enemies building magic defense.
- Holy Crystal increases magic power.
Do not blindly follow the order if the match develops differently. Item timing should reflect your gold, enemy defenses, and the pace of the game.
### Build 2 — Roam Pickoff
::build Roam Pickoff | Rapid Boots, Starlium Scythe, Lightning Truncheon, Genius Wand, Divine Glaive, Winter Crown | Jade's situational roam template.
Situational roam template
- Rapid Boots
- Starlium Scythe
- Lightning Truncheon
- Genius Wand
- Divine Glaive
- Winter Crown
This setup emphasizes movement, pickoff damage, and the ability to survive after committing.
The roam role has different economic conditions from Mid Selena. You should not assume that you will complete the same item timings as a farming mage.
Adjust your equipment according to your team's needs. If you are consistently being punished after entering Abyssal Form, prioritize survivability over greedily adding more damage.
### Situational Item Adjustments
- Winter Crown: Consider it when enemy assassins or divers can punish you after your initial combo.
- Glowing Wand: Consider it when enemy healing, shields, or regeneration are becoming difficult to deal with.
- Genius Wand: Consider it when early magic-defense reduction helps your team secure picks.
- Blood Wings: Consider it when you need additional magic power and defensive value in later fights.
- Enchanted Talisman: Consider it when repeated skill usage and cooldown availability matter more than immediate burst.
These are situational choices, not mandatory replacements. Check current item effects and prices in-game before finalizing your build.
### Emblem
::emblem Custom Mage Emblem | Inspire, Seasoned Hunter, Lethal Ignition | The most common pro setup in MPL Season 18, used in 48 of the 118 recorded games.
Mage Emblem is the most commonly represented emblem in the recent community build sample.
A curated Mid Selena setup recommends:
- Rupture
- Bargain Hunter
- Lethal Ignition
!! In the app's emblem data Rupture is listed under the Assassin emblem, not the Mage emblem. But MLBBHub's pro records show Rupture with the Mage emblem in 12 MPL Season 18 Selena games (for example Stormie, SRG, 17 October 2026), so whether it can be picked with the Mage emblem is unconfirmed. Check the in-game emblem screen; if it is not offered, Inspire is the Mage emblem talent the pros used.
This combination supports penetration, economy, and burst-oriented damage.
Recent community submissions also show Inspire being used by some players, so do not treat one talent configuration as the only viable option.
### Battle spells
::spells Flicker, Flameshot | Flicker for repositioning and survival. Flameshot for additional ranged finishing pressure when the draft allows a less defensive spell choice.
!! The pro records the app uses do not include battle spells, so these are Jade's draft's recommendations, not pro data.
Flicker
Flicker is the most frequently represented battle spell in the recent community sample.
It gives Selena an additional repositioning tool, which is especially useful when she needs to escape after entering Abyssal Form.
Choose Flicker when:
- The enemy has dangerous divers.
- You need another escape option.
- Your positioning is frequently threatened.
- You want additional flexibility in teamfights.
Flameshot
A curated Mid Selena build recommends Flameshot.
It provides additional ranged damage and can help finish targets or disrupt nearby enemies.
Choose Flameshot when:
- Your positioning is relatively safe.
- Your team can protect you.
- You want additional finishing pressure.
- You do not need Flicker as urgently for survival.
The better choice depends on the enemy composition and your role in the match.
## Early game
::map lane | Mid Lane or Roam: clear the wave or establish safe lane priority, place traps along river entrances, jungle ramps and brushes, and rotate with a teammate.
Your early objective is to establish map pressure without sacrificing necessary farm or positioning.
As Mid Selena:
- Clear your wave before rotating when possible.
- Place traps around important river and jungle entrances.
- Coordinate with your roamer and jungler.
- Avoid wandering into unlit enemy territory alone.
- Use Abyssal Arrow to punish predictable movement.
As Roam Selena:
- Help your team establish vision.
- Coordinate invades instead of entering the enemy jungle alone.
- Look for opportunities to assist lanes with vulnerable targets.
- Avoid forcing fights when your teammates cannot follow up.
Your early-game advantage comes from information and movement. A trap that reveals an enemy rotation can prevent a dangerous fight before it even happens.
## Mid game: objectives and rotations
::map turtle | Prioritize Turtle and Lord approaches: place traps along likely enemy routes and keep an arrow angle toward the choke your team wants to control.
This is where Selena should begin converting map pressure into meaningful advantages.
Look for:
- Isolated enemies.
- Vulnerable backliners.
- Opponents clearing side lanes alone.
- Enemies approaching objectives through predictable routes.
- Opportunities to invade after a successful pick.
After securing a kill, immediately consider what your team can take.
Can you invade a jungle camp? Can you establish deeper vision? Can you pressure a turret or secure an objective?
Do not treat every kill as an accomplishment in itself.
A kill that produces no map advantage may be less valuable than a successful pick that gives your team control over an important objective.
## Late game and teamfights
Selena's late-game approach becomes more cautious.
Enemies are generally more difficult to eliminate, defensive items become more common, and grouped opponents can punish her close-range commitment.
Do not repeatedly walk toward five enemies looking for an arrow.
Instead:
- Play around the edges of teamfights.
- Look for isolated targets.
- Control objective entrances with traps.
- Wait for enemies to waste important mobility skills.
- Protect your own escape route.
- Avoid committing when your teammates are too far away.
Your presence can still make the enemy team uncomfortable, even when you cannot immediately secure a kill.
## Advanced techniques
### 1. Aim Where the Enemy Must Move
Predict movement instead of reacting to it.
An enemy approaching Turtle has limited routes. A mage clearing a wave may have fewer safe escape options if your teammates control the nearby jungle.
Think about where the enemy is going and where they are forced to pass.
This is more reliable than repeatedly firing arrows at targets who have plenty of room to dodge.
### 2. Use Traps as Information
Your traps can reveal enemy movement and help protect important routes.
You do not need to trigger a kill every time a trap activates.
Sometimes knowing that the enemy jungler is approaching from a particular direction is enough to prevent your team from walking into an unfavorable fight.
### 3. Preserve Arrow Threat
Abyssal Arrow is a major part of Selena's threat.
If you repeatedly throw it without a clear purpose, enemies can become more comfortable moving through your area.
Hold it when:
- An objective fight is about to begin.
- Your teammates are preparing an engage.
- An enemy is approaching a narrow passage.
- You have information that a target is about to commit to a predictable route.
The threat of a possible arrow can influence enemy movement even before you fire it.
### 4. Respect Your Wave
Mid Selena still has responsibilities as a laner.
Leaving a wave at the wrong moment can allow the opposing mage to rotate first or pressure your turret.
Do not abandon your lane every time you see an opportunity for a possible arrow.
Clear safely, rotate with purpose, and return before the enemy can punish your absence.
### 5. Know When Not to Enter
Selena's Abyssal Form can make her vulnerable to retaliation.
Before committing, ask yourself:
- Is the target actually isolated?
- Can my teammates follow up?
- Does the enemy have crowd control ready?
- Do I have a way to escape?
- Is this pick worth the risk?
If you cannot answer these questions favorably, wait.
Discipline is a major part of playing Selena well.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs bad=Benedetta,Yve,Beatrix,Ixia,Kaja,Chip,Gloo,Popol and Kupa
!! Benedetta, Yve, Beatrix, Ixia and Kaja are the heroes the official ranked data (past 7 days, Mythical Glory and above, 11 November 2026) lists as countering Selena. Chip, Gloo and Popol and Kupa are from Jade's draft (MLBBHub). Jade's draft named no favorable heroes, so none are listed.
### Favorable Conditions
Selena benefits from team compositions that can immediately follow up on her crowd control.
She works well with:
- Junglers who can quickly capitalize on a stun.
- Teammates with reliable crowd control.
- Heroes who can pressure enemy jungle entrances.
- Drafts that benefit from early map control.
- Teams that can punish isolated opponents.
Her pickoff threat becomes much more valuable when teammates are close enough to convert it.
### Difficult Conditions
Be cautious when facing:
- Highly mobile enemies who can dodge Abyssal Arrow.
- Strong divers who can punish Selena after she enters Abyssal Form.
- Durable frontlines that can absorb her initial burst.
- Enemies who can safely clear traps.
- Compositions that repeatedly force grouped teamfights.
Selena struggles when opponents deny her opportunities to isolate targets.
### Understanding Matchups
Do not memorize counters without understanding why they work.
Ask what makes the opposing hero difficult:
- Can they dodge your arrow easily?
- Can they interrupt your close-range sequence?
- Can they survive your initial burst?
- Can they punish you after you use your mobility?
- Can they clear your traps without taking meaningful risks?
For mobile enemies, wait for their mobility skill before committing to an arrow.
Against divers, preserve an escape route and avoid spending every mobility tool offensively.
Against durable enemies, consider whether your team has enough follow-up damage to finish the target.
Recent matchup data lists Chip, Gloo, and Popol and Kupa among Selena's difficult matchups in the tracked ranked sample. Treat this as a statistical snapshot rather than a permanent counter list; matchups can change with patches, rank, and player execution. MLBBHub
## Common mistakes
### 1. Throwing Arrows Without Purpose
Abyssal Arrow should not be treated as a skill that must be used whenever it becomes available.
Repeated low-probability attempts waste opportunities and reveal your position.
### 2. Placing Traps Randomly
A trap should serve a purpose.
Place it to monitor a route, protect an entrance, prepare an arrow, or control an area your team wants to contest.
### 3. Entering Without Follow-Up
A landed arrow does not automatically guarantee a kill.
Check whether your teammates are close enough to help before committing to Abyssal Form.
### 4. Treating Garotte Resets as Invitations to Dive
The reset is valuable because it gives you another option.
Sometimes that option should be used to escape.
### 5. Ignoring the Map
Selena is especially dependent on map awareness.
If you focus exclusively on landing arrows, you may miss opportunities to protect objectives, establish vision, or punish enemy rotations.
### 6. Forcing Late-Game Pickoffs
A late-game enemy surrounded by teammates is not an easy target.
Be patient. Look for separation, wasted mobility skills, or a vulnerable approach to an objective.
## Practice drills
::steps Pickoff to objective | Clear your lane or establish safe lane priority; place traps along useful enemy routes; rotate with a teammate; hold Abyssal Arrow for predictable or committed movement; convert successful picks into objectives, invades, or vision; reposition and prepare for the next engagement
### 1. Abyssal Arrow Accuracy
Spend time practicing arrows from different distances and angles.
Practice against moving targets and experiment with firing from brush edges and narrow passages.
Focus on predicting movement rather than relying on reaction alone.
### 2. Trap Placement
Practice placing traps around:
- River entrances.
- Jungle ramps.
- Objective approaches.
- Brush edges.
- Common rotation routes.
After every match, ask whether your traps actually provided information or helped your team control space.
### 3. Form Switching
Practice the basic sequence:
Apply Mark → Land Arrow → Switch Forms → Soul Eater → Garotte → Evaluate
Do not simply repeat the combo mechanically.
Practice deciding whether to continue the engagement or disengage after the first successful hit.
### 4. Map Awareness
Review your replays and ask:
- Did I rotate after clearing my wave?
- Did my traps cover useful paths?
- Did I land arrows on targets who could actually be punished?
- Did I have teammates nearby when I committed?
- Did I use Garotte to escape when necessary?
- Did my successful picks lead to objectives?
Improving these decisions will make you more consistent than focusing exclusively on arrow accuracy.
## Accuracy and patch notes
This guide uses current November 2026 skill information and recent community build references. The skill mechanics, mark duration, mark stacking, trap-arrow interaction, and form-switch cooldown resets are supported by the current references consulted.
Builds and emblem recommendations are based on current curated recommendations and community submissions. Community build frequency does not establish that a particular setup has the highest win rate. MLBBHub +1
Important verification note: Item stats, prices, talent effects, and skill values can change with balance patches. Check the live in-game descriptions before adding this guide to the Codex. Where the available sources disagree on exact numerical skill details, this guide deliberately avoids presenting disputed numbers as certain.
Research references
- MLBB.io — Selena hero and skill data: https://mlbb.io/en/hero/selena
- MLBB Knowledge — Selena skill descriptions: https://mlbb-knowledge.vercel.app/heroes/63
- MLBBHub — Selena build and matchup guide: https://mlbbhub.com/heroes/selena
- MLBB.io — November 2026 community build aggregation: https://mlbb.io/en/hero/selena/build
- MLBB Guides — Selena skill guide: https://www.mlbbguides.com/ph/heroes/selena/skills/
!! Fact-check of Jade's draft (11 November 2026, against the app's MLBB Wiki skill data, item and emblem data, official rankings and MLBBHub pro records): one correction (the Garotte reset in the Soul Eater section) and two items marked unconfirmed (the Soul Eater dash and Rupture with the Mage emblem). Everything else matched the current data or is Jade's own advice.

guides.title: Masha
guides.sub: Three-life EXP laner whose HP bars, not her armor, decide how far she can dive
guides.body:
## Hero Overview
Masha is a physical melee fighter and tank who plays the EXP Lane. Her passive, Primal Pact, gives her three HP bars instead of one, each inheriting 50% of her equipment HP bonuses. When a bar is depleted she removes control effects on herself and blocks damage once, and her Claw Strike cooldown resets. In effect she has three short lives in every fight, and each time one ends she gets a free cleanse, a damage block and a dash.
That structure is why she is picked. She can walk into fights that would kill other fighters because the first point at which she is in danger is not when her HP is low, it is when her last bar is low. Combine that with claw strikes that deal a percentage of the target's maximum HP, and she is a natural answer to high-HP tanks and fighters, and a split-pusher who can survive the first collapse.
The counterweight is also in her kit. Her bars do not make her harder to damage, they just reset certain things when they break. Heroes that deal true or percentage damage, that cut healing, or that burst through a bar with a long lock still kill her. Understanding which situations her passive solves, and which it does not, is the core of playing her.
## Kit deep-dive
### Primal Pact (passive)
The passive has three parts. Bear's Blessing is the three HP bars with the cleanse, block and Claw Strike reset on each break. She also gains Feral by damaging enemy heroes or creeps, which converts into HP after she leaves combat, so she refills between trades. Power of Wildness is her damage engine: when her skills damage an enemy hero, she leaves a Wound in a random direction, and breaking that Wound with a basic attack puts her into the Feral state.
In the Feral state she gains 15% plus 1% per hero level in Resilience, attack speed and movement speed, and her next three basic attacks become fan-shaped claw strikes that deal extra physical damage equal to a percentage of the target's maximum HP (3% plus 0.3% per level, plus a bonus from extra physical attack) and recover 4% plus 0.4% per level of her HP. It lasts 3 seconds, breaking another Wound during Feral refreshes it, and up to 6 claw strikes can be stored.
Why this matters: Masha's damage and healing both live in those claw strikes. Every skill that hits a hero is not just damage, it is a Wound that becomes three more claws and more healing. So the question in every trade is: how many Wounds can I create and break before I disengage? The Wound appears in a random direction, which means you sometimes have to take a step to break it. Learn to glance at where it landed and walk over it with a basic attack instead of standing still.
### Feral Swipe (Skill 1)
Masha releases energy forward, damaging enemies in its path and slowing heroes hit by 50% for 1 second. It is her poke, her slow and her most reliable source of Wounds. The slow is what lets her basic attacks connect after the Wound breaks, so cast it when you are close enough to follow up, not at maximum range.
### Claw Strike (Skill 2)
A dash in the target direction that deals damage. Its cooldown resets whenever an HP bar breaks. This is both her gap-closer and her escape, and the reset means she gets one more of either each time she loses a bar. Never assume Claw Strike is on cooldown just because you used it: if a bar is about to break, a second dash is coming.
### Savage Maul (Ultimate)
Masha charges toward an enemy hero, damaging them, stunning them for 1 second and knocking back nearby enemies. The damage scales with her extra HP, so it grows as she builds health. It is a targeted engage that also separates the target from their bodyguards, which is why its best use is pulling a carry out of formation rather than hitting the closest tank.
::curve 4,5,3 | Strong in lane and very strong in the mid game split-push window; late-game fights against heavy anti-heal and percentage damage are harder.
## How the kit fits together
Masha's loop is skill, Wound, basic attack, Feral, claws, and repeat. Each skill hit gives her a Wound, each Wound gives her Feral and three claws, and claws heal her and deal percentage damage. Her bars buy time for that loop to run. When she is played well, the enemy is losing HP to claws while Masha is gaining HP from them, and every time the enemy does manage to break a bar, she cleanses their control and dashes again.
The loop breaks if she cannot reach basic-attack range or cannot break Wounds: being kited, being knocked away, or being locked long enough to lose a bar without hitting anything. That is the lens for reading every matchup.
## Combos
::combo Trade in lane | S1 > BA > BA > S2 > BA | Swipe to slow and create a Wound, break it with a basic attack for Feral, dash to stay on the target, and finish the claw strikes.
Why it works: Feral Swipe both creates a Wound and slows the target, so they cannot walk away while you break it. Claw Strike is held until the target tries to escape, which also creates another Wound when it hits, keeping Feral going.
::combo Carry pick | ULT > S1 > BA > BA > S2 | Maul the carry out of their formation, swipe immediately during the stun, then chain claw strikes and use Claw Strike to follow if they flash.
Why it works: the stun lasts 1 second, which is enough time for Feral Swipe to land and a Wound to be broken. The knockback on nearby enemies pushes the carry's protectors away, so your first seconds of claws are uncontested.
::combo Bar-break escape | S2 > BA > S2 | When a bar breaks mid-fight Claw Strike resets, so a second dash is available right away for the exit.
Why it works: if you dash in and a bar breaks, you have a fresh dash. That dash can carry you out of the fight, and the cleanse on the bar break frees you from whatever control was holding you.
## Builds and emblems
::build EXP lane bruiser | Warrior Boots, War Axe, Hunter Strike, Brute Force Breastplate, Sea Halberd, Immortality | War Axe suits her sustained skill-and-basic damage; Hunter Strike gives burst and speed; Brute Force Breastplate stacks while she keeps hitting; Sea Halberd cuts healing on the targets she fights; Immortality is a fourth life on top of three bars.
::build Tankier frontline | Tough Boots, War Axe, Dominance Ice, Antique Cuirass, Brute Force Breastplate, Immortality | When the enemy has heavy magic or sustain, Dominance Ice cuts the shields and healing of nearby enemies and adds defense for each enemy hero near her, and Antique Cuirass reduces the physical damage of enemies who hit him with skills.
How to choose: build HP-scaling items with her bars in mind. Because each bar inherits only half of her equipment HP, pure HP stacking is less efficient on her than on a normal tank, but HP still powers Savage Maul. Her damage comes from claws and skills, so items that reward hitting often fit better than pure burst. Go to the tankier frontline build when your team needs you to be the main body in fights instead of a side-lane threat.
::emblem Custom Fighter Emblem | Firmness, Festival of Blood, Brave Smite | Spell vamp and Brave Smite's heal turn her skill trades into health she keeps; Firmness adds defenses to both sides.
::spells Vengeance, Flicker, Petrify | Vengeance punishes divers who commit to her; Flicker lets her chase or reach the carry for Maul; Petrify adds control in skirmishes.
## Laning
Masha wins short trades by threatening Feral and long trades because her claw healing and Feral-to-HP conversion reset her between fights. The lane pattern is simple: when the enemy walks up to last-hit, Feral Swipe them, break the Wound, and take three claws' worth of trade before they can answer. Then step back and let the out-of-combat conversion top you up.
When the enemy has a strong all-in, let them break your first bar. It cleanses whatever lock they used, blocks one hit, and resets Claw Strike, and that often reverses the fight: they have spent their burst on a bar that was going to regenerate, while you still have two left and a fresh dash. The mistake is to panic and retreat on bar one.
## Mid game: split-pushing and pressure
Masha's best window is the mid game, when her claws deal real percentage damage and the enemy does not yet have a lot of anti-heal. She is excellent at taking side-lane turrets while her team shows on the other side. Because she has three bars, a lone defender cannot stop her, so the enemy must send two or more heroes, which leaves your team in an advantageous fight elsewhere.
::map split | Push the far lane while your team shows on the other side of the map; the enemy must answer with numbers or lose a turret.
The danger in splitting is a collapse with heavy crowd control. Watch the minimap: when two enemy heroes vanish at once, assume they are coming and either leave with your dash or fight under your turret.
## Teamfights
In teamfights she is a bruiser with a strong pick. Her two jobs are to threaten the carry with Savage Maul and to stay alive long enough for claws to matter. Use Maul on the carry who has drifted to the edge of formation; the knockback sends nearby heroes away and gives you a one-on-one. If no carry is reachable, frontline: create Wounds on the enemy tank and fighter with Feral Swipe, stay in claws, and let your bars absorb the enemy's crowd control.
## Advanced techniques
- Cleanse timing: the control removal comes from a bar breaking. If you are near the end of a bar and the enemy has a big lock ready, step forward and let the next small hit break it so their lock lands on a fresh bar with the cleanse behind you, or bait the lock just before the bar ends so the break frees you immediately.
- Wound walking: Wounds appear in random directions. When chasing, take the Wound that is on the side of the target's escape route; it keeps you in reach while you break it.
- Storing claws: up to 6 claw strikes can be stored, so a skill combo before a fight can bank claws for the moment you reach the target.
- Maul as peel: if an enemy assassin dives your marksman, Maul them away from your carry. It is not glamorous, but the stun and knockback can save a fight.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Tigreal,Hylos,Uranus,Akai | bad=Dyrroth,Karrie,Esmeralda,Baxia | ally=Angela,Estes,Floryn,Hirara
Why the good matchups are good: her percentage-HP claws are most efficient against heroes with a lot of HP, so tanks like Tigreal, Hylos, Uranus and Akai lose long trades to her.
Why the bad matchups are bad: Karrie's damage ignores how much HP she has, Dyrroth can burst through a bar and keep pressure, Esmeralda absorbs her trades with shields and sustain, and Baxia's healing reduction shuts off the claw heal that keeps her loop going.
Why the allies work: healers such as Angela, Estes and Floryn keep her bars topped up in long fights, and a jungler like Hirara follows her Maul onto a carry.
Playing against Masha: do not use your strongest control early in a fight when she has a full bar about to break; wait for the cleanse to be spent. Build anti-heal, focus her when she is on her last bar, and do not chase her through a lane where she can turn with a reset Claw Strike.
## Common mistakes
- Ignoring Wounds: skills without breaking Wounds lose most of her damage and healing.
- Mauling the tank: Maul is a pick on the carry.
- Retreating on bar one: her first bar is meant to be spent.
- Splitting with no vision: three bars do not save you from a five-hero collapse.

guides.title: Kalea
guides.sub: Water-zone fighter support who chains knock-ups, slams and enhanced attacks
guides.body:
## Hero Overview
Kalea is a physical melee support and fighter who roams. She has a lot of crowd control, short cooldowns on her slow, and a passive that turns her skills into three enhanced basic attacks with a dash, a heal and a new Water Zone. That last part is the heart of her: casting a skill makes a zone, and casting another skill inside a zone enhances her attacks and makes another zone. When she is played well, she is never without either.
She is picked for her picks: a knock-up from Tidal Strike, a second knock-up from the slam, and an ultimate that throws a target in the direction she chooses. She also gives her team sustain through the heal on her second enhanced attack. She is weaker when the enemy can keep her at range, interrupt her charge, or burst her before she builds her chain.
## Kit deep-dive
### Surge of Life (passive)
After casting a skill, Kalea creates a Water Zone on the ground. Casting a skill within that zone absorbs it and enhances her next three basic attacks: the first dashes to the target and deals physical damage; the second unleashes a flurry that deals 300 physical damage and recovers 120 HP for herself and the nearby lowest-HP ally; the third strikes the area around the target for 100 physical damage and creates a new Water Zone. Enhanced basic attacks are not affected by attack speed.
How to use it: plan every fight as skill, skill in the zone, three attacks, new zone. The third attack makes a new zone, so a full chain sets up the next one.
