::vs good=Miya,Layla,Hanabi,Lesley | bad=Zilong,Alucard,Lolita,Lesley,Franco | ally=Pharsa,Eudora,Odette,Yve
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+. Note: Lesley appears in both lists; the good list is an assessment, while the official data says she wins in ranked.
Playing against Tigreal: spread out, keep vision on bushes, and interrupt the first half of Implosion with control. Heroes who can leave a stun quickly, or who punish him with high mobility, make his engage much less reliable.
## Situational adjustments
- Against suppression: wait for the suppression to be used.
- Against magic damage: Radiant Armor earlier.
- When ahead: control objectives.
## Practice drills
- Charge drill: practice charge, Implosion and recast.
- Flicker drill: practice Flicker during Implosion.
## Common mistakes
- Engaging without the team.
- Walking in the open.
- Using Implosion on one hero.

guides.title: Lylia
guides.sub: Shadow-energy mage who chains detonations, then rewinds time to escape
guides.body:
## Hero Overview
Lylia is a ranged magic mage for the mid lane who deals damage by detonating Shadow Energy with her companion Gloom. Her passive, **Angry Gloom**, gives 15% movement speed inside Gloom's area, plus 5% each time Gloom is upgraded (up to 20%), for up to 35%.
**Magic Shockwave** sends Gloom in a line for 250-500 magic damage, slowing by 40% for 1.5 seconds and detonating any Shadow Energy it touches. **Shadow Energy** places energy that slows by 80% for 0.5 seconds; when detonated by Gloom or Magic Shockwave, it deals extra damage and turns into Gloom for 8 seconds, which can detonate more Shadow Energy in range, and each chained detonation within 8 seconds deals 30% more damage, up to 120%. Her ultimate, **Black Shoes**, returns her to where she was 4 seconds ago, restoring all 5 Shadow Energy charges and her HP and mana to that state, plus extra max HP, and she is untargetable while teleporting.
Why she is picked: very high area damage and an escape that undoes damage. In the MPL PH S18 playoffs she was picked 11 times (5 wins) and banned 11 times; in the MPL ID S18 playoffs, 11 picks (5 wins) and 13 bans. Her weakness: her combo takes practice, and she has no hard control.
## Kit deep-dive
### Angry Gloom (passive)
Movement speed in Gloom's area helps you kite.
### Magic Shockwave (Skill 1)
The detonator. Aim it through your Shadow Energy.
### Shadow Energy (Skill 2)
Place energy, then detonate. Chain detonations for more damage.
### Black Shoes (Ultimate)
A rewind: HP, mana and charges return to their state 4 seconds ago.
::curve 4,5,4 | Strong early wave clear and poke, very strong mid game, and still dangerous late.
## Combos
::combo Chain detonation | S2 > S2 > S1 > S2 > S2 | Place energy, detonate with the shockwave, then keep placing energy near Gloom.
::combo Rewind reset | S2 > S2 > S2 > ULT > S2 | Spend energy, rewind to restore all charges, spend again.
## Builds and emblems
::build Burst mage | Arcane Boots, Lightning Truncheon, Genius Wand, Holy Crystal, Divine Glaive, Blood Wings | Burst and penetration.
::emblem Custom Mage Emblem | Inspire, Bargain Hunter, Lethal Ignition | Faster items and burst.
::spells Flicker | Flicker for safety.
!! Builds are based on item effects and her kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Clear waves with Shadow Energy and Magic Shockwave, and poke the enemy mage.
Shadow Energy stores a charge every 9 seconds, up to 5, and costs only a 1-second cooldown between casts, so she can place several at once. Place two or three on the wave, then send Magic Shockwave through them: each detonation deals extra damage and turns into Gloom, which can detonate more energy nearby. Against the enemy mage, keep one or two charges for poke and the 80% slow, so they cannot step up to trade without being punished.
::map rotate | Clear mid, then rotate.
## Mid game and teamfights
Stand at the edge of fights and chain detonations on grouped enemies. Use Black Shoes after taking damage to rewind to safety.
The key to her teamfight is the chain: each time Gloom detonates another Shadow Energy within 8 seconds, the detonation damage rises by 30%, up to 120%. Place energy along the line the enemy will walk through, detonate the first one, and let Gloom jump from one to the next. Gloom's area also gives you 15% movement speed or more, which helps you stay at the right distance. Black Shoes returns you to where you stood 4 seconds ago with the HP and mana you had then and all 5 charges restored, so a common pattern is to spend every charge, take the enemy's burst, then rewind and spend them all again.
## Advanced techniques
- Rewind timing: use the ultimate after taking burst to restore HP. If you were already low 4 seconds ago, the rewind will not help, so think ahead.
- Chain stacking: each chained detonation in 8 seconds adds 30%, up to 120% on the fifth.
- Charge reset: the rewind restores all 5 charges, which makes it an offensive tool as well as an escape.
- Untargetable teleport: you cannot be targeted while teleporting, so the rewind dodges targeted ultimates.
- Speed after rewind: you gain extra movement speed for a few seconds after the rewind, useful to get away or re-enter.
## Draft and team fit
In the MPL PH S18 playoffs she was drafted most often with Nolan (7 games together, 3 wins) and Atlas (4 games, 4 wins); in the MPL ID S18 playoffs with Freya and Paquito (5 games each).
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Masha,Freya,Paquito,Aulus | bad=Barats,Chip,Hanabi,Alpha,Alice | ally=Atlas,Nolan,Freya,Paquito
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+.
Playing against Lylia: bait her rewind, then kill her. Stand apart so her detonations do not chain through your team, and dive her when Black Shoes is on cooldown.
## Situational adjustments
- Against divers: hold the rewind and keep two Shadow Energy charges for the 80% slow.
- Against magic defense: Divine Glaive earlier.
- When ahead: push waves quickly and rotate to objectives, where enemies have to group.
## Practice drills
- Chain drill: practice chaining five detonations on grouped dummies.
- Rewind drill: practice spending all charges, then rewinding to spend them again.
## Common mistakes
- Using the rewind too early, before you have taken damage.
- Missing the detonation, so the energy only slows.
- Standing in front of your tank.

guides.title: Rafaela
guides.sub: Light support who heals, speeds up her team and revives a fallen ally
guides.body:
## Hero Overview
Rafaela is a ranged magic support for the roam. Her passive, **Divine Resurrection**, lets her periodically use a special skill to instantly resurrect a fallen ally after a brief channel; they respawn at base with extra movement speed. Its cooldown depends on its base cooldown and the ally's remaining respawn time, and is not affected by cooldown reduction.
**Light of Retribution** strikes the three nearest enemies for 225-500 magic damage, reveals them briefly and slows them by 40% for 1.5 seconds; enemies hit again within 5 seconds take 20% more damage, stacking 3 times. **Holy Healing** restores 100-125 HP to nearby allies, plus 150-250 to herself and the most injured ally in range, and gives nearby allies 30% movement speed and slow immunity for 1 second. Her ultimate, **Holy Baptism**, fires a line for 460-660 magic damage and stuns for 1.5 seconds.
Why she is picked: healing, speed and a long line stun. Over the past 7 days in ranked Mythical Glory+, she has a 54.08% win rate and a 13.72% ban rate. Her weakness: fragile and without an escape.
## Kit deep-dive
### Divine Resurrection (passive)
Revive the ally who matters most.
### Light of Retribution (Skill 1)
Auto-targets the three nearest enemies.
### Holy Healing (Skill 2)
Heal and speed boost with slow immunity.
### Holy Baptism (Ultimate)
A long line stun.
::curve 3,4,4 | Solid throughout.
## Combos
::combo Stun and chase | ULT > S1 > S2 | Stun, strike, speed up your team.
## Builds and emblems
::build Healer | Magic Shoes, Enchanted Talisman, Fleeting Time, Flask of the Oasis, Oracle, Immortality | Healing and cooldowns.
::emblem Custom Support Emblem | Agility, Pull Yourself Together, Focusing Mark | Speed and cooldowns.
::spells Flicker | Flicker for safety.
!! Builds are based on item effects and her kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Roam with your jungler and marksman.
Light of Retribution has a 4-second cooldown and hits the three nearest enemies automatically, so it is easy poke that also reveals enemies and slows them by 40%. Hitting the same enemy again within 5 seconds adds 20% more damage, up to 3 times, so use it often during trades. Holy Healing restores HP to nearby allies, heals the most injured ally and you more, and gives your team 30% movement speed and slow immunity for 1 second: use it to win a chase or to escape a gank.
::map roam | Roam with your team.
## Mid game and teamfights
Stay behind, heal, and stun with the ultimate.
Holy Baptism fires a long line that stuns every enemy hit for 1.5 seconds. Aim it through the enemy frontline into their backline, or use it to stop a diver who reached your carry. Because Light of Retribution targets automatically, you can stay at a safe distance and keep it on cooldown throughout the fight. Holy Healing's speed boost is also an engage tool: cast it as your team walks in so everyone arrives together and ignores slows for a moment.
Divine Resurrection changes how you should think about deaths. When your carry falls, check whether the revive is ready: they respawn at base with extra movement speed, which can bring them back to a long objective fight in time.
## Advanced techniques
- Revive timing: the revive's cooldown depends on the ally's remaining respawn time, so late-game deaths, with long respawn timers, are where it saves the most.
- Stacking Light of Retribution: three hits within 5 seconds stack the extra damage.
- Speed scaling: every 20 magic power adds 1% to Holy Healing's movement speed bonus, up to 80%.
- Long-range stun: the line is long, so use it from behind your frontline.
## Draft and team fit
Rafaela suits teams with an immobile carry who benefits from her speed boost and slow immunity, and teams that want to chase: Holy Healing makes the whole team faster for a moment. In ranked Mythical Glory+, over the past 7 days, she has a 54.08% win rate with a 1.02% pick rate, one of the highest win rates of any support. In the MPL PH S18 playoffs she was picked 4 times (2 wins) and banned 9 times; in the MPL ID S18 playoffs, picked twice without a win.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Miya,Layla,Hanabi,Lesley | bad=Valir,Marcel,Natalia,Cici,Alpha | ally=Miya,Layla,Hanabi,Lesley
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+.
Playing against Rafaela: dive her. She has no escape, so heroes who reach the backline quickly kill her before she can heal or stun.
## Situational adjustments
- Against divers: stay near your tank and hold the ultimate for defense.
- Against poke: use Holy Healing often to keep your team healthy.
- When ahead: speed your team into objectives with Holy Healing.
## Practice drills
- Stun drill: practice the line stun through a group.
- Revive drill: in practice games, track the revive and use it on the carry.
## Common mistakes
- Wasting the ultimate on a single tank.
- Standing in front of the frontline.
- Forgetting the revive.

guides.title: Dyrroth
guides.sub: Abyss fighter who shreds physical defense and ends fights with a lost-HP strike
guides.body:
## Hero Overview
Dyrroth is a melee physical fighter for the EXP lane or jungle, built around short, violent trades. His passive, **Wrath of the Abyss**, enhances Burst Strike and Spectre Step once his Rage reaches 50%. Every 2 basic attacks he releases Circle Strike, which damages enemies around him and heals him for 50 plus 40% of the damage dealt. Each time he hits an enemy hero, Burst Strike and Spectre Step lose 1 second of cooldown, so the more he fights heroes, the more often he casts.
**Burst Strike** fires a burst for 200-450 physical damage and slows by 25% for 1.5 seconds; enhanced, it has longer range, deals 140% damage and doubles the slow. **Spectre Step** dashes and stops at the first non-minion target for 230-355 physical damage; recast to lock on with Fatal Strike for 345-570 physical damage, which reduces the target's physical defense by 40% for 4 seconds. Enhanced, Fatal Strike deals 150% damage, adds a 90% slow for 1 second and reduces physical defense by 60% instead. His ultimate, **Abysm Strike**, launches an uninterruptible strike after a short delay for 650-1250 physical damage plus 20% of the enemy's lost HP, slowing by 55% for 0.8 seconds.
Why he is picked: very high burst for a fighter, a defense shred that helps his whole team, and an ultimate that finishes wounded targets. Over the past 7 days in ranked Mythical Glory+, he is picked in 1.07% of games with a 51.38% win rate. His weakness: once his dash is spent, he has no escape, and kiting heroes outlast his burst.
## Kit deep-dive
### Wrath of the Abyss (passive)
Rage at 50% enhances his two basic skills. Circle Strike every 2 attacks is his sustain, so keep attacking between skills.
### Burst Strike (Skill 1)
Poke and slow with a 5-second cooldown. The damage decays against the same target and is lower on minions, so it is better for trades than for waves.
### Spectre Step (Skill 2)
Dash, then Fatal Strike. The physical defense reduction lasts 4 seconds, which is the window for your ultimate and your team's damage.
### Abysm Strike (Ultimate)
Cannot be interrupted once cast. Its bonus damage is based on lost HP, so it is strongest as a finisher.
::curve 5,4,3 | Very strong early trades, strong mid-game pickoffs, and weaker late against tanky, grouped teams.
## Combos
::combo Full burst | S2 > S2 > S1 > BA > BA > ULT | Dash and Fatal Strike to shred defense, Burst Strike, two attacks for Circle Strike, then the ultimate.
::combo Enhanced opener | BA > BA > S2 > S2 > ULT | Build Rage first so Fatal Strike is enhanced for the 60% shred and 90% slow.
::combo Poke and finish | S1 > ULT | Slow with Burst Strike, then finish with the lost-HP strike.
## Builds and emblems
::build Burst fighter | Warrior Boots, Hunter Strike, Blade of Despair, Malefic Roar, Queen's Wings, Immortality | Burst and penetration, with Queen's Wings and Immortality to survive after diving.
::build Sustain fighter | Warrior Boots, War Axe, Hunter Strike, Brute Force Breastplate, Queen's Wings, Immortality | More HP and spell vamp for long side-lane duels.
::emblem Custom Fighter Emblem | Firmness, Festival of Blood, Brave Smite | Defense, spell vamp and healing on skill damage.
::spells Petrify, Retribution | Petrify in the EXP lane; Retribution in the jungle.
!! Builds are based on item effects and his kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Dyrroth is one of the strongest early fighters. Build Rage by attacking the wave, then trade when your skills are enhanced: an enhanced Fatal Strike cuts the enemy's physical defense by 60% and slows them by 90% for 1 second, which wins most short trades. Each hero hit takes 1 second off both basic skills, so a good trade gives you another cast before the enemy recovers. Back off once your dash is on cooldown.
::map lane | Pressure the EXP lane with enhanced trades.
## Mid game and teamfights
Look for picks on isolated squishy heroes, and in fights, wait for the enemy's crowd control to be used before you dash in. Use Fatal Strike on the target your team is focusing: the defense shred helps every physical damage dealer on your team for 4 seconds. Save the ultimate for a target below half HP, since it adds 20% of their lost HP as damage.
## Advanced techniques
- Rage management: enter fights with Rage above 50% so both skills are enhanced.
- Cooldown cuts: hitting heroes takes 1 second off both skills each time, so in a fight, your skills come back very quickly.
- Uninterruptible ultimate: once cast, it cannot be stopped, so you can fire it into enemy control.
- Circle Strike sustain: every 2 basic attacks heal you, which is why weaving attacks between skills matters.
## Draft and team fit
Dyrroth is a solo-queue fighter more than a pro pick: in the MPL PH S18 playoffs he was picked once and banned 5 times, and in the MPL ID S18 playoffs picked once and banned twice. He pairs well with physical damage junglers and marksmen who benefit from the defense shred, and with roamers who can lock a target for his combo.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Masha,Freya,Paquito,Lukas | bad=Uranus,Alice,Esmeralda,Aldous,Phoveus | ally=Atlas,Tigreal,Kaja,Chou
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+. The good list is an assessment: fighters who trade in melee range take his full burst. Note that Dyrroth is also in the official counter list for Masha.
Playing against Dyrroth: stay out of his early trades, kite him after his dash, and build physical defense; tanks with sustain, such as Uranus and Alice, outlast his burst.
## Situational adjustments
- Against sustain tanks: Malefic Roar earlier and do not overcommit.
- Against kiting teams: Petrify to lock targets.
- When ahead: invade the enemy jungle and pick off squishy heroes.
- When behind: farm side lanes and wait for your team's engage.
## Practice drills
- Rage drill: build Rage on a dummy and practice the enhanced Fatal Strike.
- Weave drill: weave two attacks between skills for Circle Strike.
## Common mistakes
- Diving with no Rage.
- Using the ultimate on full-HP targets.
- Chasing kiting heroes after the dash is used.

guides.title: Harley
guides.sub: Card-throwing mage assassin who burns a target with a ring of fire
guides.body:
## Hero Overview
Harley is a ranged magic assassin and mage for the jungle or mid lane. His passive, **Magic Master**, makes his basic attacks deal 60 magic damage and lower the enemy's magic defense by 2 for 3 seconds, stacking 10 times.
**Poker Trick** throws 3-5 waves of cards, each dealing 130-210 magic damage to the first enemy hit and giving him 10% attack speed for 3 seconds. **Space Escape** blinks in a direction, leaving a magic hat and granting 30% movement speed for 2 seconds; recast within 4 seconds to return to the hat. His ultimate, **Deadly Magic**, fires a ring of fire at a target hero for 200-400 magic damage and a 40% slow for 1.5 seconds; it stays for 4 seconds, then explodes for 100-200 plus 50% of the damage the enemy took during that time.
Why he is picked: a reliable burst combo and an escape that returns him to safety. Over the past 7 days in ranked Mythical Glory+, he is picked in 0.62% of games with a 48.21% win rate. In the MPL PH S18 playoffs he was picked 3 times and banned 5 times; in the MPL ID S18 playoffs, picked twice (2 wins) and banned 5 times. His weakness: his ultimate can be blocked by other heroes, and he is fragile once his blink is used.
## Kit deep-dive
### Magic Master (passive)
Magic basic attacks and a magic defense shred.
### Poker Trick (Skill 1)
Waves of cards with an attack-speed bonus.
### Space Escape (Skill 2)
Blink in and return.
### Deadly Magic (Ultimate)
A ring that explodes for half of the damage dealt during it.
::curve 4,5,3 | Strong early, very strong mid and weaker late.
## Combos
::combo Ring burst | ULT > S1 > BA > S2 | Ring, cards, attack, then blink away.
::combo Blink in and out | S2 > ULT > S1 > S2 | Blink in, ring, cards, return to the hat.
## Builds and emblems
::build Burst mage | Arcane Boots, Genius Wand, Holy Crystal, Divine Glaive, Concentrated Energy, Blood Wings | Burst and penetration.
::emblem Custom Mage Emblem | Inspire, Bargain Hunter, Lethal Ignition | Faster items and burst.
::spells Retribution, Flicker | Retribution in the jungle; Flicker in mid.
!! Builds are based on item effects and his kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Farm quickly and gank once you have the ultimate.
Poker Trick throws several waves of cards, and each hit gives Harley 10% attack speed for 3 seconds, so clearing camps with skills and attacks together is efficient. His basic attacks deal 60 magic damage and shred magic defense, stacking 10 times, which helps against the jungle creeps and against enemy heroes. Gank lanes where the enemy is low or pushed up: Space Escape lets you blink in and come back to the hat if the gank goes wrong.
::map jungle | Clear and gank.
## Mid game and teamfights
Flank and burst a squishy target, then return to the hat.
Deadly Magic is the center of his damage. It deals damage and slows the target by 40% for 1.5 seconds, then explodes after 4 seconds for extra damage plus 50% of all the damage the target took during that time, from Harley and from his teammates. Cast it when your team is about to focus the same target, then throw every Poker Trick wave and basic attack you can. Because the ring is a projectile, enemy heroes standing in front of your target can block it; look for an open angle from the side. Space Escape leaves a hat where you stood, so blink in for the ring, deal your damage, and return to the hat before the enemy answers.
## Advanced techniques
- Ring explosion: deal as much damage as possible during the 4 seconds, and call for your team to focus the same target.
- Hat return: blink in, burst, then return; the recast must happen within 4 seconds.
- Card falloff: enemies hit more than 3 times by Poker Trick take less damage from later hits, so spread cards when several enemies are close.
- Magic defense shred: each basic attack lowers magic defense by 2 for 3 seconds, up to 10 stacks, so weave attacks between skills.
- Movement speed: the blink also gives 30% movement speed for 2 seconds; if you do not need to return, keep the speed to escape.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Miya,Layla,Lesley,Hanabi | bad=Melissa,Valir,Alice,Suyou,Angela | ally=Atlas,Tigreal,Kaja,Chou
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+.
Playing against Harley: stand behind your teammates to block the ring. After his ultimate lands, use your escape or a shield early, since the explosion grows with the damage you take. Heroes who can catch him after he blinks, or tank his burst, are the cleanest answers.
## Situational adjustments
- Against magic defense: Divine Glaive earlier.
- Against assassins: Blood Wings earlier and keep Space Escape for defense.
- When ahead: invade the enemy jungle and pick off isolated heroes.
- When behind: farm safely and wait for your team's engage before using the ring.
## Practice drills
- Ring drill: practice dealing damage during the ring.
- Hat drill: practice blinking in and returning within 4 seconds.
## Common mistakes
- Ulting into heroes who block the ring.
- Forgetting to return to the hat.
- Diving without vision.

guides.title: Chou
guides.sub: Kung-fu fighter who kicks one enemy across the map into his team
guides.body:
## Hero Overview
Chou is a melee physical fighter for the EXP lane or roam, known for one move: the kick that sends a carry into his team. His passive, **Only Fast**, makes his next basic attack deal 180% damage after he travels 5 units, briefly slowing by 80% and reducing physical defense, stacking twice.
**Jeet Kune Do** strikes up to 3 times for 180 physical damage each; the third cast knocks enemies airborne, and hitting a hero with it resets Shunpo. **Shunpo** charges with control immunity and a 200 physical damage shield. His ultimate, **The Way of Dragon**, kicks a target hero for 400 physical damage and knocks them back; recast to chase for a total of 480.
Why he is picked: the kick repositions an enemy carry, and his skills give him control immunity and a knock-up. In the MPL ID S18 playoffs he was picked 8 times (5 wins) and banned 10 times; in the MPL PH S18 playoffs, picked 5 times (2 wins) and banned 6 times. In ranked Mythical Glory+, over the past 7 days, his win rate is 44.68%, a sign that his kick is hard to use well in solo queue. His weakness: a missed kick leaves him exposed, and his damage falls off late.
## Kit deep-dive
### Only Fast (passive)
Move 5 units for an empowered attack. It deals 180% damage, briefly slows by 80% and reduces physical defense, stacking twice. Walking around a target before attacking keeps it ready.
### Jeet Kune Do (Skill 1)
Three strikes; the third knocks airborne. Landing the third on a hero resets Shunpo, so it is both control and mobility.
### Shunpo (Skill 2)
A charge with control immunity and a 200 physical damage shield. Use it to walk through enemy control, or to escape after the kick.
### The Way of Dragon (Ultimate)
The kick deals 400 physical damage and knocks the target back; the recast follows them for a total of 480. The direction of the knock-back is the direction you face, so position before you kick.
::curve 4,4,3 | Strong early and mid, less decisive late.
## Combos
::combo Kick into team | Flicker > ULT | Flicker behind the target, kick them into your team.
::combo Knock-up | S1 > S1 > S1 > S2 | Three strikes, then reset Shunpo.
## Builds and emblems
::build Roam fighter | Tough Boots, Hunter Strike, Dominance Ice, Antique Cuirass, Radiant Armor, Immortality | Durability and damage.
::emblem Custom Fighter Emblem | Firmness, Festival of Blood, Brave Smite | Defense and sustain.
::spells Flicker | Flicker for the kick.
!! Builds are based on item effects and his kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Trade with Jeet Kune Do. Walk around before attacking so Only Fast is ready, and finish a combo with the third strike to knock the enemy airborne and reset Shunpo. Chou's trades are short: hit, knock up, step away. As a roamer, look for picks with your jungler once you have the kick.
::map lane | Hold the EXP lane or roam with your jungler.
## Mid game and teamfights
Kick the enemy carry into your team. The usual setup is to walk around the enemy frontline, often from a bush or by Flickering behind the target, so the kick sends them toward your teammates or under your turret. Shunpo's control immunity lets you get there through enemy stuns. If the carry is out of reach, kick the enemy hero who threatens your own backline away from it instead. After the kick, stay near the target with the recast so your team's damage finishes them.
## Advanced techniques
- Flicker kick: Flicker behind the target, then kick toward your team.
- Shunpo reset: hitting a hero with the third Jeet Kune Do resets Shunpo, giving you a second charge.
- Immunity window: Shunpo grants control immunity while charging, so use it when the enemy throws their control.
- Defensive kick: kicking a diver away from your carry can save a fight.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Miya,Layla,Lesley,Hanabi | bad=X.Borg,Fanny,Beatrix,Natalia,Benedetta | ally=Pharsa,Eudora,Odette,Yve
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+.
Playing against Chou: stay near your team and avoid standing at the edge where a kick sends you into his team. Watch for him in bushes and keep control for after his Shunpo, when he no longer has immunity.
## Situational adjustments
- Against heavy control: save Shunpo for immunity.
- Against tanky teams: build more defense and focus on the kick as utility.
- When ahead: roam with your jungler for picks.
- When behind: farm safely and wait for your team's engage.
## Practice drills
- Kick drill: practice Flicker kicks in a training match.
- Reset drill: practice the three-strike combo into a Shunpo reset.
## Common mistakes
- Missing the kick, or kicking the target away from your team.
- Using Shunpo before the enemy uses their control.
- Fighting without Only Fast ready.

guides.title: Valentina
guides.sub: Shadow mage who steals the enemy's ultimate and turns it against them
guides.body:
## Hero Overview
Valentina is a ranged magic mage for the mid lane with one of the most unusual ultimates in the game: she copies an enemy hero's ultimate and casts it herself. Her passive, **Primal Force**, gives her 8-50 extra EXP each time she damages an enemy hero (every 2 seconds), and if the enemy's level is not higher than hers, 30% of the damage she deals is converted into HP. That means she out-levels her lane opponent and sustains through trades.
**Shadow Strike** fires a line for 340-665 magic damage and slows by 40% for 1 second; heroes hit are marked with a Shadow Sigil for 4 seconds and are terrified for 1 second if hit by Shadow Strike again during that time (once per 4 seconds). **Arcane Shade** dashes and fires 3 Shadow Bolts at nearby enemies for 125-225 magic damage each; it can be cast again within 6 seconds, and every bolt that hits reduces Shadow Strike's cooldown by 1 second. Her ultimate, **I Am You**, slows a target hero by 70% for 0.5 seconds and lets her cast their ultimate, taking their form and basic attack type for up to 12 seconds. The stolen ultimate is at her level, and its cooldown is 120%-100% of the original, never below 10 seconds.
Why she is picked: in the right draft, she gets a second copy of the enemy's best ultimate. Pro teams in the Philippines banned her 10 times and picked her 6 times (2 wins) in the MPL PH S18 playoffs; in the MPL ID S18 playoffs she was banned 9 times. Her weakness: her value depends on what the enemy drafts, and her ranked Mythical Glory+ win rate over the past 7 days is 45.42%, which shows she is hard to play well.
## Kit deep-dive
### Primal Force (passive)
Extra EXP every time you damage a hero, plus healing while you are not lower level. Poke early to get ahead in levels.
### Shadow Strike (Skill 1)
Two hits within 4 seconds terrify the target for 1 second. Bolts from Arcane Shade shorten its cooldown, which is how you get the second hit quickly.
### Arcane Shade (Skill 2)
A dash with three bolts and a recast. Use it to reposition, to chase, or to refresh Shadow Strike.
### I Am You (Ultimate)
Choose the ultimate before the fight. The best targets are ultimates that win fights on their own: area control, big burst or a global effect.
::curve 4,4,4 | Strong early thanks to extra EXP, flexible mid game, and as strong late as the ultimate she steals.
## Combos
::combo Terrify | S1 > S2 > S1 | Mark with Shadow Strike, dash so the bolts cut its cooldown, then hit again to terrify.
::combo Steal and cast | ULT > ULT > S1 > S2 | Copy the enemy's ultimate, cast it on their team (the second ULT), then follow with your own skills.
::combo Escape | S2 > S2 > S1 | Dash twice to get away, then slow the chaser.
## Builds and emblems
::build Burst mage | Arcane Boots, Genius Wand, Holy Crystal, Divine Glaive, Lightning Truncheon, Blood Wings | Burst and penetration for her skills and stolen ultimates.
::emblem Custom Mage Emblem | Inspire, Bargain Hunter, Lethal Ignition | Faster items and burst.
::spells Flicker | Flicker for safety.
!! Builds are based on item effects and her kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Poke the enemy mid laner often. Each hit on a hero gives extra EXP, so you can reach key levels before your opponent, and while you are not behind in level, the passive heals you for 30% of the damage. Use Shadow Strike to clear the wave and hit the enemy at the same time when they line up.
::map rotate | Win the mid lane on levels, then rotate with your ultimate.
## Mid game and teamfights
Before every fight, decide whose ultimate you will steal. Area control ultimates, such as a tank's group pull, are often the best choice, since they can start or turn a fight. Steal at the start of the fight if you want to engage, or later if you want to counter-engage. After the steal, you keep your own skills, so combine the stolen ultimate with Shadow Strike's terrify.
## Advanced techniques
- Steal priority: choose the ultimate that changes the fight most, not the closest hero.
- Morph ultimates: if the stolen ultimate has a morph effect, her regular skills change too.
- Physical heroes: stealing from a physical damage hero also gives her physical attack.
- Cooldown awareness: the stolen ultimate has 100%-120% of the original cooldown, so a short-cooldown ultimate can be used often.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Atlas,Tigreal,Lolita,Johnson | bad=Carmilla,Lukas,X.Borg,Akai,Atlas | ally=Atlas,Tigreal,Franco,Kaja
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+. Note: Atlas appears in both lists. His ultimate is one of the best to steal, but the official data says Atlas wins the matchup in ranked, so treat it as a skill matchup.
Playing against Valentina: stay out of her poke early, and dive her once her dash is on cooldown.
## Situational adjustments
- Against teams with weak ultimates: use her as a poke and burst mage instead.
- Against divers: keep Arcane Shade for escape.
- When ahead: rotate early and steal ultimates for objective fights.
## Practice drills
- Terrify drill: practice the double Shadow Strike.
- Steal drill: practice each enemy ultimate in custom games.
## Common mistakes
- Stealing an ultimate she cannot use well.
- Missing the second Shadow Strike.
- Dashing into the enemy team.

guides.title: Layla
guides.sub: Long-range marksman whose damage grows with distance
guides.body:
## Hero Overview
Layla is a ranged physical marksman for the gold lane and one of the first heroes many players learn. Her passive, **Malefic Gun**, increases her damage the farther she is from her target, from 100% up to 130% at 6 units away (turrets excluded).
**Malefic Bomb** fires a bomb for 200-400 physical damage to the first enemy hit (it can crit); on a hit, her basic attacks and Void Projectile gain extra range for 3 seconds, and she gains 60% movement speed decaying over 1.2 seconds, doubled in duration if she hits a hero. **Void Projectile** explodes for 170-320 physical damage and applies a Magic Mark for 3 seconds; hitting a marked enemy deals 100-200 physical damage to nearby enemies and stuns them for 0.25 seconds. Her ultimate, **Destruction Rush**, fires a blast for 500-800 physical damage in a line; passively, it increases the range of her basic attacks and Void Projectile by 0.6-1.8 units and slightly increases her sight range.
Why she is picked: long range and simple mechanics. Over the past 7 days in ranked Mythical Glory+, she is picked in 1.15% of games with a 47.87% win rate. Her weakness: no dash, so she relies on positioning and her team.
## Kit deep-dive
### Malefic Gun (passive)
Stand far away: at 6 units, her damage is 130%.
### Malefic Bomb (Skill 1)
Poke, a speed boost and extra range for 3 seconds.
### Void Projectile (Skill 2)
Area damage with a mark and a short stun.
### Destruction Rush (Ultimate)
A long line blast, plus permanent extra range.
::curve 2,4,5 | Weak early, strong mid and very strong late at long range.
## Combos
::combo Poke | S1 > BA > S2 > BA | Bomb for range and speed, attack, projectile, attack.
::combo Finish | S2 > ULT | Mark and stun, then the line blast.
## Builds and emblems
::build Crit marksman | Swift Boots, Berserker's Fury, Windtalker, Haas' Claws, Malefic Roar, Wind of Nature | Crit and penetration.
::emblem Custom Marksman Emblem | Fatal, Weapon Master, Weakness Finder | Crit and attack.
::spells Flicker | Flicker for safety.
!! Builds are based on item effects and her kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Farm safely. Malefic Bomb is your poke and your escape: hitting a hero doubles the duration of the speed boost.
Layla's first minutes are about surviving to her items. Her range is longer than most marksmen once she lands Malefic Bomb, since a hit extends her basic attack and Void Projectile range for 3 seconds. Use that window to poke the enemy marksman from a distance they cannot answer, then step back. Void Projectile clears the wave with area damage; its mark stuns enemies near a marked target for 0.25 seconds when you hit it again, which can interrupt an enemy dash. Without a dash of your own, ward off ganks by staying near your turret when the enemy jungler is missing from the map.
::map lane | Farm the gold lane safely.
## Mid game and teamfights
Stay as far back as you can while still hitting targets. Your damage rises with distance, so the safest position is also the strongest.
The ultimate's passive range bonus grows as you upgrade it, so each ultimate level makes her safer. Use Destruction Rush on grouped enemies or to finish a fleeing target. Void Projectile's mark and short stun can interrupt a diver, and Malefic Bomb's speed boost helps you step back after an exchange.
## Advanced techniques
- Distance: always fight at maximum range.
- Bomb range: after hitting the bomb, attack from extra range for 3 seconds.
- Mark stun: hit marked enemies to stun nearby targets.
- Vision: the ultimate's sight bonus helps you spot divers early.
## Draft and team fit
Layla needs a frontline and a support who protect her. She did not appear in the MPL PH or MPL ID Season 18 playoff stats. Pick her when your team has a strong tank and the enemy has few divers.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Belerick,Tigreal,Franco,Hylos | bad=Diggie,Phoveus,Rafaela,Edith,Bruno | ally=Estes,Angela,Tigreal,Atlas
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+.
Playing against Layla: close the distance; she has no dash. Assassins and heroes with gap closers reach her easily, and heroes who can survive her poke and dive in late fights punish her the most.
## Situational adjustments
- Against assassins: Wind of Nature earlier.
- Against tanks: Malefic Roar earlier.
- When behind: farm safely and stay behind your team.
## Practice drills
- Range drill: practice attacking from maximum range.
- Bomb drill: hit a dummy with Malefic Bomb, then attack from the extended range during the 3 seconds.
## Common mistakes
- Standing too close.
- Using the bomb without a target.
- Fighting alone.

guides.title: Yu Zhong
guides.sub: Black dragon fighter who drains HP with every hit and flies over walls
guides.body:
## Hero Overview
Yu Zhong is a melee physical fighter for the EXP lane. His passive, **Cursing Touch**, applies Sha Residue to enemy heroes each time he deals physical damage; at 5 stacks it erupts and consumes a stack every 0.4 seconds, dealing 20 plus 2.5% of the target's lost HP and restoring 6% of his lost HP per stack. When it erupts, he gains 30% movement speed for 3 seconds.
**Dragon Tail** turns his cloak into a weapon: the inner area deals 220-400 physical damage, and the sharpened edge deals 275% damage and applies 2 Sha Residue stacks. **Soul Grip** damages enemies in front for 150-300 physical damage and slows by 60% for 1 second; on hit, his next basic attack is enhanced. **Furious Dive** leaps to an area, can dash once more, and after a short delay knocks enemies airborne for 0.8 seconds. His ultimate, **Black Dragon Form**, channels for 0.6 seconds, then he transforms for up to 7 seconds: he cannot use skills, but moves freely, knocks back heroes in his path, gains 1000-2000 max HP, becomes immune to control, and ignores obstacles. Afterwards, he enters Dragonoid Form, with increased skill range for 10 seconds.
Why he is picked: high sustain in fights and a flying ultimate that crosses walls. In the MPL ID S18 playoffs he was picked 10 times (6 wins) and banned 6 times. His weakness: a long ultimate cooldown and no skills during the dragon form.
## Kit deep-dive
### Cursing Touch (passive)
Five stacks erupt for lost-HP damage and healing.
### Dragon Tail (Skill 1)
Hit with the edge for 275% damage and 2 stacks.
### Soul Grip (Skill 2)
Slow and an enhanced attack.
### Furious Dive (Skill 3)
A leap with a knock-up after a short delay.
### Black Dragon Form (Ultimate)
Fly, knock back and become immune to control.
::curve 3,4,5 | Moderate early, strong mid and very strong late.
## Combos
::combo Stack and drain | S3 > S1 > S2 > BA | Leap in, cloak edge for stacks, grip and enhanced attack for the eruption.
::combo Dragon engage | ULT > S3 > S1 > S2 | Fly over walls into the enemy, then leap and stack.
## Builds and emblems
::build Sustain fighter | Warrior Boots, War Axe, Hunter Strike, Brute Force Breastplate, Queen's Wings, Immortality | Sustain and damage.
::emblem Custom Fighter Emblem | Firmness, Festival of Blood, Brave Smite | Defense and sustain.
::spells Petrify, Flicker | Petrify for control; Flicker for engages.
!! Builds are based on item effects and his kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Trade with the cloak edge to stack Sha Residue on the enemy laner.
The edge of Dragon Tail deals 275% damage and applies 2 stacks at once, so aim for the edge rather than the center. Soul Grip slows by 60% for 1 second and enhances your next basic attack, which adds another stack. Five stacks start the eruption: lost-HP damage on the enemy, healing for you, and 30% movement speed for 3 seconds, which lets you chase or leave. Furious Dive is your gap closer and knock-up; save one dash to escape if the trade turns.
::map lane | Hold the EXP lane.
## Mid game and teamfights
Use Black Dragon Form to fly over walls and enter the fight from an unexpected angle, knocking back heroes in your path. After the transformation, Dragonoid Form extends your skill range for 10 seconds, so use your full combo then.
The eruption heals 6% of your lost HP per stack consumed, so you heal most when you are low. Stay in fights and keep stacking.
## Advanced techniques
- Edge hits: aim Dragon Tail so the edge hits heroes.
- Wall crossing: the ultimate ignores obstacles, so it can be an engage through terrain or an escape over a wall.
- Dragonoid Form: longer range for 10 seconds after the ultimate.
- Furious Dive second dash: the skill allows one more dash before the knock-up, which lets you correct your position.
- Knock-back path: in dragon form, you knock back every hero in your path, so fly through the enemy backline to scatter it.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Miya,Layla,Lesley,Hanabi | bad=Gloo,Minsitthar,Yve,Carmilla,Ixia | ally=Atlas,Tigreal,Kaja,Pharsa
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+.
Playing against Yu Zhong: anti-heal; avoid fights when his ultimate is ready. Burst him before his stacks erupt, and keep your control for after the dragon form, when he is no longer immune.
## Draft and team fit
Yu Zhong was a pro favorite in Indonesia: 10 picks (6 wins) and 6 bans in the MPL ID S18 playoffs, against 2 picks (2 wins) and 2 bans in the MPL PH S18 playoffs. In ranked Mythical Glory+, over the past 7 days, he is picked in 0.82% of games with a 48.81% win rate. He suits teams that need a durable fighter who can also engage from unusual angles.
## Situational adjustments
- Against anti-heal: more HP and defense.
- Against kiting teams: use Furious Dive and the dragon form to reach them.
- When ahead: push side lanes.
- When behind: farm safely and join fights with your ultimate.
## Practice drills
- Edge drill: practice hitting with the cloak edge.
- Dragon drill: practice flying over walls with the ultimate.
## Common mistakes
- Using the ultimate to escape too early.
- Hitting with the center of the cloak instead of the edge.
- Diving without stacks.

guides.title: Minotaur
guides.sub: Bull tank who heals his team and knocks enemies airborne three times
guides.body:
## Hero Overview
Minotaur is a melee physical tank and support for the roam. His passive, **Rage Incarnate**, gives him Motivation for 3 seconds when he uses a skill and heals him for a percentage of the damage dealt by enemy heroes; these effects are doubled while Enraged.
**Despair Stomp** jumps to a location for 280-355 physical damage, briefly knocking enemies airborne and slowing them by 40%, and enhances his basic attacks for 2 seconds. **Motivation Roar** restores 220-320 HP to himself and the most wounded nearby ally. His ultimate, **Minoan Fury**, makes him Enraged and smashes the ground 3 times: the first 2 hits deal 180-300 physical damage and slow by 60%, the final hit deals 200-300 true damage and knocks enemies airborne for 0.8 seconds. He is immune to control during this attack, and the Enraged state lasts 12 seconds.
Why he is picked: area control and healing. Over the past 7 days in ranked Mythical Glory+, he has a 52.89% win rate and a 10.29% ban rate. His weakness: a long ultimate cooldown.
## Kit deep-dive
### Rage Incarnate (passive)
Heals based on damage dealt by enemy heroes.
### Despair Stomp (Skill 1)
Jump, knock up and slow.
### Motivation Roar (Skill 2)
Heal himself and the most wounded ally.
### Minoan Fury (Ultimate)
Three smashes, true damage and a knock-up, with control immunity.
::curve 3,5,4 | Solid early, very strong mid in objective fights, durable late.
## Combos
::combo Engage | S1 > ULT > S2 | Jump in, smash, then heal.
::combo Flicker engage | ULT > Flicker | Start the smashes and Flicker into the group.
## Builds and emblems
::build Support tank | Tough Boots, Dominance Ice, Antique Cuirass, Radiant Armor, Oracle, Immortality | Defense and healing.
::emblem Custom Tank Emblem | Vitality, Tenacity, Concussive Blast | HP and defense.
::spells Flicker | Flicker for engages.
!! Builds are based on item effects and his kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Roam with your marksman and jungler; heal them with Motivation Roar.
Motivation Roar has a 10-second cooldown and heals you and the most wounded nearby ally for 220-320 HP, so it is a reliable way to win early trades for your marksman. Despair Stomp jumps to a location, briefly knocks enemies airborne and slows them by 40%, then enhances your basic attacks for 2 seconds. Use it from a bush or after your marksman has started a trade, so the enemy has no time to react. Your passive heals you based on the damage enemy heroes deal, so you can stand in front and take hits.
::map roam | Roam with your team.
## Mid game and teamfights
Wait for enemies to group, jump in with Despair Stomp, then use Minoan Fury for the knock-up. While Enraged for 12 seconds, your skills are enhanced: Despair Stomp has a larger area, and Motivation Roar heals all nearby allies.
The first two smashes slow by 60%, which keeps enemies inside for the final hit: 200-300 true damage and a 0.8-second knock-up. That knock-up is the moment your damage dealers should commit, so call it before you go in. After the smashes, the Enraged state lasts 12 seconds: use Motivation Roar to heal your whole team and Despair Stomp again if it is ready, since both are stronger during that time. With a 60-second cooldown, save the ultimate for turtle, lord and big teamfights rather than small skirmishes.
## Advanced techniques
- Enraged skills: use skills during the 12 seconds: Despair Stomp hits a larger area and Motivation Roar heals all nearby allies.
- Control immunity: you are immune to control during the smashes, so you can start them into enemy stuns.
- Flicker smash: Flicker during the smashes to move the final knock-up onto a group.
- Passive doubling: while Enraged, the passive effects are doubled, so you heal more from damage taken.
## Draft and team fit
In the MPL PH S18 playoffs he was picked 5 times (2 wins). In ranked Mythical Glory+, over the past 7 days, he is picked in 1.36% of games with a 52.89% win rate and banned in 10.29%. He pairs well with area damage dealers who follow his knock-ups, and with immobile marksmen who benefit from his heals.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Miya,Layla,Lesley,Hanabi | bad=Khufra,Lolita,Odette,Cyclops,Silvanna | ally=Pharsa,Eudora,Odette,Yve
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+.
Playing against Minotaur: spread out so his smashes catch fewer heroes, and dive his backline after his ultimate is used, since it has a 60-second cooldown.
## Situational adjustments
- Against magic damage: Radiant Armor earlier.
- Against poke: use Motivation Roar often to keep your team healthy.
- When ahead: invade the enemy jungle with your team.
## Practice drills
- Smash drill: practice Flicker during the smashes.
- Heal drill: practice healing the most wounded ally.
## Common mistakes
- Engaging alone.
- Using the ultimate on a single hero.
- Forgetting to heal allies.

guides.title: Zetian
guides.sub: Phoenix mage whose ultimate stuns every enemy hero on the map at once
guides.body:
## Hero Overview
Zetian is a ranged magic mage for the mid lane with one of the most unusual ultimates in the game: it reaches every enemy hero, wherever they are. Her passive, **Celestial Armament**, has two parts. Phoenix Crown gives her 0.5% spell vamp for 5 seconds each time Phoenix Strike or Phoenix Descent hits an enemy hero, stacking up to 10 times. Celestial Robe periodically protects her: the first enemy hero who comes close is knocked back and stunned, takes magic damage, and Zetian gains a shield for 3 seconds. That effect has a 120-second cooldown.
**Phoenix Strike** sends a Phoenix Wave in a direction; if it hits an enemy, she automatically casts another, up to 3 times, for 185, 185 and 330 magic damage. The third wave hits a larger area with a small pull, and she can move with 10% extra speed and use other skills while casting. **Phoenix Descent** summons a Phoenix Spirit for 150 magic damage and a 50% slow; it hovers for 3 seconds, dealing 20 magic damage every 0.5 seconds and reducing magic defense by 10%, and she can recast to send it charging to another location for another 150 damage and a slow. Her ultimate, **Fury of the Phoenix**, gives every allied hero 60% movement speed decaying over 3 seconds and deals 400 magic damage to every enemy hero, stunning them for 1 second. She also gains vision of all enemy heroes, and she can cast other skills while channeling it.
Why she is picked: a global stun can start a fight, stop an enemy escape, or interrupt the enemy's engage everywhere on the map at once. Over the past 7 days in ranked Mythical Glory+, she is picked in 2.03% of games, one of the highest pick rates of any mage, with a 50.14% win rate. In the MPL PH S18 playoffs she was picked 8 times (4 wins) and banned 5 times. Her weakness: a 90-second cooldown on the ultimate, and short-range skills that need setup.
## Kit deep-dive
### Celestial Armament (passive)
Spell vamp from repeated hits and an automatic knock-back with a shield once every 120 seconds. Divers who jump on her first get stunned, so track when the robe is ready.
### Phoenix Strike (Skill 1)
Each wave that hits casts the next one, up to three. Because she can move while casting, she can keep distance while the waves fire.
### Phoenix Descent (Skill 2)
A zone that slows and reduces magic defense, with a recast to move it. Place it where enemies must walk, or recast it onto a fleeing target.
### Fury of the Phoenix (Ultimate)
Global damage, a 1-second stun on every enemy hero and a team-wide speed boost. Its strength is timing: cast it when the most enemy heroes are doing something important.
::curve 3,5,5 | Moderate early, very strong mid game once the ultimate shapes every fight, and still decisive late.
## Combos
::combo Wave chain | S2 > S1 | Slow with Phoenix Descent so all three Phoenix Strike waves land.
::combo Global engage | ULT > S2 > S1 | Stun everyone, speed up your team, then zone and strike the nearest targets.
::combo Counter-engage | ULT > S1 > S2 > S2 | Cast the ultimate the moment the enemy dives, then fire waves and send the spirit after the divers.
## Builds and emblems
::build Burst mage | Arcane Boots, Genius Wand, Holy Crystal, Divine Glaive, Lightning Truncheon, Blood Wings | Burst and penetration, plus a shield for safety.
::build Sustain mage | Arcane Boots, Clock of Destiny, Concentrated Energy, Genius Wand, Divine Glaive, Blood Wings | More HP and spell vamp to go with her passive's spell vamp stacks.
::emblem Custom Mage Emblem | Inspire, Bargain Hunter, Lethal Ignition | Faster items and burst.
::spells Flicker | Flicker for safety.
!! Builds are based on item effects and her kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Clear the mid wave with Phoenix Strike and Phoenix Descent, and poke the enemy mage when they walk into your waves. The ultimate unlocks at level 4: from then on, every fight on the map is one you can join, even from mid lane.
::map rotate | Clear mid, then use the ultimate to help fights anywhere.
## Mid game and teamfights
The ultimate is a map-wide tool, so watch the minimap. Good moments: your team engages and the enemy tries to escape, the enemy dives your carry, or several enemies are contesting an objective. The 60% speed boost for your team turns the stun into a chase. In your own fights, stay behind your frontline and use Phoenix Descent to slow and weaken enemies before Phoenix Strike.
## Advanced techniques
- Global timing: the ultimate hits every enemy hero, so a teammate's fight in another lane can be won from where you stand.
- Channel and cast: you can use other skills during the channel, so keep fighting while it goes off.
- Spirit recast: send Phoenix Descent's spirit after a fleeing enemy for a second hit and slow.
- Robe awareness: the knock-back and shield return every 120 seconds; when it is ready, you can be more aggressive.
## Draft and team fit
Zetian fits teams that can follow a global stun: junglers who chase, fighters who dive, and a marksman who benefits from 1 second of free damage. In the MPL PH S18 playoffs her most frequent partner was Barats (4 games together, 3 wins). In the MPL ID S18 playoffs she was picked 3 times (2 wins) and banned 6 times.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Fanny,Ling,Lancelot,Hayabusa | bad=Lolita,Natalia,Tigreal,Popol and Kupa,Pharsa | ally=Barats,Atlas,Hirara,Freya
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+. The good list is an assessment: escape-reliant assassins lose their getaway to a global stun.
Playing against Zetian: track her ultimate cooldown and fight when it is down, and catch her when the robe is on cooldown.
## Situational adjustments
- Against divers: hold the ultimate for defense.
- Against magic defense: Divine Glaive earlier.
- When ahead: rotate with your team and use the ultimate to start objective fights.
## Practice drills
- Wave drill: practice landing all three waves on a moving dummy.
- Map drill: in practice games, watch the minimap and cast the ultimate for fights in other lanes.
## Common mistakes
- Using the ultimate on one enemy.
- Missing the first wave, so the chain never starts.
- Standing in front of your tank.

guides.title: Valir
guides.sub: Fire mage who burns a share of max HP and knocks divers away
guides.body:
## Hero Overview
Valir is a ranged magic mage for the mid lane built to control space and punish anyone who walks into him. His passive, **Ashing**, applies a stack of Ablaze with each skill hit, burning enemies for 0.6% of their max HP per second for 4 seconds. At 3 stacks, the fire detonates for 6% of the target's max HP and stuns them for 1 second; the same target can only be stunned this way once every 7 seconds.
**Burst Fireball** explodes on the first target for 235-410 magic damage, slows by 30% for 1 second, and leaves a flame that explodes again after 1 second for 118-205. He holds up to 2 charges, and hitting an enemy hero or a Legend Creep restores a charge at once. **Searing Torrent** sends a torrent that deals 200-300 magic damage and knocks enemies to the end of its path, leaving a fire wall for 4 seconds that deals 80-120 per second, with a 25% slow. His ultimate, **Vengeance Flame**, removes all debuffs, conjures 4 flames for 9 seconds that each enhance his next skill with 30% extra base damage and stronger effects, and gives him 40% movement speed that decays over 3 seconds.
Why he is picked: he is one of the hardest mages for melee heroes to reach, and his max-HP burn hurts tanks. Over the past 7 days in ranked Mythical Glory+, his win rate is 54.07%, among the highest of any mage, with a 1.3% pick rate. In the MPL ID S18 playoffs he was picked 10 times (3 wins) and banned 6 times. His weakness: short range compared to long-range mages, and he needs to land several hits for the stun.
## Kit deep-dive
### Ashing (passive)
Three stacks detonate for a max-HP burst and a stun. Every skill counts, so a fireball, the flame it leaves, and the torrent can all add stacks.
### Burst Fireball (Skill 1)
A 1.5-second cooldown, two charges, and an instant refund on hero hits, which lets him throw fireballs very often in fights.
### Searing Torrent (Skill 2)
A knock-back and a fire wall. Use it to push divers away or into a wall.
### Vengeance Flame (Ultimate)
A cleanse, speed and four enhanced skills. Use it when a diver controls you, or at the start of a fight for maximum damage.
::curve 4,4,4 | Strong early poke and control, steady mid game, and still dangerous late with max-HP damage.
## Combos
::combo Stun combo | S1 > S1 > S2 | Two fireballs and the torrent for three Ablaze stacks and the stun.
::combo Anti-dive | S2 > S1 > S1 | Knock the diver away, then fireball them as they come back.
::combo Cleanse and burst | ULT > S1 > S2 > S1 | Remove control, then enhanced fireballs and torrent.
## Builds and emblems
::build Burn mage | Arcane Boots, Genius Wand, Holy Crystal, Divine Glaive, Ice Queen Wand, Blood Wings | Burst, penetration and a slow on skill hits that keeps enemies in his fire.
::emblem Custom Mage Emblem | Inspire, Bargain Hunter, Lethal Ignition | Faster items and burst.
::spells Flicker | Flicker for safety.
!! Builds are based on item effects and his kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Poke the enemy mage with fireballs: each hero hit refunds a charge, so you can throw them often. Clear the wave with the fireball's lingering flame, which explodes after 1 second.
::map rotate | Clear mid, then rotate to side lanes.
## Mid game and teamfights
Valir is a protector as much as a damage dealer. Stand near your marksman and use Searing Torrent to knock away any diver. The fire wall slows and burns, so place it between your team and the enemy. Save the ultimate to cleanse yourself if you are stunned, or use it at the start of a fight for four enhanced skills.
## Advanced techniques
- Charge refund: every hero hit restores a fireball charge, so in fights he can throw fireballs almost continuously.
- Stun cooldown: the same target can be stunned only once every 7 seconds.
- Torrent into walls: knock enemies into your team or away from your carry.
- Legend Creep refund: fireballs on Legend Creeps also refund charges, which helps secure objectives.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Helcurt,Fanny,Ling,Lancelot | bad=Alice,Fredrinn,Balmond,Thamuz,Leomord | ally=Atlas,Tigreal,Franco,Kaja
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+. Valir is in the official counter list for Helcurt, which is the basis of the good list.
Playing against Valir: sustain fighters with high HP outlast his burn. Spread out so the torrent cannot push several heroes.
## Situational adjustments
- Against divers: hold Searing Torrent for defense.
- Against tanks: max-HP damage is your strength; keep stacking Ablaze.
- When ahead: control objectives with the fire wall.
## Practice drills
- Stun drill: practice three-stack stuns.
- Torrent drill: practice knocking a dummy into a wall.
## Common mistakes
- Using the torrent to engage instead of to defend.
- Ignoring the fireball charge refund.
- Wasting the ultimate's cleanse.

guides.title: Franco
guides.sub: Hook tank who drags a target in and suppresses them
guides.body:
## Hero Overview
Franco is a melee physical tank for the roam, famous for his hook. His passive, **Wasteland Force**, gives him 10% movement speed and 1% max HP regeneration per second if he takes no damage for 5 seconds, and builds Wasteland Force stacks (up to 10); his next skill consumes them for up to 150% extra damage.
**Iron Hook** launches a hook that snags the first enemy unit hit for 400-650 physical damage and drags them to him. **Fury Shock** deals 300-450 plus 4% of his max HP as physical damage to nearby enemies and slows them by 70% for 1.5 seconds. His ultimate, **Bloody Hunt**, suppresses a target enemy hero for 1.8 seconds and strikes them 6 times for 50 physical damage each.
Why he is picked: a successful hook plus suppression is a guaranteed kill on a squishy target. His weakness: the hook stops at the first unit, so minions and creeps block it. Over the past 7 days in ranked Mythical Glory+, his win rate is 39.42%, among the lowest in the game, which shows how much he depends on landing hooks.
## Kit deep-dive
### Wasteland Force (passive)
Build stacks while avoiding damage, then spend them on a big skill.
### Iron Hook (Skill 1)
The first unit hit is dragged. Aim around minions.
### Fury Shock (Skill 2)
A 70% slow after the hook.
### Bloody Hunt (Ultimate)
A 1.8-second suppression.
::curve 4,4,3 | Strong early picks, solid mid and less decisive late.
## Combos
::combo Hook kill | S1 > S2 > ULT | Hook, slow, suppress.
::combo Flicker suppress | Flicker > ULT > S2 | Flicker in, suppress, slow.
## Builds and emblems
::build Roam tank | Tough Boots, Dominance Ice, Antique Cuirass, Radiant Armor, Guardian Helmet, Immortality | Defense and regen.
::emblem Custom Tank Emblem | Vitality, Tenacity, Concussive Blast | HP and defense.
::spells Flicker | Flicker for surprise suppressions.
!! Builds are based on item effects and his kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Roam and look for hooks from bushes. Build Wasteland Force by staying out of combat before a hook.
::map roam | Roam and hook from bushes.
## Mid game and teamfights
Hook the enemy carry into your team, then suppress them. If the hook misses, use Fury Shock to slow enemies and protect your team.
Franco's suppression also stops channeled skills, which makes it a strong answer to heroes with long channels.
## Advanced techniques
- Hook angles: aim from the side, where minions do not block.
- Stack hooks: a fully stacked hook deals far more damage.
- Suppression: interrupts channels.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Atlas,Zhuxin,Miya,Layla | bad=Floryn,Fanny,Angela,Benedetta,Freya | ally=Pharsa,Eudora,Odette,Yve
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+. The good list is an assessment: his suppression interrupts channels.
Playing against Franco: stand behind your minions.
## Situational adjustments
- Against healers: Dominance Ice.
## Practice drills
- Hook drill: practice hooks around minions.
## Common mistakes
- Hooking tanks.

guides.title: Helcurt
guides.sub: Night assassin who blinds the enemy team and silences them with fear
guides.body:
## Hero Overview
Helcurt is a melee physical assassin for the jungle or roam. His passive, **Shadow of Styx**, keeps him in the Prowler state until he is spotted, giving him 15% movement speed and HP regeneration while he deals no damage. When spotted, he gains 50% attack speed and 50% movement speed for 4 seconds. Heroes killed after being hit by Helcurt leave a dark fog that conceals him.
**Hidden Terror** blinks to a location for 150-300 physical damage and slows by 60% for 0.75 seconds; in the Prowler state, it also terrifies enemy heroes and its cooldown decreases 3 times as fast. **Deadly Stinger** fires all stored stingers (up to 5, gained every 1.5 seconds in the Prowler state or on each basic attack), each dealing 180-280 physical damage. His ultimate, **Dark Night Falls**, reduces all enemies' sight range and makes them lose sight of their allies for 3 seconds, while he gains 40% movement speed.
Why he is picked: a global blind that splits the enemy team, and burst from stored stingers. Over the past 7 days in ranked Mythical Glory+, his win rate is 45.97%. His weakness: fragile once spotted.
## Kit deep-dive
### Shadow of Styx (passive)
Stay unseen to keep the Prowler state.
### Hidden Terror (Skill 1)
Blink and terrify from the Prowler state.
### Deadly Stinger (Skill 2)
Five stingers for burst.
### Dark Night Falls (Ultimate)
A global blind.
::curve 4,4,3 | Strong early, solid mid and weaker late.
## Combos
::combo Prowler burst | S1 > S2 > BA | Blink and terrify, fire all stingers, then attack.
::combo Night gank | ULT > S1 > S2 | Blind the enemy, blink and burst.
## Builds and emblems
::build Burst assassin | Tough Boots, Hunter Strike, Blade of Despair, Malefic Roar, Blade of the Heptaseas, Immortality | Burst and penetration.
::emblem Custom Assassin Emblem | Rupture, Seasoned Hunter, Killing Spree | Penetration and healing on kills.
::spells Retribution | Retribution in the jungle.
!! Builds are based on item effects and his kit, not a stats site. Check the in-game Pro builds before ranked.
## Early game
Clear quickly and gank from the Prowler state.
::map jungle | Clear and gank.
## Mid game and teamfights
Use the ultimate to split the enemy team, then pick off isolated carries.
## Advanced techniques
- Prowler terrify: Hidden Terror terrifies only from the Prowler state.
- Stinger stacking: five stingers before a gank.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Obsidia,Eudora,Hilda,Aulus | bad=X.Borg,Xavier,Yve,Valir,Gord | ally=Atlas,Tigreal,Kaja,Chou
The bad list is the official counter data in Mythical Glory+. Helcurt is in the official counter list for Obsidia, Eudora, Hilda and Paquito, which is the basis of the good list.
Playing against Helcurt: stay grouped and keep vision.
## Situational adjustments
- Against heavy control: wait for skills.
## Practice drills
- Stinger drill: store five stingers before a gank.
## Common mistakes
- Getting spotted before engaging.

guides.title: Karrie
guides.sub: The Lost Star shreds durable frontlines through repeated Lightwheel Marks, sustained true damage, and disciplined positioning
guides.body:
## Hero Overview
Karrie is a short-to-medium-range Marksman whose primary strength is sustained damage against high-HP opponents. Unlike conventional Marksmen who rely heavily on critical strikes or raw physical damage, Karrie has a passive that converts repeated attacks into percentage-based True Damage. This gives her a distinct purpose: punishing opponents who expect their large health pools and defensive investments to keep them alive.
You normally play Karrie in the Gold Lane. Her early priority is acquiring gold safely, reaching her core attack-speed items, and avoiding unnecessary fights. Once she has enough attack speed and access to her ultimate, she becomes considerably more threatening in extended engagements.
Her biggest advantage is that her damage does not depend entirely on penetrating Physical Defense. Her passive deals True Damage, allowing her to remain relevant against tank-heavy compositions. This does not mean she automatically defeats every tank. She still needs time to apply marks, maintain attack range, and survive long enough to complete her damage cycle.
Her weaknesses are equally important.
- Limited effective range: Karrie must approach enemies relatively closely to deal consistent damage. Long-range opponents can threaten her before she reaches a comfortable attacking distance.
- Vulnerability to burst: her mobility comes primarily from Phantom Step. Once that skill is unavailable, divers have a much easier time reaching her.
- Crowd control: immobilization, suppression, and chained control effects can prevent her from maintaining Basic Attacks.
- Dependence on items: her sustained damage improves substantially with attack-speed and attack-effect items. Falling behind delays her ability to threaten frontliners.
- Positioning requirements: her damage is excellent when she can continuously attack, but poor positioning can make her strengths irrelevant.
You should pick Karrie when the enemy composition contains durable frontline heroes and your team can provide enough protection for you to attack consistently. You should reconsider her when the opposing team has several long-range threats, reliable backline access, or enough burst damage to eliminate you before you can respond.
Where she stands right now: in the official rankings for the past 7 days at Mythical Glory and above, Karrie has a 0.61% pick rate, a 48.48% win rate and a 0.66% ban rate. She is a niche pick, not a meta staple, which is exactly why knowing when she fits matters more than forcing her every game.
## Kit deep-dive
### Passive: Lightwheel Mark
Karrie's Basic Attacks and skills apply a stack of Lightwheel Mark when they hit an enemy. Once a target reaches 5 stacks, the marks turn into a lightwheel and deal True Damage equal to 6%-8% of the target's Max HP. Against Creeps, the passive deals only up to 300 damage.
!! Jade's draft gave the passive as "5% plus 1% per Extra Physical Attack" of Max HP. The MLBB Wiki's current text (checked 11 November 2026) says 6%-8% of the target's Max HP, so the guide uses that. Check the in-game skill screen if the wiki and the client disagree.
This passive defines practically every decision you make with Karrie. You are not simply trying to land individual attacks. You are building toward repeated passive activations. Every successful attack contributes to that process, making attack speed particularly valuable.
The distinction between percentage-based True Damage and conventional physical damage matters enormously. Physical Defense does not reduce the True Damage component, so opponents cannot neutralize your passive simply by purchasing defensive armor. However, do not confuse this with complete damage immunity to defensive builds. Your regular attacks and physical skill damage still interact with Physical Defense normally.
How to use it:
- Maintain attacks on a single priority target when possible. Splitting your damage between several opponents delays passive activations against each individual target.
- Use your skills to contribute additional marks instead of relying exclusively on Basic Attacks.
- Attack frontline heroes when reaching the enemy backline would require an unsafe commitment.
- Track which opponents have already accumulated marks. A nearly completed passive cycle can make a target particularly vulnerable.
Common misuse: a common mistake is abandoning a nearly completed mark sequence to chase another opponent. You lose the immediate pressure created by your previous attacks and may have to rebuild the sequence from the beginning. Another mistake is assuming that your passive makes you an automatic tank counter. You still need sufficient attack speed, positioning, and uninterrupted attacking time.
### Skill 1: Spinning Lightwheel
Karrie releases a sphere of surging energy in a selected direction. It deals 250-375 (+90% Extra Physical Attack) Physical Damage to enemies along its path. Once it reaches an enemy hero or its maximum travel distance, it stops and continuously deals 150-200 (+20% Extra Physical Attack) Physical Damage to nearby enemies, slowing them by 80% for 1 second. Its cooldown is 8.0 seconds.
Its primary value is not simply its damage. It provides an important combination of mark application, area pressure, and movement control.
How to use it: use Spinning Lightwheel to slow an approaching opponent before they reach your position. This creates a small window to reposition or continue attacking. During lane engagements, aim it where the opponent is moving rather than where they currently stand. This is particularly effective against opponents who are trying to retreat after trading.
In teamfights, the skill becomes a useful tool for controlling the space between you and the enemy frontline. A properly placed sphere can interfere with an advancing formation and make it easier to maintain your preferred distance. You can also use it to contribute passive marks before committing to Basic Attacks.
What to watch for: the sphere stops when it hits an enemy hero. Therefore, its final position matters. Do not assume it will travel through the frontline and automatically reach the backline.
Common misuse: using the skill purely for damage without considering its slow. Its utility can be more valuable than its immediate damage, particularly when an enemy assassin is approaching.
### Skill 2: Phantom Step
Karrie dashes in the selected direction while throwing a lightwheel at the nearest enemy. The lightwheel deals 150-275 (+70% Extra Physical Attack) Physical Damage and applies a stack of Lightwheel Mark. During Dual Wield, Phantom Step throws two lightwheels instead.
This is Karrie's primary repositioning tool and one of the most important abilities to manage correctly. Its cooldown drops from 4.5 seconds at rank one to 2.5 seconds at max rank, so you get frequent opportunities to adjust your position, but that does not mean you should spend it carelessly.
How to use it:
- Dash sideways to avoid predictable skillshots while maintaining your attacking position.
- Dash backward when an enemy fighter or tank begins closing the distance.
- Use it offensively only when you have enough information about the enemy's remaining crowd control and mobility.
- During your ultimate, use the additional lightwheel to accelerate passive activations.
The skill's targeting behavior deserves special attention. The lightwheel targets the nearest enemy, which means your dash direction and the surrounding enemy positions influence your damage distribution. You should not automatically dash toward your intended target if another enemy is closer.
Common misuse: using Phantom Step to enter a fight before the enemy's important abilities have been used. Remember that your dash is also your escape mechanism. If you spend it to deal a little additional damage, you may lose the ability to survive the actual engagement.
### Ultimate: Speedy Lightwheel
Karrie enters Dual Wield state for 6, 8 or 10 seconds depending on the skill's rank. During this state, she gains 20% Movement Speed and throws two lightwheels with each Basic Attack. Each lightwheel deals 50%-70% of her Basic Attack damage (by rank) and inherits a portion of Attack Effects. Its cooldown is 35.0 seconds.
!! Jade's draft described the ultimate as a flat 10 seconds with lightwheels dealing "40 plus 50% of Total Physical Attack". The MLBB Wiki's current text gives 6 / 8 / 10 seconds and 50% / 60% / 70% of Basic Attack damage, so the guide uses those values. Check the in-game skill screen if they differ.
This is your major sustained-damage window. The additional lightwheels improve your ability to apply marks and activate your passive. The movement-speed bonus also helps you maintain attacking distance while following moving opponents. Because the duration grows with each rank, the ultimate is noticeably stronger once it is maxed: a rank-one Dual Wield gives you much less time to work with.
How to use it: do not treat Speedy Lightwheel as an ability that must always be activated immediately. Its value depends on how much time you can spend attacking after activation. If the enemy frontline is approaching and you have a safe position, activating your ultimate can allow you to punish the engagement. If the enemy's primary diver is still hiding, however, you may want to preserve your ultimate until that threat reveals itself.
During an objective contest, activate it when you have a reliable target and can maintain sustained damage.
Common misuse: activating the ultimate while retreating without an opportunity to attack. You are wasting much of its offensive value if you cannot maintain contact with an enemy. Another mistake is using it too early in a fight and allowing its duration to expire before the actual frontline engagement begins.
::curve 2,4,4 | Modest early while she lacks attack-speed items, strong from the mid game once her core and a ranked-up ultimate come online; late game depends on protection.
## How the kit fits together
Karrie's abilities form a sustained-damage system rather than a traditional burst combination. Her passive rewards repeated hits. Spinning Lightwheel helps control enemy movement and contributes marks. Phantom Step adds mobility and another mark application. Speedy Lightwheel increases her hit frequency and improves her ability to activate the passive.
The central principle is simple: maintain uninterrupted damage without sacrificing your positioning. Your ideal engagement usually follows this sequence:
- Identify the closest enemy you can safely attack.
- Use Spinning Lightwheel to slow or pressure that opponent.
- Begin applying Basic Attacks.
- Activate Speedy Lightwheel when the engagement becomes favorable.
- Use Phantom Step to reposition and contribute additional marks.
- Continue attacking until the target becomes an unacceptable threat or the engagement changes.
You should understand that Karrie's effectiveness is not determined exclusively by how quickly she kills an individual opponent. Her ability to remain alive while continuously damaging the frontline can determine whether your team wins the entire engagement.
## Combos
::combo Safe Mark Rotation | S1 > BA > BA > S2 > BA | Builds Lightwheel Marks while preserving an escape direction.
This is your standard controlled trading sequence. Start with Spinning Lightwheel to slow the opponent and establish pressure. Follow with Basic Attacks while maintaining your preferred distance. Use Phantom Step when another mark application or repositioning opportunity becomes worthwhile. The important detail is that Phantom Step should not automatically be used toward the opponent. If the enemy is preparing a counterattack, dash away while maintaining a useful target for the lightwheel. This sequence is particularly effective when trading against opponents who need to approach you before they can deal meaningful damage.
::combo Dual Wield Punishment | S1 > ULT > BA > BA > S2 > BA | Maximizes sustained damage and passive applications against an accessible target.
Use this combination when you have already established a safe attacking position. Spinning Lightwheel slows the opponent and makes it harder for them to disengage. Activate Speedy Lightwheel and immediately begin attacking. Do not rush Phantom Step simply because it becomes available. Wait until you have a reason to reposition or accelerate your mark applications: during Dual Wield it throws two lightwheels, so it is worth more inside the ultimate than outside it. This combination works particularly well against frontline heroes who cannot immediately reach you.
::combo Defensive Reposition | BA > S1 > S2 > BA > ULT | Creates distance, interrupts pursuit, and turns a failed enemy engagement into a damage opportunity.
This sequence is intended for situations where an opponent is approaching aggressively. Begin attacking if the opponent is within safe range. Use Spinning Lightwheel to slow their advance, then Phantom Step away from the incoming threat. Once the opponent has committed important abilities and you have enough distance, activate your ultimate and punish their retreat or continued pursuit. The critical decision is recognizing whether the opponent has genuinely lost the ability to reach you. Activating your ultimate while an enemy still has reliable engagement tools can turn a defensive maneuver into a disastrous commitment.
::combo Objective Pressure | ULT > BA > BA > S2 > BA | Sustains damage on an accessible objective while contributing passive damage.
Use this when your team has established control around Turtle or Lord. The ultimate improves your repeated attack output, while Phantom Step can contribute additional marks. Remember that Karrie's passive deals only up to 300 damage against Creeps. Do not assume that the passive will scale against Lord in the same way it does against enemy heroes: on objectives your damage comes mainly from your Basic Attacks and items.
