## Builds and emblems
Your build should emphasize attack speed, repeated attack effects, and enough defensive utility to survive engagements. There is an important distinction between a commonly recorded ranked build and a verified professional tournament build, so this section starts with what pros actually built in MPL Season 18 and then gives the ranked and community setups from Jade's research.
What the pros did: the app has 12 recorded Karrie games from MPL Season 18 (Indonesia, Philippines and Malaysia). Corrosion Scythe and Golden Staff were in all 12 final inventories and Demon Hunter Sword in 10. Warrior Boots were the usual boots (7 games), and the finished defensive item was Wind of Nature (5 games), Rose Gold Meteor (3) or Immortality (2). Every recorded game used the Fighter emblem with Quantum Charge.
::build Pro build: Teddy | Warrior Boots, Corrosion Scythe, Golden Staff, Demon Hunter Sword, Malefic Gun, Immortality | Teddy (Team Liquid PH), MPL PH Season 18, 18 September 2026, a win with 13063 gold. Final inventory as recorded by MLBBHub.
!! Pro item lists are the final inventory at the end of the game, shown in slot order, not the order the items were bought.
- Warrior Boots: Physical Defense, plus Valor, which adds more Physical Defense for a few seconds when you take Physical Damage. Pros took them over attack-speed boots because divers and marksmen are what kill Karrie.
- Corrosion Scythe: attack speed and movement speed, Basic Attacks that deal extra Physical Damage and slow (the slow is halved for ranged attacks like hers), and Impulse, which stacks more attack speed as you keep hitting. Every extra attack is another mark.
- Golden Staff: its Endless Strike makes the attack after every two non-Crit Basic Attacks much faster and trigger Attack Effects two extra times. Without Crit items almost all of her attacks are non-Crit, so this fires constantly, and those extra Attack Effects feed Corrosion Scythe and Demon Hunter Sword.
- Demon Hunter Sword: Basic Attacks deal a share of the target's current HP as extra Physical Damage and heal you on every hit. Together with the passive's Max HP true damage, this is how she melts tanks.
- Malefic Gun: Physical Penetration and, more importantly for Karrie, a longer Basic Attack range. It directly patches her biggest weakness.
- Immortality: a resurrection, so the first dive on you does not end your teamfight.
::build Pro build: NETS | Golden Staff, Corrosion Scythe, Demon Hunter Sword, Malefic Gun, Wind of Nature, Rose Gold Meteor | NETS (AC), MPL MY Season 18, 30 August 2026, a win. Two defensive damage items in place of boots by the end of the game.
- Wind of Nature: attack speed, Physical Attack and lifesteal, plus the short Physical Damage immunity Jade's draft describes. It is the answer to physical divers and enemy marksmen.
- Rose Gold Meteor: Lifeline gives a shield and a burst of movement speed when a hit drops you low, which buys time against magic burst.
!! The app's item data has no full description of Wind of Nature's immunity effect (how long it lasts or what triggers it). Check the in-game item screen.
Ranked and community setups from Jade's research (not pro builds): MLBBHub's curated ranked build for Patch 2.2.16a (15 August 2026) is the same core with Swift Boots instead of Warrior Boots: Swift Boots, Demon Hunter Sword, Corrosion Scythe, Golden Staff, Malefic Gun, Wind of Nature. MLBB.io's community records (three builds submitted between 14 August and 13 October 2026) add a frontline-pressure variant:
::build Community anti-frontline | Tough Boots, Corrosion Scythe, Demon Hunter Sword, Golden Staff, Malefic Roar, Rose Gold Meteor | MLBB.io community build aggregation, small sample of three builds; not a pro build.
!! This build comes from community records you found, not from a recorded pro game. No pro in the 12 recorded games bought Malefic Roar.
- Tough Boots: consider them when enemy crowd control and magic damage create problems during engagements. Their Fortitude shortens control and slow durations.
- Malefic Roar: consider it when Physical Defense becomes a significant obstacle to your regular physical damage. Its Breaker passive gives more penetration the more Physical Defense the target has.
- Rose Gold Meteor: provides additional defensive utility against threatening magic burst.
Do not blindly follow the purchase order. If your lane opponent is creating significant pressure, prioritize the item components that address your immediate problem. The pro pattern is a good guide: get Corrosion Scythe and Golden Staff first, Demon Hunter Sword third, then choose range (Malefic Gun) or survival based on who is trying to kill you.
### Emblem
::emblem Custom Fighter Emblem | Swift, Festival of Blood, Quantum Charge | Tied for the most common pro setup in MPL Season 18, used in five games (Bennyqt, Teddy, Arfy): attack speed, spell vamp on her skills, and movement speed with healing from Basic Attacks.
Why pros used a Fighter emblem on a Marksman: Karrie's damage is spread over many hits and two damaging skills, and her problem is survival, not raw damage. The Fighter emblem's lifesteal and Hybrid Defense help her stay in fights. Quantum Charge was in all 12 recorded games: hitting with a Basic Attack gives a burst of movement speed and restores HP, which is exactly what a short-range kiter needs.
!! In the other five-game group the source lists Bargain Hunter as the second talent with the Fighter emblem, but in the app's emblem data Bargain Hunter belongs to the Mage emblem. Treat that variant as unconfirmed.
::emblem Custom Marksman Emblem | Swift, Weapon Master, Quantum Charge | The ranked setup from Jade's research (MLBBHub): more attack speed and more value from item stats, with the same Quantum Charge.
- Swift: helps improve attack frequency and passive stacking.
- Weapon Master: increases the Physical Attack you gain from equipment and other sources.
- Quantum Charge: provides movement speed and healing when your Basic Attacks deal damage.
### Battle spells
::spells Flicker, Purify, Inspire | Flicker provides repositioning; Purify addresses crowd control; Inspire supports an aggressive sustained-damage approach.
!! The pro records the app uses do not include battle spells, so these are Jade's draft's recommendations, not pro data.
Flicker is the safest general-purpose option. Karrie has limited range and needs another way to escape dangerous positioning. Purify is valuable when the enemy composition relies on crowd control to prevent you from attacking: the spell removes negative effects and gives a short window of control immunity. Inspire is an offensive alternative when your team already has sufficient protection and you expect extended Basic Attack engagements, since it raises her attack speed and its cap for several attacks.
As Jade's draft says, Purify cannot remove or block suppression; the wiki's notes on the spell confirm it, and add that it cannot remove the root from Minsitthar's Royal Guards either.
## Early game
Your early game should revolve around preserving your Gold Lane economy. Karrie is not at her strongest before acquiring her important attack-speed items. You should not attempt to imitate the aggressive laning patterns of Marksmen who have stronger early burst or longer effective range. Your first responsibility is collecting minions without taking unnecessary damage.
::map lane | Gold Lane: farm the wave, keep Phantom Step for the enemy roamer or jungler, and only rotate to Turtle when your team already controls it.
### Laning priorities
- Position yourself where you can last-hit without exposing yourself to the enemy roamer.
- Use Spinning Lightwheel to discourage aggressive approaches and create favorable trading opportunities.
- Preserve Phantom Step when the enemy jungler or roamer has not revealed their position.
- Avoid extended fights when you lack the equipment to sustain meaningful damage.
- Watch the minimap before stepping forward to pressure the enemy Gold Laner.
The most common early-game mistake is confusing a successful short trade with an opportunity to force a kill. Your objective is not necessarily to dominate the lane. It is to reach your first major item without surrendering unnecessary deaths.
### Managing the first Turtle
The first Turtle contest can create a difficult decision. If your team has established control and your presence can meaningfully contribute, rotate. However, abandoning an entire wave to participate in a fight your team cannot win is usually a poor exchange. Look at the number of visible enemies, your team's positioning, and whether your own jungler can contest the objective. If the situation is unfavorable, preserve your economy and communicate your intention through pings.
## Mid game: objectives and rotations
The mid game is where Karrie's damage begins becoming more relevant. You should now think beyond your own lane. Your priority shifts toward joining coordinated objective fights and establishing a position from which you can attack the enemy frontline.
### Rotating after destroying the Gold Lane turret
Once the enemy's outer Gold Lane turret is destroyed, you have more flexibility. You can rotate toward the mid lane to help your team pressure the map, but avoid remaining in dangerous territory without vision. A good rotation should accomplish something:
- Help your team establish control over the Turtle or Lord area.
- Defend a threatened mid turret.
- Join a fight where your presence can produce a numerical advantage.
- Collect a safe wave before returning to the next objective.
Do not rotate simply because the laning phase has ended.
### Playing around Lord
Lord fights are particularly important for Karrie because both teams often gather in predictable areas. Use your range and positioning to attack whichever enemy enters your safe damage zone. Do not walk into the enemy jungle simply because your teammates are already fighting there. Your team needs your sustained damage more than it needs you to become another initiator. If the enemy frontline approaches through a narrow passage, Spinning Lightwheel can help disrupt their advance: the sphere stops on the first hero, so in a choke point it lands right on the front of their formation.
## Late game and teamfights
Late-game Karrie can become extremely dangerous when given sufficient protection. However, the same late-game environment also makes positioning mistakes much more expensive. One successful enemy initiation can eliminate you before you contribute meaningful damage.
### Front-to-back fighting
Your default teamfight strategy should be front-to-back. This means attacking the closest enemy you can safely reach rather than forcing your way toward the enemy Marksman or Mage. Your passive makes this approach particularly effective against durable frontline heroes. A tank with a large health pool can still become vulnerable when you repeatedly activate Lightwheel Mark.
Do not interpret this as permission to stand still and attack. Continue moving between Basic Attacks, watch enemy cooldowns, and maintain an escape direction.
### When to attack the backline
There are situations where reaching the backline is worthwhile. For example, if the enemy Assassin has already committed their mobility and the opposing Mage is isolated, you may have an opportunity to reposition aggressively. But you should evaluate the risk first.
- Is Phantom Step available?
- Has the enemy's primary crowd control ability been used?
- Can your roamer follow your movement?
- Will the enemy frontline immediately punish your repositioning?
If the answers suggest that you cannot safely complete the engagement, stay with your frontline.
### Ultimate management
In late-game teamfights, do not activate Speedy Lightwheel merely because several opponents appear on screen. Wait for an opportunity where you can maintain attacks. The ultimate is most valuable when you have a target, sufficient protection, and room to maneuver. With its cooldown of 35.0 seconds, a wasted Dual Wield usually means fighting the next objective without it.
## Advanced techniques
### Attack between repositioning movements
Karrie should rarely remain stationary during extended engagements. Move between attacks to make enemy skillshots more difficult to land. This requires familiarity with her attack animation and a consistent rhythm. You want to preserve attacking uptime without becoming predictable. Quantum Charge rewards this: each time it triggers from a Basic Attack, you get a short burst of movement speed to step to a new spot.
### Use Phantom Step to dodge, not simply approach
Your dash is one of your strongest survival tools. When an enemy fighter approaches, consider moving diagonally rather than directly backward. Diagonal movement can help you avoid linear skillshots while preserving access to the enemy target.
### Understand passive target selection
Your passive rewards concentrating damage. During teamfights, identify the enemy who is easiest to attack safely. If the enemy tank is standing in front of you, attacking them can be more productive than attempting to reach a distant damage dealer.
### Recognize when to stop chasing
Karrie has sufficient mobility to pursue certain opponents, especially during her ultimate. However, chasing beyond your team's vision can expose you to enemy reinforcements. If the target moves into an unprotected area, reconsider the pursuit. A surviving Karrie can continue defending objectives and clearing waves. A dead Karrie contributes nothing to either.
### Adapt your damage priorities
Your damage priorities should change according to the game state. When the enemy frontline is healthy and approaching, sustained damage is valuable. When the enemy backline is isolated, eliminating a damage dealer may be more important. When Lord is available, maintaining map control and avoiding unnecessary deaths should take precedence over chasing kills.
## Draft and team fit
Karrie benefits from teammates who can provide reliable initiation, protection, and crowd control. She does not need every teammate to protect her constantly, but she benefits enormously from a composition that creates opportunities for uninterrupted attacks.
Good team characteristics:
- A reliable frontline that can absorb enemy engagement abilities.
- A roamer who can peel for the backline.
- A Mage who can control space and prevent enemy divers from freely approaching.
- A Jungler capable of contesting objectives and creating pressure elsewhere.
Difficult team characteristics:
- Multiple fragile teammates with little frontline presence.
- A composition that depends entirely on Karrie initiating damage.
- Teammates who constantly split away from objective fights.
- No reliable response to enemy assassins.
Karrie is particularly uncomfortable when your entire team expects you to provide both the primary damage and the defensive structure of the formation. You are a Marksman, not a frontline substitute.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Argus,Minsitthar | bad=Alice,Baxia,Esmeralda,Balmond,Leomord | ally=Tigreal,Khufra,Estes
The "bad" list is the official ranked data: the heroes mobilelegends.com lists as countering Karrie (past 7 days, Mythical Glory and above). The "good" list is the official data read the other way: Argus and Minsitthar are the heroes whose own counter lists include Karrie. The allies are an assessment from Jade's draft, not statistics.
!! Jade's draft listed Alice, Baxia and Esmeralda as favorable matchups (from MLBBHub). The official ranked data lists all three as heroes that counter Karrie, so the guide treats them as difficult.
### Favorable matchups
Argus: he is a melee fighter who has to walk to you, and Spinning Lightwheel's 80% slow plus a short-cooldown dash let you keep him at arm's length. His ultimate gives him Death Immunity for 4 seconds and turns his damage into healing, and it triggers automatically when he takes fatal damage. Do not waste your burst into it: kite until it ends, then finish him. Even a rank-one Dual Wield (6 seconds) outlasts his 4-second immunity.
Minsitthar: a durable frontliner who has to reach you, which is the kind of target Lightwheel Mark punishes. The danger is his ultimate: inside King's Calling enemies cannot use movement skills, so Phantom Step will not get you out. Purify will not save you either: the wiki notes it cannot remove the root from his Royal Guards. Stay at the edge of the field and fight him only after it is used.
### Difficult matchups (official counters)
Alice: she blinks onto you with Crimson Gleam, slows you with Doom Waltz and heals from it, and her ultimate gives her Control Immunity and Damage Reduction while she charges it. Your slow does nothing during that window and your damage is cut. Back off when she starts the ultimate, then punish once it lands.
Baxia: his passive reduces the final damage he takes by a flat amount on every hit, and his ultimate multiplies that reduction. Karrie deals damage in many small hits, so a flat reduction per hit hurts her more than most marksmen. His skills also cut HP Regen and shields, and his stun lets his team reach you. Do not try to out-trade him alone; shoot whoever he is protecting.
Esmeralda: her shields soak your damage, her damage ignores shields, and she converts nearby enemies' shields into her own. Her ultimate blinks onto you and immobilizes you. Fight her only after the ultimate is used, and keep Phantom Step for that blink.
Balmond: his ultimate deals True Damage based on your lost HP, so a Karrie who has already taken a few hits is an easy kill. Soul Lock also slows and shreds Physical Defense. Respect his charge, and keep your HP high before fights.
Leomord: once mounted, he gets a burst of movement speed and his Basic Attacks hit an area and can be used while moving. He reaches you from the jungle faster than you can kite. Keep Spinning Lightwheel for his approach and fight near your team.
### Also hard, according to Jade's draft
Jade's draft cites MLBB.GG's ranked matchup information for these three. They are not in the official counter list, so treat them as an assessment.
Melissa: her ultimate creates a dome for 4 seconds that damages enemies inside and knocks back anyone who tries to enter. A short-range marksman cannot reach her through it. Avoid fighting inside her effective engagement area without considering her ultimate and available protection.
Irithel: she shoots while moving, which makes her difficult to punish through conventional positioning. Avoid extended pursuits in which she can continuously deal damage while maintaining distance.
Beatrix: she carries two of four weapons with different attack patterns and can threaten Karrie from ranges that make direct retaliation difficult. Your positioning must account for her weapon choice and available burst potential.
### Teammate synergy
Tigreal: his initiation and crowd control can create opportunities for Karrie to attack clustered opponents. His ultimate pulls enemies together and stuns them, which is free attack time for you.
Khufra: his ability to disrupt mobile enemies can help protect Karrie from aggressive divers. Enemies who try to blink across him while he is a bouncing ball get knocked airborne.
Estes: his healing can help Karrie remain active during extended engagements, although healing does not replace proper positioning.
## Situational adjustments
### Against heavy Physical Damage
Consider Wind of Nature, as most pros did in the recorded games. Its physical-damage immunity gives you a critical defensive window against physical burst. Use it in response to a real threat rather than waiting until you are nearly eliminated. Warrior Boots, the pros' usual boots, also help here.
### Against heavy Magic Damage
Consider Rose Gold Meteor or other appropriate defensive purchases. Your priority is surviving the initial burst so you can continue contributing damage.
### Against heavy Crowd Control
Consider Tough Boots and Purify when appropriate. However, identify the exact crowd control effects before committing to Purify.
### Against high Physical Defense
Consider Malefic Roar, or keep Malefic Gun, which also gives Physical Penetration. Your passive already provides percentage-based True Damage, but your regular physical damage still benefits from penetration.
### When your team is behind
Do not force fights simply because your teammates are looking for kills. Focus on safe minion collection, defensive positioning, and avoiding unnecessary deaths. A delayed item spike is recoverable. Repeated deaths that surrender objectives and map control can make the game significantly harder.
### When your team is ahead
Use your advantage to establish vision and objective control. Do not chase opponents into their jungle without information. Your objective is to convert your lead into structures, Lord control, and a decisive teamfight.
## Practice drills
::steps Lightwheel Familiarity | Enter Practice Mode; attack a stationary enemy repeatedly; watch the five-mark activation; repeat while alternating Basic Attacks and skills
The objective is to understand how quickly you can activate Lightwheel Mark under different attacking conditions. Pay attention to how your skills contribute to mark application.
::steps Defensive Dash Training | Position near an enemy target; practice diagonal and backward dashes; keep up Basic Attack pressure; repeat without using Phantom Step offensively unless necessary
You are training the habit of treating Phantom Step as a survival resource.
::steps Dual Wield Management | Activate Speedy Lightwheel; keep attacking while moving; use Phantom Step to reposition; repeat while minimizing time spent without a target
The goal is to understand how much attacking time you can extract from the ultimate at each rank.
::steps Teamfight Positioning | Enter a custom match with allied frontline protection; attack the closest enemy; reposition whenever threatened; avoid chasing the backline
Focus on maintaining damage output without becoming the first target eliminated.
::steps Gold Lane Awareness | Clear a wave; check the minimap; identify missing enemy heroes; decide whether to stay, rotate, or retreat; repeat at different objective timings
You should develop the habit of making movement decisions based on information rather than instinct alone.
## Common mistakes
- Using Phantom Step aggressively without checking enemy abilities. You surrender your primary repositioning tool and become vulnerable to follow-up attacks.
- Activating Speedy Lightwheel without an accessible target. The ultimate's offensive value depends on maintaining attacks throughout its duration.
- Chasing the enemy backline unnecessarily. Karrie's strength is sustained damage, not automatically reaching the farthest opponent.
- Ignoring Spinning Lightwheel's slow. The skill offers meaningful control, especially when you need to prevent an enemy from approaching.
- Splitting passive applications across multiple targets. Concentrating your damage is often more effective than spreading attacks without a clear purpose.
- Building exclusively for damage. Additional offensive items are useless if you cannot survive long enough to attack; every recorded pro build carried something defensive, at least Warrior Boots or Tough Boots.
- Assuming True Damage makes Physical Defense irrelevant. Your passive bypasses Physical Defense, but your other physical damage does not.
- Rotating without considering minion waves. Unnecessary rotations can delay your item timings and weaken your mid-game presence.
- Fighting without checking the minimap. Karrie's limited range makes surprise engagements particularly dangerous.
- Standing still during teamfights. Even when your target is within range, remaining stationary makes you easier to hit.
- Using the ultimate as an emergency escape without considering alternatives. Its movement-speed bonus can help you reposition, but you should understand when preserving it for damage is more valuable.
- Forcing objectives without team support. Karrie can contribute meaningful objective damage, but she should not become an isolated target while attempting to secure Lord or Turtle.
The strongest Karrie players understand that damage is only half of the equation. Your real advantage comes from knowing when to attack, which opponent to prioritize, and how to remain alive long enough for your passive to repeatedly punish the enemy's durability. Your objective is not to deal the most damage in the shortest possible moment. It is to maintain enough safe attacking uptime that the enemy frontline eventually collapses.
Sources: guide written by Jade, formatted and fact-checked for the app. Skill text from the MLBB Wiki (checked 11 November 2026). Pro builds from MLBBHub's MPL Season 18 match pages. Ranked numbers and counters from mobilelegends.com/rank. Ranked and community builds as cited in Jade's research: MLBBHub (Patch 2.2.16a), MLBB.io, MLBB.GG and MLBB Draft.

guides.title: Baxia
guides.sub: Rolling into the fight, cutting every heal and shield, and walking out through the lava
guides.body:
## Hero Overview
Role: Tank Primary positions: Jungle, Roam Specialty: Support / Damage
Baxia is an engage tank whose real value is not his stun. It is what his passive does to the enemy team. Every skill he lands lowers an enemy hero's Shield and HP Regen by 40% for 4 seconds, and he keeps a flat reduction on all the damage he takes. Against a draft built on healing or shields, Baxia brings healing reduction on every skill without spending an item slot on it.
His engage is a rolling shield that stuns the first enemy it hits, with a recast that launches him over walls and minions to slam a hero for a longer stun. His thrown shield is his damage and his slow, and it refunds most of its own cooldown when it lands. His ultimate is a 10-second sprint with a lava trail that slows anyone who stands in it, while his damage reduction more than doubles.
Why he's picked: to make sustain heroes and shield items worth much less, to start fights from unexpected angles, and to give a team a frontline that can walk through the enemy for 10 seconds.
What he's weak to: heroes whose damage keeps growing past a flat reduction, and fights that last longer than his ultimate. His roll also stops on the first enemy unit it touches, so a minion or a jungle creep can take a stun meant for a hero.
Where he stands right now: in the official rankings for the past 30 days at Mythical Glory and above, Baxia has a 0.06% pick rate, a 47.16% win rate and a 0.08% ban rate. He is a rare pick, so the win rate comes from a small sample.
If you remember one idea from this guide, make it this: Baxia's job is to keep skills landing. A Baxia who rolls in and then stops casting lets the enemy heal back four seconds later.
## Kit deep-dive
### Passive: Baxia Mark
Baxia reduces the final damage he takes by a flat amount: 15, plus 1 per hero level, so 30 at level 15. His skills also reduce the Shield and HP Regen of enemy heroes they hit by 40% for 4 seconds.
Flat reduction is strongest against many small hits (minions, jungle creeps, fast basic attacks, damage over time) and weakest against a single large hit.
The second half is why he gets drafted. It covers heals that work through HP regeneration and shields from items, emblems or allies.
Practical application:
- Count your skill hits. Each one refreshes the 4-second reduction.
- Aim at the hero whose healing or shield matters most, not the closest one.
- Do not buy a separate healing-reduction item by reflex. Your skills already apply 40%.
### Skill 1: Baxia-Shield Unity
Baxia retracts into his shield and accelerates forward for up to 9 seconds. When he hits an enemy unit, he deals 300 to 400 Magic Damage (plus 60% of his total Magic Power) to it and nearby enemies, stuns the target for 0.8 seconds and slightly knocks back other nearby enemies.
While rolling, a recast launches him upward so he can cross obstacles and enemy minions. If an enemy hero is under him when he leaps, he strikes them down for 375 to 500 Magic Damage (plus 75% of his Magic Power), stunning them for 1.5 seconds and knocking back nearby enemies. The cooldown is 15 seconds at level 1 and 12 at max.
The detail that decides most rolls: the rolling hit stops on the first enemy unit, minion or creep included.
Practical application:
- Approach from the side of the lane without minions, or leap the wave.
- Use the 9 seconds to steer. The roll does not have to go in a straight line at the target.
- Recast about one step before the target, so you land on them for the 1.5-second stun instead of in front of them.
- Keep the leap in mind as an escape: roll away and leap a wall.
### Skill 2: Shield of Spirit
Baxia throws his shield forward. It deals 120 to 220 Magic Damage plus 100% of his Magic Power plus 5% of the target's total HP to enemies on its path, marks them for 5 seconds and slows them by 50% for 1 second. It stops on the first enemy hero or creep it hits. When it hits an enemy hero or creep, its cooldown is reduced to 15% of normal. The cooldown is 10 seconds at level 1 and 7 at max.
!! The MLBB Wiki text says the shield "marks" enemies for 5 seconds but does not say what the mark does. This guide does not assume an effect.
Practical application:
- A hit means you can throw again almost at once. Two hits in a row double the slow and the percent-HP damage.
- It is your poke in lane and your fastest way to clear camps, since creeps also trigger the refund.
- It is also your peel: a 50% slow stops a diver's approach.
### Ultimate: Tortoise's Puissance
Baxia holds his shield in front and sprints for 10 seconds with 30% extra Movement Speed, leaving a lava path. Enemies on the path take 40 to 50 Magic Damage (plus 30% of his Magic Power) and are slowed by 15% for 0.5 seconds, every 0.5 seconds. For the duration, the damage reduction from Baxia Mark rises to 200%, 230% or 260% of its normal value as the ultimate levels. The cooldown is 40 seconds at level 1 and 35 at max.
!! The skill text gives the boosted reduction as "200/230/260% (85)". What the 85 means is not explained in the source, so this guide only says the reduction is roughly doubled or more.
Practical application:
- It has no stun. It is a sustain and chase tool, not an engage by itself.
- Cast it just before you roll in, so the boosted reduction covers the moment the enemy turns on you.
- Walk back and forth through the enemy team while it lasts: the lava slows them every half second.
::curve 3,4,3 | Early: the roll's stun makes every gank a threat. Mid: grouped enemies at objectives and heavy healing are where his passive matters most (his peak). Late: still a reliable engage, but his flat reduction counts for less as enemy damage grows.
## How the kit fits together
### The anti-heal cycle
Baxia's kit has one goal: stay on the target long enough for the 40% reduction to matter. The roll lands the first application. A shield throw at the stunned target refunds most of its cooldown, so a second throw follows. The lava trail adds a hit every half second while the ultimate lasts. A Baxia who keeps landing something every few seconds keeps the enemy's healing cut for the whole fight.
### Roll and leap
The roll and the leap are one skill with two uses. The roll is the approach and the short stun. The leap crosses walls and minions and turns the stun into 1.5 seconds. The best Baxia players use the leap on almost every engage, because it solves the minion problem and gives the longer stun.
### When to sprint
The ultimate does not start fights. It makes Baxia hard to kill while he is in the middle of one, and it makes him fast enough to catch a hero who runs. Cast it a moment before the engage, or the moment your team commits, never as the opener on its own.
## Combos
::combo Standard Engage | ULT > [Baxia-Shield Unity] > [Baxia-Shield Unity] > [Shield of Spirit] > [Shield of Spirit] | Sprint in with the boosted reduction, roll, leap onto the target for the long stun, then throw the shield twice while they are held.
Sequence: Tortoise's Puissance → Baxia-Shield Unity (roll) → recast (leap) → Shield of Spirit → Shield of Spirit
The ultimate's boosted reduction is already active when the enemy focuses you. The leap's 1.5-second stun gives time for both throws, and the first hit refunds most of the shield's cooldown.
::combo Quick Pick | [Baxia-Shield Unity] > [Shield of Spirit] > [Shield of Spirit] | Roll into a lone target for the short stun, then two throws for the slow and percent-HP damage.
Sequence: Baxia-Shield Unity → Shield of Spirit → Shield of Spirit
The roll's stun holds the target for the first throw, which slows them by 50% and refunds itself, so the second throw follows while they are still slowed.
::combo Wall Leap | [Baxia-Shield Unity] > [Baxia-Shield Unity] > [Shield of Spirit] | Roll toward a jungle wall and leap it onto a hero on the other side.
Sequence: Roll toward the wall → leap over it onto the target → Shield of Spirit
The target sees no direct path, so they do not expect the stun, and landing on them gives 1.5 seconds instead of 0.8.
::combo Peel | [Shield of Spirit] > [Baxia-Shield Unity] | Slow a diver with the shield, then roll into them to stun them off your carry.
Sequence: Shield of Spirit → Baxia-Shield Unity
The 50% slow stops the diver's approach, and with no minions in the way the roll reaches them before they reach your carry.
## Builds and emblems
Baxia's build should reflect his job: stay alive in the middle of the enemy team while his skills keep landing.
What the pros did: the app has four recorded Baxia games from MPL Season 18. Three were played by Lunnn (iG) as a jungler in MPL MY, two of them wins, and one by Tracyyy (Twisted Minds PH) as a roamer in MPL PH, a loss. Chastise Pauldron and Cursed Helmet were each in three final inventories; Guardian Helmet and Immortality in two.
::build Pro build: Lunnn | Guardian Helmet, Chastise Pauldron, Cursed Helmet, Radiant Armor, Immortality | Lunnn (iG), MPL MY Season 18, 11 September 2026, a win from the Jungle (4/2/8). Final inventory as recorded by MLBBHub.
::build Pro build: Lunnn (game 2) | Guardian Helmet, Chastise Pauldron, Cursed Helmet, Dominance Ice, Immortality | Lunnn (iG), MPL MY Season 18, 11 September 2026, a win from the Jungle (4/5/10). Dominance Ice in place of Radiant Armor.
!! Pro item lists are the final inventory at the end of the game, shown in slot order, not the order the items were bought. The pro records also list no boots for Baxia.
- Cursed Helmet: deals 1.2% of his total HP as Magic Damage per second to nearby enemies, which adds up while he sits in the enemy team.
- Chastise Pauldron: slows the Attack Speed of enemies who hit him, which helps against marksmen and fighters.
- Dominance Ice: reduces the Shield and HP Regen of enemies within 5 units to 60% of normal, a second source of anti-heal for games with very heavy healing.
!! Whether Baxia Mark's reduction stacks with item-based reduction such as Dominance Ice is not stated in the app's data.
### Build 1 — Jungle Tank
::build Jungle Tank | Guardian Helmet, Chastise Pauldron, Cursed Helmet, Radiant Armor, Immortality | Lunnn's winning build, as the template for a jungle Baxia.
Why it works as a template: Guardian Helmet and Immortality keep him alive long enough to cast every skill, Cursed Helmet adds area damage, and Chastise Pauldron and Radiant Armor cover both damage types.
### Build 2 — Physical-heavy enemy
::build Physical-heavy Enemy | Tough Boots, Dreadnaught Armor, Chastise Pauldron, Antique Cuirass, Dominance Ice, Immortality | Our adjustment for drafts with several physical damage dealers.
Dreadnaught Armor, Antique Cuirass and Dominance Ice each appeared in one pro inventory. Tough Boots is our addition, since the pro records list no boots.
### Emblem
::emblem Custom Tank Emblem | Thrill, Seasoned Hunter, Concussive Blast | Lunnn's setup in all three of his games. Seasoned Hunter helps on Turtle and Lord.
::emblem Custom Tank Emblem | Firmness, Tenacity, Concussive Blast | Tracyyy's roam setup. Firmness gives 8 extra Physical and Magic Defense, and Tenacity adds 5% Damage Reduction below 50% HP.
Firmness is listed under the Fighter emblem, but any talent can go with any set; the pros mix talents from different sets all the time.
### Battle spells
::spells Retribution, Flicker | Retribution when you jungle. Flicker when you roam, to reposition before a roll.
!! The pro records the app uses do not include battle spells, so these are our recommendations, not pro data.
## Early game
::map roam | Jungle or Roam: gank side lanes through the jungle walls, where the leap lets the roll arrive from an angle the enemy does not watch.
Level 2 gives you the roll and the shield, which is enough for a gank if a laner can follow. Approach from the side without minions, or leap the wave onto the hero.
As a roamer, stay with your gold laner and poke with the shield. Every hit on a hero refunds most of its cooldown, so a well-aimed throw is free damage and a 50% slow.
As a jungler, the shield clears camps quickly because hitting a creep also refunds it, and the percent-HP damage helps against large monsters.
During the early game, focus on:
- Landing the leap on ganks, not just the roll.
- Poking with the shield whenever it can hit a hero.
- Being at the first Turtle, where grouped enemies are easy roll targets.
## Mid game: objectives and rotations
::map turtle | Hold the Turtle and Lord approaches: roll from the fog into enemies grouping at the pit, and sprint through the pit to slow them while your team hits.
The mid game is where Baxia's passive matters most. Enemies group, healers and shield items come online, and every skill you land cuts their sustain.
Play for picks between objectives: roll from fog onto a hero walking alone, especially a healer or a hero with a shield item. A pick before an objective means the fight never starts on equal numbers.
## Late game and teamfights
In late fights, cast the ultimate just before the engage, roll in on a backline hero if the path is clear or leap over the frontline to reach them, then keep the shield on whoever is being healed.
After the engage, walk through the enemy team for the rest of the 10 seconds. The lava slows them by 15% every half second, which makes it hard for them to chase your damage dealers or to walk out of your mage's area skills.
When the ultimate ends, leave or switch to peel. Your normal reduction is a flat number that large late-game damage ignores.
If your team is behind, stay next to your carry, shield the diver for the 50% slow, and roll into them for the stun.
## Advanced techniques
### 1. Leap the Wave
The most common way a Baxia engage fails is a roll that stuns a minion. Go around the wave, or leap it. The leap clears minions and lands on the hero behind them.
### 2. Use the Walls
The leap crosses walls. A roll that starts in your jungle can land on a hero on the other side of a wall who thinks they are out of reach.
### 3. Keep the Shield Refund Going
A shield hit on a hero or creep reduces its cooldown to 15% of normal. In a fight, throw it again immediately after a hit. Two hits double the slow, the percent-HP damage and keep the anti-heal on the target.
### 4. Chase With the Sprint
30% extra Movement Speed for 10 seconds plus the lava slow helps Baxia catch a fleeing hero, especially once the roll is ready again.
### 5. Pick the Anti-heal Target
The 40% reduction only applies to heroes your skills hit. Throw the shield at the hero being healed or the hero with a shield item, not the nearest tank.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Bane,Lolita,Beatrix,Atlas | bad=Lukas,Obsidia,Alice,Natan,Argus | ally=Zhuxin,Yve,Pharsa
### Favorable Conditions
Baxia appears on the counter lists of Bane, Lolita, Beatrix and Atlas in the official rankings (Mythical Glory and above, past 30 days). He is at his best when the enemy relies on HP regeneration or shields, groups up for objectives, and lacks damage that grows past a flat reduction.
### Difficult Conditions
The official counter list for Baxia in the same data is Lukas, Obsidia, Alice, Natan and Argus. The app's data lists Lukas and Alice with Regen as a specialty, so keep your skills landing on them to hold the 40% reduction. Obsidia and Natan are marksmen and Argus a fighter, damage dealers whose damage grows past his flat reduction as the game goes on, so do not stay in the fight after your ultimate ends.
### Understanding Matchups
The ally list is our reading: Zhuxin, Yve and Pharsa are mages whose area skills benefit from enemies held by his stuns and slowed by the lava.
!! The ally list is not from a data source.
## Common mistakes
### 1. Rolling Through the Wave
The roll stops on the first enemy unit, so the hero behind the minions is never stunned. Leap the wave or go around it.
### 2. Using the Ultimate as an Engage
It has no stun. Cast it so its boosted reduction covers the moment the enemy focuses you.
### 3. Forgetting the Anti-heal
The passive only applies when skills hit. A Baxia who rolls in and then stands there lets the enemy heal back after 4 seconds.
### 4. Staying After the Sprint
The boosted reduction lasts 10 seconds. When it ends, leave or peel.
### 5. Shielding the Tank
A throw at the enemy tank when a healer is in reach wastes the anti-heal on the hero who needs it least.
## Practice drills
::steps Roll to anti-heal | Roll toward the target from the side without minions; recast one step before them to land the 1.5-second stun; throw the shield at the stunned target; throw again as soon as the refund lands; cast the ultimate before the enemy turns on you
### 1. Leap Timing
In practice mode, roll at a dummy behind a minion wave and recast so you land on the dummy, not the minions. Repeat until the long stun lands every time.
### 2. Shield Refunds
In the jungle, throw the shield at a camp and throw again the moment the cooldown drops. Learn how quickly the second throw is ready after a hit.
### 3. Wall Angles
Find the jungle walls next to each lane and practise rolling from your side and leaping over onto a target point on the other side.
### 4. Fight Review
After each game, ask:
- Did my rolls stun the hero I aimed at, or a minion?
- Did I keep landing skills on the hero being healed?
- Did I cast the ultimate before or after the enemy focused me?
## Accuracy and patch notes

guides.title: Luo Yi
guides.sub: Pairing Yin and Yang to stun whole groups, and moving the team across the map in three seconds
guides.body:
## Hero Overview
Role: Mage Primary positions: Mid Lane Specialty: Support / Crowd Control
Luo Yi is a mage whose damage and control both come from one mechanic. Her skills leave Sigils of Yin or Yang on enemy heroes and on the ground. When two sigils of opposite attributes are close together, they trigger a Yin-Yang Reaction: heavy Magic Damage to the marked heroes, a 1-second stun, and a pull that drags them toward each other. A Luo Yi who lands her sigils on a grouped enemy team stuns several heroes at once and pulls them into a tighter group for her next skill.
Her ultimate is a map tool rather than a damage skill. Diversion opens a Teleport Circle and sends every allied hero standing in it to a point up to 20 units away after 3 seconds. A mid-lane mage becomes a way for the whole team to arrive at a Turtle, a Lord or a side-lane fight before the enemy can react.
Why she's picked: group stuns from range, steady poke, and a teleport that creates fights the enemy does not have numbers for.
What she's weak to: heroes who reach her quickly. She has no dash, and her only defense is the shield from her passive, which she earns by landing new sigils. Her damage also depends on landing skillshots in the right colour order.
Where she stands right now: in the official rankings for the past 30 days at Mythical Glory and above, Luo Yi has a 0.15% pick rate, a 47.18% win rate and a 0.03% ban rate. At every lower rank in the same data her pick rate is around 0.17%, with win rates between 47.9% and 48.7%.
If you remember one idea from this guide, make it this: a single sigil does almost nothing. Luo Yi plays in pairs.
## Kit deep-dive
### Passive: Duality
Her skills create Sigils of Yin and Yang that last up to 6 seconds. When sigils of opposite attributes are within a certain distance, they trigger a Yin-Yang Reaction, dealing 365 (plus 20 per hero level, plus 190% of her total Magic Power) Magic Damage to the marked enemy heroes, stunning them for 1 second and pulling them toward each other.
Each time she applies a new sigil to a marked enemy hero, she gains a shield of 300 (plus 10 per hero level, plus 150% of her Magic Power), stacking up to 3 times, and 30% extra Movement Speed that decays over 2 seconds.
!! The MLBB Wiki text does not give the distance at which opposite sigils react. This guide only says "close together".
Practical application:
- Build pairs: two enemies close together with opposite colours, or one enemy and a ground sigil of the opposite colour.
- The shield and speed come from landing new sigils, so her defense comes from aggression.
- The pull drags the two marked heroes toward each other. Use it to drag a carry toward your team.
### Skill 1: Dispersion
She sends Yin or Yang energy in a direction, dealing 210 to 410 Magic Damage (plus 120% of her Magic Power) to the first enemy hit and those behind it in a cone, and marking enemy heroes hit with a sigil. She stores up to 4 charges, gains a charge every 8 seconds, and gains an extra charge every time a Yin-Yang Reaction triggers. The attribute changes on each cast. The cooldown between casts is 1.2 seconds.
Practical application:
- The cone reaches heroes behind the first target, including behind minions.
- Each reaction refunds a charge. A Luo Yi who keeps triggering reactions never runs out.
- Four casts without a reaction empty her charges, and each new one takes 8 seconds.
### Skill 2: Rotation
She summons Fire of Yang or Aqua of Yin at a target location, dealing 250 to 350 Magic Damage (plus 50% of her Magic Power) and slowing enemies hit by 60% for 0.5 seconds. The fire or water stays for 6 seconds, dealing 50 to 70 Magic Damage (plus 10% of her Magic Power) every 0.7 seconds, and it can trigger a Yin-Yang Reaction with a mark of the opposite attribute. Its attribute also changes on each cast. The cooldown is 12 seconds.
!! The source does not say whether Dispersion and Rotation share one Yin or Yang state or each keep their own. Watch the colour of each skill's icon in game before you rely on a reaction.
Practical application:
- A field of the opposite colour turns a single marked enemy into a reaction.
- Place it where an enemy has to walk. It lasts 6 seconds.
- The 60% slow on impact is her only self-peel besides Flicker.
### Ultimate: Diversion
She creates a Teleport Circle around herself and marks a destination within 20 units. After a 3-second delay, allied heroes in the circle, herself included, are teleported there. It also has a passive: her Cooldown Reduction rises by 6% to 10% as the ultimate levels. The cooldown is 55 seconds at level 1 and 45 at max.
!! Whether enemies can interrupt the teleport by stunning Luo Yi during the delay is not stated in the app's data.
Practical application:
- Call it before you cast it. Your team must stand in the circle for 3 seconds.
- Pick a destination in the fog near the fight, so the enemy has no time to leave.
- It also saves your team: a teleport back to your tower moves several heroes out of a lost fight.
::curve 3,4,4 | Early: strong poke through the wave. Mid: reactions on grouped enemies at objectives and the teleport for map plays (her peak). Late: the teleport and group stuns keep their value to the end.
## How the kit fits together
### Thinking in pairs
There are two ways to build a reaction. Mark two enemy heroes standing close with opposite Dispersion casts, or mark one enemy and place Rotation's field of the opposite colour next to them. Both work; the first is stronger in teamfights, the second works on a single target.
### The charge economy
Each reaction refunds a Dispersion charge, so in a good fight her casts chain: reaction, refund, mark, reaction. Charges thrown without a pair are gone for 8 seconds each. Spend them where a reaction is likely.
### The teleport is separate
The ultimate has nothing to do with the sigils. It is a map decision, made by watching where your team and the enemy are, and its passive Cooldown Reduction helps her cast Rotation more often.
## Combos
::combo Two-target Reaction | [Dispersion] > [Dispersion] > [Rotation] | Mark one enemy with one colour, the enemy next to them with the other, then drop Rotation on the pulled-together pair.
Sequence: Dispersion → Dispersion (opposite colour) → Rotation
The two casts change colour each time, so two enemies standing close react, which stuns both, pulls them together and refunds a charge. Rotation then lands on a tight pair and slows them by 60%.
::combo Single-target Reaction | [Dispersion] > [Rotation] | Mark a lone enemy, then place a field of the opposite colour on them.
Sequence: Dispersion → Rotation (opposite colour)
The field can react with a mark of the opposite colour, so one enemy can still be stunned. The refunded charge lets you mark them again for a shield stack.
::combo Poke Cycle | [Dispersion] > [Dispersion] > [Dispersion] | Throw Dispersion through the wave at enemies behind it, alternating colours.
Sequence: Dispersion → Dispersion → Dispersion
The cone hits those behind the first target, so it reaches heroes behind minions. Each new sigil on a marked hero adds a shield stack and a burst of Movement Speed.
::combo Teleport Engage | ULT > [Rotation] > [Dispersion] > [Dispersion] | Teleport the team onto a grouped enemy, then open with Rotation and two Dispersions.
Sequence: Diversion → Rotation → Dispersion → Dispersion
The arrival point can be beside or behind the enemy. Rotation's slow holds them, and two opposite Dispersions on grouped heroes trigger reactions while your team hits them.
## Builds and emblems
Luo Yi's build should support constant casting: cooldown reduction, mana, and enough protection for a mage without a dash.
What the pros did: the app has five recorded Luo Yi games from MPL Season 18, two of them wins: three by SuperFrince (ONIC PH) in MPL PH, one by Stormie (SRG) in MPL MY and one by Hijumee (AE) in MPL ID. Glowing Wand was in all five final inventories; Divine Glaive, Enchanted Talisman, Magic Shoes and Mystery Codex in three; Blood Wings in two.
::build Pro build: Stormie | Divine Glaive, Magic Shoes, Enchanted Talisman, Glowing Wand, Wishing Lantern | Stormie (SRG), MPL MY Season 18, 8 October 2026, a win from the Mid Lane (4/0/9). Final inventory as recorded by MLBBHub.
::build Pro build: SuperFrince | Magic Shoes, Glowing Wand, Enchanted Talisman, Blood Wings, Mystery Codex | SuperFrince (ONIC PH), MPL PH Season 18, 30 August 2026, a win (0/1/3) with 7,710 gold. Mystery Codex is a component still in the inventory when the game ended.
!! Pro item lists are the final inventory at the end of the game, shown in slot order, not the order the items were bought.
- Glowing Wand: its burn deals 1% of the target's max HP per second and reduces Shield and HP Regen, which suits a mage who keeps hitting the same heroes with Dispersion. Pros bought it in every game.
- Enchanted Talisman: 15% Cooldown Reduction, and it restores 15% of max Mana every 10 seconds.
- Divine Glaive: Magic Penetration against heroes with high Magic Defense.
- Blood Wings: a shield of 800 plus 100% of her Magic Power, the extra protection a hero without a dash needs.
### Build 1 — Mid Lane Control
::build Mid Lane Control | Magic Shoes, Glowing Wand, Enchanted Talisman, Divine Glaive, Blood Wings, Wishing Lantern | Our template from the items pros bought most often.
Why it works as a template: Glowing Wand and Enchanted Talisman were the most common pro items, Divine Glaive adds penetration, Blood Wings covers her lack of a dash, and Wishing Lantern finished Stormie's winning build.
### Emblem
::emblem Custom Mage Emblem | Inspire, Tenacity, Brave Smite | SuperFrince's setup in three of the five pro games. Inspire gives 5% Cooldown Reduction and 2 Mana Regen. Brave Smite recovers 5% of max HP when her skill damage hits an enemy hero, every 6 seconds.
::emblem Custom Mage Emblem | Inspire, Wilderness Blessing, Brave Smite | Stormie's setup, in a win. Wilderness Blessing gives 10% Movement Speed in the jungle and river, halved in combat.
Hijumee ran Pull Yourself Together as the second talent instead, which cuts battle spell and item active cooldowns by 12%, plus 1% per kill or assist up to 8 stacks. Brave Smite is listed under the Fighter emblem and Tenacity under the Tank emblem, but any talent can go with any set.
### Battle spells
::spells Flicker | Flicker, because she has no dash of her own.
!! The pro records the app uses do not include battle spells, so this is our recommendation, not pro data.
## Early game
::map mid | Mid Lane: hold behind the wave and throw Dispersion through it at the enemy mage, alternating colours.
Dispersion's cone reaches the enemy mage while they clear the wave. Alternate colours to keep refreshing your shield, and do not spend all four charges at once unless a reaction is likely.
Use Rotation to clear and to set up reactions. A field placed where the enemy mage stands to clear will react with a Dispersion mark of the opposite colour, which is a kill window when your jungler is near.
During the early game, focus on:
- Poking with charges you can afford to spend.
- Keeping one charge for defense.
- Watching the side lanes once you have the ultimate.
## Mid game: objectives and rotations
::map turtle | Turtle and Lord: poke the enemy as they gather, then look for two grouped heroes to react; teleport your team in from the fog when the enemy commits.
The teleport is your main mid-game decision. Use it to join a side-lane fight (two heroes arriving turns a 2v2 into a 4v2), to take an objective while the enemy is on the other side of the map, or to save your team when it is caught.
The destination is up to 20 units away. Pick a spot the enemy cannot easily see, behind a wall near the fight.
## Late game and teamfights
Stand behind your frontline. Start the fight with Dispersion at the enemy frontline, then at the hero next to them in the other colour. The reaction stuns both and pulls them together for your team's area damage and for Rotation.
After the first reaction, look for the next pair. Keep moving between casts: each new sigil gives Movement Speed and a shield.
If a diver reaches you, slow them with Rotation and Flicker away. Do not stand still trying to finish a reaction while a diver hits you.
## Advanced techniques
### 1. Track the Colour
Both skills change attribute on each cast. Count your casts, or watch the skill icons, so you know which colour comes next before you aim.
### 2. Use the Pull
A reaction pulls the two marked heroes toward each other. Mark the enemy carry and a hero standing between them and your team, and the pull drags the carry toward you.
### 3. Pre-place Rotation
The field lasts 6 seconds. Place it on a path an enemy has to take, then mark them with the opposite colour when they walk in.
### 4. Keep a Charge for Defense
One Dispersion on a diver who already carries a sigil gives a shield stack and Movement Speed, which can be enough to escape.
### 5. Teleport From the Fog
A circle the enemy cannot see gives them no warning. Cast it behind a wall, out of their vision.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Novaria | bad=Baxia,Estes,Faramis,Phoveus,Popol and Kupa | ally=Atlas,Tigreal,Khufra
### Favorable Conditions
Luo Yi appears on Novaria's counter list in the official rankings (Mythical Glory and above, past 30 days). She is at her best against teams that group up and lack heroes who can reach her quickly.
### Difficult Conditions
The official counter list for Luo Yi is Baxia, Estes, Faramis, Phoveus and Popol and Kupa. Baxia's skills reduce Shield and HP Regen by 40% for 4 seconds, which weakens her passive shield. Phoveus is a fighter with Regen as a specialty, and his ultimate leaps onto enemy heroes carrying his Sinner's Mark. Estes and Faramis are supports with Regen and Guard specialties in the app's data, so they keep their team alive through her poke.
### Understanding Matchups
The ally list is our reading: Atlas, Tigreal and Khufra are tanks with Crowd Control specialties who group enemies, which makes her two-target reactions easier.
!! The ally list is not from a data source.
## Common mistakes
### 1. Throwing Charges Without a Pair
A single sigil does little. Wait for two enemies to stand close, or pair a mark with Rotation.
### 2. Losing Track of the Colour
Two sigils of the same colour do nothing. Count your casts.
### 3. Teleporting Without a Call
Your team must stand in the circle for 3 seconds. Tell them first.
### 4. Standing Too Close
She has no dash. Her shield helps, but not against a diver who reaches her.
### 5. Ignoring the Map
The ultimate moves your whole team up to 20 units. Using it only in your own lane wastes it.
## Practice drills
::steps Pair to reaction | Find two enemies standing close; mark the first with Dispersion; mark the second with the opposite colour; drop Rotation on the pulled-together pair; spend the refunded charge on a new sigil for the shield
### 1. Colour Counting
In practice mode, cast Dispersion and Rotation in different orders and say the next colour before each cast until you never miss.
### 2. Rotation Pairing
Mark a dummy, then place a field of the opposite colour on it. Learn how close the field has to be for the reaction.
### 3. Teleport Calls
In a custom game with friends, practise calling the teleport, waiting for everyone in the circle, and landing in fog near a target.
### 4. Fight Review
After each game, ask:
- How many of my Dispersion casts became reactions?
- Did I use the teleport for the map, or only in my lane?
- Did I keep a charge for defense?
## Accuracy and patch notes
This guide uses the skill text in the app's data (MLBB Wiki, fetched November 2026), the official hero rankings for the past 30 days (updated 9 November 2026), and MLBBHub's MPL Season 18 match records. Skill values can change with balance patches; check the in-game descriptions after a patch.
Research references
- MLBB Wiki — Luo Yi skills: https://mobile-legends.fandom.com/wiki/Luo_Yi
- Official MLBB hero rankings: https://www.mobilelegends.com/rank
- MLBBHub — SRG vs FL, MPL MY Season 18 (Stormie): https://www.mlbbhub.com/mpl/my/match/W7D1SRGvsFL
- MLBBHub — ONIC vs OMG, MPL PH Season 18 (SuperFrince): https://www.mlbbhub.com/mpl/ph/match/onic-omg-20260830
- MLBBHub — FLCN vs ONIC, MPL PH Season 18 (SuperFrince): https://www.mlbbhub.com/mpl/ph/match/flcn-onic-20260926

guides.title: Wanwan
guides.sub: Breaking every weakness with constant dashes, then finishing from the air where nothing can touch her
guides.body:
## Hero Overview
Role: Marksman Primary positions: Gold Lane Specialty: Finisher / Burst
Wanwan is a marksman built around one passive. Tiger Pace exposes the weaknesses of enemy heroes she hits and reveals their position for 5 seconds. Hitting a weakness deals extra True Damage and makes the target take 10% more damage from her later attacks. Once every weakness on a hero has been hit, her ultimate can be cast on them: she leaps into the air, becomes untargetable and invincible, and fires a stream of arrows.
The same passive gives her movement. After each arrow from her basic attack, she can dash a short distance, and the dash speed scales with her Attack Speed. A Wanwan with Attack Speed items moves constantly while she attacks.
Her second skill removes all control effects on her, so she does not depend on a battle spell or an item to escape crowd control.
Why she's picked: a marksman who can enter a fight that would lock most marksmen down, and an ultimate that finishes several heroes in a row while nothing can hit her.
What she's weak to: her ultimate does nothing until every weakness on the target is hit, so early in a fight she relies on basic attacks and Swallow's Path. The dash after each arrow is short, so it repositions her rather than getting her out of a bad fight.
Where she stands right now: in the official rankings for the past 30 days at Mythical Glory and above, Wanwan has a 0.16% pick rate, a 46.95% win rate and a 0.06% ban rate. At Legend and Mythic in the same data her win rate is higher, 48.8% and 48.56%.
If you remember one idea from this guide, make it this: Wanwan's ultimate is earned. Hit everything early in the fight so it is ready when it matters.
## Kit deep-dive
### Passive: Tiger Pace
Enemy heroes hit by her attacks have their weaknesses exposed and their position revealed for 5 seconds. Hitting a weakness deals 67 (plus 3 per hero level) extra True Damage and increases the damage they take from her later attacks by 10% for 5 seconds. After each arrow from her basic attack, she can dash a short distance; the dash speed scales with her Attack Speed.
!! The MLBB Wiki text says "weaknesses" without saying how many each hero has or how exactly one is hit. This guide relies only on the text: attacks hit weaknesses, and both skills trigger Tiger Pace.
Practical application:
- Attack to move. A Wanwan who stops attacking also stops dashing.
- The 5-second reveal lets you see a hero who runs into a bush after being hit.
- Attack Speed makes the dashes faster, so it comes first in her build.
### Skill 1: Swallow's Path
She throws a Fire Swallow that triggers Tiger Pace and deals 120 Physical Damage (plus 40% of her total Physical Attack) to enemies in its path. It then becomes 3 rotating Swallow Daggers that fly back to her one after another after a short delay, each dealing 60 Physical Damage (plus 65% of her Physical Attack) and slowing by 30% for 1.5 seconds. An enemy hit by the daggers twice is immobilized for 0.5 seconds. The cooldown is 10 seconds at level 1 and 8 at max.
Practical application:
- It helps break weaknesses alongside basic attacks.
- The daggers fly back to you, so walking so that they pass through the target again makes the second hit, and the immobilize, more likely.
- It is her lane poke and wave clear.
### Skill 2: Needles in Flowers
She removes all control effects on herself, triggers Tiger Pace, and shoots needles in all directions for 150 Physical Damage (plus 60% of her Physical Attack). The cooldown is 24 seconds at level 1 and 20 at max.
Practical application:
- It is her only cleanse. Keep it for the crowd control that would kill you.
- It also triggers Tiger Pace, so after a cleanse it helps finish breaking weaknesses.
### Ultimate: Crossbow of Tang
She leaps into the air and fires arrows at the target enemy hero for 2.5 seconds, 60 Physical Damage (plus 35% of her Physical Attack) per arrow. If the target dies, she switches to another enemy hero in range, gains 30% Attack Speed and extends the skill by 1 second, up to 3 times. She is untargetable and invincible for the duration, gains 100% Movement Speed, and triggers Tiger Pace on a kill and at the end. It can only be cast on an enemy hero whose weaknesses have all been hit. The damage is regarded as basic attack damage, and the firing rate scales with her Attack Speed. The cooldown is 50 seconds at level 1 and 42 at max.
!! Whether item effects that trigger on basic attacks (such as Corrosion Scythe's extra damage or crits) apply to every ultimate arrow is not stated in the app's data.
Practical application:
- Start it on a low target next to other enemies, so the first kill comes fast and the chain begins.
- It is also a dodge: invincible for its duration, so skills cast at her miss.
- No eligible target means no ultimate, for damage or for escape.
::curve 2,4,5 | Early: modest while she lacks Attack Speed. Mid: strong once her first two attack items are done. Late: the ultimate can chain through a team (her peak).
## How the kit fits together
### Everything feeds Tiger Pace
Basic attacks hit weaknesses. Swallow's Path and Needles in Flowers trigger Tiger Pace. Once every weakness on a hero is hit, the ultimate unlocks on that hero. Every action in a fight should move a target closer to eligible.
### Attack Speed links damage and movement
Faster attacks mean faster dashes, faster weakness breaks, and more arrows in the ultimate's 2.5 seconds. That is why every pro build in the app's data starts with Attack Speed items.
### The cleanse window
When an enemy tank uses their crowd control on her, Needles in Flowers removes it and the tank's next crowd control is on cooldown. Those few seconds are her safest time to attack.
## Combos
::combo Weakness Break | [Swallow's Path] > BA > BA > [Needles in Flowers] > ULT | Throw Swallow's Path through the target, attack while dashing around them, cleanse when they try to lock you, then ultimate once every weakness is hit.
Sequence: Swallow's Path → basic attacks with dashes → Needles in Flowers → Crossbow of Tang
Both skills trigger Tiger Pace and help break weaknesses. The returning daggers slow by 30% and immobilize on two hits, holding the target in range.
::combo Chain Finish | BA > BA > ULT | Attack a low target until their weaknesses are broken, then ultimate to kill and jump to the next hero.
Sequence: Basic attacks → Crossbow of Tang → switch on kill
A kill during the ultimate switches it to another hero in range, adds 30% Attack Speed and 1 second, up to 3 times.
::combo Cleanse and Punish | [Needles in Flowers] > BA > [Swallow's Path] > BA | When a tank stuns you, cleanse at once, then attack and throw Swallow's Path while their crowd control is on cooldown.
Sequence: Needles in Flowers → basic attack → Swallow's Path → basic attack
The tank has just used their control, so the next seconds are safe, and the daggers' slow stops them from walking away.
::combo Air Dodge | BA > ULT | When an enemy casts a big skill at you and a nearby hero is eligible, ultimate on them.
Sequence: Basic attack → Crossbow of Tang
She is untargetable and invincible for the ultimate's duration, so a skill aimed at her misses, and she gains 100% Movement Speed while firing. This only works when an eligible hero is in range, which is one more reason to hit every enemy you can early in a fight.
## Builds and emblems
Wanwan's build is Attack Speed first: it powers her dashes, her weakness breaks and her ultimate.
What the pros did: the app has three recorded Wanwan games from MPL Season 18: two by KennzySkie (GEEK) in MPL ID, one win and one loss, and one loss by NETS (AC) in MPL MY. Haas' Claws, Malefic Gun and Corrosion Scythe were in all three final inventories; Windtalker and Berserker's Fury in two.
::build Pro build: KennzySkie | Haas' Claws, Windtalker, Malefic Gun, Corrosion Scythe, Berserker's Fury | KennzySkie (GEEK), MPL ID Season 18, 11 October 2026, a win (5/1/10) with 11,315 gold. A Regular Spear component was also in the inventory.
::build Pro build: NETS | Haas' Claws, Malefic Gun, Corrosion Scythe, Demon Hunter Sword | NETS (AC), MPL MY Season 18, 17 October 2026, a loss from the Gold Lane (4/1/3). Two Dagger components were also in the inventory.
!! Pro item lists are the final inventory at the end of the game, shown in slot order, not the order the items were bought. The pro records list no boots for Wanwan.
- Haas' Claws: 15% Attack Speed and 20% Crit Chance, and critical strikes add 20% Attack Speed for 2 seconds.
- Corrosion Scythe: 30% Attack Speed and extra damage on each basic attack.
- Malefic Gun: 30% Physical Penetration and 12% more basic attack range, which keeps her safer while she attacks.
- Demon Hunter Sword: each basic attack deals 8% of the target's current HP and heals her a little.
### Build 1 — Attack Speed Core
::build Attack Speed Core | Haas' Claws, Windtalker, Malefic Gun, Corrosion Scythe, Berserker's Fury | KennzySkie's winning build as the template.
Why it works as a template: three Attack Speed items make the dashes and the ultimate fast, Malefic Gun adds penetration and range, and Berserker's Fury adds critical damage on top of Haas' Claws.
### Emblem
::emblem Custom Fighter Emblem | Swift, Bargain Hunter, Weakness Finder | All three pro builds (KennzySkie twice, NETS once). Swift gives 10% extra Attack Speed, and Bargain Hunter buys items at 95% of their base price.
Weakness Finder makes her basic attacks slow by 50% and cut Attack Speed by 30% for 1 second. Each basic attack takes 1 second off its 10-second cooldown, down to 3 seconds, which suits a hero who attacks as often as Wanwan. Bargain Hunter is listed under the Mage emblem and Weakness Finder under the Marksman emblem, but any talent can go with any set.
### Battle spells
::spells Flicker | Flicker, since her only movement is short dashes.
!! The pro records the app uses do not include battle spells, so this is our recommendation, not pro data.
## Early game
::map gold | Gold Lane: farm the wave and attack the enemy marksman between last hits to break weaknesses.
Early, Wanwan wants farm and her first Attack Speed item. Throw Swallow's Path through the wave at the enemy marksman behind it.
Attack, dash sideways, attack again. Keep attacking something, even a minion, when you need to move.
Keep Needles in Flowers for ganks. When the enemy jungler or roamer locks you, cleanse and walk back toward your tower.
During the early game, focus on:
- Finishing the first Attack Speed item.
- Dodging skill lines with the dash after each arrow.
- Saving the cleanse for ganks.
## Mid game: objectives and rotations
::map turtle | Turtle and Lord: stay behind your frontline and hit whoever is in range, so targets become eligible for the ultimate before the fight peaks.
With two attack items, Wanwan can fight at objectives. Stay behind the tank, hit the closest safe target, and let the reveal track anyone who tries to slip into a bush.
Push side towers with your Attack Speed when the enemy is busy elsewhere.
## Late game and teamfights
Wanwan enters a fight after the enemy has used their crowd control. Hit whoever is in range with attacks and Swallow's Path, and dash out of skill lines.
Once a target is eligible and low, ultimate. If they die, the ultimate jumps to the next hero in range with 30% extra Attack Speed and 1 more second. A full chain can decide a fight on its own.
If a tank locks you before you are ready, cleanse. Keep Needles in Flowers for that, not for damage, unless the fight is already won.
## Advanced techniques
### 1. Attack to Move
The dash after each arrow is your main movement. Kite by attacking the nearest unit, even a minion, then dashing away.
### 2. Watch Eligibility
Keep track of which nearby heroes have all weaknesses broken. A target that has just become eligible is also an escape: cast the ultimate to dodge an incoming skill.
### 3. Use the Dagger Return
Throw Swallow's Path past a target, then move so the returning daggers pass through them again for the second hit and the immobilize.
### 4. Cleanse Late
Needles in Flowers has a long cooldown: 24 seconds at level 1. Wait for the crowd control that actually matters.
### 5. Start the Chain Low
Cast the ultimate on the lowest eligible target with other enemies in range, so the first kill comes fast.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Khufra,Bruno,Irithel,Faramis,Lunox,Khaleed,Phoveus | bad=Yin,Ixia,Hanabi,Atlas,Guinevere | ally=Tigreal,Khufra,Estes
### Favorable Conditions
Wanwan appears on the counter lists of Khufra, Bruno, Irithel, Faramis, Lunox, Khaleed and Phoveus in the official rankings (Mythical Glory and above, past 30 days).
### Difficult Conditions
The official counter list for Wanwan is Yin, Ixia, Hanabi, Atlas and Guinevere. Yin and Guinevere are listed with Burst as a specialty; Ixia and Hanabi are marksmen; Atlas is a tank with Crowd Control and Initiator specialties. Against Atlas, keep Needles in Flowers for his engage.
### Understanding Matchups
The ally list is our reading: tanks who start fights and absorb crowd control, and a support who keeps her alive while she breaks weaknesses.
!! The ally list is not from a data source.
## Common mistakes
### 1. Waiting for the Ultimate
It needs every weakness broken first. Attack and use skills from the start of the fight.
### 2. Cleansing for Damage
Needles in Flowers is her only cleanse. Spending it early leaves her open to the next stun.
### 3. Standing Still
The dash after each arrow is free movement. Use it.
### 4. Ultimate on a Full-HP Tank
The chain needs a kill. Pick a low target with allies nearby.
### 5. Damage Before Attack Speed
Her dashes, weakness breaks and ultimate all scale with Attack Speed.
## Practice drills
::steps Break to chain | Throw Swallow's Path through the target; attack and dash around them; cleanse the first crowd control; ultimate on the lowest eligible target; follow the switch to the next hero in range
### 1. Kiting
In practice mode, attack a dummy and dash after every arrow in a circle around it, without stopping.
### 2. Dagger Returns
Throw Swallow's Path past a dummy and move so the daggers come back through it. Aim for the two-hit immobilize every time.
### 3. Cleanse Timing
In custom games, practise saving Needles in Flowers for the second crowd control a tank uses, not the first poke.
### 4. Fight Review
After each game, ask:
- Was my ultimate ready when the fight peaked?
- Did I save the cleanse for the crowd control that mattered?
- Did I start chains on low targets?
## Accuracy and patch notes
This guide uses the skill text in the app's data (MLBB Wiki, fetched November 2026), the official hero rankings for the past 30 days (updated 9 November 2026), and MLBBHub's MPL Season 18 match records. Skill values can change with balance patches; check the in-game descriptions after a patch.
!! The app's data has no basic attack range for Wanwan, so this guide does not compare her range with other marksmen.
Research references
- MLBB Wiki — Wanwan skills: https://mobile-legends.fandom.com/wiki/Wanwan
- Official MLBB hero rankings: https://www.mobilelegends.com/rank
- MLBBHub — MPL ID Season 18 (KennzySkie, win): https://www.mlbbhub.com/mpl/id/match/1097
