guides.title: Lolita
guides.sub: Banking shields for the whole team, turning enemy projectiles around, and holding a fan of enemies in place for two seconds
guides.body:
## Hero Overview
Role: Support / Tank Primary position: Roam Specialty: Guard / Crowd Control
Lolita is a guard. Her kit is built around one question: how much of the enemy's damage can she stop before it lands? Her passive keeps stacking a shield on her and every ally near her, her second skill is a wall that sends ranged basic attacks and projectiles back the way they came, and her ultimate is one of the largest area stuns in the game if she gets the full charge.
Her offence is small on purpose. The official ratings in the app give her 10 for durability, 9 for control and 1 for offence. Lolita wins fights by making the enemy's best skill miss and by holding three or four enemies still while her team does the damage.
Why she's picked: to blank ranged damage and skill shots, to protect a marksman or mage from poke, and to give a team a fan-shaped two-second stun that turns a fight at a choke point.
What she's weak to: melee heroes and damage that is not a projectile, since her wall does nothing against them, and anyone who can walk out of the fan during the charge. Her ultimate slows by 50% while she charges, but a hero with a dash or a cleanse can still leave before the slam.
Where she stands right now: in the official rankings for the past 30 days at Mythical Glory and above, Lolita has a 0.08% pick rate, a 51.24% win rate and a 0.15% ban rate. She is a rare pick, so the win rate comes from a small sample.
If you remember one idea from this guide, make it this: Lolita's wall is worth as much as her stun. A Lolita who saves the wall for the enemy's key projectile wins more fights than one who uses it to block minion damage.
## Kit deep-dive
### Passive: Noumenon Energy Core
Every 2.5 seconds, Lolita's core gives a shield of 50 (plus 10 per hero level) to her and nearby allies. The shield stacks up to 6 times and each stack lasts 30 seconds.
This is the quiet half of her value. While she walks next to her marksman between fights, both of them are banking shields. A full stack takes 15 seconds to build, and by the time a fight starts, the ally next to her already has several layers of protection that cost nothing.
!! The skill text does not say whether a stack is lost when the shield absorbs damage, or how the six stacks combine. This guide treats them as separate layers that each absorb damage until broken.
Practical application:
- Walk with the ally you are protecting, not ahead of them. "Nearby" means the shield only reaches allies close to you.
- Before an objective or a fight you can see coming, spend the last 15 seconds next to your carry so the stack is full.
- After a fight, stay grouped while the stacks rebuild instead of splitting up at once.
### Skill 1: Power Charge
Lolita dashes in the target direction. Her next basic attack within 4 seconds performs a short dash to the target, dealing 300 to 550 Physical Damage (plus 100% of her total Physical Attack) and stunning them for 0.5 seconds. The damage is doubled against minions. The cooldown is 10 seconds.
The skill is two pieces: a free dash for positioning, and a charged basic attack that closes the last gap and stuns. The 4-second window means the dash does not have to land next to the target. You can dash to a better angle and then let the empowered attack carry you in.
Practical application:
- Use the first dash to get around the enemy frontline, then attack the backline hero for the stun.
- It is also her only mobility. Dash away from a gank, and keep the empowered attack for whoever chases.
- The doubled minion damage makes it a wave-clearing tool when she has to defend a tower alone.
### Skill 2: Guardian's Reflection
Lolita raises her shield and reflects all incoming ranged basic attacks and projectiles in the direction of the shield for 3 seconds. The shield breaks after taking 1500 to 3000 damage (plus 15% of her total HP). Damage and effects from the unique passives of the attacker's items do not apply to the shield and are not reflected. The cooldown is 17.5 seconds at level 1 and 15 at max.
The shield faces one direction. Everything that flies into its front for 3 seconds is sent back, until it has absorbed its limit. That covers marksman basic attacks and the many skills that travel as a projectile.
!! The skill text says projectiles are reflected but not how much damage a reflected projectile deals or whom it can hit. This guide does not assume the reflection damages the enemy; treat the skill as a block that can also turn shots around.
!! Which enemy skills count as projectiles is not listed in the app's data. Test the ones you care about in practice mode before relying on them.
Practical application:
- Stand between the enemy's ranged damage and your carry, and face the shield toward the threat.
- Hold it for the one skill that decides the fight: a long-range stun, an execute or a marksman's burst window.
- Three seconds is short. Raise it when the attack is coming, not when the fight starts.
### Ultimate: Noumenon Blast
Lolita charges for 2 seconds, slowing enemies in a fan-shaped area by 50%. When the charge completes or is stopped, she slams her hammer down, dealing up to 500 to 900 Physical Damage (plus 100% of her total Physical Attack) to enemies in the area and stunning them for up to 2 seconds. The damage and stun duration depend on how long she charged. Recasting slams at once. The cooldown is 55 seconds at level 1 and 45 at max.
The full charge gives the full 2-second stun. A quick recast gives a shorter stun but leaves enemies less time to walk out of the fan.
!! The skill text does not give the stun or damage for a partial charge. This guide only says that a shorter charge means a shorter stun and less damage.
Practical application:
- The 50% slow during the charge is what makes the full charge possible. Start it where enemies cannot easily leave: a choke, a jungle entrance, the Turtle or Lord pit.
- Against heroes with dashes, slam early. A short stun that lands beats a long stun that misses.
- Cast it after the enemy uses their escape skills, not before.
::curve 3,4,3 | Early: the passive and the stun make her a strong lane partner for a marksman. Mid: grouped fights at objectives are where a full ultimate charge lands most often (her peak). Late: still the best answer to a ranged-heavy enemy, but enemies with cleanse items can walk out of the charge.
## How the kit fits together
### Shield, block, stun
Each part of Lolita's kit covers a different moment of a fight. Before it starts, the passive banks shields on the team. When the enemy opens with ranged damage, the wall absorbs and turns it. When the enemy commits or groups, the ultimate holds them. A Lolita who uses all three in the right order makes the enemy's opening worthless and then punishes it.
### The dash buys the ultimate's angle
Power Charge is not only an engage. Its free dash is the best way to reach a position where the ultimate's fan covers several enemies. A common pattern is to dash to the side of the enemy group, start the charge so the fan covers them while they are slowed, and slam.
### When to wall and when to stun
Against a ranged team, keep the wall ready and use the ultimate as the counter-engage once they step forward. Against a melee team, the wall does little, so play around the dash and the ultimate as the engage, and treat the passive as your main protection.
## Combos
::combo Fan Lock | [Power Charge] > ULT > ULT > [Power Charge] | Dash to the side of the group, charge the slam while they are slowed, recast or let it complete, then attack the stunned target with the empowered basic attack.
Sequence: Power Charge (dash) → Noumenon Blast (charge) → slam → empowered basic attack
The dash puts the fan over the most enemies. The 50% slow during the charge keeps them in the area, and the empowered attack is still ready inside its 4-second window after a short charge.
::combo Block and Punish | [Guardian's Reflection] > [Power Charge] > ULT | Raise the wall into the enemy's ranged opening, then dash in and slam while their damage dealers are out of position.
Sequence: Guardian's Reflection → Power Charge → Noumenon Blast
The wall takes the opening shots, so your team keeps its HP. The ranged heroes who just fired are standing forward, which is where the dash and the slam can reach them.
::combo Quick Peel | [Power Charge] > ULT | Dash into a diver on your carry and slam at once with a quick recast.
Sequence: Power Charge → Noumenon Blast → immediate recast
An instant slam gives a short stun that the diver cannot walk out of, and the empowered attack adds the 0.5-second stun for one more moment of control.
## Builds and emblems
Lolita's build should make her wall last longer and keep her near her carry with her skills ready.
What the pros did: the app has one recorded Lolita game from MPL Season 18. Zehn (TNC Pro Team) played her in MPL PH on 4 September 2026, game 2, a loss (0/3/5) that ended with 6409 gold. His recorded inventory was Flask of the Oasis, Oracle and two Magic Wands, an unfinished build in a short game.
!! One game is too small a sample to call a pro build. The builds below are our reading of her kit and the item effects in the app's data, not pro data.
- Oracle: increases shield and HP Regen effects she receives by 25%, so her own passive stacks count for more.
- Flask of the Oasis: when one of her shield skills hits an ally below 35% HP, that ally gets an extra shield of 100 per hero level, and her skill cooldowns drop by 2 seconds.
!! Whether her passive shield counts as a "shield skill" for Flask of the Oasis is not stated in the app's data. Test it in practice mode before you build around it.
### Build 1 — Guard Support
::build Guard Support | Tough Boots, Oracle, Fleeting Time, Antique Cuirass, Radiant Armor, Immortality | Our template: Oracle strengthens her shields, Fleeting Time brings the ultimate back sooner after each kill or assist, and the rest keeps her alive in front of her carry.
Fleeting Time reduces the ultimate's current cooldown by 30% on each hero kill or assist, which matters on a hero whose ultimate is her biggest play.
Radiant Armor covers Magic Damage: it adds 950 HP and 40 Magic Defense, and taking Magic Damage stacks more Magic Defense.
### Build 2 — Ranged-heavy enemy
::build Ranged-heavy Enemy | Warrior Boots, Oracle, Fleeting Time, Antique Cuirass, Blade Armor, Immortality | Our adjustment for drafts with a marksman and other physical ranged damage.
The wall breaks after 1500 to 3000 damage plus 15% of her total HP, so items with HP make it last longer. Antique Cuirass adds 920 HP and Physical Defense, and Blade Armor punishes the marksman who keeps shooting her.
### Emblem
::emblem Custom Support Emblem | Inspire, Tenacity, Concussive Blast | Zehn's setup in his MPL PH game. Inspire gives 5% Cooldown Reduction and 2 Mana Regen, Tenacity adds 5% Damage Reduction below 50% HP, and Concussive Blast adds area Magic Damage to her next basic attack.
Tenacity and Concussive Blast are listed under the Tank emblem and Inspire under the Mage emblem, but any talent can go with any set.
### Battle spells
::spells Flicker, Petrify | Flicker repositions the ultimate's fan after the charge starts or saves her from a dive. Petrify adds area control for a team that needs more lockdown.
!! The pro records the app uses do not include battle spells, so these are our recommendations, not pro data.
## Early game
::map lane | Roam: start with your gold laner. The passive shields both of you while you trade, and the empowered attack stuns anyone who steps up.
Level 1 and 2 are about the passive. Stay close to your marksman so both of you keep stacking shields, and use Power Charge only when the empowered attack can land on a hero.
When the enemy marksman trades, step in front of your carry and raise the wall. Ranged basic attacks into its front are reflected, and the trade goes your way.
At level 4, the ultimate makes every gank a threat: dash to an angle that cuts off the enemy's escape, start the charge, and let your laner follow the stun.
During the early game, focus on:
- Staying near your carry so the shield stacks build on both of you.
- Using the wall on enemy basic attack trades, not on minions.
- Roaming to mid or the jungle only when your laner is safe under tower.
## Mid game: objectives and rotations
::map turtle | Hold the Turtle and Lord pits: the walls around them make it hard to leave the fan during the charge.
The mid game is where Lolita's ultimate is at its best. Enemies group at the Turtle, the Lord and jungle entrances, all places where a fan-shaped stun can catch three or more heroes.
Before each objective, spend 15 seconds with your team so the passive is full on everyone. Then hold the wall for the enemy's opening and wait for them to step into the pit.
## Late game and teamfights
In late fights, stand in front of your carry and face the wall toward the enemy's ranged damage. A full block of a marksman's burst window can decide the fight on its own.
Use the ultimate as a counter-engage: when the enemy commits into your team, dash to the side and charge the slam while they are slowed. If they have dashes, slam early.
If your team is ahead, look for the full charge at a choke. If your team is behind, keep the ultimate for peel and use the dash and the empowered attack to stop a diver.
## Advanced techniques
### 1. Pre-stack Before Objectives
The passive gives a stack every 2.5 seconds, up to 6. Arriving early at the Turtle or Lord and standing with your team for 15 seconds means everyone starts the fight with a full stack.
### 2. Face the Wall, Not the Enemy
The wall only reflects shots that come into its front. When the threats come from two directions, face it toward the one with the most dangerous projectile, usually the marksman or a long-range mage.
### 3. Charge Behind a Wall
Start the ultimate from fog or just around a jungle wall. Enemies see the charge later and have less time to leave the fan.
### 4. Short Slams on Mobile Targets
Against heroes with dashes, recast the ultimate early. A short stun that lands lets your team follow, while a full charge often hits an empty fan.
### 5. Use the Dash Window
The empowered attack is ready for 4 seconds after the dash. Dash first for position, then wait for the best target to come in range before attacking.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Pharsa,Esmeralda,Kagura,Clint,Claude,Zhuxin | bad=Cyclops,Edith,Harley,Baxia,Floryn | ally=Layla,Miya,Lesley
### Favorable Conditions
Lolita appears on the counter lists of 26 heroes in the official rankings (Mythical Glory and above, past 30 days), including Pharsa, Esmeralda, Kagura, Clint, Claude, Zhuxin, Aulus, Tigreal and Grock. She is at her best against teams that rely on ranged basic attacks and projectile skills, and against drafts that group at objectives.
### Difficult Conditions
The official counter list for Lolita in the same data is Cyclops, Edith, Harley, Baxia and Floryn. Baxia's skills cut shields by 40% for 4 seconds, which works directly against her passive. Against heroes whose damage is not a projectile, keep the wall for whatever projectile they do have and play around the dash and the ultimate instead.
!! The reasons for the other counters are not given in the data; the official list only names them.
### Understanding Matchups
The ally list is our reading: Layla, Miya and Lesley are marksmen who stand still to deal damage, which is when the passive stacks and the wall protect them most.
!! The ally list is not from a data source.
## Common mistakes
### 1. Walking Ahead of the Carry
The passive only reaches nearby allies. A Lolita who wanders off leaves her marksman without shields.
### 2. Raising the Wall Too Early
It lasts 3 seconds. Raised at the start of a fight, it is gone when the real burst arrives.
### 3. Full Charge Into Dashes
Heroes with dashes walk out of a 2-second charge. Slam early against them.
### 4. Ultimate as the Opener
The ultimate is strongest as a counter-engage, after the enemy has stepped forward and used their escape.
### 5. Facing the Wrong Way
The wall reflects only what comes into its front. A wall facing the tank while the marksman shoots from the side does nothing.
## Practice drills
::steps Dash to fan | Dash to the side of a group of dummies; start the ultimate so the fan covers all of them; recast early once, then let a full charge complete; attack a stunned dummy with the empowered basic attack inside its 4-second window
### 1. Wall Facing
In practice mode with an allied bot, practise turning the wall toward an enemy marksman while staying between it and your ally.
### 2. Charge Timing
Practise both slams: a quick recast and a full 2-second charge. Learn how far a slowed hero can walk before the full slam.
### 3. Stack Before Objectives
In normal games, count your stacks before each Turtle and Lord. Aim to arrive with your carry 15 seconds early.
### 4. Fight Review
After each game, ask:
- Did my wall block the enemy's key shot, or minion damage?
- Did my ultimate land on several heroes, or did they walk out of the fan?
- Was I next to my carry when fights started?
## Accuracy and patch notes
This guide uses the skill text in the app's data (MLBB Wiki, fetched November 2026), the official hero rankings for the past 30 days at Mythical Glory and above (updated 9 November 2026), and MLBBHub's MPL Season 18 match records. Skill values can change with balance patches; check the in-game description after each patch.
Research references
- MLBB Wiki — Lolita skills: https://mobile-legends.fandom.com/wiki/Lolita
- Official MLBB hero rankings: https://www.mobilelegends.com/rank
- MLBBHub — TNC vs ONIC, MPL PH Season 18 (Zehn): https://www.mlbbhub.com/mpl/ph/match/tnc-onic-20260904

guides.title: Chip
guides.sub: Shielding through every fight, opening portals for the whole team, and stunning everything his mark touches
guides.body:
## Hero Overview
Role: Support / Tank Primary position: Roam Specialty: Support / Crowd Control
Chip is a map-control support. Most supports decide fights by where they stand. Chip decides them by where his team can be. His ultimate drops a portal on an enemy hero and opens connecting portals next to his allies across the map and behind his own base, so the whole team can arrive on the target at once. His special skill teleports him between four beacons on the map out of combat, so he is rarely late to anything.
In the fight itself, his first skill is a short-cooldown slam that shields him and marks enemies, and his empowered basic attack then turns into a ranged hit that detonates every mark nearby for a stun. His second skill is a speed burst that ends in a charge and a knockback.
Why he's picked: to bring the whole team to a pick or an objective at once, to keep a frontline with a shield that grows with every enemy hit, and to give a team a support who is always where the next fight is.
What he's weak to: heroes who punish him for being alone while he rotates, and the portal itself, which enemies can also use. His control is short stuns and a one-second immobilise, not long lockdown.
Where he stands right now: in the official rankings for the past 30 days at Mythical Glory and above, Chip has a 0.05% pick rate, a 48.49% win rate and a 0.18% ban rate. He is a rare pick in ranked, so the win rate comes from a small sample.
If you remember one idea from this guide, make it this: Chip's ultimate is a team skill. A portal that only Chip walks through is a waste of a 70-second cooldown.
## Kit deep-dive
### Passive: Snack Time!
Out of combat, Chip takes a bite of potato chips every 2 seconds. After a whole bag, which takes 4 bites, he regenerates HP equal to 300 plus 45% of his lost HP. He is then full and cannot eat again for 5 seconds. If he enters combat before finishing a bag, the bite count is saved.
The heal scales with missing HP, so it is strongest exactly when he needs it. A Chip who steps out of a fight at low HP for a few seconds can come back with a large part of his health.
Practical application:
- Between skirmishes, step out of combat for a moment. Four bites at 2-second intervals is about 8 seconds out of combat for one full bag.
- The saved bite count means short breaks still count. Two bites before a fight leave only two for the next break.
- Use the heal to stay on the map instead of recalling after a small trade.
### Skill 1: Crash Course
Chip rams his hovercraft into the ground, dealing 100 to 200 Magic Damage plus 4% of the target's max HP and applying Chip's Mark to enemy units hit. He gains a shield of 300 to 800 (plus 60% of his total Magic Power) when he hits an enemy hero, and the shield grows by 40% for each additional enemy hero hit. His next basic attack becomes ranged and hits every nearby enemy with Chip's Mark, detonating the marks for 150 to 275 Magic Damage (plus 30% of his Magic Power) and stunning each target for 0.6 seconds. The cooldown is 5.5 seconds at level 1 and 4 at max.
This is his main skill. The cooldown is short, the shield is large when he hits several heroes, and the follow-up attack turns one slam into an area stun.
Practical application:
- Slam into the middle of the enemy group, not the edge. Each extra hero hit adds 40% to the shield and one more target for the stun.
- Always follow the slam with the basic attack. The stun only comes from the detonation.
- Use it on the wave or a camp when no hero is near. The 4% max-HP damage helps against large monsters.
### Skill 2: Overtime
Chip rushes for 2 seconds, gaining up to 65% extra Movement Speed, then keeps the maximum speed for 2 more seconds. His next basic attack makes him charge at the enemy, dealing 200 to 300 Magic Damage (plus 30% of his Magic Power) and knocking them back slightly. The cooldown is 13 seconds at level 1 and 10 at max.
It is his engage, his chase and his escape. The knockback is small but the direction matters: a charge from the right angle pushes an enemy toward your team.
Practical application:
- Use the speed to reach a fight or to get around the enemy frontline, then charge the target toward your allies.
- Keep it for escapes when you rotate alone.
- The charge and the slam's empowered attack are both basic attack effects. Use the slam first in a fight, so the stun from the detonation is not wasted.
!! The skill text does not say which empowered attack fires first if both Crash Course and Overtime are active. Test it in practice mode.
### Ultimate: Shortcut
Chip drops the Main Portal on an enemy hero, dealing 200 to 300 Magic Damage (plus 60% of his Magic Power) and slowing them by 25%. After a delay, the Main Portal deals 2 times that damage and immobilises the target for 1 second. At the same time, Connecting Portals appear near allied heroes 10 units away and behind the allied base. The portals last up to 15 seconds. The cooldown is 70 seconds at level 1 and 50 at max.
Heroes on both teams can teleport from a Connecting Portal to the Main Portal. Allied heroes who do gain burst Movement Speed for 1.5 seconds and a shield of 500 to 1000. The Main Portal inherits 70% of Chip's attributes. A hero who stands on the Main Portal for 2 seconds returns to the Connecting Portal they came from, and casting skills or attacking resets that timer.
!! The skill text does not explain what "inherits 70% of Chip's attributes" changes in a game, for example whether the portal can be attacked. This guide does not assume an effect.
Practical application:
- Cast it on a hero your team can kill in the 1-second immobilise plus the slow, not on a tank.
- Tell your team before you cast. The portals only matter if allies use them.
- Enemies can use your Connecting Portals too. Do not open one next to an ally who cannot defend it.
- The portal behind your base lets a dead or recalling ally rejoin the fight at once.
### Special skill: Why Walk?
Chip starts each battle with 4 Beacons on the map. This skill teleports him to any other Beacon, with a 60-second cooldown, and cannot be used in combat.
Practical application:
- Use it to rotate between lanes and objectives faster than walking.
- Check the minimap before teleporting. Arriving at a Beacon alone next to the enemy jungler is the main risk.
::curve 3,4,4 | Early: the slam's short cooldown and shield make him a safe lane partner, and the beacons let him roam early. Mid: the ultimate turns every pick into a five-player fight (his peak). Late: still a strong engage and rescue tool, and the base portal brings back allies who just respawned.
## How the kit fits together
### Slam, shot, shield
Chip's fighting loop is short. Slam into enemies to mark them and take the shield, then basic attack to detonate the marks for an area stun. With a 4-second cooldown at max level, he can repeat it several times in one fight, and each slam that hits several heroes gives a bigger shield.
### The portal is the engage, the team is the damage
Chip's damage is small; the official ratings give him 2 for offence. His ultimate does not kill on its own. It brings four allies to one target with shields and burst speed. The skill is only as strong as the team's reaction to it.
### Beacons and portals make him fast
Between the beacons, the portal behind his base and Overtime's speed, Chip has more ways to move around the map than any other support. Use them to be at every objective first.
## Combos
::combo Portal Pick | ULT > [Crash Course] > [Crash Course] | Drop the portal on a lone target, slam them as your team arrives, then detonate the mark with the ranged basic attack.
Sequence: Shortcut → Crash Course → empowered basic attack
The portal's slow and 1-second immobilise hold the target while allies teleport in. The slam and detonation add a 0.6-second stun just as the immobilise ends, so the target is held long enough for the team's damage.
::combo Group Stun | [Overtime] > [Crash Course] > [Crash Course] | Rush into the enemy group, slam in the middle to shield yourself and mark them, then detonate every mark at once.
Sequence: Overtime → Crash Course → empowered basic attack
The speed gets you into the middle before they react. Each hero hit adds 40% to the shield and one more target for the area stun.
::combo Push Into Team | [Overtime] > [Overtime] > [Crash Course] > [Crash Course] | Rush around the target, charge them back toward your allies, then slam and detonate for the stun.
Sequence: Overtime (rush past) → charge attack → Crash Course → empowered basic attack
The charge's knockback moves the target toward your team, and the stun from the detonation holds them there.
## Builds and emblems
Chip's build should make him hard to kill while he stands in the middle of the enemy, and bring his ultimate back as often as possible.
What the pros did: the app has seven recorded Chip games from MPL Season 18, all in MPL ID, by AudyTzy (GEEK, three games), Said (RRQ, two), Lyoni (Team Liquid ID) and Aprho (Natus Vincere). Only one was a win. Fleeting Time was in all seven final inventories. Oracle, Antique Cuirass and Dominance Ice each appeared in three.
::build Pro build: AudyTzy | Valkyrie's Shield, Fleeting Time, Oracle, Immortality, Antique Cuirass | AudyTzy (GEEK), MPL ID Season 18, 16 August 2026, the only recorded win (1/3/17, 11491 gold). Final inventory as recorded by MLBBHub.
::build Pro build: Said | Antique Cuirass, Fleeting Time, Dominance Ice, Radiant Armor, Immortality | Said (RRQ), MPL ID Season 18, 22 August 2026, a loss with 14408 gold, the highest gold total of the seven games. A full defensive set with Dominance Ice for anti-heal.
!! Pro item lists are the final inventory at the end of the game, shown in slot order, not the order the items were bought. The pro records also list no boots for Chip.
!! Six losses in seven games is a small sample in one region. It does not show that Chip is weak in pro play, only that his recorded games were mostly losses.
- Fleeting Time: each hero kill or assist cuts the ultimate's current cooldown by 30%, which is why every pro took it on a hero whose ultimate is a 70-second team engage.
- Oracle: increases shield and HP Regen effects he receives by 25%, which applies to the slam's shield.
- Dominance Ice: reduces the Shield and HP Regen of enemies within 5 units to 60% of normal, useful when he stands in the enemy team after a slam.
### Build 1 — Portal Support
::build Portal Support | Tough Boots, Fleeting Time, Oracle, Antique Cuirass, Valkyrie's Shield, Immortality | AudyTzy's winning items with Tough Boots added, as the template for a roaming Chip.
Tough Boots is our addition, since the pro records list no boots. It reduces crowd control and slow duration by 25%.
### Build 2 — Sustain-heavy enemy
::build Sustain-heavy Enemy | Tough Boots, Fleeting Time, Dominance Ice, Antique Cuirass, Radiant Armor, Immortality | Said's items, for drafts with heavy healing or shields.
### Emblem
::emblem Custom Support Emblem | Inspire, Wilderness Blessing, Concussive Blast | AudyTzy's setup in all three of his games, including the win. Inspire gives 5% Cooldown Reduction and 2 Mana Regen, and Wilderness Blessing gives 10% Movement Speed in the jungle and river.
::emblem Custom Tank Emblem | Thrill, Wilderness Blessing, Concussive Blast | Said and Lyoni's setup. Thrill gives 16 Adaptive Attack. Concussive Blast adds Magic Damage equal to 100 plus 7% of his total HP to his next basic attack, every 15 seconds.
Wilderness Blessing and Concussive Blast were in all seven pro setups. Any talent can go with any set.
### Battle spells
::spells Flicker, Vengeance | Flicker lands the slam in the middle of a group or saves him after a portal engage. Vengeance punishes the burst he draws when he stands in the enemy team.
!! The pro records the app uses do not include battle spells, so these are our recommendations, not pro data.
## Early game
::map roam | Roam: use the beacons to move between lanes, and arrive where your jungler or laners can follow your slam.
At level 1, the slam is enough to protect your gold laner: its shield absorbs trades, and the stun from the detonation punishes an enemy who steps up.
Use Why Walk? as soon as it helps. A Chip who appears in mid lane through a beacon a few seconds after leaving the gold lane catches enemies who thought he was still there.
Between trades, step out of combat for a moment to let the passive finish a bag. It heals 45% of lost HP, so you rarely need to recall early.
During the early game, focus on:
- Following every slam with the detonating basic attack.
- Using beacons to reach the first Turtle and your jungler's ganks.
- Keeping your bite count up between fights.
## Mid game: objectives and rotations
::map rotate | Rotate between objectives with the beacons and Overtime. Arrive first, slam the enemies who contest, and open the portal on whoever is caught.
The mid game is where Chip's ultimate matters most. Before each objective, look for an enemy who rotates alone. A portal on that hero brings your whole team on top of them with shields and burst speed.
Talk to your team. The best portal is the one cast when allies are ready to teleport, not the one cast first.
## Late game and teamfights
In late fights, the portal behind your base is a comeback tool. When allies respawn or recall during a fight, they can teleport straight to the Main Portal.
Open with Overtime or the portal on the enemy damage dealer, then slam the group and detonate for the area stun. The slam's cooldown is 4 seconds at max level, so keep slamming as long as you are in the fight.
If your team is behind, keep the portal for defence: drop it on the enemy diver who reaches your base, and let your team arrive from the Connecting Portals.
## Advanced techniques
### 1. Call the Portal
Before you cast Shortcut, ping the target. The portals last up to 15 seconds, but the target is only immobilised for 1 second after the delay.
### 2. Watch the Enemy at Your Portals
Enemies can also teleport from your Connecting Portals to the Main Portal. Do not cast it when an enemy is standing next to an ally's portal.
### 3. Slam the Middle
The shield grows by 40% for each additional enemy hero hit. One slam into three heroes gives a much bigger shield than one slam into a single target.
### 4. Snack Between Fights
Four bites, one every 2 seconds, then a heal of 300 plus 45% of lost HP. Step out of combat for those few seconds between fights instead of recalling.
### 5. Beacon Before the Objective
Why Walk? cannot be used in combat. Teleport before the objective fight starts, not when it has begun.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Carmilla,Odette,Alice,Vexana,Alpha,Martis,Lapu-Lapu,Roger,Lancelot | bad=Zilong,Jawhead,Helcurt,Gusion,Floryn | ally=Hayabusa,Lancelot,Saber
### Favorable Conditions
Chip appears on the counter lists of Carmilla, Odette, Alice, Vexana, Alpha, Martis, Lapu-Lapu, Roger and Lancelot in the official rankings (Mythical Glory and above, past 30 days). He is at his best when the enemy groups up for his slam and when his team has damage dealers who can follow a portal.
### Difficult Conditions
The official counter list for Chip in the same data is Zilong, Jawhead, Helcurt, Gusion and Floryn. Several of them are assassins and divers who can catch a support alone while he rotates between beacons.
!! The reasons for each counter are not given in the data; the official list only names them.
### Understanding Matchups
The ally list is our reading: Hayabusa, Lancelot and Saber are burst heroes who can delete the portal's target in the 1-second immobilise.
!! The ally list is not from a data source.
## Common mistakes
### 1. Portal Without the Team
A portal no ally uses is a 70-second cooldown spent on a slow and a short immobilise.
### 2. Forgetting the Detonation
The slam only marks. The stun comes from the next basic attack. A Chip who slams and then walks away throws away his control.
### 3. Opening Portals Next to Enemies
Enemies can use the Connecting Portals. Check where they are before casting.
### 4. Beaconing Into Fog
Teleporting to a Beacon next to an unseen enemy jungler is the easiest way for Chip to die.
### 5. Recalling Instead of Snacking
The passive heals a large part of lost HP. A few seconds out of combat often saves a trip back to base.
## Practice drills
::steps Slam to stun | Slam into a group of dummies; basic attack at once to detonate every mark; count how many dummies were stunned; repeat while moving to land the slam in the middle of the group
### 1. Portal Callouts
In custom games with friends, practise pinging the target, casting Shortcut and timing your allies' teleports for the immobilise.
### 2. Beacon Routes
Learn where the 4 Beacons are and which one is closest to each objective, so you know where to teleport before each Turtle and Lord.
### 3. Snack Timing
In practice mode, take damage and step out of combat. Learn how long one bag takes and how much it heals.
### 4. Fight Review
After each game, ask:
- Did my team use my portals, or did I cast them alone?
- Did every slam get its detonating attack?
- Did any enemy use my Connecting Portals against us?
## Accuracy and patch notes
This guide uses the skill text in the app's data (MLBB Wiki, fetched November 2026), the official hero rankings for the past 30 days at Mythical Glory and above (updated 9 November 2026), and MLBBHub's MPL Season 18 match records. Skill values can change with balance patches; check the in-game description after each patch.

guides.title: Roger
guides.sub: Shooting in human form, finishing in wolf form, and switching between them every few seconds
guides.body:
## Hero Overview
Role: Fighter / Marksman Primary position: Jungle Specialty: Finisher / Burst
Roger is two heroes in one. In human form he is a ranged shooter with a slowing net, a Physical Defense shred and a speed boost. In wolf form he is a melee finisher who lunges onto low targets, becomes untargetable for the jump, and gets his lunge back almost at once after every kill or assist. His ultimate is the switch between the two, and at max level it has only a 4.5-second cooldown.
His passive is what decides which form to fight in. In human form, his basic attacks and skills deal extra damage equal to 4% of the target's current HP, which is best against healthy targets. In wolf form, they deal 4% of the target's lost HP, which is best against hurt ones. Roger opens in human form and finishes in wolf form.
Why he's picked: to clean up fights with chained wolf lunges, to punish a team that lets its damage dealers drop low, and for a jungler who can poke at range and still dive.
What he's weak to: early pressure and heroes who burst him before he gets to switch. His official control rating is 1, so outside the net he has little to hold a target with.
Where he stands right now: in the official rankings for the past 30 days at Mythical Glory and above, Roger has a 0.22% pick rate, a 45.56% win rate and a 0.04% ban rate. He has no recorded games in the app's MPL Season 18 data.
If you remember one idea from this guide, make it this: Roger is played in a rhythm. Human form while targets are healthy, wolf form once they are low, and the switch is a skill that comes back every few seconds.
## Kit deep-dive
### Passive: Full Moon Curse
Roger can switch freely between human and wolf forms. In human form, his basic attacks and skills deal extra damage equal to 4% of the target's current HP. In wolf form, they deal extra damage equal to 4% of the target's lost HP. Against creeps, this extra damage is capped at 60.
The two halves cross over at half HP. Above 50% HP, the target has more current HP than lost HP, so human form adds more. Below 50%, wolf form adds more.
Practical application:
- Poke from human form while the enemy is above half HP.
- Switch to wolf once your target drops below half. Every attack after that adds more.
- The 60-damage cap against creeps means the passive does little for jungle clear. Clear with your skills and basic attacks, not the passive.
### Human Skill 1: Open Fire
Roger fires two quick shots in the target direction, dealing 250 to 500 Physical Damage (plus 125% of his total Physical Attack) in total. The first shot is a net that slows the enemy by 80% for 1.5 seconds. The second is a bullet that reduces their Physical Defense by 10 to 30 for 5 seconds. The cooldown is 7 seconds.
This is his setup skill. The net's 80% slow is the strongest control in his kit, and the defense shred lasts 5 seconds, long enough to cover the wolf follow-up.
Practical application:
- Open every fight with it. The slow and the shred make the wolf lunge easier to land and hit harder.
- Use it to stop an escaping target before you switch to wolf.
- In the jungle, it is part of your clear.
### Human Skill 2: Hunter's Steps
Roger gains 20% to 40% Movement Speed and 20% to 40% Attack Speed for 2.5 seconds. The cooldown is 10 seconds at level 1 and 8 at max.
A short burst for kiting in human form: shoot, step back, shoot again while the passive adds 4% of current HP to each attack.
Practical application:
- Use it to kite a melee hero in human form while they are still above half HP.
- It also gets you into net range on a fleeing target.
### Ultimate (human form): Wolf Transformation
Roger lunges in the target direction and turns into a wolf, dealing 150 to 300 Physical Damage (plus 100% of his extra Physical Attack) to enemies hit and slowing them by 90% for 0.8 seconds. In wolf form, he gains 20 to 65 Physical and Magic Defense and 25 Movement Speed. The cooldown is 6 seconds at level 1 and 4.5 at max.
The transformation is an attack. Its lunge slows by 90%, so switching right on top of a target holds them for the first wolf attacks.
### Wolf Skill 1: Lycan Pounce
Roger lunges at the enemy, becoming untargetable while dealing 250 to 500 Physical Damage (plus 125% of his total Physical Attack) to up to 3 enemies in the area. A kill or assist reduces its cooldown by 80%. The base cooldown is 15 seconds at level 1 and 12 at max.
This is the finisher. A pounce that kills comes back almost at once, so one kill in a fight can lead straight into the next. Being untargetable during the lunge also lets him dodge a skill aimed at him.
Practical application:
- Pounce onto the lowest target in range first. A kill resets most of the cooldown for the next one.
- Use the untargetable lunge to dodge a key skill, not only to reach a target.
- It hits up to 3 enemies, so pounce where low enemies are grouped.
### Wolf Skill 2: Bloodthirsty Howl
Roger howls, increasing his Attack Speed to 1.15 to 1.4 times for 5 seconds. During this time, he gains 50% Movement Speed if an enemy hero below 40% HP is in his vision. The cooldown is 10 seconds at level 1 and 7 at max.
This is his chase. Any enemy below 40% HP in sight turns the howl into a big speed boost, and the attack speed makes every hit count with the lost-HP passive.
### Ultimate (wolf form): Restore Human Form
Roger rolls in the target direction and turns back into a human, gaining a shield of 200 to 350 (plus 200% of his extra Physical Attack) for 1.5 seconds. The cooldown is 6 seconds at level 1 and 4.5 at max.
The way back is an escape. It moves him, shields him, and puts Open Fire back in his hands for another net.
::curve 2,3,4 | Early: he needs levels for short switch cooldowns and items for damage, so he farms and picks his fights. Mid: chained pounces start to clean up fights. Late: with full items, every low enemy is a target for a pounce that resets on the kill (his peak).
!! The power curve is our reading of the kit, not data.
## How the kit fits together
### Net, switch, pounce
The basic loop: Open Fire to slow and shred, Wolf Transformation onto the target for the 90% slow, wolf basic attacks, then Lycan Pounce to finish. The net's 1.5-second slow and the lunge's 0.8-second slow keep the target close enough for the attacks between them.
### Switch back to reset the shooter
After a kill or when the fight turns, Restore Human Form rolls him out with a shield. Back in human form, Open Fire is available again for the next target. With a 4.5-second cooldown on each switch at max level, he can go back and forth several times in one fight.
### Pounce resets chain the cleanup
A kill or assist takes 80% off Lycan Pounce's cooldown. In a fight where the enemy is low, Roger pounces from one target to the next. The howl's 50% speed toward enemies below 40% HP keeps him in range.
## Combos
::combo Open and Finish | [Open Fire] > ULT > [Bloodthirsty Howl] > [Lycan Pounce] | Net and shred the target, lunge into wolf form on top of them, howl for attack speed, then pounce to finish.
Sequence: Open Fire → Wolf Transformation → Bloodthirsty Howl → Lycan Pounce
The net and the transformation's slow hold the target. The defense shred lasts 5 seconds, covering the whole combo, and the lost-HP passive adds more with each hit as the target drops.
::combo Chain Cleanup | [Lycan Pounce] > [Lycan Pounce] > [Bloodthirsty Howl] | Pounce the lowest enemy for the kill, pounce again on the next one with the cooldown reset, and howl to chase the last.
Sequence: Lycan Pounce (kill) → Lycan Pounce → Bloodthirsty Howl
The 80% cooldown cut on a kill or assist makes the second pounce ready almost at once. The howl's 50% speed toward enemies below 40% HP covers the chase.
::combo Roll and Reset | ULT > [Open Fire] > ULT | When the fight turns, roll back to human form for the shield, net the closest chaser, then switch back to wolf onto them.
Sequence: Restore Human Form → Open Fire → Wolf Transformation
The shield absorbs the damage while you reset, and the net slows the chaser for the next switch.
## Builds and emblems
Roger has no pro games in the app's data, so his build comes from his kit and the item effects in the app's data.
!! The builds below are our reading of his kit and item effects, not data from a stats site or pro games.
- Hunter Strike: 80 Physical Attack, 10% Cooldown Reduction and 15 Physical Penetration, and 50% extra Movement Speed that decays over 3 seconds after five hits on the same target.
- Blade of Despair: 160 Physical Attack, and 25% more Physical Attack for 2 seconds when he hits a non-minion enemy below 50% HP, the same moment his wolf passive starts to outdamage the human one.
- Malefic Roar: 30% Physical Penetration, plus more against targets with high Physical Defense.
### Build 1 — Burst Jungler
::build Burst Jungler | Ice Retribution, Swift Boots, Hunter Strike, Blade of Despair, Malefic Roar, Rose Gold Meteor | Our template: Hunter Strike for the early spike, Blade of Despair for the finish, Malefic Roar for penetration and Rose Gold Meteor for a shield when he is caught.
Rose Gold Meteor gives a shield of 120 per hero level and 50% Movement Speed when damage drops him below 30% HP.
!! The app's data has no effect text for the Retribution jungle items, so this guide does not say which one to choose.
### Build 2 — Sustained Fighter
::build Sustained Fighter | Ice Retribution, Warrior Boots, Hunter Strike, Demon Hunter Sword, Corrosion Scythe, Blade of Despair | Our adjustment for longer fights against tanks: Demon Hunter Sword adds 8% of the target's current HP to each basic attack, and Corrosion Scythe adds Attack Speed and a slow.
### Emblem
::emblem Custom Assassin Emblem | Rupture, Master Assassin, Killing Spree | Our template for a jungler who dives and needs to stay in the fight after a kill.
!! This emblem is our recommendation; the app has no pro or stats data for Roger's emblem.
### Battle spells
::spells Retribution | Retribution for the jungle.
## Early game
::map jungle | Jungle: clear with Open Fire and basic attacks in human form, and look for a gank only when a lane has slowed or low enemies.
Roger's early game is about farm and timing. His passive is capped at 60 extra damage against creeps, so his clear relies on his skills.
At level 4, the ultimate is his first real power spike: the switch to wolf form gives him the lunge, the defenses and the pounce. Look for ganks on enemies who are already below half HP.
During the early game, focus on:
- Clearing efficiently and staying even in farm.
- Ganking lanes where your allies have already damaged the enemy.
- Avoiding fights against full-HP enemies with stronger early damage.
## Mid game: objectives and rotations
::map river | River: fight around the Turtle when your team has damaged the enemy. A low enemy in the river is a pounce that resets.
In the mid game, Roger's job is to follow his team's damage. Let your laners and mage take the enemy down, then switch to wolf and finish. With Hunter Strike and Blade of Despair, each pounce on a low target is close to a kill.
## Late game and teamfights
Late fights are where Roger is strongest. Stay at the edge of the fight in human form, poke with Open Fire, and wait. Once enemies drop below half HP, switch to wolf and pounce on the lowest one. Each kill or assist takes 80% off the pounce cooldown, so a good fight becomes a chain of pounces.
If you are focused, roll back to human form for the shield and leave. The switch comes back in 4.5 seconds at max level, and you can return.
## Advanced techniques
### 1. Switch at Half HP
The human passive scales with current HP and the wolf passive with lost HP. Switching as the target crosses 50% gets the most from both.
### 2. Dodge With the Pounce
Lycan Pounce makes him untargetable during the lunge. Time it to dodge a stun or a big skill aimed at him.
### 3. Shred Before the Switch
Open Fire's defense shred lasts 5 seconds. Fire it first, so the whole wolf combo hits a target with less Physical Defense.
### 4. Howl for the Chase
The howl gives 50% Movement Speed only if an enemy hero below 40% HP is in vision. Use it after the target drops, not before.
### 5. Roll Out, Shoot Back
Restore Human Form shields and moves him. Use it as an escape, then net whoever follows.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good= | bad=Harley,Chip,Gusion,Benedetta,Baxia | ally=Atlas,Tigreal,Pharsa
### Favorable Conditions
No hero lists Roger as a counter in the official rankings (Mythical Glory and above, past 30 days). His best fights are ones where his team has already done damage, so his lost-HP passive and pounce resets can finish them.
### Difficult Conditions
The official counter list for Roger in the same data is Harley, Chip, Gusion, Benedetta and Baxia. Baxia's skills cut shields and HP Regen by 40% for 4 seconds, which weakens Restore Human Form's shield.
!! The reasons for the other counters are not given in the data; the official list only names them.
### Understanding Matchups
The ally list is our reading: Atlas and Tigreal group enemies for a pounce that hits up to 3 targets, and Pharsa's area damage drops enemies below half HP for his wolf form.
!! The ally list is not from a data source.
## Common mistakes
### 1. Fighting in the Wrong Form
Wolf form against a full-HP target wastes the passive. Human form against a low target does the same.
### 2. Diving Without the Net
Open Fire is his only real control. Diving without it lets the target walk away.
### 3. Pouncing the Tank
The pounce resets on a kill or assist. Pouncing a full-HP tank gives no reset and leaves him without his finisher.
### 4. Forgetting the Roll Out
Restore Human Form is a shield and an escape. Many Roger deaths happen with it unused.
### 5. Ganking Healthy Lanes
Early, his damage relies on enemies already being hurt. Gank lanes where your allies have done damage first.
## Practice drills
::steps Form rhythm | Net a dummy with Open Fire; switch to wolf onto it; howl and attack; pounce to finish; roll back to human form; repeat as fast as the cooldowns allow
### 1. Half-HP Switch
In practice mode, damage a dummy to just below half HP before switching. Learn to read when the wolf passive becomes stronger.
### 2. Pounce Chains
In practice, set up several low dummies and chain pounces. Feel how fast the reset makes the next one available.
### 3. Dodge Timing
With a friend in a custom game, practise pouncing through a skill shot to dodge it.
### 4. Fight Review
After each game, ask:
- Did I switch forms at the right time?
- Did my pounces land on low targets for resets?
- Did I use Restore Human Form to escape before dying?
## Accuracy and patch notes
This guide uses the skill text in the app's data (MLBB Wiki, fetched November 2026) and the official hero rankings for the past 30 days at Mythical Glory and above (updated 9 November 2026). Roger has no games in the app's MPL Season 18 records. Skill values can change with balance patches; check the in-game description after each patch.
Research references
- MLBB Wiki — Roger skills: https://mobile-legends.fandom.com/wiki/Roger
- Official MLBB hero rankings: https://www.mobilelegends.com/rank

guides.title: Edith
guides.sub: Locking enemies in place from inside Phylax, soaking damage to fill her Wrath, then flying out to turn that damage into a shield, attack speed and lifesteal
guides.body:
## Hero Overview
Role: Tank / Marksman Primary position: EXP Lane or Roam Specialty: Control / Burst
Edith is a tank who becomes a marksman. She starts every fight inside Phylax, her stone guardian, with two physical skills that scale with her HP: a delayed slam that knocks enemies airborne and a charge that throws the first hero it hits over Phylax's shoulder. While she is inside, every point of damage she takes fills her Wrath. Her ultimate ejects her out of Phylax and into the air, where she fights with ranged basic attacks, two new magic skills, and a shield, attack speed and lifesteal that grow with the Wrath she stored.
The official ratings in the app give her 10 for control, the highest possible, with 7 for durability and 3 for offence.
Why she's picked: for a frontline with an airborne and a throw, for a tank who still deals real damage late in fights, and for a hero whose second half gets stronger the more the enemy hits her first.
What she's weak to: heroes who outlast her flight or burst her while she is out of Phylax. Her control is in Phylax form, so once she is flying she gives up the airborne and the throw for a single 0.8-second immobilise.
Where she stands right now: in the official rankings for the past 30 days at Mythical Glory and above, Edith has a 0.27% pick rate, a 51.23% win rate and a 0.1% ban rate. She has two recorded games in the app's MPL Season 18 data, one win and one loss.
If you remember one idea from this guide, make it this: Edith's ultimate is paid for with damage taken. Take the enemy's damage in Phylax first, then fly.
## Kit deep-dive
### Passive: Overload
After each skill cast, Edith and Phylax become Overloaded for 3 seconds. During that time, every basic attack triggers chain lightning that deals extra Magic Damage equal to 30% of her total Magic Power plus 4% to 8% of the target's total HP, to up to 4 enemies. The chain lightning deals 150% damage to minions.
This is the glue of her kit. Every skill is followed by a 3-second window in which her basic attacks hit up to four enemies for a percentage of their max HP.
Practical application:
- Weave basic attacks between skills. Each skill opens 3 more seconds of chain lightning.
- The damage scales with the target's total HP, so it stays useful against tanks.
- The 150% damage against minions makes her lane clear faster than her offence rating suggests.
### Phylax Skill 1: Earth Shatter
After a 0.75-second delay, Edith controls Phylax to strike in the target direction, dealing 225 to 450 Physical Damage (plus 10% of her total HP) to enemies hit and knocking them airborne for 1 second. It deals 120% damage to minions. The cooldown is 8.5 seconds at level 1 and 6.5 at max.
Regular control effects do not interrupt it, only suppression does. The delay is the cost: enemies who see it coming can walk out of the line.
Practical application:
- Cast it where the enemy will be in 0.75 seconds, not where they are now.
- Use it after Onward's throw or on enemies who are already slowed, stuck or fighting your team.
- Since only suppression interrupts it, you can cast it through a stun aimed at you.
### Phylax Skill 2: Onward
Edith controls Phylax to charge in the target direction, dealing 90 to 140 Physical Damage (plus 3% of her total HP) to enemies along the way. If Phylax hits an enemy hero, it stops at once and throws them over its shoulder, dealing 108 Physical Damage (plus 5% of her total HP). The cooldown is 10 seconds.
The throw moves the enemy behind Phylax. Charging from the right side throws a backline hero toward your team.
Practical application:
- Charge from behind or beside the target, so the throw sends them toward your allies.
- Follow the throw with Earth Shatter. The thrown enemy lands where the slam is easy to aim.
- It also works as a dash to start a fight or reach a better angle.
### Ultimate: Primal Wrath
Passive: while inside Phylax, Edith stores Wrath based on the damage she takes, counted before damage reduction.
Active: Edith ejects herself forward from Phylax, knocking back nearby enemies, and takes flight. In flight, her basic attacks are ranged and deal 35 to 65 Magic Damage (plus 75% of her total Physical Attack and 25% of her total Magic Power). Based on her stored Wrath, she gains a shield of 350 to 650 (plus 5% to 20% of her total HP), 50% to 150% extra Attack Speed and 5% to 20% Hybrid Lifesteal. Each point of extra Physical and Magic Defense is converted into 3.5 Magic Power. Flight lasts 8 to 12 seconds. The cooldown is 40 seconds at level 1 and 34 at max.
The more damage she took before flying, the closer she gets to the top of every range. Because Wrath counts damage before reduction, her defense items do not slow it down.
!! The skill text does not say how much damage fills Wrath to the maximum. Watch the indicator in game.
Practical application:
- Do not fly at the start of a fight. Stand in Phylax, take the opening damage, and let Wrath build.
- The defense-to-Magic Power conversion means her tank items also raise her flight damage.
- The ejection knocks back nearby enemies. Use it to push a diver off your backline as you take off.
### Flight Skill 1: Divine Retribution
Edith strikes a target area, dealing 170 to 320 Magic Damage (plus 40% of her total Magic Power) to enemies hit and slowing them by 30%. She then deals 68 to 128 Magic Damage (plus 16% of her total Magic Power) to enemies in the area every 0.5 seconds for the next 1.5 seconds. The cooldown is 5 seconds at level 1 and 3.5 at max.
The short cooldown is the point. Each cast also opens a new 3-second Overload window, so in flight she alternates this skill and chain-lightning basic attacks.
### Flight Skill 2: Lightning Bolt
Edith fires a bolt in the target direction, dealing 150 to 300 Magic Damage (plus 50% of her total Magic Power) to the first enemy hero hit and immobilising them for 0.8 seconds. The cooldown is 10 seconds.
Her only control in flight. Keep it for the diver who reaches her, or for a fleeing target.
::curve 3,4,4 | Early: the throw and the airborne make her a dangerous lane and roam partner, but her flight is short at level 4. Mid: grouped fights at objectives let her fill Wrath and get full value from the flight (her peak). Late: flight lasts 12 seconds at max level and her defense items turn into Magic Power.
!! The power curve is our reading of the kit, not data.
## How the kit fits together
### Control first, damage second
Edith's fight has two halves. In Phylax, she starts the fight with Onward and Earth Shatter, controlling enemies while she takes their damage. Once her Wrath is high, she flies out and turns that damage into a shield, attack speed and lifesteal for the second half.
### Overload connects both forms
Every skill in both forms opens a 3-second Overload window. In Phylax, that means chain lightning after each charge and slam. In flight, Divine Retribution's 3.5-second cooldown at max level keeps the window open almost all the time.
### Defense items do double work
Each point of extra Physical and Magic Defense becomes 3.5 Magic Power in flight. A tank build is also a damage build for Edith's second half.
## Combos
::combo Throw and Shatter | [Onward] > [Earth Shatter] > ULT | Charge into the backline to throw a target toward your team, slam them airborne as they land, then fly out once you have taken the enemy's damage.
Sequence: Onward → Earth Shatter → basic attacks → Primal Wrath
The throw places the target where the 0.75-second delay of Earth Shatter is easy to land. Both skills open Overload windows for chain lightning.
::combo Flight Burst | ULT > [Divine Retribution] > [Lightning Bolt] > [Divine Retribution] | Eject to knock back nearby enemies, strike the group, immobilise the main target, then strike again as the cooldown comes back.
Sequence: Primal Wrath → Divine Retribution → Lightning Bolt → Divine Retribution
Each skill opens a new Overload window, so every basic attack between them chains to up to 4 enemies.
::combo Peel Lift-off | [Earth Shatter] > ULT > [Lightning Bolt] | When a diver reaches your carry, slam them airborne, eject next to them for the knockback, then immobilise them if they come back.
Sequence: Earth Shatter → Primal Wrath → Lightning Bolt
The airborne holds the diver for 1 second while you eject beside them, and the knockback and the 0.8-second immobilise keep them off your carry.
## Builds and emblems
Edith's build should make her durable in Phylax, since her damage there scales with HP, and give her defenses that turn into Magic Power in flight.
What the pros did: the app has two recorded Edith games from MPL Season 18. Ryota (TNC Pro Team) won in MPL PH on 23 August 2026, game 1, with 3/1/4 and 11615 gold. Joshua (RRQ) lost in MPL ID on 19 September 2026, game 2, with 2/4/1 and 4609 gold, a short game with an unfinished build.
::build Pro build: Ryota | Rapid Boots, Dominance Ice, Antique Cuirass, Radiant Armor, Immortality, Starlium Scythe | Ryota (TNC Pro Team), MPL PH Season 18, 23 August 2026, a win. Final inventory as recorded by MLBBHub, boots moved to the front.
!! Pro item lists are the final inventory at the end of the game, not the order the items were bought. Two games is too small a sample to call a standard pro build.
- Starlium Scythe: after a skill, her next basic attack within 3 seconds deals 90 (plus 60% of her total Magic Power) extra True Damage and slows by 15%. It fits her loop of a skill followed by basic attacks.
- Dominance Ice: Hybrid Defense grows by 8 for each enemy hero within 5 units, up to 40, and it cuts the Shield and HP Regen of nearby enemies to 60%.
- Rapid Boots: 55 Movement Speed, 35% Slow Reduction and 12 HP Regen.
### Build 1 — Ryota's frontline
::build Frontline Flight | Rapid Boots, Dominance Ice, Antique Cuirass, Radiant Armor, Starlium Scythe, Immortality | Ryota's items, with Starlium Scythe as the fifth item so the flight damage comes online before the last defensive item.
!! The item order is our suggestion; the pro data shows only the final inventory.
### Build 2 — Magic-heavy enemy
::build Magic-heavy Enemy | Tough Boots, Radiant Armor, Dominance Ice, Antique Cuirass, Starlium Scythe, Immortality | Our adjustment, based on Joshua's Tough Boots and Radiant Armor start: more Magic Defense against mage-heavy drafts.
### Emblem
::emblem Custom Tank Emblem | Swift, Festival of Blood, Brave Smite | Ryota's winning setup. Swift gives 10% extra Attack Speed, Festival of Blood gives 6% Spell Vamp plus 0.5% per kill or assist up to 12 stacks, and Brave Smite recovers 5% of her max HP when her skill damage hits an enemy hero, every 6 seconds.
::emblem Custom Tank Emblem | Swift, Tenacity, War Cry | Joshua's setup. Tenacity adds 5% Damage Reduction below 50% HP, and War Cry adds 8% damage for 6 seconds after three separate hits on enemy heroes.
Festival of Blood and Brave Smite are listed under the Fighter emblem, but any talent can go with any set.
### Battle spells
::spells Flicker, Vengeance | Flicker lands Onward's throw from an angle the enemy does not expect. Vengeance punishes the damage she wants to take in Phylax anyway.
!! The pro records the app uses do not include battle spells, so these are our recommendations, not pro data.
## Early game
::map lane | EXP Lane: trade with chain lightning after each skill, and use Onward's throw to pull your opponent toward your tower or your jungler.
In lane, her Overload passive is her trading tool: cast a skill, then basic attack during the 3-second window. The chain lightning deals 150% damage to minions, so her wave clear is strong.
As a roamer, Onward is her gank tool. Charge from behind the enemy laner to throw them toward your ally, then slam them airborne.
During the early game, focus on:
- Weaving basic attacks into every Overload window.
- Using Earth Shatter on enemies who are already held, not on free targets.
- Taking trades in Phylax to build Wrath before level 4.
## Mid game: objectives and rotations
::map turtle | Turtle: stand in front of your team in Phylax, take the enemy's opening damage, and fly once your Wrath is high.
The mid game is where Edith's two halves fit best. Objective fights start with both teams trading damage. Be the hero who takes it: your Wrath fills, and your flight comes out with a bigger shield, more attack speed and more lifesteal.
## Late game and teamfights
In late fights, open with Onward on the enemy carry and Earth Shatter on the group. Stay in Phylax while the enemy focuses you. When your Wrath is high or Phylax is about to fall, eject to knock back nearby enemies and fly.
In flight, keep moving and alternate Divine Retribution with basic attacks. Keep Lightning Bolt for the diver who reaches you. At max level, flight lasts 12 seconds.
## Advanced techniques
### 1. Fill Wrath Before Flying
Wrath counts damage before reduction. The best moment to fly is after the enemy has spent their burst on Phylax.
### 2. Throw Toward Allies
Onward's throw sends the target over Phylax's shoulder. Charge from the far side so they land among your team.
### 3. Cast Shatter Through Control
Earth Shatter can only be interrupted by suppression. Cast it even when a stun is coming your way.
### 4. Eject for Peel
The ejection knocks back nearby enemies. Fly out next to a diver to push them off your carry.
### 5. Keep Overload Open
Every skill gives 3 seconds of chain lightning. In flight, Divine Retribution's short cooldown keeps it open almost constantly.
## Matchups and counterplay
::vs good=Gord,Lolita,Beatrix,Aurora,Layla | bad=Alice,Harith,Silvanna,Faramis,Mathilda | ally=Pharsa,Lunox,Yve
### Favorable Conditions
Edith appears on the counter lists of Gord, Lolita, Beatrix, Aurora and Layla in the official rankings (Mythical Glory and above, past 30 days). Several of them are backline heroes that Onward's throw can pull out of position.
### Difficult Conditions
The official counter list for Edith in the same data is Alice, Harith, Silvanna, Faramis and Mathilda.
!! The reasons for each counter are not given in the data; the official list only names them.
### Understanding Matchups
The ally list is our reading: Pharsa, Lunox and Yve deal area damage that lands on enemies held by Earth Shatter's airborne.
!! The ally list is not from a data source.
## Common mistakes
### 1. Flying Too Early
A flight with low Wrath gives a small shield, little attack speed and little lifesteal. Take damage first.
### 2. Casting Shatter on Free Targets
The 0.75-second delay gives enemies time to walk out. Cast it on enemies who are already held or committed.
### 3. Throwing the Wrong Way
Onward throws the target behind Phylax. A charge from your side throws them back toward their own team.
### 4. Basic Attacks Outside Overload
Her damage comes from chain lightning after skills. Basic attacks without a skill before them lose most of it.
### 5. Wasting the Bolt
Lightning Bolt is her only control in flight. Firing it at the first enemy in range leaves her open to the diver who follows.
## Practice drills
::steps Throw to slam | Charge a dummy with Onward from behind; cast Earth Shatter where it lands; basic attack during the Overload window; repeat from different angles
### 1. Shatter Timing
In practice mode, cast Earth Shatter on moving bots. Learn how far a target walks in 0.75 seconds.
### 2. Flight Rhythm
After flying, alternate Divine Retribution and basic attacks. Count how many basic attacks fit in each 3-second window.
### 3. Wrath Reading
In normal games, watch the Wrath indicator and fly at different levels. Compare the shield and attack speed you get.
### 4. Fight Review
After each game, ask:
- Did I fly with high Wrath?
- Did my throws send enemies toward my team?
- Did I save Lightning Bolt for the right target?
## Accuracy and patch notes
This guide uses the skill text in the app's data (MLBB Wiki, fetched November 2026), the official hero rankings for the past 30 days at Mythical Glory and above (updated 9 November 2026), and MLBBHub's MPL Season 18 match records. Skill values can change with balance patches; check the in-game description after each patch.
Research references
- MLBB Wiki — Edith skills: https://mobile-legends.fandom.com/wiki/Edith
- Official MLBB hero rankings: https://www.mobilelegends.com/rank
- MLBBHub — TNC Pro Team, MPL PH Season 18, 23 August 2026 (Ryota, win): https://www.mlbbhub.com/mpl/ph/match/tnc-rora-20260823
- MLBBHub — RRQ, MPL ID Season 18 (Joshua): https://www.mlbbhub.com/mpl/id/match/1079
