b.q: A fearless gunslinger and sheriff, carving his own justice into the sands with grit and unwavering resolve.

b.p: On the edge of the Moniyan Empire, a small town nestled among the shifting sands began to stir with an unusual restlessness. Whispers rode the breeze, spreading rumors of a hidden treasure buried within its borders and drawing the attention of the local Sand Hunters. Before long, the imposing Blandy and his men stormed in and clashed with the town's gold prospectors. As both sides prepared for war, fear and anxiety took over the townsfolk caught in the middle.

Meanwhile, inside the restaurant, Sheriff Clint donned his worn-out coat and played the part of a carefree onlooker. He laughed and raised a mug with the prospectors, acting as if the storm brewing outside held no weight at all.
"Bah! And he calls himself a sheriff?!"
People whispered behind Clint's back, accusing him of abandoning his sworn duty. He kept silent as he drifted through the dust-filled restaurant with a wheat straw hanging from his mouth.
The tension finally boiled over one blistering afternoon.

A minor quarrel, stirred by those with hidden agendas, erupted into a shootout. In the midst of the chaos, Clint "accidentally" discharged his gun, grazing Blandy in the arm. Seizing the advantage, the gold prospectors swiftly restrained Blandy, thus leading to the swift defeat of the Sand Hunters.

But the cheers were short-lived as Blandy growled out his true identity. He was the nephew of Waldo Kane, the iron-fisted ruler of Los Pecados. Before his capture, he had sent his men for back-up, and now they've returned with a message. Should Blandy have so much as a scratch on him, Kane would wipe the town from the map of Agelta.

The threat hit the townsfolk like a sledgehammer and shattered the prospectors' bravado. They quickly loosened the ropes, offered treasures, and pleaded for Blandy's mercy. In silent agreement, they pushed the blame onto Clint. Out of fear, the entire town demanded his exile. If Clint did not leave town before sunset, the wrath of Los Pecados would fall upon them.
Amid a sea of cold indifference, Clint gathered his belongings and vanished beyond the dunes.

But Clint's exile did not settle the gunsmoke. Before long, Blandy returned, leading an even larger posse of Sand Hunters. There was no way he'd let anyone else find that treasure first. The air was thick with tension. Gold prospectors and Sand Hunters faced off like hungry beasts, each side determined to claim what was theirs.

Gunfire erupted once more through the streets, more ferocious and desperate than ever. It was a brutal shootout. Blood seeped into the yellow sand until sundown. Blandy, leaning against a shattered blade, stood amidst the wreckage, flanked by only a handful of men. He looked across the carnage, bared his bloodstained teeth, and let out a hoarse, unhinged laugh. The prospectors lay dead or scattered, and victory was his.
But was it really over?

As Blandy's laughter trailed off, a familiar figure emerged from the edge of town. In dusk's dying light, one could only see the outline of a leather jacket and the dull glimmer of a worn-out badge at his waist. He stared like a hawk as he spat out the wheat straw, one hand on his rifle, and the other drifting toward his trusty old revolver.
"You! Didn't learn your lesson, huh?! " Blandy's laughter suddenly cut off. He fixed his bloodshot eyes on the newcomer as he struggled to hoist his blade.
"Heh, I've been waiting for you. " Clint spoke in a rough yet resolute voice. "Well then, looks like justice is right on time."

Gunfire erupted as the sheriff advanced steadily, boots treading across the blood-soaked sand. From a dark alley, a figure sprang into view—it was Mathilda! Clint's hidden partner had executed the plan without a hitch. She was the one who spread rumors of the treasure to bait the two unscrupulous forces into wiping each other out. The final pieces had fallen into place. Now, it was time for the last showdown.

The empty street transformed into the final arena. Despite Blandy fighting like a frightening beast, Clint's gun was just too fast, too accurate, and too deadly. After a few precise hits, silence came over the town. Having been completely incapacitated, Blandy was dragged away by what was left of his posse.

Clint calmly reloaded his revolver as he stopped Mathilda from giving chase. He brushed the dust and blood from his jacket and polished the worn-out badge that had seen better days before fastening it back to his waist.
The plan went off without a hitch. The gold prospectors and Sand Hunters would terrorize the town no more, and the townsfolk had their peace at last.
But this isn't the end of the story. Clint turned down the townsfolk's requests to stay as their sheriff, and set off with Mathilda on the long road to Los Pecados.

The setting sun spilled crimson upon the endless sea of sand and stretched Clint's shadow into the distance. As he whistled a tuneless melody, his gaze fell upon the blurred, jagged silhouette ahead. It was the city of crime—Blandy's refuge, Waldo Kane's domain, and their inevitable battlefield.

"Chivalry is dead, and I will revive it." Clint looked toward his destination. As long as evil still festered, his gun would not rest until the last trace of darkness was crushed. Justice will prevail.

f: Power of Holy Light through healing allies and inflicting damage to enemies.; Penalizes target after death
Unnamed mother (deceased); Argus (twin brother); Unnamed mother's lover (biological father, deceased); Kaja (companion)

b.p: Rafaela and her twin brother Argus are both angels, but Argus was treated differently because of his status as a male angel. All praise was given to Rafaela, and all criticism was left to Argus. After a series of events that were left to ferment, rifts appeared in the relationship between the two siblings. Argus finally fell into the Abyss, but she was helpless to do anything about it. She is an angel whom people admire, but her brother continues to perish in pain. With the end of the Golden Era, a monstrous Abyssal fissure had once more been rent within the Land of Dawn, and from its depths dark energies surged forth again.
The dark of night was to fall once more. The Abyss loomed menacingly.

To protect this world, the Lord of Light selected a number of pure maidens to fall pregnant with angels. The legends said that only females could be angels—as such, those chosen by the Lord of Light could only give birth to girls.

Argus and Rafaela are twin siblings born in the Moniyan Empire. The Monastery of Light Sacrists forced their mother to imbibe holy water, in the name of the Lord of Light. Hence she would birth an angel in his temple. Their mother was by all means an ordinary woman, both she and her lover loyally devoted to one another. Yet under the Sacrists' supervision and persuasion, she had little choice but to accept the 'honor' given to her by the Lord of Light.

The pregnancy of one who bears an angel is an unimaginably long and slow process. Over the three-year period her heart only grew heavier, tortured by the loneliness of such a lengthy ordeal. She longed for her lover, yearned to be with him once again. After two years had passed, she could take it no more, and escaped the temple to reunite with him; together, they lived happily once more. Yet it was to be a short-lived happiness.
The Sacrists found her before long. Her lover was slain before her eyes for threatening to defile the Lord of Light's divine bloodline, and she was returned to the Monastery.
Another year passed, at the end of which she died during childbirth. To everyone's surprise, she gave birth to a set of twins: and one was a baby boy.

The infant's eyes bore a striking resemblance to those of his late mother's lover. The Cleric of Light quickly caught on to this, realizing that the boy was born of humankind – yet incredibly, he too possessed the power of the angels. The Sacrists tried to slay him but their efforts were thwarted, for each time they tried, a dazzling light would burst from Rafaela, protecting her brother from all harm.

This was considered a miracle. They hence abandoned all ideas of killing the boy. Instead, in silent unanimity, it was decided that the circumstances of his birth were to be kept a secret from everyone.
The Monastery of Light covered up the truth so masterfully that even the twins themselves knew nothing of it.

And so, Argus and Rafaela grew up together, undergoing the same teaching and training. What set them apart, however, was the fact that she was seen as a beautiful ray of light: a holy, immaculate being. In the eyes of the people, Rafaela was their one true angel. Argus was kept in the shadows, on the other hand, and forever barred from the glory so rightfully his.

Yet Rafaela loved her brother dearly, as he loved her. The two experienced entirely different treatments, and Argus was constantly warned that his only choice was to live in her shadow, yet the two were nonetheless an inseparable pair that cared deeply for one another. Both were kind-hearted to a fault, and as soon as they came of age, swore to uphold their common mission: to use their power to protect peace and spread the Light.

Praise and admiration arrived in waves, but alas, it fell only upon Rafaela. While Argus was every bit as outstanding as his sister, and like her had put tremendous effort into upholding the way of the Light, everyone's praise was directed solely at the gentle Rafaela instead. While he fought for the Light, it was in the darkness that Argus remained.

Rafaela bore witness to this, and many times wished to speak out for her brother: to change the attitude people held toward him. Not once was she successful, however. She couldn't understand: why was he treated like such an outcast? No matter how hard he tried, how great his sacrifices, they knew it all yet still treated him the same…

Rafaela was always an attentive soul, and so she soon noticed when Argus' attitude toward humankind began to change. In his eyes, human nature was a malevolent and selfish thing. This being the case, why should he even bother trying to ingratiate himself with them? The twins had several arguments concerning this, for Rafaela conversely believed that the Abyss was the root of all Darkness in life. She believed that humanity was good and kind, yet such qualities were lost once tainted by the Abyss. Neither was willing to change their standpoint, no matter how hard they tried to persuade the other.
The two diverged in terms of their individual philosophies. In time, however, their tactics on the battlefield began to differ too.

In the midst of the battle, Argus forged on tirelessly as he hungered for a swift victory, yet as a result fell into the demons' trap. Rafaela commanded that the troops retreat, but Argus disregarded her as he headed deep into the demons' nest.

Argus returned from the enemy camp with demonic blade in hand, a weapon emanating a malicious aura. An ominous dark haze swirled around him. Though Rafaela toiled to purge him of this darkness, he broke away and slayed the troops all around her before escaping.

From then on, Rafaela would tirelessly search for each and every scrap concerning her brother's whereabouts. His behavior came as no surprise to the Monastery of Light Sacrists; on the contrary, they claimed that they'd long considered him a corrupted soul and that this day was inevitable. Their words shook Rafaela to her core, and for the first time her faith was shaken also. She punished them severely, and left the Monastery of Light to find her lost brother.

Several months passed. Finally, it was in the Barren Lands that she was reunited with Argus. What she hadn't accounted for, though, was that the Argus she knew was now long gone. The golden aura in which he was once bathed, his radiant wings, they were nowhere to be seen; and in their place was an oppressive aura of cruelty and pitch-black wings of darkness.

There was no going back now... Rafaela wanted to raise her staff and bring an end to this, as was her duty. Yet memories of the past floated into her mind, one after another, and she couldn't bring herself to do it. Argus gazed at her from afar, and silently turned to leave.

From then on, he would only fall further into the darkness of the Abyss. Constantly wracked by pain and confusion, constantly sinking ever deeper. As time went on, Rafaela grew into the woman she is today: an angel admired by all, the savior of the apocalypse and embodiment of the Light. Despite this, she could never bear to face the one closest to her.
Time passes, never to return. No matter human or angel, none can turn back the hands of time.

f: Lightning Weaver; Headmaster of the Magic Academy

b.p: Eudora was born in a remote mountain village deep within the Moniyan Empire. In such a closed community, her half-elf blood and innate lightning magic made her an outcast. Discrimination and prejudice rendered her silent and withdrawn, locking herself away from the world.
Eventually, her family chose to abandon their home in search of a new start. Yet misfortune seemed determined to follow them. Eudora tragically lost her loved ones during the perilous journey north.

Thunder roared across the sky, echoing the girl's anguish, and it was this very tempest that drew the attention of Archmage Theresa, who was traveling through the area. She brought Eudora to the Magic Academy and raised her with the tender care of a devoted mentor.

The Magic Academy welcomed students of many talents and bloodlines. Among such diversity, the small half-elf found herself unremarkable. For the first time, when her lightning manifested, she met no hostile stares. The girl who had shut herself in began to cautiously emerge from her shell, tentatively exploring this new world that might truly be her own.

Until that fateful day during a magic lesson, when Eudora's lightning accidentally surged forth and tore through her opponent's robes. The singed wound and collapsed student brought back familiar gazes.
She could hear their whispers: Look, it's that monster.

Once more, the girl retreated behind her impenetrable walls. She became a ghost of herself—silent, solitary, shunning all contact and use of her magic. She barely managed to pass her classes. She wished for everyone to forget that terrible incident, to forget the monster who commanded lightning. And she succeeded. Eudora's name faded from conversations, and when anyone bothered to mention her at all, they would simply say: That talentless disciple of the Archmage.

Years passed, and a vacancy emerged for the position of headmaster at the Magic Academy. All eyes turned to Theresa, whose mastery of elemental magic had earned her great admiration. Yet the Archmage remained silent, and ultimately declined the honor. Instead, she recommended her disciple, Eudora.
"The Magic Academy needs a new vision to guide it. Eudora is better suited for this role than I."

This proclamation sent shockwaves through the academy, and that forgotten name surged back into every conversation—this time with unanimous skepticism. Theresa had long anticipated such a reaction. She publicly declared that she would engage her disciple in a public duel. Should Eudora's abilities prove insufficient to convince the doubters, Theresa would surrender her title as Archmage and depart the Magic Academy alongside her student.
For the first time in years, Eudora cast aside all concern for others' judgment, bursting into Theresa's office to confront her mentor.
"Why are you doing this?! Call off this duel!"
"This is a sacred duel of magic, Eudora. Under the solemn witness of Ursula, the Prophet of Magic, we make our choice and give everything we have. I believe in you, my disciple."
The duel proceeded as promised. Eudora took her place on one side of the arena, her gaze meeting that of her beloved mentor on the other side.

She had always been a cause of misfortune... always struggled to find her place in this world. If not for her, her parents would never have needed to flee their homeland. If not for her, her family would not have perished in that merciless blizzard. If not for her, the Archmage's reputation would remain untarnished even now—
A bolt of lightning screamed past Eudora's ear, singeing strands of her long silver hair.

"Do you have the luxury of being distracted during our duel, Eudora?" Theresa unleashed another attack, then another. Eudora scrambled to evade them, her movements clumsy with shock. The crowd watched in tense silence, eager to see how the Archmage intended to prove her disciple's abilities.

Eudora could not understand why her mentor had recommended her for the headmaster position, why Theresa proposed a duel that she would lose no matter the outcome. Lightning crackled around Eudora as she relied on pure instinct to avoid Theresa's devastating strikes.
"If all you plan to do is run, why did you step into this arena?"
Because refusing meant Theresa would forfeit her Archmage title and be exiled from the Magic Academy, of course!
"If you've truly abandoned magic, then why are your hands covered in scars?"

Eudora's fingers instinctively curled into fists. Her once-pristine palms bore a web of scars, proof of her relentless pursuit. Half-elves do not scar easily—only through repeated injuries could such marks be etched into their skin.

Eudora had never abandoned magic. On the desolate frozen plains far from the Magic Academy, streaks of lightning split the darkness every night. The girl would clench the untamed lightning with her bloodied hands, wrestling to master the most destructive elemental force.
Why not simply fade into obscurity and embrace mediocrity? Why continue on this pain-filled path when the entire world had already forgotten her?
"...Because I refuse to surrender." The words left Eudora's lips like a sacred vow.

Surrender was never in her nature. Lightning coiled around Eudora's fingertips, writhing and rebelling against her touch, desperate to break free from those deceptively fragile hands. It yearned to rend flesh and escape as it had countless times before—just like Eudora, the one deemed an outcast and a monster.
When the pain sank in, she fled. When fear consumed her, she lashed out. When despair overwhelmed her, she retreated into isolation.

But some battles cannot be avoided. She could not reshape the world or change its prejudice, so she would forge herself anew. If mockery was her burden, she would armor her heart against it. If her power threatened harm, she would gain complete control over it. If fate had cast her as an eternal outsider, she would embrace it with pride.

Lightning danced in her palms, its radiant beauty manifesting a slender magic wand—elegant and unyielding like Eudora herself... brimming with raw power! The girl raised her weapon high, and a colossal pillar of lightning erupted across the arena. In the eyes of a mage, those electric torrents pulsed with vitality and joy, singing triumphant hymns for their master.
This duel had served its purpose—the Magic Academy welcomed its new headmaster.

i: Eudora in 2019 (see BOOM: The Revial of Black Magic)

f: Spear of Dragon; Cloud Dragon; Son of Dragon (formerly)

Great Dragon (master); Ling (co-Oriental Fighter, fellow disciple, rival); Baxia, Wanwan (co-Oriental Fighters, ally); Yu Zhong, Luo Yi (enemies); Chang'e (adoptive younger sister); Zetian (companions); Saber (as Duan Meng); Master Longma; The Spirit of Cloud Dragon

b.p: Zilong was taken in by the Tianyin Swordmaster Sect when he was just a child. Although the Sect was famous for their mastery of the "Jian," Zilong chose to take up the spear. Without a teacher, he practiced the basics of the spear day in and day out with unwavering determination. After leaving the Sect, he became a disciple of the Great Dragon under the guidance of Baxia, the Mystic Tortoise, and trained at the Dragon Altar. But with the changing of the times, the spirit of the Cloud Dragon appeared on the tip of his spear one day to the surprise of his peers. That was when everyone, including Zilong, realized he had become one with the Cloud Dragon of the Oriental Fighters and inherited the Great Dragon Spear.

Even though the spear is known as the "King of Weapons," Zilong had no desire for power. No matter where he was or who he was supposed to be, Zilong was content to protect his homeland with a spear in hand. As long as he still breathed, there would be peace in the Cadia Riverlands.
"Why do you train with the spear?" Duan Meng asked Zilong in front of the other disciples.

This was the Tianyin Swordmaster Sect, after all, known as the zenith of swordsmanship in all of the Cadia Riverlands. Duan Meng had roamed the Cadia Riverlands as an assassin to perfect his skills, becoming one with his sword, and was unrivaled soon after joining the Sect.

Zilong was different. Even though he had been a disciple of the Sect since childhood, he trained only in the spear. As wave after wave of disciples advanced their training from twigs to wooden swords to blades of steel, Zilong continued practicing the basic spear moves: thrust, parry, shuttle.
"Why do I practice the spear?" Zilong contemplated while lowering his eyes, as his body continued to move on its own."I don't know."

Zilong had never thought about it. Picking up a spear was as natural as breathing to him. Does one need a reason to breathe? The onlooking disciples thought Zilong was disrespectful to Duan Meng and chided him. "Then can you stop practicing in the middle of the night? We can't rest with you making a racket."
"It is my fault. Please accept my apology."

Zilong's response was so sincere that the mob lost interest and gradually dispersed. He changed his routine after the incident—he ventured further out to train so nobody would be disturbed no matter how late it was.

Rain or shine, Zilong maintained his training. The Sect did not keep any manuals of spear techniques, so Zilong could only repeat the same basic movements, a thousand times, a hundred thousand times...
From behind Duan Meng, Master Longma answered his question. "He has the will, but not the talent..."
Indeed, he did not fit.

The Tianyin Swordmaster Sect had no place for Zilong. Thus, Zilong packed his bags and left the Sect. He had arrived alone and would depart alone. As he looked back at the mountain where the disciples used to train, he couldn't help but wonder
—Why did he choose the spear?

For Zilong, training with the spear was no different than eating and sleeping. The spear was simply a natural part of his life. When he trained, his mind was clear, and as long as he held the spear, the days felt normal.

It was only when his old friend Ling, and Baxia, the Mystic Tortoise of the Oriental Fighters, came looking for Zilong that he suddenly remembered why he chose the spear. It was when Ling's life was in danger during a mission for the Finch Sect. At that time, Zilong felt an extra weight on the spear that he had swung countless times. But it was not a physical weight... it was something else, something deep inside. And as if something had taken over him, with a fiery resolve and clear mind, he managed to save Ling.

Baxia came here specifically for Zilong. He talked about how Zilong was the chosen successor of the Cloud Dragon, and Ling was inextricably linked to the Vermillion Bird. Since the time of the Endless War, the Four Immortals went into deep slumber and their power has been passed down amongst the disciples of the Great Dragon. When a mortal is chosen by an Immortal, they become an Oriental Fighter and take on the duty of protecting the Cadia Riverlands.
As Baxia told the ancient tale, Zilong listened and pondered, then finally understood why he picked up the spear back then and followed Baxia and Ling into the Dragon Altar.
Baxia took them in as disciples in place of his master and the three of them became like brothers, watching over the Dragon Altar together.

Ling was the most talented. He was ethereal and swift with the sword like the wind, and his progress was rapid. Zilong continued to train silently like his time in the Tianyin Swordmaster Sect: carrying out each motion with unwavering determination. Ling would often seek out Zilong to spar and exchange techniques with him, but Zilong never won once.
"You've been swinging that spear day in and day out without making any progress. What are you training for?"
Ling asked after finishing their sparring one day.
"Do I need a reason to master the spear?" Zilong seemed to have returned to the time when he was in the Tianyin Swordmaster Sect.
"Everything we do has a reason. Whether it's to chase fame, fortune, life, death... There's always a reason."
"Then what are you chasing?"
Zilong thought for sure that Ling would give him an answer that could guide his own path, but Ling simply leaped into the air and disappeared behind the roof tiles.
Zilong did not get an answer. Ling stood across from him and drew his sword.

On that day, Ling touched the Black Dragon seal in the Dragon Altar and Baxia was forced to confront him. Unable to stop the fight and unwilling to hurt either side, Zilong drew a small portion of the Cloud Dragon's power in desperation. His spear soared like a dragon and exuded overwhelming strength, and Zilong was able to deflect Ling and Baxia's attacks with one swing.
Zilong, who had never won a sparring match against his brothers, sent both of them staggering backward. Surrounded by green silhouettes, Zilong fell into a trance.
While his mind was still a blur, he saw Baxia standing in front of him, looking at Ling warily. He then shifted his eyes to Ling, who looked at him coldly.
"For the mission."This was Ling's answer: "For the Finch Sect, the harder the mission, the sharper the blade that completes it. That's all."
Night came. As the sword and spear came into contact, Ling turned and departed.
Zilong wanted Ling to stay; he wanted to tell Baxia that there was no need to worry, but it was as if he was caught in a vast illusion. Then, a majestic voice echoed across heaven and earth.
"Why do you practice the spear?"
The scene when he drew his spear played over and over in Zilong's mind until he finally was able to answer that question.
"For me."
"What is 'me'?"
"The spear is me, and I am the spear. I will follow my heart and protect what's dear to me."
A long sigh can be heard, partly of approval, and partly of resignation.
"When the mind is clear, the spirit is whole. Continue on the path of the righteous and protect this world."
—the Cloud Dragon's parting words.
Zilong opened his eyes as power surged around him before settling down.
He thanked Baxia who had been watching over him and looked towards the direction that Ling went. He knew that Ling would return one day, and he had prepared his answer.

Saving one person or protecting this land... both are one and the same. He would protect heaven and earth wherever his spear was needed, as long as he still breathed, and keep the Cadia Riverlands safe.
Tranquillity returned to the Dragon Altar and Zilong picked up the spear, practicing the most basic moves...
As in many years past, and many more to come.

f: Tigreal (older brother, Lightborn co-member); Silvanna, Alucard, Granger, Harith (Lightborn co-members); Claude, Clint (companions)

b.p: Fanny is the younger sister of Tigreal, who grew up under the protection of her family and her elder brother since she was a child. But Tigreal took the blame for a mistake in battle and left home. Disregarding obstructions from her family, Fanny joined the army, and through her own designed weapons, she successfully completed one task after another, becoming an outstanding fighter who can take care of herself. Fanny Wertz is the youngest daughter of the Wertz family and the youngest sister of Tigreal. Although the men of the Wertz family served in the army for generations and guarded the Moniyan Empire, the female members of the family were never allowed to join the army. From the perspective of the men in the family, their duty was to protect the country and family from threats, and women were to stay away from war.

Therefore, ever since she was a child, Fanny had been asked to study painting and design art. The elders of the family hoped that she could become a famous artist or designer, and help manage the family’s business. But Fanny regarded this as beneath her. From ever since she could remember, Tigreal was Fanny’s greatest hero. She also hoped that one day, like her brother, she could fight on the front lines for the Imperial Army and guard the empire.

After she grew older, the active and rebellious Fanny became a nightmare for her tutor. She was very tired of these old-fashioned classes. She often ran away for various reasons and had a soft spot for dancing with weapons: but Fanny was so smart that even though she was tired of her lessons, she was able to gain an understanding in very short time. Tigreal showed extreme affection to his rebellious sister. Each time Tigreal returned to the Lumina City for repair and maintenance with the army, it was Fanny’s happiest day, because Tigreal would not only tell her some peculiar anecdotes and thrilling battlefield stories from various places, but also teach her some useful fighting skills, which made Fanny yearn even more for the military life.
However, Tigreal firmly refused Fanny’s desire to join the army as he always did. He did not want his only sister to be in danger.

Out of love for his younger sister, Tigreal promised that when Fanny turned 18, he would take her to the base of the Light’s Order to show her what it was like, so this expedition had special meaning for both Tigreal and Fanny. However, just as Fanny was awaiting the triumphant return of her brother day and night, some news came from the front lines: Although the battle against the frontier demons was won, Tigreal, who lead the Second Division of the Light’s Order, had left his ranks for unknown reasons and disappeared.

While the empire was holding a national celebration, the Wertz family entered a crisis. For a time, deserters and cowards replaced heroes and commanders, and these words became synonymous with Tigreal. The Wertz family, once famous throughout Moniyan, was discredited. On the one hand, she worshiped her beloved brother, and the other hand, there were overwhelming rumors. In the face of all this, Fanny fell into confusion, but after the confusion, she told herself in her heart: my brother is no coward, let alone a deserter. In his absence, I must stand up and revitalize the glory of the Wertz family.

Afterwards, despite the fierce opposition from her mother and other elders, Fanny resolutely chose to join the army. She wanted to use her actions to protect the dignity of her brother and the Wertz family. But it did not go as smoothly as she had imagined. When Fanny came to the barracks, she was greeted with laughter and derision: the soldiers were fully of prejudice against this pampered noble lady, and life in the barracks was far more difficult than she imagined. The heavy training and lack of material conditions made it difficult for Fanny, who was used to a privileged life. For this reason, Fanny got rid of her long hair that she loved, devoted twice as much effort to training, and successfully passed the recruitment test. She was incorporated into the scout unit of the Imperial Garrison.

Several years into her scouting career, Fanny had truly grown and transformed. As an imperial scout, Fanny often needed to roam between various steep mountains or other difficult terrain. In order to overcome her physical and strength shortcomings, she inconceivably learned from Tigreal, combining her fighting skills with the design knowledge she learned before by designing and building a pair of long swords with steel cables for herself. When she pulled the trigger, the steel cables would shoot from the hilt, grab on to the target, and pull Fanny over towards it. After endless practice, Fanny finally mastered the sword, and with it, she shuttled between the cliffs, gracefully skimming all kinds of difficult and complicated terrain, successfully completing her missions again and again. Her performance not only convinced those who were full of contempt and prejudice against her before, but also won her respect and prestige. For her graceful and exquisite figure as she danced through the air, the soldiers kindly called her the “Blade Dancer”.

With her outstanding performance in the garrison, Fanny finally obtained the qualifications needed to be selected into the Light’s Order. Even more surprisingly, Tigreal, her older brother who had been away from the Moniyan Empire for many years, also returned to his homeland from the distant Northern Vale. Seeing what his sister had done for the family, Tigreal praised Fanny, believing that she had become a great warrior, and invited her to stay by his side and fight shoulder to shoulder.
Travelers on the Land of Dawn, if you see a person flying by in the mountains and forests like a free bird, you must have seen Fanny’s graceful and swift figure.

In Eruditio—the City of Scholars, there's hardly anyone who doesn't know of Layla. She's the "daughter of Eruditio", just like a bright star that shines over the streets of Eruditio in the darkness of night. Brave and selfless, she always had a bright and happy smile on her face while toting the gun handed to her by her grandfather, protecting Eruditio in her own way. As a child, Layla would always ask her grandfather about her parents, but his reluctance to tell her and his sad face told her it was something tragic. Because of that, Layla decided to never pain her grandfather anymore, so she stopped pursuing the matter. However, as secrets cannot be hidden forever, the truth of her birth eventually surfaced, and it turns out that her parents have always been watching her from the skies—well, in the literal sense. center|512px "Layla Grant, a prominent member of the Eruditio Rangers, bravely protected the core of Eruditio tech—the Starlium Reactor during a vicious attack on Eruditio just a day earlier. While her actions protected civilization, it also proved that the youth of the city possessed resilience and perseverance and that the love and belonging for this home they shared was the life force flowing through the veins of Eruditians. Thus, the honorary title of "Shining Star" was given to her."

This year, the title of Shining Star was not awarded to a Scholar, but to a member of the Eruditio Rangers. and it was no other than the "daughter of Eruditio". She grew up in the streets of Eruditio, and every Scholar in the Spire of Knowledge had experienced her mischievous nature at some or other. Somehow though, the trouble she caused would miraculously help a Scholar breakthrough in their research. Other times, Layla would suddenly try to strike a deal on behalf of the traders with her funny accent when they find it difficult to converse with foreign visitors. Every porter at the docks has also enjoyed her assistance in one way or another. Like an ever-diligent watchman, she watches over the city like a shining star.

Meanwhile, Layla's only blood relative; the old but still strong-as-a-bull, former captain of the Eruditio Rangers, Thomas, had never shown signs of joy. Sitting in a backlit room, his silhouette was like the distant shadow of the lofty mountains. Stroking an old-fashioned gun, he looked imposing yet desolate.

Holding a crying baby in his arms, Thomas' beloved daughter vanished behind the "Infinite Gateway" that turned into stardust in the sky, leaving him only this precious little thing. As if she knew what was going on, her cries echoed into the night sky endlessly. Hurriedly, he ran home with the infant in his arms as the morning star in the east gradually rose. He didn't want the daylight to hurt her as the protection of the night was fading fast. He had lost a daughter for the dawn of mankind, and the one in his arms was all he had left.
He would swaddle the baby in the cloak of darkness in order to hide her, naming her after night—Layla.

Over time, she grew up and was such a delight to Thomas' barren life. She loved both the sky and the earth, and her little life was always bursting with joyful energy. Because of this, Thomas' face once marked by pain began to smile again. He picked up the equipment from his youth when he was still a young Ranger, and together with Layla, he leaped from the ground and flew across the skyline of Eruditio, becoming the biggest headache for the young Eruditio Rangers. What were these poor lads supposed to do, chase down and arrest the old man whose face is printed on the Ranger's rulebook? She was everything to Thomas—dawn, high noon, and dusk. But deep down, she still wanted to know her parents.
"It's a tragedy that they had to die during the meteor crash. Hey, why don't you check out Grandpa's newly fine-tuned weapon for you? It's got three times the firepower of the previous one!"

'When Layla's ponytails reached her shoulders, she stopped asking him about her parents because she couldn't bear to see the sadness and evasiveness in her grandfather's eyes any longer. She soon realized that the grandfather who never left her side always left the house before dawn one day each year. So, Layla followed him quietly and discovered the answer to her question. He had gone to a cemetery to pay his respects to a woman named Lillian, a name Layla had seen in an old newspaper, and which had appeared in an official obituary of the Spire of Knowledge. She was a great Scholar who died for the advancement of Eruditio. Layla realized it was her mother, and that knowledge made her proud beyond measure, but she was also saddened by the thought that they could never be together. The tombstone next to Lillian had no name or photo but just a line—I'll hold your hands amidst the starry sky.

Layla understood that her grandfather wanted to erase all traces of her parents from her life so that she'd never have to grieve. Though Layla understood, she still wanted to leave a little door in her heart for the woman named Lillian, so that if Lillian ever missed her, she could still visit her in dreams. As for the mysterious man's tombstone, since she didn't have a single clue at all as to who he was, she hoped that he'd one day walk through that little door with her mother and finally reveal his true identity.

In her heart. Layla vowed that she'd remember her mother no matter what, and that she would protect Eruditio—the city which mother had laid her life down for. In her grandfather's eyes, Layla was on a very different path from her mother. She disliked studying and flunked every single test she sat for, but she was strong, and no scoundrel had ever walked away without learning a lesson. However. this was just great news to her grandfather, because that way she'd never end up a Scholar, sacrificing herself for the future of humanity. And most important of all, she'd never share the same fate as... Lillian.

So when Thomas learned that Layla almost died protecting Eruditio, he went into the room that he had sealed for 15 years and sat in there for a long while. The entire life of Lillian played back in his mind. She was incredibly passionate, intelligent, and courageous, and she was also protecting Eruditio in her own way. She was the brightest star in the sky, and they were exactly the same.
"Hey, Grandpa."

The girl's timid voice sounded in the doorway, and a sash was seen hanging across her body. It seemed that the treatment at the Spire of Knowledge had restored her body perfectly. However, Layla was filled with guilt as she knew the lengths her grandfather would go through for her, even for just a little scratch. So, this time, since she had been severely injured while protecting Eruditio, she expected her grandfather to get really angry...
But he just held her tightly to him, his entire body trembling violently.
"Your mother would be so proud of you."

Thomas handed Layla the gun he had locked away in the cabinet—a prototype gun left by Lillian. For 15 years, he could not bear to see any trace of Lillian, but he forgot that the girl in front of him was the deepest trace Lillian had left him with.
"If you want to protect Eruditio, then you'll need to do it with the strongest firepower. This is a gun... that your mother and father made. So--hold it tight and protect yourself with it!"

With the malefic gun in Layla's hands, no evil stands a chance in front of her. As if the stars would always guide her, whenever Layla is holding her gun, she feels that Lillian is just beside her. Even that nameless man, too, is there for her.

In olden times, there was once a state named Minoa in Agelta Drylands. The prince in the state, Minotaur fatally injured his father in a fit of rage, after which he exiled himself to the Minoan Labyrinth in shame and regret. When he stepped out of the Labyrinth again, he found his state had long perished, his kin long gone. With his teeth set, Monitor embark on the path to restoring his homeland to its former glory. In olden times, the Minoans founded a mysterious and prosperous state named Minoa in Agelta Drylands.

The once-bustling Emerald Road connected Minoa with other western cities, creating a network of trade routes, while Minoa stood tall among all others with its advanced civilization and martial traditions.

Prince Minotaur of Minoa was the most esteemed warrior back then. Passionate about fighting and often fueled by his rage, Minotaur would demonstrate terrifying bursts of strength in battle. Few were those who could even hope to last more than a few rounds against him.

The people grew to worship Minotaur, yet his father was deeply concerned about him. While reaping great success on the battlefield, Minotaur's savagery and impulsive behavior was unbecoming of the successor of the state.

To forge Minotaur into a suitable heir to the throne, the old king arranged for a special trial-one in which the prince must defeat a mysterious figure from foreign lands to qualify for the throne of Minoa.

Minotaur accepted this unarmed duel without hesitation. He stepped onto the arena with his head held high and attempted to crush his opponent with brute force as he'd always done. However, his opponent this time was much tougher, and Minotaur had soon exhausted himself, losing his advantage.
In the end, the mysterious figure defeated the "invincible" Minotaur with measured counterattacks.
The crowd cheered for the strong and graceful victor, yet Minotaur was overwhelmed by rage and shame.

And when the mysterious figure stretched out his hand to help Minotaur get back to his feet, Minotaur grabbed the unsuspecting hand and pinned the grabbed the unsuspecting hand and pinned the mysterious figure to the ground, before throwing a series of vicious punches at him.

As his fists were covered in blood and the mysterious figure stopped struggling, Minotaur tore off the latter's mask amidst the boos of the crowd-and that was when his whole body stiffened. The severely injured figure on the ground was actually his father!

The old king grasped Minotaur's hand with his last strength and uttered his final words of instruction to his son, "You must learn to shoulder the responsibility as a king and continue the glory of Minoa..."
Consumed by shame and regret, Minotaur headed to the Minoan Labyrinth-the burial ground of the Minoan ancestors-and began his training and repentance.
Over time, Minotaur gradually gained control over his rage and became able to tap into his raging powers at will.

As Minotaur thrust himself into this arduous training, an unexpected catastrophe struck. The entire Minoa. was flattened by the explosion of the Twilight Orb, and only Minotaur was left unharmed under the protection of the Labyrinth. Minotaur rushed toward the state amidst the tremors, wanting to find out what had happened, when a broken piece from the Twilight Orb plummeted into the Labyrinth and sealed it whole. Minotaur, who was half a step out of the Labyrinth, was sealed altogether and put into a deep slumber.

The catastrophe erased all traces of the Minoan civilization, leaving only the Minoan Labyrinth half-hidden in the sand. After countless days and nights, the broken piece from the Twilight Orb turned into Lunox and left.
The seal was then lifted. Time in the Labyrinth began to flow again, while Minotaur slowly opened his eyes....
Aldous, the guardian of the Labyrinth, told Minotaur his state had long turned into dust, and he and his memories were all that remained. Minotaur, however, would believe none of those.
With his father's final entrustment still fresh in his mind, the prince vowed to himself that he must find his lost kin and rebuild the Minoan civilization.
In the boundless sands, a set of hoof-prints extended into the horizon...

f: Noumenon Energy Core; Provide shield for her team; Summons a shield from her hammer
Dr. Rooney; Bruno, Chou, Ixia, Johnson, Layla, Diggie, Kimmy, Nolan (companions); X.Borg (enemies); Bane (know of)

b.q: Member of the Eruditio Rangers and protector of the Leviathan workshop.

b.p: Lolita was a gentle and tenacious half-elf girl. After she was rescued from the war and brought to Eruditio, she became a craftsman in the workshop. But she had an uncommon ambition: to join the Eruditio Rangers and fight like those who had rescued her. However, every battle proved to be overwhelming for her, because although she was a good fighter, she couldn't bear to hurt anyone. During an attack on the workshop, Lolita protected the Noumenon Energy Core with her body and was severely wounded. It was through this incident that her courage was acknowledged by the Eruditio Rangers, and they decided to take her in. Eventually, she understood that it didn't matter if one had destructive powers, because protecting too requires courage, and gentleness itself is also strength. Are you curious as to how steel is made?
"First of all, you'll need raw materials and the best iron ores from the Business District..."
After reading just one line, Lolita threw the book away.
"Isn't there a way to make steel without using iron ores?"

Just so that you don't get the wrong idea, Lolita wasn't trying to be unreasonable. In fact, she usually comes across as gentle and understanding. Of course, she wasn't trying to invent a new way of making steel, but more of a way to 'strengthen herself'. She was always looking for ways to make herself as powerful, formidable, and indestructible as steel...

Because then she would be able to protect everyone. Lolita was a half-elf—except for her pointy ears, she was literally no different than an ordinary human. She was born in a village that was later destroyed by war, and from that devastating night, she was the sole survivor. When she finally regained consciousness, the City of Scholars—Eruditio welcomed her with warmth, passion, and freedom that protected her like a beast of steel for the rest of her life.

Later, Leviathan Workshop took her in. It's the center of applied technology in Eruditio, where the dreams of all scholars were realized. If the Spire of Knowledge was the brain of the city, then the workshop was the heart, supplying the blood of technology to the entire city. Though the fancy concepts and odd job craftsmen had little to do with Lolita, she occupied herself with as much as she could each day, and even when the tasks were dull and insignificant, she would still give her very best.

Occasionally, she'd stare with fascination at the blazing red Noumenon Energy Core—the precious Starlium Reactor, which was also the power source of the workshop. It wasn't just any ordinary workshop furnace, because it also served as the power generator for Eruditio. And as long as it remained burning, Eruditio would never stop advancing.

Lolita lived in the workshop, and the warmth of the blaze had always accompanied her to sleep. Every time she recalled the night when the war broke out, the souls of the dead would always let out a painful wail that haunted her. And whenever this happened, a large and impenetrable figure of steel would always stand before her, leading her to the warmth of Eruditio.

Though Lolita couldn't remember his face, she clearly recalled that he had an unknown marking on his back that resembled a tree. So, Lolita concluded that it must be a tree that grew in the desert, and that the tree served as the hope of an oasis ahead.
But when she learned that it was the symbol of the Eruditio Rangers, Lolita made up her mind to join them and protect the city as they did.

So she began to train herself, and it took her exactly 49 trials for her to finally accept the cruel reality that she wasn't good at fighting. Her gentleness proved a disadvantage on the battlefield, she wasn't able to maneuver freely and repel the ruthless and destructive attacks, and even the shield magic from her elven blood didn't make her a more intimidating opponent.

She looked at her small, thin arms that couldn't even lift the slightly larger hammer, but that was her —a "chunk of low-grade ore that probably didn't contain any iron in it". She sighed deeply, disappointed in herself for having no talents whatsoever.
She thought that since she didn't have the talent, she'd make up for it with time, but fate never waits for anyone.

Late that night, Lolita was awoken by an explosion, and she saw the workshop go up in flames. An unidentified enemy had launched a surprise attack. Fierce gunfire broke out everywhere, and though all defense machinery was activated, they failed to repel the enemy's invasion. The guarding craftsmen covered Lolita and retreated to the core—the last line of defense. If the Noumenon Energy Core is damaged, the consequences would be unthinkable.

Suddenly, Lolita saw her past flash before her eyes. It was as if she was back in her childhood village lit up by war. The same moans of pain, the same helpless eyes, and the same weakness that required protection. Sorrow, guilt, cowardice, anger... a mix of emotions surfaced, but her body froze.
Sure enough, a "low-grade ore" like her will never become "steel"...
She became determined and looked into the still-blazing core.
"Is there really no way to make steel without iron ores?"
"There is. The element of iron can be found everywhere in nature, but is only revealed under extreme heat... Can you bear it?"

Wordlessly, her body started to move. Everything around her stood still—the sound of gunfire, explosions, and shouting faded away, and there was only one target in her eyes: the Noumenon Energy Core. No matter the cost, she will protect this land...
Suddenly, a blinding light shot straight up into the sky, and that was the flames of life.
After an indeterminate amount of time, Lolita struggled to open her eyes, and standing in front of her was that tree, the tall figure.
"What... did I do?" Lolita mumbled.
"You touched the core with your bare hands and it's a miracle you're even alive." said the man with awe.
"The surging energy of the core penetrated your body and miraculously activated the shield magic in your blood that protected the workshop..."
"You saved us, and you deserve to be recognized for your courage. As the captain, I now welcome you to the Eruditio Rangers."
"But I'm weak, and I don't know how to fight..."
"Fighting is not the only way, because protecting is equally important, and we need you." After saying that, he turned around and walked out the door.
"Don't worry about the rest."
He smiled and said, "Eruditio is a place where miracles happen."

With the technology of Eruditio, Lolita was given a pair of mechanical gloves with great powers. The workshop even crafted a sledgehammer for her from a fragment of the Noumenon Energy Core—a symbol of the workshop's will and an affirmation of her courage. Since the core was integrated with elven magic during the invasion, she could now work with it effortlessly.

With the courage to use her body as a shield, Lolita became a member of the Eruditio Rangers. Though she was the youngest, she took good care of everyone, and whenever danger arise, she'd always rush to the frontlines.
So, are you still curious as to how steel is made? That's no longer important. Because her courage and gentleness have become stronger than steel, forever protecting the city.

f: Unnamed father; Kurēn (elder brother, deceased); Hanabi (childhood sweetheart); Kagura (close as siblings); Hanzo, Hirara (enemies)

b.p: As the second heir to the Shadow Sect of the Scarlet Shadow, Hayabusa had always looked up to his brother, a figure who he saw as the moon itself. To preserve the delicate balance of power between the Shadow and Scarlet Sects, Hayabusa willingly took his brother's place to be a political pawn and hostage, to be raised within the rival Scarlet Sect. Every day spent in the Scarlet Sect, Hayabusa lived by his brother's principles. He mastered his unique Shadow Shuriken technique and forged an unbreakable bond with Hanabi, a kunoichi of the Scarlet Sect. But when Hanzo's betrayal and his brother's disappearance shattered their hopes for peace, Hayabusa realized that the moonlight that had always guided him was gone. Yet, he gripped his blade firmly, determined to forge ahead through the shadows, following his brother's nindo. When clouds obscure the moon,
Where shall shadows find their place?

As descendants of the Shadow Sect, Hayabusa and his brother underwent rigorous training from childhood. Even as a young boy, Hayabusa knew his brother's skills far surpassed his own. But what truly seemed beyond his reach was his brother's vision of nindo, the ninja way: integrating ninja tools with ninjutsu to end the hostility between ninja clans.
In Hayabusa's eyes, his brother shone as bright as the moon, illuminating not only himself but all of the Scarlet Shadow. Hayabusa only wished to be his shadow.

However, his brother wasn't the only genius in the Shadow Sect—there was another named Hanzo. Soon, the Scarlet Sect, the other half of the Scarlet Shadow, sent a warning to the Shadow Sect: the balance of power in the Scarlet Shadow must not be challenged. Hayabusa learned that the two sects would use their own bloodlines as pawns to keep each other in check, and either he or his brother would have to become that pawn.
On the rooftop, Hayabusa found his brother. Though no words were spoken, the moonlight bridged their hearts.
To Hayabusa, the world could survive without shadows, but without moonlight, the night would reign eternal...
Sitting beside his brother, Hayabusa removed his mask. A childlike smile broke through his stern countenance.

In his first years at the Scarlet Sect, Hayabusa, as a pawn, was met with contempt. He found companionship only in his own shadow. During training, he constantly worked to integrate ninja tools with his ninjutsu, creating his unique Shadow Shuriken technique. Gradually, more and more people came to challenge him. Hayabusa calmly accepted each challenge and silently departed after each victory. For him, winning or losing mattered less than fulfilling his brother's will—ending the hostility between the two sects.

Until one day, he met a girl whose convictions rivaled his own—Hanabi. As the successor of "Scarlet," Hanabi always held her head high. She saw her victories as victories for the Scarlet Sect, and her fierce competitive spirit drove her to challenge Hayabusa again and again. Hidden valleys, bamboo forests, rooftops... Every corner of the Scarlet Shadow bore witness to their battles. Every time Hayabusa won, Hanabi would ask,"Why did I lose...", but he would only shrug in return.

Hayabusa had long accepted that he possessed no extraordinary talent. In pursuit of his brother's nindo, he trained alone, until he finally understood that the relationship between ninja tools and ninjutsu was like that of scarlet and shadow—two sides of the same coin. They were inseparable. The Scarlet Sect and Shadow Sect surely knew this too, yet they chose to remain fixated on winning over each other.
But illusions will eventually shatter.

The genius ninja Hanzo broke into the forbidden grounds, stole the sealed weapon Ame no Habakiri, and fled. Hayabusa's brother, who had gone with him, vanished without a trace. Overnight, Hanzo became the Scarlet Shadow's greatest threat, and peace teetered on a blade's edge.
To capture Hanzo and retrieve the cursed weapon, both sects dispatched their best, and both Hayabusa and Hanabi were among them.

Before departing, Hayabusa received a secret order from his father: "Reclaim the Ame no Habakiri for the Shadow Sect, and kill Hanzo and anyone else who stands in your way." Strangely, the order made no mention of his brother. Filled with doubt, Hayabusa tracked Hanzo's trail—he had to find him.

During his pursuit, Hayabusa discovered Hanabi lying on the ground, surrounded by ninjas from both sects writhing in agony. As Hayabusa tried to wake Hanabi, a malevolent aura struck at him. He gripped his blade tightly. Then, he saw a familiar yet strange figure—it was his brother, radiating with murderous intent.
He saw blood staining his brother's hands... He saw the light had vanished from his eyes...
No matter how Hayabusa called out, he was met only with increasingly violent attacks, each aimed to kill.
Never had Hayabusa imagined the moon could become so blood-red.
Darkness engulfed Hayabusa's heart. He lowered his blade as his brother rushed toward him.
"Hayabusa, don't you dare lose to anyone but me!"
Hanabi's voice echoed in his memory, like a flame igniting in his heart.
Deep within, Hayabusa saw the moonlight, and beneath it, Hanabi.
Hanabi's eyes burned as she looked at Hayabusa while gently twirling her Higanbana, "I'm going to surpass you."

In that instant, Hayabusa regained consciousness. With one hand, he formed a seal, activating Quad Shadow to send forth four shadows that restrained his opponent with lightning speed. He gripped his blade and struck without a moment of hesitation.
Hayabusa watched as the murderous aura gradually dissipated along with his brother's image, revealing Ame no Habakiri's true form, glaring with rage and laughing maniacally.

The cunning Ame no Habakiri had tried to use illusions to exploit the weakness in human hearts, only to encounter such resilience within. Breaking free from the illusion, Hayabusa was no longer bound by the darkness. Though he knew Ame no Habakiri was powerful, behind him stood Hanabi, Kagura, and the unknown fate of his brother. He had no choice but to stand up.
Even without the moon's guidance, a shadow must forge its own path.
"Wherever I shall go, I do so without fear."

f: Frozen Sea warriors (allied); Black Shark Pirates (hostile)
Sword and shield which can turn into a battleaxe
Bringing fallen warriors to Valhalla; Turns into Valkyrie mode
Skuld (elder sister, fate unknown); Franco (companions); Bane, Atlas (enemies); Popol and Kupa (companions); Hilda (rescued); Aurora

b.p: Since the fall of the previous Valkyrie and disappearance of the Aurora Heart, Sessrumnir's sacred legacy, Freya has embarked upon an arduous quest to uncover the truth and reclaim their lost relic. Through howling winds and endless snow she journeyed, her sword ever at her side, driven by unwavering faith to protect Northern Vale as she rescues countless souls trapped within the merciless snowstorms. In time, the lost Valkyrie tradition blazed anew within Freya's heart, echoing the founder of Sessrumnir from times long forgotten. With the aurora as her guide and the tundra as her witness, Freya carved her glory into the wind and ice, and cast her body into an invincible weapon to become the new Valkyrie.
What is the Valkyrie?
"What is the Valkyrie?" As smoke began to rise from Sessrumnir's sacred halls, this question—one that had haunted Freya's thoughts for so long—surfaced once more in her troubled heart.

"...The Valkyrie is a legacy." When Freya was but a child, her sister Skuld—newly chosen as the next Valkyrie—took her small hand in hers, and together they grasped the ancient sword and shield. Little Freya could not yet comprehend the fierce light burning in her sister's eyes, but she felt, for the first time, the profound weight of the sword and shield pressing into her palms.

Fate, however, is a cruel and fickle thing. Years later, Skuld perished during a perilous mission, and with her death came the disappearance of the Aurora Heart—that sacred relic preserved in Sessrumnir for countless centuries, the very embodiment of Northern Vale's strength and heritage. The people mourned Skuld's sacrifice, yet whispers began to slither through the blizzards like poison: some dared to brand Skuld a failure, an incompetent Valkyrie who had betrayed Northern Vale itself. Freya spoke no words in her sister's defense. Instead, she simply tightened her grip upon her sword and shield—as though she were clasping her sister's hand once more.

She stepped forth into the endless, howling blizzard, her heart set upon recovering the lost Aurora Heart. Never would she allow her sister's hands—hands worn raw from protecting others—to be stained with the mark of treachery, nor would she permit the sacred title of "Valkyrie" to fade into the vast and merciless snowstorm.
Sword in hand, Freya pressed onward through the endless expanse of Northern Vale, gathering the myriad answers to a single, haunting question: "What is the Valkyrie?"
The common folk whispered that the Valkyrie was salvation incarnate. She had raised her blade high amidst the bloody feuds of the Garland tribe, rescuing Hilda and her kinsmen from certain doom.

The battle-scarred warriors proclaimed that the Valkyrie is glory made manifest. Had she not braved the treacherous Frozen Sea, forging an alliance with Franco to shield innocent fishermen from Bane's relentless attacks?
Yet countless others throughout Northern Vale declared that the Valkyrie is faith itself—for within Sessrumnir's hallowed halls burns a forge powered by the sacred Aurora Heart.

Here, for the first time, Freya uncovered the true genesis of the Valkyrie legacy: Eons ago, when the world was young, the Frost Giants raised a mighty forge deep within the snowbound wilderness to defy the two gods themselves, blessing Northern Vale with eternal spring. But the gods' wrath was swift and merciless—glaciers descended like divine judgment, shattering the forge and leaving the northern lands broken and bleeding. Only when Sigrun, the first Valkyrie—a half-giant of legendary prowess—wielded a fragment of the Twilight Orb called the Aurora Heart to rekindle the forge's dying embers did Northern Vale draw breath once more. Sigrun entrusted this sacred power to the most valiant of female warriors, charging them to guard both homeland and the Aurora Heart. Future generations would know them by a single, revered name—Valkyries.
Through the howling wind and swirling snow, Freya gazed upon Sessrumnir in the distance. It stood cold and silent, like Northern Vale's own heart, frozen and still.
Though her relentless pursuit had yet to reveal the whereabouts of the Aurora Heart, Freya drew ever closer to the terrible truth behind her sister's sacrifice.

The glaciers, born of the God of Light's divine will, had drawn countless devotees who transformed them into strongholds, expanding their deity's dominion across the realm—even inadvertently nurturing the birth of the divine maiden Aurora. After the Endless War's conclusion, these followers of light vanished like phantoms, only to resurface years later with treacherous intent. They laid cunning traps that claimed Skuld's life, and in the ensuing chaos, the Aurora Heart disappeared into legend. Yet the followers' dark ambitions remained unbroken—they sought to drain the forge's very essence and destroy it utterly, clearing all obstacles for the God of Light's inevitable return.
Thick, choking smoke was billowing from Sessrumnir's sacred halls!

When Freya reached the battlefield, Sessrumnir lay in utter ruin. The followers of light were greedily siphoning the forge's power with reckless abandon. The Northern Vale warriors fought desperately against overwhelming odds, while the aurora-hued flames within the forge flickered ever weaker. Deep tremors shook the land's very foundation—everything teetered on the precipice of collapse...

Spotting Freya's arrival as reinforcement, the followers of light prepared to flee like cowards. Every fiber of Freya's being screamed to pursue them, to exact vengeance for her fallen sister—but the forge's power was hemorrhaging away, demanding her presence to safeguard Northern Vale's very survival.
How could she choose between revenge and duty? Freya's gaze fell upon those dying aurora flames—
The forge demanded sustenance; only new energy could reignite its sacred fire.
—With resolve burning in her heart and defiance coursing through her veins, Freya charged toward the forge's dying light.
"...What is the Valkyrie?"
Within the swirling dance of aurora and flame, her sister Skuld's ethereal form materialized once more, her spectral hand tenderly clasping Freya's own.
"You have already given your answer."
At last, Freya understood the radiant light that had always burned within her sister's eyes.

For a thousand years, when the two gods cast down their glacial curse to freeze Northern Vale in eternal winter, the people kept the forge burning and built Sessrumnir's mighty walls around it. Generation upon generation of Valkyries had fought within these hallowed halls, had bled and died here—they faced death without fear, knowing that the roaring flames of the forge would recast their essence into weapons of unimaginable power, to be passed down to the next Valkyrie.
Now, Freya too embraced that eternal duty and cast herself into the flames.

Her sacrifice earned her recognition from the collective will of every Valkyrie who had come before, whose spirits still dwelled within the forge—but in truth, she had long gained Northern Vale's blessing. Not through the Aurora Heart, but like Sigrun, the very first Valkyrie: with the aurora as her guide and the tundra as her witness, Freya carved her glory into the wind and ice, and cast her body into an invincible weapon.

Freya's sword and shield, clutched tight in her grasp, were reforged as a halberd amid the roaring flames, while golden wings spread majestically behind her. Having passed the final trial, she returned to Sessrumnir as the glorious Valkyrie. Sword raised high, she pursued the fleeing followers of light—this was her vengeance, her duty, and her answer.
"I am a daughter of Northern Vale, and I will defend this land to the death!"

f: Professor of the Mystic; Dean of the Icarus School of the Magic Academy
Elward (mentor); Eudora (colleague); Valir (ex-apprentice); Harley, Lylia (students); Guinevere (possible student)

b.q: Dean of the Icarus School of the Magic Academy

b.p: Gord has always been the living proof of excellence in the magic academy. He was born with the gift to manipulate the mystic powers which allowed him to master several sophisticated spells at an early age. But this is clearly a double-edged sword as Gord became increasingly arrogant over time. Once he stumbled across a forbidden book in the academy which recorded the method to forge the pure mystic existence out of human body using mystic powers.

The young wizard buried himself in the book and launched his study without respecting the opinions from the outside. It worked out successfully in the beginning, the pure mystic energy started to flow in Gord's veins, thus he was able to cast even more powerful spells. Unfortunately, Gord was not able to control this power and he became overwhelmed with mystic energy. Gord then tried to seek a solution from ancient magic sources. With the combination of the two different energies, Gord's body was almost devastated. Thanks to the help from Elward, the chief wizard, the turbulence in his body was finally able to be controlled. The incident took a huge toll on Gord, leaving his body half red and half blue. While he was saved, Gord can never again control the magic contained in pure mystic energy.

Elward encouraged Gord until he finally got back on his feet. Elward then invited Gord to continue his career as a wizard and invited him to teach at the academy. After careful consideration, Gord accepted the offer. He wished to find a student who will carry on his studies without making the same mistakes. From that day, Gord started a new life as the strictest professor in the magic academy.

b.q: Assassin exiled by the Moniyan Empire.

b.p: The chief assassin of the Church of Light. She once made a mistake during an assassination mission, making companion encounter unprecedented disaster. Although she was able to escape with the assistance of Tigreal, she was later exiled to the border to the Empire to perform more dangerous tasks. Natalia was orphaned from the war and she was raised as a little girl by the Monastery of Light. Natalia was trained into becoming one of the Light assassins. This young phenom had risen to become the top assassin for the Monastery, via her outstanding talents. However, on one assassination mission, she failed in her execution, causing her companions to meet with unprecedented disaster and death. Although she managed to escape danger, with Tigreal's help, this was undoubtedly a severe blow to Natalia's pride. To prove herself again, she exiled herself to the outskirts of the land, far from the Moniyan Empire and the Monastery of Light, to carry out more dangerous missions. It is never known who her target is or where she might strike next. All that people know is that Natalia intends to win back all that she once possessed.

f: Hayabusa (close as siblings); Hanabi (close friend); Hirara (enemies); Seimei

b.p: Though the Scarlet Shadow bestowed her a name and Hayabusa taught her of peace, the young Kagura remained uncertain of her true path. When she opened her umbrella in contemplation, she beheld not gentle rain but visions of calamity, eternities of regret, and a past seen through her umbrella. At last, Kagura understood: though born from lingering attachments, her path led toward freedom. She would carry both the regrets and hopes of those who had passed to experience the beauty of the mortal realm they were never able to, and embrace the future they were robbed of yet graciously bestowed upon her. The story of Kagura's origins was sketchy at best. The elderly man who had brought her to the Scarlet Shadow was well past his years, and whenever asked, he would simply repeat the same recollection: on a rainy spring day over a decade ago, he found an abandoned infant under an umbrella and named her Kagura. Nothing more could be gleaned from him. The Shadow Sect sensed a mysterious power within her, and after much deliberation, decided to raise the infant. Yet Kagura was destined to remain distant from them—the power within her rejected their ninjutsu, and she could not understand why these warriors lived and died by their nindo. Only the umbrella, whose origins were equally as mysterious, kept her company, through joy and sorrow.

As time went on, Kagura learned to find her own peace within the Scarlet Shadow. She observed the ways of the ninja and cared for those exhausted from training. A young Shadow Sect member named Hayabusa told her they strived tirelessly for honor, and while Kagura nodded in response, she could not grasp the meaning of those words.

On spring days, when cherry blossoms fell like rain, Kagura would sit in the trees, watching the people hurrying about below. Everyone had a destination and their steps were hasty yet determined. But not knowing where she came from, she never knew where her destination lay. She could only brush away the fallen petals and drift off to sleep.

Kagura had always sensed another world within her umbrella, but despite countless tries, she could never unlock its mysteries. Until one late spring day, when she fell asleep as usual among the blossoms up in a tree. As the spring breeze curled around her fingers and soft petals settled in her hair, her umbrella suddenly felt different.

It was a dream unlike any other. Kagura could only watch as things unfolded around her; before her eyes was a young spiritualist who gave off a familiar feeling. He was calling for his sister, with both sorrow and joy so vividly real it was like she was there. However, Kagura could not respond to him. His gaze shot through her, onto a figure in the distance.

Kagura looked on as the young man worked on his spirit tools, and soon learned of his name—Seimei, the legendary Spirit Craftsman. The young man aired his sorrows as he toiled in his craft: When the imbalance of Yin and Yang caused widespread calamity across the Cadia Riverlands, Seimei set out to find the Great Dragon to quell the unrest. But when he returned with the Great Dragon, he was greeted by the lifeless body of his sister. But he refused to accept this cruel fate. He would do anything to see his sister again, and so he created a special spirit tool made of spirit insects: the Seimei Umbrella.
When Seimei opened the umbrella, he was able to see his sister, smiling and calling out to him. But how could a mere illusion born from his longing, a puppet constructed from his memory, be enough?

A tear of blood fell on Kagura as darkness consumed Seimei's once-bright eyes. A fragment of the Twilight Orb had unknowingly resonated with his obsession, driving him to madness. Kagura could only watch helplessly as the balance of Yin and Yang crumbled, and countless souls surged forth from the Lanterns of Endless Lights, bringing catastrophe once again. The Great Dragon had no choice but to subdue Seimei. In the end, Seimei coughed up his last breath of blood as his eyes glared with defiance. Kagura's vision blurred with tears before fading to darkness.

When she opened her eyes again, Kagura found herself by the Lantern of Endless Lights. As the souls continued to ran rampant, Seimei's apprentice, Akazawa, exhausted himself creating minor spirit lanterns to contain them all, yet their restlessness could not be quelled.

The legend says that it was the Seimei Umbrella that appeared in the sky at this critical juncture, but now, it was Kagura instead. She finally understood—this was no dream, but the umbrella's memories, and she was the spirit of the Seimei Umbrella.

The souls gathered around her, whispering. As she listened, these victims of the calamities told her why they lingered in the mortal realm. It wasn't over worldly desires or bloody vengeance, but because of regrets and unfulfilled wishes. They simply wanted to see more of the beauty of the Cadia Riverlands, to witness the spring flowers bloom once more. They hoped the umbrella that had accepted all their regrets would see these sights in their stead.

And so, through the accumulation of these lingering thoughts, the umbrella spirit took the form of a young girl, carrying the regrets of all those who still held attachments, born amidst the spring rain of falling cherry blossoms.
Now, open your eyes, Kagura.

The dream ended here. Familiarity set in again as the bustle of Scarlet Shadow members and falling cherry blossoms filled her vision. But the lingering warmth in her palm and the tears on her face told Kagura that was no mere dream. She looked at the umbrella in her hands, gently turning it. Though it no longer echoed with voices, the spring breeze chose that moment to brush past her, petals softly wiping away the tears, as if delivering their unspoken message:

Those born from longing need not be bound by the past; only through the girl's blooming growth can these lingering regrets find their answer. To dwell in past sorrows would only lead to becoming trapped in despair like Seimei. Those past regrets can never truly be mended, but now that you know where you come from, use these eyes to witness the beauty of this world that they could not.

As the dream faded away and spring stirred anew, Kagura understood where her path would lead. She would see, hear, and feel all the beauty this world had to offer. She would bloom with her own radiance—only then could she truly honor their kindness.
Below the tree, voices called out her name. Kagura looked down to see Hayabusa and Hanabi ready to catch her.
The mortal realm was rich with splendor, and there was always someone waiting for her to float back down. Perhaps this was what made life so precious—these simple moments of happiness.
