b.q: Leader of Nazar who guards the Celestial Palace

b.p: Born of thunder, Kaja, the Nazar King, was once the Ancient Ones' most loyal blade. With lightning whip in hand, he judged the sins of all creatures and safeguarded the sanctity of Sanctum Island. But after the war against the two gods, he fell into a long slumber. When he finally awoke, the allies and foes he once knew had been lost to time. Faced with an unfamiliar world, Kaja spread his wings—still shining as they once did. The Ancient Ones may be gone, but his justice will roar across the skies like thunder once more. They were a race born of courage and defiance.

Thousands of years ago, a group of Ancient Ones witnessed a flock of birds cutting through a raging storm, their fragile bodies enduring the sky's wrath, defying fate and death. The unyielding will of these birds and the lightning that rent the sky left an unforgettable impression on these artisans. Enlightened by this vision, they tempered the power of thunder and wove it into living essence, forging the wondrous Primal Lightning. They breathed life and will into this formless power, and from it, rose the Nazar.
With the power of Primal Lightning, they raised Sanctum Island above the skies—a majestic palace atop the sea of clouds, under the Nazar's eternal vigil.
Forged from the fiercest tempest, the King of the Nazar, Kaja, has watched over Sanctum Island since his creation.

His eyes flicker with lightning, revealing all that hides in the darkness. When he sets his eyes on his prey, his whip cracks like thunder as his wings and claws tear through wind and demons alike. The gale sings his praises, the blessed rain celebrates his victories, and the sky roars in awe of their fearless guardian.

In that golden age, Kaja held guard alongside the Aethereal Defender Uranus and upheld justice with the Primal Warden Edith. Sanctum Island stood as a beacon of order and light under their watch; a brilliant pearl nestled among the clouds.
Yet, even the brightest pearl will lose its luster.

The war against the two gods raged across heaven and earth. When all seemed lost, the Ancient Ones exhausted the last of their power to seal the two gods to the Land of Dawn. To preserve a spark of hope for the future, they split Sanctum Island and hid its upper portion somewhere in the world.

Kaja led the Nazar with unyielding valor, fighting to the very last moment. His thunder tore through countless foes, but it was not enough as he watched his comrades fall from the sky like shooting stars. Edith was gravely injured and nowhere to be found, while Uranus, drained of all his energy, sank into a long slumber. In the end, only Kaja remained, but he too soon drifted from consciousness.
When Kaja opened his eyes again, thousands of years had already passed.
The world had changed beyond recognition.

By then, the Awakening project was already in motion. The world's barrier cracked under the clash of light and darkness, leaving the influence of the two gods at their weakest. At the crucial moment, they left the Land of Dawn, and the Twilight Orb shattered.

Amidst this turmoil, the hidden portion of Sanctum Island reappeared. A fragment of the shattered Twilight Orb—the Heart of Anima—descended upon Sanctum Island, becoming the core that held it aloft. The island, now floating above its original location, became known as the "Celestial Palace."
Kaja, the last remaining Nazar, was the first to awaken in this forgotten place.

The plaza that once echoed with hymns now held only the cries of the wind, and the once-brilliant colonnades had all fallen into ruin. The great island had become the tomb of a lost age. Kaja cried out the names of his companions to the sky, but only the ruins echoed back. In the dead silence, the conviction he upheld for millennia finally failed him: "If all that I was sworn to protect is gone, what is left for me to live for?"

But before Kaja could even arrange his thoughts, the palace came under attack. Forces coveting the fragment of the Twilight Orb had already converged upon the palace, and a frantic battle ensued. Eventually, the Heart of Anima fell into the hands of Kalon, the Evil God who had possessed Gusion. Without its power core, the Celestial Palace plummeted from the sky, crashing into the ground below.
The fall of the Celestial Palace sent ripples through time, stirring what had long been lost: Edith's memories returned, and Uranus finally awoke from his long slumber.

Standing amidst the ruins, Kaja watched his long-lost companions rush toward him. His gaze shifted from them to the scattered remnants of what was once glory and honor. Stories he had heard from the time of his creation: Mortal beings who fought desperately for freedom; the Ancient Ones who refused to yield before unfathomable divine power; and the origin of the Nazar—the fragile yet fearless flock that plunged into the raging storm, defying the wrath of the skies as they faced death head-on.
The legacy of the Ancient Ones was never some ruin to be guarded, but a future to be forged.
The birds that braved death, the Ancient Ones that defied fate—the same belief flowed through their souls: never to yield to power, and to fight for all living things.
At last, Kaja understood what remained was worth fighting for.

What he had sworn to protect was not a ruined castle—it was each and every life, struggling against the odds. Alongside his companions, he would carry forward the unfinished work of the Ancient Ones; he would remind the world that the arbiter of justice had never left, that the thunder still roared for the weak.

Light pierced through the clouds and shone upon the wings of the Nazar King. From the ruins, he shot into the sky, his gaze flashing like lightning across the vast lands below. It was a new, chaotic world, filled with unknown dangers and challenges.
But what did that matter?
"All that lies beneath the sky is mine to protect!"
Then, like a bolt of lightning tearing across the sky, Kaja began his new journey without hesitation.

b.q: Dark Elf girl who fell into the Abyss

b.p: In the Southern Moniyan Empire, a bottomless abyss is carved into a barren landscape—As if an ancient demon used a powerful blade to permanently scar the Land of Dawn. The local populace call this place the Abyss. In ancient times, this was the realm of the God of Darkness. In recent times, in the god's absence, its followers yearn for its return. The demons who dwelled in the darkest depths of the Abyss tirelessly schemed to strengthen their power over the darkness. Many misguided believers offered sacrifices to the Abyss, unknowingly feeding the demons, formed of dark energy in its purest form, always lurking in the darkness waiting to devour the carcasses for sacrifices. They then used the sacrifices to breed the "Abyssal Demons," demonic creatures formed by the purest dark energy, which could perfectly blend into the darkness to wait and engulf the prey.

One day, Selena, a young dark elf, was sacrificed by fanatic dark elves in exchange for dark energy. Elves being the demon's favorite sacrifice, Selena was mercilessly thrown into the Abyss. The Abyssal Demons filled Selena with pain and despair, which coursed through every vein of her body. Just as Selena was about to be consumed by the darkness, a miracle happened. A mysterious, warm-blue light enveloped her and appeared to be battling with the darkness for control over her body. When Selena woke, she found herself still lying in the Abyss, but her skin was now exuding some strange blue glow, and her once lavender eyes were filled with a majestic scarlet glow. It was the Abyss Demon resting within her. The demons frantically wondered what happened.

The God of Darkness then spoke: "This dark elf is special. A great power dwells within, inherited from her ancestry, from her blood." An ancient and deep voice echoed through the minds of the demons, "Leave this girl to me. She will become the new master of the darkness!" The Demons obeyed the commands and left Selena as she was. When Selena stood before the demonic inhabitants of the Abyss, with the Abyssal Demons at her side, she quickly discovered that she could manipulate the dark magic of the Abyss. She could absorb the power of the Abyss into her body to transform herself into a full demon, capable of tearing her enemies into shreds. The God of Darkness appointed her as its voice, giving Selena uncontested rule over the demons of the Abyss. Even Alice, the proud Queen of Blood, felt unsettled when she laid eyes upon this dark elf girl. Alice could sense a terrifying power slumbering within this mischievous maiden.

A guard of the Minos Labyrinth, who kept his pledge even after the kingdoms fall. He has blocked off intruders who covered the kingdoms heritage for a century with an unusually huge arm. Legends from the Land of Dawn say that the Western Desert's Minoan Kingdom possesses a mysterious labyrinth. In the maze is a statue of giant minotaur, which the people consider to be the mecca of the Minoan Kingdom. Some say that there is a group of mercenaries who guard the entire maze. The Kingdom produced a lot of precious jade, which brought the Minoan people great wealth. Very quickly, the entire kingdom was lost in the intoxicating allure of gems. Even many mercenaries, tasked with guarding the sacred maze become corrupted, abandoning their duty. Only one stayed―Aldous, who had never forgotten his duty and guard the Minoan Labyrinth.

Until one day, a god came from the heavens to punish these lands. The powers of light and dark decimated the entire Minoan Kingdom, which even Aldous could not escape. The two streams dark and light energy surged into his body. Aldous thought he was about to die. However, the two streams of energy collided, causing great changes to his body. His skin grew long-black scales that could resist most attacks and monstrously large arms that could easily strike fear into people's hearts.

When Aldous awoke from his daze, he found his people's kingdom all gone and the mysterious maze was now sealed by some unknown force. The remaining minotaurs decided that Aldous would stay to defend the maze, while the others travel across the Land of Dawn to find answers. News of a mysterious force sealing the Minoan Maze spread quickly to the Abyssal Kingdom. To gather this strange energy, Selena decided to bring her Abyssal Demons with her to the entrance of the Minoan Maze―A huge battle was about to begin.

f: Master Thief; Partners in Crime (former); Lord of Thieves
Dexter (sidekick); Clint, Mathilda, Merlin (companions); Alucard, Tigreal, Fanny, Harith (allies); Waldo Kane, Barats, Alice (enemies); Blandy (enemy, deceased)

b.p: Claude grew up living in Los Pecados. The circumstances in his life forced him into becoming an incredible thief. But he was used by Kane and went to prison and chains. In prison, he met Merlin, the god of thieves, and inherited his mantle, successfully escaping from prison. After completing an agreement with Merlin, Claude returned to Los Pecados with his new partner Dexter, ready to take revenge on Kane. Claude was born in Los Pecados, a western city in the Land of Dawn. An infamous city of sins without a ruler or order, lawless and ravaged by crime.

Growing up in such a place as an orphan, Claude soon learned how to fight, lie, gamble and steal: tricks of the trade he had to rely upon to survive. He was especially talented in the latter, and no cutpurse he'd ever met matched him when it came to his sharp eye and nimble fingers.

It wasn't long until he became leader of a vagrant band, relying upon his 'skills', and making a name for himself in Los Pecados. He found one who would offer him and his gang protection—Waldo Kane. Kane was yet to achieve the monopoly over Los Pecados that he'd dreamed of. Wild ambition and conspiracy brewed deep within him. To him, this motley crew of street roamers with no place to call home were the perfect tools to achieve his goals. Behind a mask of benevolence, he manipulated these kids, with smooth lies and false compassion leading them down a dark path. He molded them into becoming members of his criminal group, each misguided child referring to him as 'Father'.

At the age of 18, Claude was given a monumental task: he was to head to Castle Grandrock in northern Moniyan, sneak into the Duke of Vance's home. Then, he would feign stealing secret accounts, while actually casting the blame on another gang. Kane promised Claude that he'd have people waiting for him once he was inside. Once he'd completed his mission Claude and his team would be rewarded with a place to live of their own. No longer would they need to live in the slums.

The truth, however, was nothing Claude could have ever imagined. There was nobody waiting for him: he was but a mere pawn, and neither he nor his brothers would be receiving any kind of reward. Like Claude, they were just stepping stones for their 'Father' to become king of Los Pecados.

And so, when he slipped into the Duke's mansion, he found an inescapable trap awaiting him. All Claude could do was accept his fate, and he was taken into custody. Following a hasty trial, he was soon pronounced guilty of all charges, and thrown into a cold, dark cell.
Locked up in chains, Claude burned with regret. The only thing in his mind that kept him going was his gang of brothers, lost with nowhere to go.

The days passed slowly. One day, Claude was made to switch cells, his new cell shared with an old man with a beard and hair as white as snow. That peculiar old fellow was none other than the master thief of legend—Merlin. The powerful and incredibly resourceful Merlin had a reason for being locked up in a cell. A reason that left Claude dumbstruck: he just wanted a quiet place to retire.

The cunning Claude reminded Merlin of his younger self. Hence, he decided to pass on to him his legacy. Yet, in return, Claude would need to acquiesce to a most peculiar request of Merlin's. Once out of prison, he must loot each city across the Land of Dawn, leaving behind his name as a calling card.

In the two years that followed, Claude inherited each of Merlin's wondrous techniques of deceit, escape and combat among others. His abilities grew until he was ready to steal anything he could imagine. One night, Claude enacted upon his perfect prison break plan, stealing back his freedom.

To make good on his promise, Claude traveled throughout the Land of Dawn in the several years that followed. The streets bristled with whispers of the master thief Claude, his charm and his incredible skill. With his trademark carefree smile, Claude was your man if you ever needed something stolen, no matter what. All he asked is that the pay be generous, and the one to be stolen from, evil.

As this continued, Claude came to be joined by the perfect partner—the mysterious Dexter. This mischievous little monkey first met Claude in Moniyan, when he stole a lucky gold coin straight from under his nose. After a brief pursuit, their friendship blossomed, and Claude took Dexter on as his partner-in-crime. And so, their adventures began.
On the fifth year of his departure from Los Pecados, Claude finally completed the promise he'd made to Merlin. He'd left his traces in every city in the Land of Dawn.

Next, he would return to Los Pecados. Yet nothing could have prepared Claude for what he saw when he returned after those five years away. His brethren of old hadn't risen up the underworld ranks, escaped from poverty with their manipulative 'Father'. No, a fate quite different had befallen them. Instead, he saw that not only were there still pitiable street kids around every corner of this run-down city, ones like Claude of the past; there were even more than before.

Claude had been deceived and it filled him with a violent rage. He began to plan his revenge as it swirled up inside him. Waldo Kane had achieved his monopoly over the city, becoming the kingpin of Los Pecados. In order to exact his revenge, Claude slipped into Eruditio and with Dexter's aid feigned capture, entering prison. He then stole Dr. Rooney's latest invention—a most odd holographic mirror device.

Pleased with his success, it was then that Claude noticed a line of text upon the device: "I hope this device serves you well. If you've any ideas or suggestions on how to improve it, contact me immediately!—Rooney."

With this 'gift' from Dr. Rooney, Claude and Dexter made tracks for Los Pecados. In this chaotic city of nefarious deals outside of the law, he would make he who had deceived him in the past pay the price.

f: King of the Valley of Winds (Father); Valir (childhood friend)

b.p: A magician of Wind Fort and the only genius in the entire family who can change the form of wind magic at will. Once a close friend of Valir of Fire Throat. After the changes in the Land of Fire and Valir left his hometown, Vale has always adhered to the agreement he made with him, waiting for his return. “Valir, my beloved brother. You lost everything the day we made The pact. I'll see to it that the Fire Kingdom restores everything to the way it once was. Even if you still wish to avenge your cruel father, I do not blame you as long as you can cast away the storm within your heart. Nothing is as important as your happiness, not even my life.” Vale fell into deep contemplation as he wrote his letter to Valir. Those first few lines brought Vale back to the days of his youth, when he and Valir were the closest of friends.

As Vale fell further into nostalgia, he remembered the day they met at a royal party. Ever since then, they both felt a strong affinity towards each other's magic. For a long time, Vale and Valir were inseparable. Together they left many memories in the Valley of the Winds, the Fire Kingdom and many other exotic lands. When unrest flooded the Fire Kingdom, Valir quickly made his leave. Only Vale knows exactly how much Valir sacrificed that day.

b.h: The Song of Wind and Fire

b.p: As time went on, the day of The pact was coming soon. Vale's magical abilities to control winds had grown more sophisticated over the years. In fact, he was the only member of his family who could change the winds with magic. Yet, Vale had never shown his magic to anyone before. Vale waited and waited for the day of The pact to come. On that day, he would put on a spectacular display of wind magic for Valir. Vale believes that Valir will see his magic, remember the precious times they had together, and return how things were in their youth.

f: Unnamed royal guard ancestors; Atticus (close friend, deceased); Barbiel (pet); Vexana, Faramis (ally); Alice (enemy); Terizla (enemy); Benedetta, Brody (enemies; pre-2022 revamp)

b.p: Once a sworn knight of Ridgeburg, Leomord was forced to shatter the oath he made with his own sword in an unfortunate turn of events. Since then, he had borne the curse of the Mist and guarded the land abandoned even by death. The light had faded, yet his watch had just begun... Perched upon the crags of the Lantis Mountains, the colossal spires of Ridgeburg overlooked the blackened plains of the Abyss. The rot had almost crept up to the city's outskirts, but no farther. For thousands of years, the fortified towers had stood guard right at the doorstep of the Abyss, keeping the Moniyan Empire untouched by its blight. Leomord was born in this border fortress. Coming from a long line of Royal Guards under the Lords of the South, he was pledged as personal squire to Atticus, the son of the Duke of Ridgeburg, not long after he was born.

Together, the two boys trained under the finest champions of the Ridgeburg army and listened to grey-bearded tutors droning on about history and politics. Atticus excelled in every lesson, showing remarkable maturity beyond his years, while Leomord found it hard to keep up with his young master. Reluctant to being left behind, he kept training in secret, toiling alone day and night to further hone his skills.
Being the slightly older one, Atticus would often help the young Leomord during their training. Leomord, in turn, looked up to Atticus as not only his future lord but also an older brother.

Upon reaching the age of seven, the two boys took part in the birthing of their horses, as was customary among the people of Ridgeburg. Leomord named his pony Barbiel, with whom he grew to become allies and close friends. Although Leomord never openly expressed his feelings, Barbiel always seemed to know what he had in mind. And whenever Leomord felt down, Barbiel would rub his head to offer some form of relief.
Over the next few years, the two boys grew into formidable fighters on the training ground, and that was when fate struck.

After the Old Duke's untimely passing, Atticus was forced to take on his father's mantle as the new Duke of Ridgeburg, with Leomord standing beside him as captain of his Royal Guard. The boys had never had a taste of real battle, but seeing the gravity of the situation, they shortly set off to rid the border outposts of demonic intruders. For years, the two fought endlessly, until they finally cleansed every trace of the Abyss from the outskirts.

Once the city regained some respite from the onslaught, Atticus decided it was time to start forging bonds with other noble houses of the Empire. He sought an alliance with the Royal House of Gaius, offering a marriage proposal to Princess Vexana. Lord Gaius welcomed the offer and promptly arranged for the Princess to set forth for Ridgeburg and meet her betrothed.

And yet, fate had something else in mind for the young Duke. Shortly before Vexana was expected to arrive, he received a letter from one of the border towns. An unusually vicious breed of demons had started turning up along the border, and strangely enough, they bore traces of the very same putrid magic that had once plagued his father. Some townsfolk had gone missing as well, and the outpost sought the Duke's aid in ridding the town of this threat.
Atticus gathered his men right away. He had no doubt this quest could finally unravel the mystery of his father's death. Leomord, on the other hand, only felt a dreadful sense of foreboding.

Before the departure, Atticus led Leomord to the top of the city wall. He pulled out his sword and motioned Leomord to kneel on one knee. Knowing exactly what was coming, the young soldier took a deep breath and solemnly knelt in front of Atticus as he was told.

"Duke Atticus, I hereby swear this oath, in the name of my father and his House, that I shall always lend my sword to your service, provide counsel when you seek it, and lay my life down should your safety require it. This I swear on this day, unto the day of my death." Atticus placed the blunt of his sword on Leomord's shoulder and declared him a Sworn Knight of Ridgeburg. The young soldier found it hard to contain himself. For more than twenty years, they trained and rode to battle together. And on this day, Atticus had deemed him worthy of his trust.

As the Duke handed him the Sword of Oath, Leomord knew this was his fate—to ride with his lord on this battle that might very well be his last. Except, Atticus had a different task for him—Leomord was to remain and stand guard at Ridgeburg.

The knight couldn't believe what he had just heard, but Atticus's eyes were grave and stern. Princess Vexana would be arriving any day soon; she would need all the help and protection she could get. And there was no one else the Duke could trust to carry this delicate burden than his closest friend, Leomord.

And thus, by first light, the young knight watched as Atticus and his party faded into the horizon. He clenched the Duke's Sword of Oath, pondering upon the new task at hand, which he reckoned was far heavier than any battle he had ever fought.
For two years, Leomord and Princess Vexana waited. The quest took much longer than expected, and at some point, Atticus even stopped sending back letters.

And then one day, out of blue, a messenger came announcing the Duke's return. Leomord let out a long sigh, as his mind finally felt at ease. Except, instead of the joy he'd expected to see in Atticus's eyes, he saw nothing but… emptiness.

The campaign must have been brutal and arduous, he could only surmise. Leomord opted not to prod any further and promptly set out to join the city folk in preparation for the long-delayed wedding of Duke Atticus and Princess Vexana.

The people of Ridgeburg greeted the evening with festivity and cheer. The time had come at last for Atticus to give Vexana the wedding ring. However, as the Duke opened the box, what came out instead was a pair of magic wings, as a deep, grating voice shook the stone walls of the fortress:

Embrace the world of death!' Atticus and his men turned into demons at that exact moment, their eyes burning with malice. They reeked of foul magic—rotten and vile—the putrid blight of the Abyss. The once devoted guardians of the city became destroyers and the bane of their existence; the holy wedding morphed into a massacre.

Leomord clasped at the Sword of Oath, his mind blank as bloodcurdling screams pierced his ears and drilled into his skull. He couldn't fathom what was happening before him, and most importantly, why Atticus would draw his blade against the people he'd loved as his own, against the girl he'd sworn to protect to his death.
The rampaging Duke lunged at Princess Vexana.
"STOP!"
Vexana's voice echoed throughout the hall. Atticus froze, his legs shaking as his labored breaths scraped against his lungs.
"Kill me…Leo— K-kill me…beg of you—"
Leomord could only stare in horror. All he could think of was the vow he had made two years ago.
"I hereby swear this oath…in the name of my father and his House, that I shall…lay my life down should your safety require it."

Does the safety of the Duke weigh heavier than the safety of the city? The young knight silently asked himself, right before he clenched his teeth and drove his blade into Atticus's chest. The Duke's eyes cleared up, as if he was lifted from a curse. Grasping at Leomord's vest, the words that came out of his mouth were raspy and garbled. "Bro…ther… I am…free—"
And as he breathed his last, he turned his eyes to Vexana and whispered. "The Mist… If there is no other choice—"

Watching Atticus's body slowly wither into ashes, Leomord wished nothing more than to follow his lord into death, but he couldn't die yet. He had a more important mission on his shoulders—Ridgeburg, sieged from both sides, needed his sword. Ridgeburg would fight till the last, even at the cost of releasing the Mist.

A hundred years had passed, yet time in Ridgeburg seemed to have frozen in place. Shrouded by heavy, dark fog, the city was known to be cursed, shunned by both the light and the dark. Necrokeep, they called it.

Leomord could sometimes be seen standing on one of its towers, gazing far into the horizon. His skin was sickly pale, neither living nor dead. His eyes were tired from a hundred years of half-death, but they still sparkled with a glimmer of hope. He knew in his heart that he and Vexana would eventually find a way to reverse the curse of the Mist.
From that day a hundred years ago, his life no longer belonged to himself, but to Ridgeburg. As long as there was still one soul in the city, he would guard them until his last breath."

b.q: Miraculous creatures born in Twilight Orb

b.p: Lunox was born with magical powers, and her dreamworld reflects and changes the real world. With this power, she uses her dreamworld to temporarily maintain the balance of energy between order and chaos. But as the power of order and the power of chaos rushed into her dreams, Lunox fell into a long sleep and turned into one of the "Twilight Orbs." As the final battle started, the Twilight Orb devoured the energies within the Mage and opened, from which stepped out a girl, who was surrounded by the power of Chaos and Order. Her eyes are deep as the ancient lake.

The mysterious atmosphere she created then put all of the heroes into dreamland… The power of Chaos and Order have been struggling against each other since the ancient time, and the struggle had driven the world into desperation. Lunox, the mysterious maiden, is the one who survived the desperation. With her unique talent, she can project her dream into reality and change it.

One day, a sound whispered to her and told her to balance the two powers with her dreamland ability. But the cost would be hunger than ever. For the world she loves, she accepted this fate, channeled the two powers into dreamland and became one of the Twilight Orb, at the cost of falling into an endless sleep. But the sound also told Lunox that one day, she will wake up to proceed with her fate: to find other Twilight Orbs that are forgotten by history

b.q: Genius ninja in the Shadow Sect who is at the crossroads

b.p: A genius ninja of the Shadow Sect in the Scarlet Shadow. In order to pursue great power, he absorbed the "Hanekage" into his body, and used the enemy's flesh and blood to provide nourishment for the "Hanekage". After gaining power, he took away the most powerful supreme ninjutsu and Ame no Habakiri in the Scarlet Shadow, and went further and further on the road of killing. "To protect the secrets of the Sacred Tools is your duty; value it more than your life."

As Hanzo awoke in the middle of the night due to pain inflicted by the Ame no Habakiri, he recalled this teaching that led him down this path of no return. Before turning his back on the Scarlet Shadow, Hanzo was the Shadow Sect's sharpest blade.

Adopted by the Shadow Sect at a young age, Hanzo was lucky to escape the fate of a wandering beggar. He learned the ways of Nindo, to "uphold justice and endure hardship", and lived his new life by its teachings. For the Scarlet Shadow, his cherished home, he was willing to do anything.

Fierce and tenacious like the wolf, Hanzo always took on the most perilous missions. Even when he returned with grave injuries, he would make his report in full before seeking treatment. Failure was something not even Hanzo's greatest rivals would dare think of. They knew Hanzo would stop at nothing to achieve his objectives.

Over the course of a decade, Hanzo accumulated so many merits that his peers saw him, a commoner by birth, as only second to Kurēn, the clan's next heir. Hanzo acknowledged Kurēn's unmatched wisdom. If Kurēn vowed to uphold Nindo after he took power, then Hanzo would become his sharpest blade.
Until now, Hanzo never thought his past self was wrong, but it was his near-obsessive persistence that led him to this point.

Some time ago, Hanzo, while engrossed in the Nindo scriptures, suddenly realized that his peers, other orphans adopted by the clan, had routinely disappeared with little explanation. Greatly puzzled, Hanzo began to investigate on his own. During his search, he crossed more than a few elders, resulting in him being stripped of all rank in the clan. The merits he earned at the risk of his life were erased overnight. Hanzo cared little for fame, but he knew something sinister was being covered up. Eventually, he discovered that the elders had been sending ninjas on missions to the forbidden grounds to steal a Cursed Tool that was supposed to be sealed within: the demonic blade Ame no Habakiri.
Countless lives had been sacrificed to the demon blade. Hanzo couldn't bear to think how many in the Scarlet Shadow who simply sought to uphold justice ended up with this fate.
A momentary lapse in concentration caused Hanzo to be discovered by another ninja in the forbidden grounds—it was Kurēn.

In the dark, stone chamber, Kurēn revealed the truth of the Scarlet Shadow: The two factions within the clan had been vying for control of the Seven Sacred Tools, each trying to shift the balance of power in their favor. The elders of the Shadow Sect were sacrificing their own to the Ame no Habakiri in order to awaken its true power.
Kurēn had been secretly gaining influence to abolish this vile practice once he became the clan leader, and seeing Hanzo, he was eager to have a ninja of Nindo help him change the future of the clan.
"Those that were sacrificed to Ame no Habakiri... what of their futures?"

Kurēn had no answer to his question, which sent Hanzo into a rage. He had seen too many hypocrites claiming to act for the greater good, and in that moment, he realized the Scarlet Shadow was no different. His Nindo did not tolerate evil deeds, thus the Scarlet Shadow should not exist. If they craved Ame no Habakiri's power so much, he would show them its true might!
As Hanzo reached for the demon blade on the pedestal, he thought to himself, "Come, either devour me, or let me devour everything!"

The moment he grasped the Ame no Habakiri, its unbridled demonic power invaded his body. In a trance, he saw a whirlpool swallowing ships, or was it a leviathan devouring entire islands? Quickly he realized what he was actually seeing:

It was a vortex of souls; the ninjas who had been sacrificed, and countless more before them. Their wills had long been erased, leaving only an insatiable hunger and darkness churning within the blade; a madness that was neither human nor demon.
The demonic power invaded Hanzo's very being, but his pride refused to be consumed. Feeding on his rage and obsession, he finally tamed the Ame no Habakiri.
"Naive pretender, you will witness my reign from within this blade."

And with that, Hanzo swung the blade at his former comrade Kurēn. "Gaining influence"... that's merely the cowardly compromise of the weak. Without the courage to make the first cut, there would never be change.

After devouring Kurēn, Hanzo left the forbidden grounds. He knew his path as a ninja of the Shadow Sect was forever severed. But what of it? This Akuma shall carve out the rot from within the Scarlet Shadow once and for all.

b.q: Kind and fraternal elemental creatures

b.p: Many a race has risen and fallen throughout the expansive history of the Land of Dawn. Belerick is one of the few who have borne witness to all this throughout the mists of time. When the world was first formed, the mysterious Ancient Ones aided the Forefathers as they created all things in this universe. Together they constructed the grand and massive Celestial Palace and the myriad elemental creatures, who would live as successors to their bloodlines.

When Belerick was but a young sapling, he was chosen by the Ancient Ones and given the essence of life and Mother Nature; this bestowed upon him the powers of intelligent thought, deep wisdom, and the wondrous ability of reincarnation. Under the Ancient Ones' protection he lived together with the elemental creatures within the Lantis Mountain ranges, a place flourishing with life and vitality.

However, this blissful existence would not last long. The Forefathers departed and the Endless War descended upon the lands, plunging the Land of Dawn into the throes of fierce battle and slaughter; the Ancient Ones retreated to the Celestial Palace and the elemental creatures thus lost the protection they'd once been granted. The creatures were left without a safe home of their own, and slain en masse as the fires of war blazed ever on.

They were forced to wander the lands for an entire age. Belerick watched as the Land of Dawn was ravaged by the raging war, no corner left untouched by the fighting. As he did so, Belerick grew from a sapling into a mighty tree. The warfare had stripped him of his former life, and hardened his power of will; despite having lost many of his companions in the process, he nonetheless refused to give up the hope he had in life. He sought to use his power to the best of his ability in helping out those weaker than him. In the later stages of the Era of Strife, the Ancient Ones who had returned to their Celestial Palace long ago could no longer stand the pitiable state of the world below, and went against the orders of the Forefathers as they rashly used the Twilight Orbs' power to try and end the war.

The incredible power of the Twilight Orbs sealed the Lord of the Abyss and isolated the Lord of Light, yet on top of this, it caused an unprecedented surge in energy. There was an earth-shaking explosion, and in its wake, the once brilliant and powerful Ancient Ones were gone without a single trace, lost to history. This was when Belerick's long journey was to begin: while continuing to come to the aid of all the needy in the Land of Dawn, he would also search for the whereabouts of his ancestors—the Ancient Ones.

This journey of his stretched over several millennia, the sands of time granting Belerick not only additional growth rings within his mighty trunk, but also a wealth of experience, wisdom, and an ever-greater compassion for all living things. Starting out from the Lantis Mountains, he would travel onward to every single corner throughout the Land of Dawn, and whenever his branches started to wither he'd transform once more into a tiny seed. From this seed he would grow once more, an infinite cycle of reincarnation. Throughout this time he endeavored to utilize his wisdom and power to aid everyone he met, big or small, no matter their race. Yet he could never find any clues as to the whereabouts of his ancestors, the Ancient Ones, or of the Twilight Orbs.

As trade thrived and the Emerald Road flourished, rumors of the Twilight Orbs began to spread throughout the Agelta Drylands, which sparked hope in the heart of Belerick. However, upon finally finishing his arduous trek to the western wastelands, he was met with a distressing sight: its city-states had been locked in battle over the Twilight Orbs, which had once again led to their explosion. A fatal blow had been dealt to the once-prosperous Emerald Road. The ubiquitous oases of Agelta and its cities with their burgeoning populations were no more. In their place stood instead dilapidated ruins, and desert as far as the eye could see. As he laid eyes upon the poor folk struggling in the harsh, sandy environment, Belerick decided to use the entirety of his powers to bring forth a great oasis where the Emerald Road center once was. The oasis was a godsend, a place teeming with life and vitality that served as a shelter and home to all those who needed it.

Belerick exerted himself to the limit in order to bring about such a miraculous oasis, and fell into a deep slumber. A millennium passed, during which the Twilight Orbs reappeared once more and awakened him from his ancient sleep. Upon awakening, the blood of the Ancient Ones that flowed within him reacted with the Twilight Orbs and gave rise to the most incredible resonance; more than this, however, it freed Lunox who had been sealed within. It was then that Belerick finally realized the answers he had sought for so long were here, in Lunox and the other Twilight Orbs. Hence he set upon his journey once again, roaming the wide world in a search for the remaining Twilight Orbs.

Eventually, Lunox and Belerick arrived within the Elf kingdom of Azrya. The demon armies had long been preparing to set out from the Shadow Swamp, and they broke through the enchantments placed by the Moon Goddess to launch their invasion upon the Moonlit Forest. Through Azrya, they would then siege the whole of the Moniyan Empire. Estes and Miya led the Moon Elves to put up a desperate resistance, dealing a heavy blow to the demon forces; yet the demons were so enraged by this hindrance to their march that they used arcane fire to set the Tree of Life, upon which all Elves depended, alight. The furious flames roared high in the skies within a matter of seconds, and proved impossible to quench: the distraught Elves could only watch with horror on their faces as their sacred tree went up in flames. There was nothing they could do.

The fires burned ever brighter, and the Elves fell ever further into despair. Just when all hope had been lost, a web of thick vines stretched across the furious flames and wrapped the Tree of Life tightly in their grasp; first one layer of vines, then another, and another... Belerick extended his branches and all of his leaves, and with his own body he enveloped the Tree of Life. In its place, his leaves began to fall.

The fire blazed harder, with no sign of stopping. Belerick's body grew a charcoal-black, and he started to fall repeatedly. By the time the last flame began to dwindle, Lunox's tragic cries and the mournful song of the Elves could be heard throughout the expanse of the Moonlit Forest. Just at that moment, from beneath the withered and blackened branches buried in ash, there burst forth a surge of vitality. The silver moon rose high in the sky as leaves sprouted anew, and the Tree of Life's bountiful energies flowed forth into a tiny seed that remained. With a monumental force that shook the ground, the seed split off into branches and sprouts, growing at an unreal rate—not only was Belerick returned to life, but he was brought back a stronger and taller being, a truly magnificent tree.

Lunox and Belerick bade the Elves their farewell, and set off once more upon their journey to seek out the other Twilight Orbs. With his new, reinvigorated body, Belerick's faith had grown only stronger, and he knew that the true meaning of life was to help others, with all his strength.

b.p: Born into a traditional military family in the Moniyan Empire, she received military education from an early age, so she was a little boyish. At the same time, Kimmy is not bound by tradition. She is obsessed with technology and inventions In order to prove herself to her father, Kimmy picks up her invention and joined the Imperial Expeditionary Army.

If you were to ask Kimmy about her most vivid childhood memory, she would tell you without hesitation - it was the weight of the medals adorning her father's military uniform. Born into a military family, the young girl secretly vowed to become an even greater soldier than her father.
But when she enthusiastically shared her dream with him, his usual gentle demeanor turned stern as he rejected her aspirations. Putting his calloused hand
over her little head, he said, "I want my daughter to have a peaceful, carefree life."

Though her wings were confined within the cage her father built, Kimmy never abandoned her dreams of soaring. She read military books in secret, looked through her family's military records, and even after being sent to Eruditio for schooling, she never stopped dreaming.

Perhaps Kimmy's most carefree and joyful days were spent in Eruditio. She cut her hair short and made many friends, and one in particular, Beatrix, became her closest companion. The two were drawn together by the fierce determination they shared. Kimmy helped Beatrix test various weapons - no matter how complex their design or intricate their controls, she always seemed to bring out their true potential.
"Why not just go for it? Enlist first and tell him later!" Kimmy's heart raced at
Beatrix's suggestion. As their fists bumped together, their rebellious alliance was officially sealed.
Kimmy packed up and left Eruditio to join the Moniyan Empire's Western Border Guard. The closer she got to the military outpost, the more desolate the surroundings became, but her heart had

never felt more fulfilled. She stretched her hand upward, as though she could grasp the sky itself. Kimmy's early days in the Border Guard were anything but easy. Her time spent in Eruditio and her young age led many of the hardened soldiers to dismiss her as a privileged girl who was just looking for some cheap thrills. She paid their gossip no mind, instead throwing herself into her training, using her pent-up ambition as fuel for her fire, and the results showed; she came first in the Imperial Joint Tactical Exercise and demonstrated extraordinary talent in both marksmanship and close- quarters combat. Her achievements finally silenced the rumors and naysayers. Many began to see Kimmy in a new light, and some were even inspired to train harder.

It was then that the Weapons Department invented a new weapon - a Starlium- powered jetpack and rifle. However, its complex operation was too much for most of the testers, yet Kimmy's talent and experience allowed her to master it almost immediately. The weapon found its full potential in her hands, shocking even the researchers. The flashes of the muzzle illuminated Kimmy's path forward - the Hoverjet Blaster became her weapon, and together they would shine in battle.

Kimmy paid no mind to others' cold stares, focusing solely on her own efforts. The fledging had shed her down and was ready to spread her wings and soar. Yet... thoughts of her father still filled her with doubt.

Soon after, Kimmy was assigned to an elite squad, deploying her weapon into battle for the first time on an important rescue mission. The enemy, highly mobile and intimate with the terrain, had the upper hand. Though it was Kimmy's first real combat mission, she remained remarkably calm. She quickly identified the enemy's movement patterns, tracked them to a small outpost, and launched a successful first strike on her own.
Before the thrill of victory could fade, the full scope of the enemy's operations was revealed: they had kidnapped military

researchers to force them to create new weapons. Worse still, they had already used stolen weapons to ambush the front- line troops, causing heavy casualties. With no time to call for backup, Kimmy disguised herself with the enemy's attire and infiltrated their stronghold, quickly locating the holding cells.

Behind iron bars were over a dozen imprisoned allies. Kimmy acted decisively, blasting open the prison doors with her rifle. The sound alerted her comrades waiting to launch their attack outside. With their coordinated assault from both inside and out, chaos erupted in the enemy stronghold, leading to their quick defeat.

As Kimmy evacuated the prisoners, an older officer, slowed due to his injuries, caught her attention. Those familiar shoulders, that crew cut of gray hair - it was her father. The usually fearless Kimmy felt her confidence waver. She had never told her strict father about enlisting. As their eyes met, Kimmy braced for the worst. However, after a moment's pause, he simply gave her a formal military salute pretending not to recognize his masked daughter. His voice was no longer as deep as she remembered, and his injured stature seemed smaller than she remembered. He advised the "new recruit" to make something of herself in the military. Kimmy shouldered her weapon and nodded solemnly while trying to keep her voice from trembling.
New missions awaited on the horizon. Kimmy looked to the sky, knowing that her wings now carried her father's
expectations. She was bound for even greater heights.

b.q: The lord of the Fire Demons who seeks to reignite the flames of the Abyss through war and violence.
You must never allow the Heart of Lava to become cold and harden.

b.p: In the deepest depths of the Abyss, molten magma churns at the birthplace of the formidable Fire Demons. Among them was Thamuz, who rose to become the mightiest Fire Demon and their leader. With his overwhelming strength and blazing temper, he controls the depths of the Abyss with an iron fist. Now, as the corruption seeping through the Abyss threatens to wipe out his race, Thamuz seeks to ascend to godhood and crush fate with his own hands. To this end, he and his Fire Demons will burn everything to ash, until nothing is left.

Thamuz still remembered the words of the former Lord of Lava. Thamuz was just a general back then—when the Sovereign of the Abyss ordered them to go to war, he forged his scythes from obsidian and lava, and reaped the battlefield with his blazing flames. However, the former lord saw in him not just strength that surpassed all others, but also wisdom rare among their kind. After the sovereign issued another call to arms, the former lord summoned Thamuz once more to the birthplace of the Fire Demons.
This time, however, it wasn't to send him off to battle—it was to keep him from it.

The Heart of Lava is the essence of the Fire Demons. As the wars raged on, more and more Fire Demons perished on the battlefield, littering them with grim statues. And with each loss, the Heart of Lava grew colder, spelling the downfall of the Fire Demons.
The call of war could not be refused, but the Fire Demons desperately needed a new future—one that only the new generation like Thamuz could forge.

After his succession, Thamuz began the revival of the Fire Demons. During the brief respites from the fighting, the Fire Demons would see a resurgence in influence. But Thamuz was not fooled by these illusions. Looking at the races of the Abyss and the above races driven by the God of Light, he saw how race after race had disappeared from history in the Endless War. The obsidian and granite structures his ancestors once erected as the builders of the Abyss civilization now lay in ruins. The so-called gods sought only victory, treating all life as mere pawns in their petty game. The suffering of the Abyss must end.

With this conviction, Thamuz led the Fire Demons to join the rebels, and in the final battle, commanded his forces deep into the Night Palace in the lowest depths of the Abyss. As he confronted the creator of the Abyss civilization, the power stirring in his blood confirmed the sovereign's words about the Abyss's nurturing nature. But the power that once nourished the Abyss like a sun had become its enemy, discarding the lives of its subjects at will—and for that, she had to perish!

After an earth-shattering battle, Thamuz ended the sovereign's life with his own hands, while the rebels succeeded in their plan to defeat both the God of Light and God of Darkness. Standing upon the ravaged pits of the Abyss, Thamuz resolved to forge a new Abyss, one that could stand equal to the surface world. Using the sovereign's blood as fuel, Thamuz brought the Abyss into a new era.

But fate is a cruel mistress. The sovereign's blood curse began to spread through the Abyss, corrupting the very essence of many Abyssal beings, driving their minds mad and twisting their bodies. Even the Heart of Lava, nourished by the sovereign's blood, was not spared. Watching his brethren fall to madness one by one, Thamuz's ideals crumbled.

Amidst this chaos, Thamuz also had to fight against the mad Abyssal beings who sought to claim the sovereign's remains slumbering within the Night Palace—should they succeed, the outcome would make the current dark corruption seem gentle in comparison. The endless battles and fruitless labor let pain and rage devour Thamuz's heart. He gradually realized that only overwhelming power could subdue these lesser beings, and only transcendent power could overcome the curse.
He must become a god, and then surpass even godhood.

This shift disappointed many of his former allies and even made them fearful of Thamuz. But against the unstoppable dark corruption, their counsel rang hollow. Someone had to shoulder the fate of the Abyss, and Thamuz was convinced it had to be him. Thousands of years passed, and as madness and mutation grew ever worse, the Abyss became unrecognizable. The Lord of Lava, constantly reforging himself in the flames of war, continued his conquest and ascension toward godhood.
His pride would not allow him to forget that promise—
I will become the new sun of the Abyss, and my blood will ensure that the lava burns eternal!

b.p: Legends say that an ancient race of elves reside in the Land of Dawn's Enchanted Forest. The stories often depict this cat-like race as small in stature, agile, playful, independent, and highly intelligent. However, few are aware of the longstanding alliance between the Leonin Elves and the Moon Elves.

From a young age, Harith surpassed his peers in talent and wisdom. He quickly became the strongest mage among the Leonins, perhaps as strong as other in the Land of Dawn. Although, the Leonins never step foot outside of the Enchanted Forest, living a peaceful and safe life on their own. The Leonins became so complacent with their blissful existence that they no longer pursed the magic arts, a hallmark of their people. Harith became very discontent with this trend and confidently set out of the Enchanted Forest to see the outside world at the young age of 15. Harith was driven by his and passion for the magic arts, aspiring to become his people's leader in magic.

Harith arrived at the Moniyan Empire, where he joined armies to fight off the invading orc tribes. Proving himself in battle, Harith gained the recognition of Tigreal, who came to appreciate Harith's lovely spirit and strong abilities. People say, Harith was given the rank of lieutenant and will soon be appointed as an Imperial Master of Magic of the Moniyan Empire. With that said, Harith has imperial authorization to use magic to control space and time to unlock the Secrets of Dawn to seal away evil and protect justice.

Full of excitement and fervor, Harith also knew that once he is appointed the title of Master of Magic that he will become a target of public criticism. Committed to his dream of becoming his people's leader in magic, Harith fearlessly marched forward alone. Over time, Harith discovered that his life was consumed by his mission and by the empire. Harith slowly grew lonely and reclusive. Even when he met his fellow Leonin, Nana, he was unable to maintain a normal conversation. Despite Nana showing signs of affection towards him, he could not express his feelings, believing that the best way to protect her from criticism was for him be alone. After all, whenever the empire needed magical assistance, the Master of Magic was on the job to seal away the dangers of evil.

b.p: A prince of the Vonetis Sea's Mahar Pura, good at fighting and winning. He was expelled by his father because of a heretical love affair he had. When his brother raised the flag of rebellion, Minsitthar, who was in exile, returned to his motherland, put down the rebellion and became the new king.

I stood under the towering castle wall, it was just another day in my commonplace life as a noteless maid. A sudden baby cry shook the sun but the birth of a prince could not awaken my stranding life. I stood under the towering castle wall, praises and blessings came to my ears: Some wished him to be benevolent; some wished him to be brave; some wished him to have a great future... I have seen so many royals and nobles in my life, their authorities are like knives at my throat. Just like this moment, I am waiting for my masters to punish me as my senility made me break the dishes. A little figure stands in front of me with a short wooden sword — the praised prince is protecting me just like he swore to protect his subjects. Now I wish so much he could grow up safely and bring warmth to people like the sun over Mahar Pura.

Kneeling on the cracked farmland, I prayed for the rain to save our dying crops, parched mouth, and despairing hearts. But what came before the rain was our savior in golden armor, he brought us food and relieved our suffering. When he looked down at his subjects, I could see a whole world in the depth of his eyes, a world that was as beautiful as a landscape. When he raised his eyes, he noticed the figure of a little rosewood flower, which made the world in his eyes jump with joy. Later, I was told that our savior, the crown prince of our kingdom, fell in love with a civilian girl. He shook off his royal trifles and chased free life with the girl. However, free life is not all about the starry sky and love. It also means paddy, sack clothes, and hard work within fields. This time, the prince finally got the chance to see the truth of the world and the lives of his fellow subjects. I marched to the battlefield with my comrades as the enemy warships once again broke through our naval defenses. The black waves flooded from the horizon toward us and soon turned into millions of blades. My comrades, my brothers, were pierced by the blades. They told me to bring their last smile back to our hometown. The black clouds poured out from enemy ships, covering the sun. We fought for our lives desperately but no hope could be seen. Suddenly, a golden light split across the gloomy sky, driving away all the darkness on the battlefield. I recognized the Sacred Spear in the comer's hand. That was our crown prince! The sun of Mahar Pura! He blocked all the enemy attacks with his tough body. He blew the horn to rally the desperate soldiers. Torches gathered from all over the battlefield and formed a wildfire. Under his leadership, we wrapped up all the darkness and pushed them back to where they came from. Later, we knelt before our new king and swore to be his feet and spear. May Mahar Pura shine forever. I met him again at a very old age. He returned to the palace and basked in the radiance of the crown again. I was told he once put aside his duties and lived a farmer's life with his true love. However, he couldn't turn a blind eye to the bitterness of his people. He left his rosewood flower garden, reforged his Sacred Spear, and went back to the brutal battlefield. Now I live behind the castle walls, free from the sound of battle horns. Thanks to warriors like him, I can still pour wine with care and respect. I offer him the cup of wine, he looks down, there's loneliness in his eyes. But the bright sun still shines upon the unvarying land of Mahar Pura as always.

b.q: Beautiful and powerful mermaid queen

b.p: The waters of the ancient Vonetis Sea are unforgiving and unpredictable, yet the islanders who navigate them do so without fear. Ask them why, and they will answer: because Kadita, the Ocean Goddess, watches over them. Despite the moments of doubt, suffering, and despair, this young protector still chose to wield the Trident of the Seas. Baptized by the tides and commanded by the waves, the legend of the "Ocean Goddess" flows with the currents, reaching every shore beneath the stars. Kadita's life was once like the gentle sea breeze—serene and beautiful.

As a revered princess, she understood the language of the ocean—when the tides would rise and fall, and when the storms would come and go. She passed this knowledge to the fishermen, safeguarding them from tempests and earning her the affectionate title "Daughter of the Ocean".

But one day, a sudden calamity from the sea shook her entire island. Their peaceful life came to an end as giant waves swallowed the coast and creatures corrupted by the Abyss rose and attacked the villages.
Consulting the ancient texts, Kadita learned that only by sealing the corrupted Eye of the Sea could this crisis be averted.
For the sake of her people, Kadita bravely stepped forward and ventured alone into the ruins beneath the tides.

However, the young princess was unable to withstand the Abyss's corruption. Not only did she fail to find the Eye of the Sea, her body also began to mutate under the corruption. The once beautiful princess found herself transformed into a hideous monster!
When Kadita swam back to the island with what little strength she had left, she was met with fear and rejection.

At that moment, the Abyss's corruption surged from the depths, causing giant waves to batter Blue Flame once again. Seizing the opportunity, a scheming minister branded Kadita as an "incarnation of calamity", leading her people to shun her. Devastated by this betrayal, the young princess could only respond with silence.
In the end, Kadita was exiled to a deserted island.
The Abyss's corruption continued to torment her body, but the agony in her heart was far greater—the very people she loved, the subjects she vowed to protect, had abandoned her.
Several times, she thought of throwing herself into the sea, letting the waves swallow her whole. Yet, whenever she gazed at the endless coast, she felt the ocean's power still pulling at her.
The ocean had not betrayed her; the surging waves were calling to her. Her people might have abandoned her, but she could not abandon her oath to protect the sea.
Kadita pulled herself together—she had to save this ocean!

Kadita recalled reading about a sacred artifact in the ancient texts: the Trident of the Seas. Legend held that it could purify any corruption and sever all impure energy. Though no living soul had ever seen it, the artifact was her last hope to save the ocean.

Rumors whispered that the Trident of the Seas slumbered in the deepest trenches of the Vonetis Sea. Kadita knew that to reach it, she would have to withstand the full corrupting powers of the Abyss. She would lose her elegant form forever, perhaps never to walk upon land again. Yet, the moment she plunged into the sunken ruins, her mind was fixed on only one thing—her duty as a princess to protect this ocean and all the lives within it.

Down she swam, deeper and deeper! The immense pressure of the deep wrapped around her body, and bellows from the darkness flooded her ears. The crushing weight and the chill of corruption clung to every inch of Kadita's skin like invisible hands.
Her legs gradually morphed into a fish tail. In bone-piercing agony, the corruption seared through her flesh, which was constantly being torn apart and remade.
But she could not stop here.
She was a princess. Whether her subjects who had abandoned her still recognized this mattered not. To protect this sea and these lives remained her lifelong duty.
She must press on. She must descend, no matter the cost.... In the deepest darkness, she finally found it: the Trident of the Seas.

But exhaustion finally set in. As Kadita sank, her trembling fingertips managed to graze the artifact—suddenly, the trident began to resonate with her! A powerful, pure force burst forth with azure light and gently lifted Kadita up. A soft pulse flowed from the trident and synced with Kadita's heartbeat.
It was the rhythm of the tides, the life pulse of the sea.

The tainted waters around Kadita began to purify as the turbid ripples returned to clarity. The sea then bestowed its blessing upon its guardian: Kadita not only regained her former appearance and body but also gained the ability to freely shift between her human and mermaid forms. From then on, she was no longer just the princess of Blue Flame; she had become one with this sea.
—A daughter of the sea, and the Ocean Goddess.

When Kadita returned, she swiftly calmed the restless waves and brought a long-awaited peace. The minister's scheme crumbled, and the people who had once misunderstood her now sought her forgiveness. Yet, none of this mattered to Kadita anymore.
Or rather, a higher calling now beckoned to her.
"Upon the tides, protect this sea."

In the days that followed, Kadita set aside her royal title and roamed between the sea and the land. In human form, she walked the beaches, teaching children to feel the pulse of the currents; as a mermaid, she traversed the Vonetis Sea, swimming alongside the fish.

The Vonetis Sea flourished under her protection. However, the story of the Ocean Goddess was far from over. Kadita cast her gaze toward the broader ocean, toward the threat of the Abyss. Though the waters before her had returned to azure, the future of this world remained fragile. She turned back to look at Kalea and Badang with a gentle smile upon her face:
"The sea is still calling. Let us answer it, together."

f: Absorbs soul fragment as health; Enters shadow state; Casts bursts of Nether Energy; Summons a Nether Realm

b.q: A necromancer in Necrokeep who's determined to find a cure for the Mist.

b.p: A gifted physician who came to Necrokeep to study the mysterious plague. Instead of finding the key to controlling life and death, he met Vexana, duchess of the cursed land and the girl who'd brought sunshine to his gloomy life twice. Vowing to find a way to revert the curse and repay the kindness of Vexana, Faramis voluntarily got eroded by the Mist and used himself as the specimen for his research. Faramis came from a long line of physicians. With the ancestral staff passed down the family, his grandfather combined magic and medicine and developed cures for many once-incurable diseases. The feat earned the gifted physician a title from the Moniyan Empire, and the family had since served the royalties as their personal physicians.

None of these proved adequate to earn the family respect from their equals, though. The other nobles viewed them as mere servants with some special medical skills, while young Faramis, for this reason, was often bullied and ridiculed by his peers.

At a banquet, the boys struck again, and poor Faramis was left fainted on the ground of the back garden. When he regained consciousness, he saw a highborn girl half-knelt by his side, giving him medicine. That was the only time young Faramis had received kindness from his peers. The encounter, despite being brief, was like a ray of sunshine into his gloomy life.

Frail and sickly from birth, Faramis had brushed with death numerous times and survived only because of his parents' meticulous treatment. After many near-death experiences, he vowed to conquer death and take life into his own hands and was reluctant to serve the royalties as his family did.

He found the royalties' minor ailments extremely boring and wanted nothing to do with those hypocritical nobles. He yearned to challenge complex, intractable diseases to bring his skills to heights no other physicians had ever reached before.

With this goal in mind, Faramis left Lumina City and embarked on his journey alone, solving one after another inexplicable disease along the way, not out of the responsibility of a physician, but to explore the possibility of going beyond life and death.
Upon learning about the incident in Necrokeep, Faramis believed that he'd found the perfect integration of life and death and headed to the city right away, searching for the key to controlling both.

Protected by his ancestral staff, Faramis found himself immune to the Mist that plagued the city. He walked through crowds of desolate residents and came upon Duchess Vexana, ruler of the ruined fortress. She was brewing and handing out the "Moonlight Brew", a remedy made of Moonlight Grass that was said to be the "cure" for the erosion of the Mist.
At first, Faramis thought that was all a blunt lie—she was only putting on an act, ignorant and hypocritical as the other nobles.
Until that one time, Vexana thrust the last "Moonlight Brew" in his hands without a second thought—Faramis was stunned. It was equal to giving up the "hope of life" to him.
The "hypocrite" really wanted to save everyone.
Looking at the noble lady in a new light, Faramis couldn't help but think of his brief encounter with the kindly girl in his childhood...

The Mist was nothing like the incurable diseases Faramis had encountered before. After many failed attempts, he finally made a breakthrough by infusing magic into the herbs. And with every progress he made, he insisted on testing the effects on himself. Except, his frail body could only take so much abuse. He soon started feeling the aftermath of his experiments, eventually falling faint in his laboratory. Lying on the cold floor, Faramis felt his life quickly draining out of him. He clenched his fists and tried to get up, only to find he couldn't even peel open his eyes, his consciousness gradually fading. Faramis never thought he could open his eyes again, and when he did, he saw a young lady leaning over, parting his lips to drop a bitter liquid into his mouth. With his mind in a haze, Faramis found the sight overlapped with his memory of the girl in the garden. Looking at the strange but familiar face, Faramis recognized that she was the very same noble girl who'd helped him back then.

The girl who'd brought light to his childhood had come to his aid again! During his recovery, Faramis found himself smitten with the young lady who'd saved him from darkness twice. She was the only person who'd never given him up except for his parents.

As soon as Faramis recovered, however, Vexana urged him to leave the place, saying it was dangerous for a living person to continue to stay in Necrokeep. The Mist was starting to overpower his enchanted staff. If he stayed any longer, he would soon meet a fate like theirs.

Faramis said not a word; his eyes fixated on the Moonlight Grass and the fading staff in his hands. His reason told him it was time to leave, but when he stood in front of the castle's gate and saw the forced smile on Vexana's face, he found himself unable to leave like this. Memories of the childhood encounter and the meticulous care in Necrokeep flashed across Faramis's mind. He could not give up the young lady who'd brought light and warmth twice to his life. He had made his choice, he would stay in Necrokeep and finish the task yet to be done.

Faramis let go of the protection of his staff, finally basking in the blight of the Mist. His skin turned sallow and pale, and yet he felt no fear. He knew he could conquer this scourge. And to do so, to uncover the secrets of life and death, he must experience the curse for himself.
This time, it was his turn to pull Vexana out of the misery she was in.

Badang, Guardian of Solari Isle, was raised by its tides and storms. When the Tidecaller, a sea beast, fell to the Abyss and was driven mad, Badang rallied the islanders and fought to free it from corruption. In return, he earned the sea beast's recognition and a Gem of Power imbued with its strength. With it, Badang cleansed other corrupted sea creatures and guided Kalea, the proud descendant of the Great Serpent, to claim her own power. The people place their faith in him—not only for the surging might of his fists, but also the unshakable courage in his heart.
Summer lingers on Solari Isle.

Warm, humid winds drift in from the Vonetis Sea. Along the shore, people mend their nets, humming songs as old as the tides. Weathered totems of the Great Serpent stand in quiet watch, while the Tidecaller rises now and then in the distance, its back breaking the surface like a living reef. At harvest time, offerings of fruit and grain are cast into the waters it roams. In return, it calms the waves for the fishing boats and leads the fish to shore.
This is where Badang was raised.

One day, the Tidecaller stopped appearing. In its place, a vast and distorted shape rose from the sea. It struck at every passing boat and lashed out at any soul it saw. The fishermen had no choice but to haul in their nets and abandon the sea. As their stores of grain and fish ran low, the people gathered before the ancient totem at the village gate, offering prayers into the silence. No answer came.

Badang knelt among them. He looked up at the Great Serpent carved upon the totem. Something within him sank, then slowly rose again. He clenched his fists. The truth settled in his heart. The divine would not return. Then they would have to stand on their own.

After days of watching from behind the reefs, he noticed something strange. The creature never came close to the shallow waters, as if held back by an unseen force. Its power was strongest in the deep sea. If there was any chance to bring it down, they would have to bring it ashore.
When he spoke of his plan, silence fell over the people. Only a handful stepped forward to stand with him.

The day that followed would be told in tales for years to come. As the nets tightened in the deep waters, the monster's thrashing shook the sea itself. With each pull, the ropes bit into their hands until blood ran into the water. Badang stood at the front, feet buried in wet sand, pulling with all his might. They could not fail. If they let go, the island will eventually wither and die. Badang's resolve spread through the crowd. One by one, more villagers rushed in from the shore, until at last the creature was dragged onto the beach.

Once on the sand, it was clear that its power was draining away. Twisted horns and fractured limbs began to shed from its body. As the corruption fell away, Badang recognized it—the long-lost Tidecaller. It was no evil monster, but a creature of the sea, bound by a force it could not resist. Only on land, weakened and stripped of the Abyss' influence, did its true form begin to return. Badang felt both shock and clarity: so the strength and courage of humans can do things that even the mighty Tidecaller could not.

The Tidecaller created a gemstone and offered it to Badang. When he held it in his hands, the lacerations on his arms from the rope turned burning hot. Then, a warmth spread from his palms to his shoulders, and a newfound power surged through his fists, vast and relentless like the sea. He bowed toward the creature as it returned to the sea. The gift was not just power, but recognition. Acknowledgment of the courage of humans.

With this strength, he purified the corrupted sea creatures from the surrounding waters. He cracked the earth to release hidden springs during the dry season. He lifted stranded boats back into the sea. People began to trust in him... Ships once again set sail with hope. Children returned to the shore to play. Families waited for boats to come home heavy with fish and free of fear.

During harvest seasons, people still cast fruit and grain into the waters where the Tidecaller roamed. But no longer as offerings for protection. Now they were gestures of respect. A shared understanding between the sea and land, earned through courage.

But the strange corruption did not stop. Mutated sea creatures continued to surge up from the deep. Badang purified them again and again, but the source remained hidden. Only later did he learn the truth from Kadita: this was an ancient evil—the Abyss. She also spoke of a descendant of the Great Serpent, raised under her care, who would arrive at Solari Isle—and who would need Badang's guidance to awaken her power.
Badang hesitated. He was only human. Could he truly guide the power of the Great Serpent?

The Great Serpent, who had once given its life to protect the Vonetis Sea a thousand years ago, was both legend and totem. With sincere respect, Badang received Kalea, its living descendant. Yet she was nothing like what he had imagined. Her strength surpassed that of sea monsters, while her mind was as simple as the tide itself. She was prideful of her lineage, yet quick to help the islanders, fighting alongside Badang without ever stepping back. Over time, Kalea became part of Solari Isle in his eyes—not a descendant of the Great Serpent, but a stubborn girl who never gave up.

Badang did not teach her through words. He simply showed her the way. And in time, under his guidance, Kalea found her own strength. When she understood what it meant to protect others, the power of the Great Serpent finally awakened.

Sails dot the sea. Children chase crabs along the shore. A totem stands at the village entrance. This peace was once protected by the Great Serpent. Now it is guarded by Badang and Kalea, standing side by side. They were the strength and will to protect that had been passed down for thousands of years.
Badang clenched his fist. The power had always been there, within his hands—waiting for the courage in his heart to awaken it.
