focus: Johnson is a Roaming tank whose job is to start fights and protect his carry. Impact Wrench stuns enemies around its landing point for 0.8 seconds, Electromagnetic Waves slows and makes enemies take more damage from it, and Full Throttle turns him into a car that explodes on the first enemy hero or wall it hits. At this win rate, most Johnson losses come from driving the car alone into five enemies. Take an ally with you, or drive only at a target your team can reach.

Your next step is the car's speed. Full Throttle accelerates over time, and the explosion's damage and stun (0.5 to 1 second) grow with the speed before impact, so a long, straight drive hits harder than a short one. Hold Nitrous for more speed, tap Brake to stop, and remember the enemy sees you for 3 seconds when you cast it. After the crash, Impact Wrench and Electromagnetic Waves keep the target in place while your team arrives.

Johnson is rarely picked or banned in Mythical Glory+ (pick about 0.37%, ban 0.45%, win about 46%, official site, past 30 days), so the enemy may not know how to play against him. Use that: drive in from angles they do not watch, carry your jungler or an assassin in the car (Hop In, one ally only), and save the car for the carry, not the tank. Valentina, Zilong, Natalia, Floryn and Layla are listed as his counters; Valentina can take the ultimate itself.

At the top, Johnson is a map threat more than a fighter. The car crosses lanes fast, and an ally inside arrives with you, so a two-hero gank can come from anywhere. Plan routes with walls in mind (the car also explodes on obstacles) and time drives for when the enemy's escape skills are down. Review drives that hit nobody or arrived with no follow-up: those are the lost fights.
tips: Stay with your carry in the early game. Johnson is a tank and support: his stun and slow protect the hero who deals damage. Electro Airbag gives you a 300 shield when your HP drops below 30% (100-second cooldown), but it does not save you if you walk in alone.

Aim Impact Wrench at the landing point, not the path. The wrench damages enemies in its path, but only enemies around the landing point are stunned for 0.8 seconds. Throw it onto the enemy, not short of them.

Do not drive the car into five enemies alone. Full Throttle explodes on the first enemy hero or obstacle and stuns nearby enemies, but if your team is far away, the enemy simply kills you after the stun. Drive at a target your team can reach in the next second or two.

Use Electromagnetic Waves on a target you are already next to. It keeps hitting in a fan, slows by 20%, and each hit makes the target take 15% more damage from the skill, up to 45%. You can basic attack and use skills while it runs, so hold it on one enemy rather than turning away.

Make the car fast before it hits. The explosion deals more damage and stuns longer (0.5 to 1 second) the faster the car is going before impact. Hold Nitrous on a long straight path and avoid turning at the last moment.
Carry an ally. One allied hero near you can Hop In, so your jungler or assassin arrives with the crash and can act during the stun. This turns a tank engage into a kill.
Watch the reveal. Casting Full Throttle shows your location to the enemy for 3 seconds. Start the drive from fog and far enough away that the reveal does not give them time to walk to their tank.

Follow the crash. The explosion leaves an electrified zone that keeps damaging and slowing enemies inside it. Throw Impact Wrench onto anyone trying to walk out and hold Electromagnetic Waves on the main target.

Use the car's brake on purpose. Brake stops the car at once, so you can drive toward a fight, stop in fog and wait for the right moment, then walk in, or stop short of a trap. A drive you can cancel is safer than one you cannot.

Crash into walls when the target is next to one. The car explodes on obstacles too, so a target hugging a wall in the jungle can be stunned without a direct hit. This makes narrow jungle paths the car's best ground.

Check the listed counters. In Mythical Glory+ the official site lists Valentina, Zilong, Natalia, Floryn and Layla as Johnson counters. Valentina can copy your ultimate, so bait her skill before you drive; against Floryn, the car's damage may be healed back, so drive at her first or at a target outside her reach.

Full Throttle's passive raises your Physical Defense by 10% to 30% as the skill levels up. That makes you sturdier against physical damage all game, so you can stand in front of a physical carry longer than his HP suggests.

Use the car for map moves, not only fights. With an ally inside, two heroes cross a lane in seconds. Time a drive to a side lane right after your mid wins its wave, and the enemy has to answer two heroes arriving at once.

Save the car for the carry. A car that stuns the enemy tank starts a fight your team may not win; a car that stuns the marksman or mage behind them wins it. Drive around the frontline when the path allows it.

Count escape skills before you drive. The stun lasts at most 1 second, so a target with a dash or a purify ready walks out of it. Drive when their escape is down, or follow with Impact Wrench for a second stun.
Review every drive: did it hit, did anyone follow, and did you survive? A Johnson who reviews drives quickly learns which angles work in his games.

focus: Kagura's game is the Seimei Umbrella. Seimei Umbrella Open sends it to a spot, damaging and slowing enemies on its way, and when it comes back to her she gets a 450 shield and stuns nearby enemies for 0.5 seconds. Rasho Umbrella Flee dashes and clears debuffs while the umbrella is with her, or teleports her to the umbrella when it is away. At this win rate, most losses come from sending the umbrella and then dashing toward it into the enemy team. Learn where the umbrella is at every moment, and use the dash to leave first.

Your step now is the two versions of each skill. With the umbrella in hand, Yin Yang Overturn knocks nearby enemies back (a self-peel); with it away, it damages around the umbrella and pulls enemy heroes into it after 1.5 seconds for big damage. So: send the umbrella onto the enemy, ult to start the pull, and keep the dash ready. Seimei Umbrella Open has a 5-second cooldown and deals 130% damage to non-heroes, so it also clears waves fast; clear first, then roam.

Kagura is a steady pick in Mythical Glory+ (pick about 1%, win about 51%, ban under 1%, official site, past 30 days). The listed counters are Lolita, Valir, Silvanna, Hanabi and Hanzo; Lolita leads the list by a wide margin. Against her, throw the umbrella from angles her shield does not cover. Poke before objectives with the umbrella and save the ultimate for a pull that catches two or more heroes.

At the top, Kagura is about umbrella geometry. Park it where enemies must walk (Turtle entrance, a jungle choke), so its pull and your teleport both threaten that spot. Use the return as your defence: the shield and stun come every time it reaches you, with a 4.5-second cooldown. Review fights where the umbrella was far away when a diver reached you, because those are the deaths that a mage at this level should not take.
tips: Always know where the umbrella is. Most of her skills change depending on whether the umbrella is with her or away. Before each fight, glance at it, and keep it close if an enemy assassin is near.

Use Rasho Umbrella Flee to escape first. With the umbrella in hand, it removes all debuffs and dashes you away, leaving the umbrella behind. That one button is your answer to a stun or slow, so do not spend it to chase.
Clear waves with Seimei Umbrella Open. It has a 5-second cooldown, deals 130% damage to non-hero enemies, and hits everything on its path. Clear the wave, then look for a roam or an objective.

Let the umbrella come back to you when an enemy dives you. When it returns, you get a 450 shield, and nearby enemies are stunned for 0.5 seconds and slowed by 60% for 1 second. That effect has a 4.5-second cooldown, so it is there in most fights.

Learn both ultimates. With the umbrella in hand, Yin Yang Overturn damages nearby enemies and knocks them back, which pushes a diver off you. With the umbrella away, it damages enemies around the umbrella, then after 1.5 seconds pulls enemy heroes to it for heavy damage.

Send, then pull. Throw the umbrella into the middle of the enemy team, then cast the ultimate: the first hit slows them by 60% so they struggle to walk out before the pull. The pull is her biggest damage, so it should catch the carry.

Teleport only when it is safe. With the umbrella away, Rasho Umbrella Flee teleports you to it and damages nearby enemies. That is a strong follow-up when the umbrella sits on a low target, and a death when it sits next to their tank.
Poke before objectives. The umbrella's 5-second cooldown lets you hit enemies again and again while they wait at the Turtle or Lord. A team that starts the fight at half HP loses it.

Check the counters. In Mythical Glory+ the official site lists Lolita, Valir, Silvanna, Hanabi and Hanzo as Kagura counters, with Lolita far ahead of the rest. Against Lolita, throw the umbrella from the side; against Silvanna or Hanzo, keep the dash for the moment they reach you.
Use the umbrella as vision bait. Park it in a bush or at a jungle entrance where you expect enemies. Anyone who walks past it is inside the zone of your pull ultimate and your teleport.
Mix the return into trades. Throw the umbrella, walk toward the enemy, and let it return when they step in. The 0.5-second stun on return turns a losing trade into a winning one.

Her pro sample is small (3 MPL Season 18 games), and all three builds had Divine Glaive and Genius Wand. Both reduce the target's Magic Defense or ignore part of it, which helps the umbrella's damage hold up when enemies build defense.

Plan the umbrella's spot before the fight. Park it where enemies must walk (Turtle entrance, a narrow jungle path). The pull ultimate then catches whoever enters, and your teleport threatens the same spot.
Bait with the shield. When a diver commits to you, let the umbrella return to stun and shield you, then use Rasho Umbrella Flee to leave. Their combo misses while you take almost nothing.
Hold the ultimate for two or more heroes. A pull on one hero is a kill at best; a pull on two or three wins a Lord fight. If only one enemy is near the umbrella, wait.
Review deaths where the umbrella was far away when the diver arrived. At this level, a mage who keeps the umbrella close when assassins are missing from the map loses far fewer fights.

focus: Hayabusa is a jungle assassin. Phantom Shuriken throws three returning shurikens that slow, Quad Shadow dashes and leaves four phantoms you can teleport to, and Ougi: Shadow Kill hits enemies in an area six times while he is hidden. His attacks mark enemies (up to 4 Shadow Marks), and each mark makes him deal 5% more damage to that enemy. At this win rate, most losses come from using Quad Shadow to go in and having no phantom left to leave with. Keep one phantom behind you, and mark the target before the ultimate.

Your step now is marks and phantoms. Shadow Kill prioritizes enemies with Shadow Mark and each attack consumes a mark for extra damage, so a target with four marks takes far more than one with none. Quad Shadow's phantoms stay at the end of their paths or stick to the first enemy hero hit; teleporting to a stuck phantom deals damage, teleporting to a free one is your escape. Each teleport cuts Phantom Shuriken's cooldown by 1 second, so shuriken, teleport, shuriken is the core of his damage.

Hayabusa is a quiet pick in Mythical Glory+ (pick about 0.82%, win about 48%, official site, past 30 days). The listed counters are Aamon, Yve, Nolan, Zhuxin and Karrie. Against Yve and Zhuxin, their zones slow and catch an assassin who walks in, so enter from the side after their main skill is down. Farm with Phantom Shuriken (each non-minion hit restores 10 energy) and gank side lanes where the target has no escape.

At the top, Hayabusa is about where the phantoms land. Throw Quad Shadow so one phantom sticks to the target and others land behind walls or toward your team, so every fight has a built-in exit. Use the ultimate as a finisher on marked targets, not an opener; it hides you, which also dodges skills aimed at you during it. Review fights where you ended next to the enemy team with no phantom left: that is where his deaths come from.
tips: Mark the target before you ult. Each basic attack and skill hit adds a Shadow Mark (up to 4, 6 seconds each), and each mark makes you deal 5% more damage to that enemy. Shadow Kill also consumes marks for extra damage, so hit with shurikens first, then ult.

Throw Phantom Shuriken through the target. The three shurikens return to you, slow by 35% for 2 seconds, and hit again on the way back. Extra hits on the same enemy deal only 30% after the first, so it is best through groups and creeps.

Keep one phantom as your exit. Quad Shadow dashes and sends four phantoms in different directions; you can teleport to any of them. Before you teleport onto the target, check that one free phantom sits somewhere safe.

Do not open fights with the ultimate. Shadow Kill launches 6 single-target attacks in an area and prioritizes marked enemies. It is a finisher: used too early, it splits across tanks and kills nobody.

Weave shurikens between teleports. Each teleport to a phantom cuts Phantom Shuriken's cooldown by 1 second, and the shuriken already has a 4-second cooldown. Shuriken, teleport, shuriken, teleport keeps damage and marks coming while you move.

Stick a phantom to the target. A phantom that hits an enemy hero attaches to them and deals damage; teleporting to it deals the damage again. Aim Quad Shadow so its paths cross the target, and the dash stops on the first hero it hits.

Use the shuriken's energy refund. Phantom Shuriken restores 10 energy for each non-minion enemy hit, so throwing it through jungle camps and heroes keeps you fuelled. It also gives permanent Spell Vamp (3% to 18% as it levels), so it is your sustain.
Gank side lanes, not the middle of the enemy team. His damage kills one or two heroes; it does not survive five. A lone gold laner or mage pushing a side lane is your best target.

Check the counters. In Mythical Glory+ the official site lists Aamon, Yve, Nolan, Zhuxin and Karrie as Hayabusa counters. Yve and Zhuxin's zones slow and catch an assassin who walks in; enter after those skills are spent, from the side.
Use the ultimate's hiding. During Shadow Kill you blend into the shadows, so skills aimed at you can miss. Cast it when the enemy starts a big skill at you, and it doubles as a dodge.
Phantoms are vision and escape at once. Throw Quad Shadow toward fog before you enter an unknown area: the phantoms show what is there, and you can teleport to the safest one.

In his 11 MPL Season 18 pro games, every build had Hunter Strike, and most had Malefic Roar and War Axe, with the Assassin emblem. Hunter Strike's speed after five hits in a row on one target fits a hero whose shurikens and teleports hit often.
Plan the phantom layout. Throw Quad Shadow so one phantom sticks to the target and another lands behind a wall or toward your team. Every engage then has a built-in exit before you even start.
Ult to finish, then leave. After Shadow Kill, the marks are spent and your damage drops. Use the free phantom to leave right away rather than staying for a second target with no cooldowns.
Time ganks to the enemy's escape cooldowns. A mage who just used their dash, or a marksman who used their blink, cannot outrun four phantoms. Watch fights and enter when the escape is gone.
Review fights where you ended next to the enemy team with no phantom left. At this level, those are the deaths that cost games, and almost all of them start with a Quad Shadow thrown with no exit.

focus: Sora is an EXP lane fighter whose ultimate, Shifting Skies, chooses a style for 10 seconds: swipe left for Thunder (bonus speed, briefly untargetable, three lightning strikes, assassin style) or swipe right for Torrent (a pull on nearby enemies, tank style). Both forms change Sundering Strike and Windstride. At this win rate, most losses come from picking the form without a plan. Decide before the fight: Thunder to kill a squishy target, Torrent to start a fight and hold enemies for your team.

Your next step is landing skills so Windstride comes back faster: a hit reduces its 8-second cooldown by 2 seconds. In either form, damaging heroes or summoned units builds Cloudstep, and five stacks unlock the True Art, a second big skill (Heaven's Wrath strikes an area 15 times; Stormbind strikes 5 times and stuns briefly each time and ignores terrain). So the 10 seconds are a race: hit five times early, then use the True Art while the form lasts.

Sora has a mid profile in Mythical Glory+ (pick about 0.87%, win about 50%, ban about 2%, official site, past 30 days). His listed counters are Estes, Popol and Kupa, Rafaela, Natan and Karina: two healers who undo his damage, a trapper, and two ranged burst heroes. In MPL Season 18, Sora was played with the Tank emblem in 30 of 34 games and built defense, which points to Torrent as the pro choice. Copy that while you learn him.

At the top, Sora's skill is choosing the form for the fight in front of him. Torrent's pull plus Stormbind's repeated stuns lock a group for your damage dealers; Thunder's untargetable start and Heaven's Wrath can delete a marksman who is alone. Read the enemy positions as you cast. Review fights where the 10 seconds ran out before the True Art came up: those are the ones where you entered too far from targets to build Cloudstep.
tips: Pick the form before the fight, not during it. Swipe left for Thunder (speed, briefly untargetable, three lightning strikes; assassin style) or right for Torrent (after a delay, pulls nearby enemies; tank style). If you are unsure, Torrent next to your team is the safer choice.

Land Windstride on a hero. If it hits an enemy hero or reaches max range, Sora slams the ground for extra damage and a 40% slow, and a successful hit cuts its cooldown by 2 seconds. Missing it means a full 8-second wait.
Use Sundering Strike's dash. Sundering Strike strikes twice, lunges forward, and lets him dash after striking. Use the dash to stay on a target who walks away, or to leave a trade you are losing.
The form lasts 10 seconds. Cast it next to enemies, not on the way to them, so every second of it counts.

Build Cloudstep fast. After ascending, each time you damage a hero or a summoned unit you gain a stack, and at five stacks you unlock the True Art. Hit with Sundering Strike and Windstride first, then the True Art comes while the form still lasts.

Know what each form does to your skills. In Thunder, Sundering Strike (Thunderflash) strikes four times and lets you move, and Windstride (Thunder Rush) can be recast within 4 seconds if it hits. In Torrent, Sundering Strike (Overwhelm) slows by 40% and stuns for 0.5 seconds, and Windstride (Skyfall) knocks enemies back to the landing point and airborne.
Use Thunder's untargetable start. When you ascend into Thunder, you gain brief bonus speed and become untargetable. Cast it as an enemy skill comes at you, then turn the lightning strikes onto them.
Torrent's pull has a delay. Stand in the middle of the enemies, or in their path, before you swipe right, so they are still there when the pull lands.

Check the counters. In Mythical Glory+ the official site lists Estes, Popol and Kupa, Rafaela, Natan and Karina as Sora counters. Against Estes or Rafaela, his damage gets healed back, so focus the healer first or wait until their heal is spent.

Follow the pro build while you learn. In 30 of 34 MPL Season 18 games Sora used the Tank emblem, and the most common items were Tough Boots, War Axe, Queen's Wings and Radiant Armor. Torrent's damage scales with his Max HP, so HP and defense items also raise his damage there.

Use Stormbind for terrain plays. It strikes 5 times, stuns briefly each time, and lets Sora move freely and ignore terrain. That makes it a tool for chasing a target over a jungle wall while keeping them stunned.
Keep one skill for the end of the form. When the 10 seconds end, Sora goes back to his base skills. Holding Sundering Strike's dash until then gives you a way out once the form drops.

Choose the form by the target. Torrent's pull and Stormbind's stuns lock a group for your damage dealers; Thunder and Heaven's Wrath (15 hits in an area) delete one squishy hero who is alone. Read where the enemy carry stands as you swipe.
Start fights for your team with Torrent. A pull plus Skyfall's airborne gives your mage and marksman a group that cannot move. Ping before you swipe so they are in range.
Time the ultimate around Turtle and Lord. The ultimate has a cooldown of 32 to 24 seconds as it levels. Push your lane after winning it, then arrive at the objective with the ultimate ready.

Review fights where the form ended before the True Art. Those fights started too far from targets to build five Cloudstep stacks, and fixing the entry point is the fastest way to raise Sora's win rate.

focus: Miya is a Gold Lane marksman who wins by attacking for a long time. Each basic attack gives her 5% Attack Speed for 4 seconds, up to 5 stacks, and at full stacks each attack also summons a Moonlight Shadow. Hidden Moonlight removes all debuffs, hides her and gives her 65% extra speed for 2 seconds. At this win rate, most Miya losses come from standing in front, or from using the ultimate to walk in instead of out. Stay behind your frontline, attack the closest safe target, and keep the ultimate for the moment you are caught.

Your step now is the skill order. Arrow of Eclipse immobilizes enemies in the area for 1.2 seconds, then splits into six arrows that slow by 30%; Moon Arrow adds two extra arrows to each attack for 4 seconds, splashing 30% to nearby targets. Lock with Arrow of Eclipse, then turn on Moon Arrow and attack: that is her burst. Hidden Moonlight is also an attack-speed tool: when it ends, she gets full Moon Blessing stacks at once.

Miya is a steady pick in Mythical Glory+ (pick about 1.36%, win about 50%, ban about 1.93%, official site, past 30 days) and was played in 69 MPL Season 18 games. Every pro build had Corrosion Scythe, and most had Golden Staff and Demon Hunter Sword: attack-speed and on-hit items that fit Moon Blessing and Moon Arrow. Her listed counters are Saber, Guinevere, Obsidia, Kalea and Jawhead, heroes who reach her fast. Play near your tank when they are on the enemy team.

At the top, Miya is about uptime. A marksman who attacks for the whole fight wins it; one who dies in the first two seconds loses it. Stand where divers must cross your frontline, keep Arrow of Eclipse for the diver rather than the tank, and use Hidden Moonlight before a lock lands, not after. Review fights where you died with the ultimate up: those are the ones to fix first.
tips: Stay behind your tank. Miya has no dash; her only escape is Hidden Moonlight. If you stand in front, you will be the first target of every fight.

Keep attacking. Each hit gives 5% Attack Speed for 4 seconds, up to 5 stacks, and full stacks add a Moonlight Shadow to each attack. Walking away for too long resets that, so attack the closest target you can hit safely.
Use the ultimate to escape. Hidden Moonlight removes all debuffs, hides you and gives 65% extra speed for 2 seconds or until you attack. Walk away during it; attacking ends it early.
Copy the pro core while you learn. All 69 MPL Season 18 builds had Corrosion Scythe, and most added Golden Staff and Demon Hunter Sword. That way, a loss teaches you about position, not items.

Lock, then shoot. Arrow of Eclipse immobilizes enemies in the area for 1.2 seconds and splits into six arrows that slow by 30% for 2 seconds. Cast Moon Arrow while they are held: two extra arrows per attack for 4 seconds, splashing 30% to nearby targets.
Use the ultimate for stacks. When Hidden Moonlight ends, you gain full Moon Blessing stacks. Hide, reposition, then start attacking at full speed instead of building stacks under fire.
Push with Moon Arrow. The extra arrows hit nearby targets for 30%, so Moon Arrow clears a wave quickly. Clear, then walk to where your team is.
Keep Arrow of Eclipse for the diver. A 1.2-second immobilize on the assassin who jumps on you saves your life; the same skill on the tank does little.

Check the counters. In Mythical Glory+ the official site lists Saber, Guinevere, Obsidia, Kalea and Jawhead as Miya counters. Saber's and Jawhead's ultimates go through Hidden Moonlight's escape if they lock you first, so cast it the moment they are near, not after.

Know your on-hit items. Corrosion Scythe adds damage and a slow to basic attacks, Golden Staff makes every third basic attack faster and trigger attack effects two extra times, and Demon Hunter Sword adds damage based on the target's HP. All three work with Moon Arrow's extra arrows, which inherit part of your attack effects.
Move between attacks, not instead of them. Short steps after each attack keep your stacks while making you harder to hit.
Hidden Moonlight's cooldown drops from 30 to 20 seconds as it levels. Fights that last longer than the cooldown give you a second use, so after a hide, watch for its return.
Plan your stand point. Stand where divers must cross your frontline and your tank's control to reach you. That alone decides most fights a hypercarry plays.
Hide before the lock. Cast Hidden Moonlight when the enemy assassin commits, not after their stun lands; once you are stunned, you cannot cast it.
Focus the closest target. A Miya who walks forward to reach the enemy carry gives up her position; one who shoots the tank in front of her while staying safe still wins long fights.
Review fights where you died with the ultimate ready. At this level those are reaction mistakes, and fixing them is worth more than any build change.

focus: Layla is a Gold Lane marksman with long range. Her passive, Malefic Gun, makes her deal more damage the farther the enemy is (100% up to 130% at 6 units away, not against turrets). Her ultimate, Destruction Rush, fires a long line blast and also raises her attack and Void Projectile range for the rest of the game as you level it. She has no dash. At this win rate, most Layla losses come from standing close. Keep distance, hit from max range, and let your tank stand between you and the enemy.

Your step now is using Malefic Bomb as your movement. A hit gives 60% Movement Speed that decays over 1.2 seconds (doubled when it hits a hero) and extra range on attacks and Void Projectile for 3 seconds. Void Projectile marks enemies for 3 seconds, and hitting a marked enemy deals more damage and stuns for 0.25 seconds. Bomb a hero, attack from the extended range, then step back with the speed.

Layla is a common pick in lower ranks, and in Mythical Glory+ she sits at pick about 0.99%, win about 47.6% and ban about 0.53% (official site, past 30 days), with no MPL Season 18 games. Her listed counters are Phoveus, Edith, Rafaela, Diggie and Marcel. Against heroes who reach her quickly, her lack of escape is the whole problem, so play closer to the tank and farther from the bushes.

At the top, Layla's job is to never let the enemy reach her. Ward bushes with your team, stand behind your tank's control, and use the ultimate's extra range to hit the enemy from outside their reach. Use Destruction Rush as a finisher or a long-range poke through a group. Review deaths where an enemy reached you from a bush: almost all of them come from walking forward without vision.
tips: Keep your distance. Malefic Gun makes your damage grow with distance, from 100% to 130% at 6 units. Standing close lowers your damage and puts you in reach of the enemy, so take the farthest spot from which you can still hit the target.
Stay behind your tank. Layla has no dash or blink in her kit, so your safety is your position and your team. If your tank is dead or far away, step back and wait instead of taking a fight alone.

Bomb first. Malefic Bomb hits the first enemy for damage that can crit and gives your attacks and Void Projectile extra range for 3 seconds. Open every trade with it, because those 3 seconds of range let you hit from safety.

Use the ultimate as a finisher. Destruction Rush deals damage to all enemies in a line, so it hits a fleeing target or a group from far away. Firing it at a full-HP tank wastes a skill with a long cooldown (37 seconds at first).
Use Malefic Bomb's speed. A hit gives 60% Movement Speed that decays over 1.2 seconds, and the duration doubles when it hits a hero. Use it to step back after attacking, or to reach a better spot.

Mark, then hit. Void Projectile applies a Magic Mark for 3 seconds. Hitting a marked enemy deals damage to nearby enemies and stuns them for 0.25 seconds. A short stun is enough to stop an enemy walking toward you.
Clear waves from far away. Void Projectile's area damage hits a group of minions. Clear the wave from max range, then step back.

Level the ultimate early. Destruction Rush's passive adds 0.6 to 1.8 units of range to your attacks and Void Projectile as it levels, and a little sight range. That range is your safety for the whole game.

Turrets do not count for Malefic Gun. Her distance bonus does not include turrets, so pushing a turret does not get the extra damage. Push with your minions in front and leave when enemies appear.
Save the stun from Void Projectile for a diver. A 0.25-second stun is short, but it can stop an enemy's walk or cancel their momentum long enough for you to step away.

Fire Destruction Rush through a line of enemies. The blast hits all enemies in a line; aim it through the frontline into the carry behind.
Hit the closest target from max range. Walking toward the enemy carry gives up the distance that makes her strong.
Review deaths where an enemy reached you from a bush. Almost all Layla deaths start that way, and fixing them is worth more than any build change.

focus: Zhuxin is a mid lane mage built around Lantern Flare: you hold the button to move the Spirit Lantern, damaging enemies in range every 0.33 seconds and stacking Soul Snare on heroes. At 10 stacks, the Crimson Butterflies capture the hero and pull them airborne for 1 second; when you release, you throw them to a target spot for big damage. Every tick costs 90 Mana. At this win rate, most losses come from holding the lantern until your Mana is empty. Hold it only while it hits heroes, and release before you run dry.

Your step now is the Mana loop. Mana spent on Lantern Flare becomes up to 15 Crimson Butterflies, and when you stop channelling, each one returns 3% of your Max Mana. Her base Max Mana is high but does not grow with level. So channel in bursts: a short hold that lands, a release, a pause for the butterflies to return. Fluttering Grace (a fan that slows heroes by 20% to 40% and gives you speed for 1.5 seconds) adds one Soul Snare stack and starts each engage.

Zhuxin is a pro favourite: 119 MPL Season 18 games, almost all with Glowing Wand. In Mythical Glory+ she is less common (pick about 0.41%, win about 51%, official site, past 30 days). Her listed counters are Lolita, Khufra, Lukas, Gloo and Aulus: Lolita's shield blocks the lantern's ticks, and Khufra's jump interrupts the channel. Against them, hold the lantern from behind your tank.

At the top, Zhuxin is about where you throw. A captured hero can be thrown into your team, under your turret, or into a wall of your damage. Crimson Beacon blinks you with a 400 to 700 shield and a field that adds a Soul Snare stack every 0.5 seconds for 6 seconds, which is your fastest path to 10 stacks on several heroes at once. Review fights where you captured a hero and threw them somewhere useless: that is the gap between good and great on her.
tips: Hold Lantern Flare only while it hits heroes. Each tick costs 90 Mana whether it hits or not. A lantern held over empty ground empties your Mana bar.
Get to 10 Soul Snare stacks. Each tick on a hero adds a stack. At 10, the Crimson Butterflies capture the hero, pulling them airborne for 1 second. That capture is your main tool.

Throw captured enemies somewhere useful. On release, you throw all captured enemies to the target spot, dealing damage plus 10% to 15% of their Max HP. Throw them toward your team or under your turret.
Start with Fluttering Grace. It damages a fan in front of you, adds a Soul Snare stack, slows heroes and speeds you up for 1.5 seconds. Use it to open a fight or to leave.

Use the butterflies to refill Mana. Mana you spend on the lantern becomes up to 15 Crimson Butterflies; when you stop channelling, each returns 3% of your Max Mana. Hold, release, pause, and your bar refills.
Her Mana does not grow with level. Zhuxin has a high base Max Mana that does not scale with level. Late in the game, long holds cost as much as early, so stay in short bursts.

Use the ultimate to stack faster. Crimson Beacon blinks you to a target spot with a 400 to 700 shield and creates a field for 6 seconds that adds a Soul Snare stack every 0.5 seconds. Combined with the lantern, it reaches 10 stacks on several heroes at once.
Clear waves with the lantern. Its Magic Power scaling rises to 60% against minions. Clear quickly, then stop channelling so your Mana comes back.

Check the counters. In Mythical Glory+ the official site lists Lolita, Khufra, Lukas, Gloo and Aulus as Zhuxin counters. Against Lolita, the lantern struggles to reach targets behind her shield; against Khufra, stand behind your tank so his jump hits someone else first.

Copy the pro build while you learn. In MPL Season 18, Glowing Wand was in 118 of 119 Zhuxin builds, and most added Ice Queen Wand and Elegant Gem. Glowing Wand's burn adds percent-HP damage, and Elegant Gem adds Mana for her lantern.

After a capture, the target cannot gain Soul Snare for 4 seconds, but the lantern deals 15% more damage to them during that time. Keep the lantern on them for damage, or move it to the next target to build their stacks.
Plan where you throw. A captured hero thrown into your team or under your turret dies; one thrown back to their team escapes. Decide the throw spot before the capture lands.
Use the ultimate to start, not to finish. Crimson Beacon's blink and field stack Soul Snare on everyone near you, so it is best as the opening of a fight where your team is ready to follow.
Watch for channel breakers. Heroes like Khufra can reach you mid-channel. Release before they arrive, or keep the ultimate's shield for that moment.
Review fights where a capture was thrown somewhere useless. At this level, the throw decides the fight more than the damage.

focus: Chou is an EXP lane fighter. Jeet Kune Do strikes three times, and the third cast knocks enemies airborne and, if it hits a hero, resets Shunpo. Shunpo dashes with control immunity and a 200 shield. The Way of Dragon kicks a target hero back, and a recast chases them. At this win rate, most Chou losses come from kicking enemies away from your team. Kick the enemy toward your team, or kick a diver off your carry.

Your next step is the Shunpo reset. Hit a hero with the third Jeet Kune Do, and Shunpo is ready again, so you can dash in with control immunity, knock up, and dash again. His passive, Only Fast, makes the next basic attack deal 180% damage, slow by 80% and lower Physical Defense after he travels 5 units. Walk or dash before you attack, and the first attack lands hard.

Chou is a regular pick in Mythical Glory+ (pick about 0.91%, win about 44.6%, ban about 1.38%, official site, past 30 days) and was played in 42 MPL Season 18 games. His listed counters are X.Borg, Fanny, Natalia, Beatrix and Benedetta. In pro builds, the emblems were split between Tank and Fighter, and the most common items were Endless Battle, War Axe and Brute Force Breastplate. Choose the tank build when your team needs a frontline and the fighter build when it needs damage.

At the top, Chou is a pick-off and peel hero. The kick decides fights: a carry kicked into your team dies; a diver kicked off your marksman saves her. Read where your team is before you cast it. Review fights where the kick sent a target to safety: at this level, those are the ones that cost games.
tips: Kick toward your team. The Way of Dragon kicks the target back from you. Stand so that back is your team or your turret, not theirs.
Use all three Jeet Kune Do casts. The skill strikes three times before its cooldown; the third cast knocks enemies airborne. Do not stop after one or two.
Keep Shunpo for escape early. Shunpo dashes with control immunity and a 200 shield. Until you learn the reset, it is your way out.
Use the passive. After travelling 5 units, your next basic attack deals 180% damage, slows by 80% and lowers Physical Defense. Walk or dash before you attack.
Reset Shunpo with the third Jeet Kune Do. Hitting a hero with the third cast resets Shunpo's cooldown. Dash in, knock up, dash again.
Use Shunpo's control immunity. During Shunpo, crowd control cannot stop you. Dash through a stun aimed at you.
Recast the ultimate to chase. The Way of Dragon can be cast again to chase the target. Use the first kick to send them where you want, then follow.
Kick divers off your carry. The kick works as peel too: a diver kicked away from your marksman loses their combo.

Check the counters before you pick a target. In Mythical Glory+ the official site lists X.Borg, Fanny, Natalia, Beatrix and Benedetta as Chou counters. Fanny and Benedetta move too often for the kick to land reliably, so keep The Way of Dragon for the moment they stop or are slowed, and spend Jeet Kune Do on whoever is easier to reach.

Choose the build by what your team lacks. In MPL Season 18 Chou's emblems were split between Tank (22 games) and Fighter (20), and the most common items were Endless Battle, War Axe and Brute Force Breastplate. With no other frontliner on your team, take the tank route and play as peel; with a tank already there, the fighter route makes your kicks lethal.

Use the passive's defense cut for your team. The empowered attack after 5 units of travel lowers the target's Physical Defense by 10 for 3 seconds, stacking twice. Land it on the enemy your marksman or jungler is about to hit, so their damage gains from it too.

Plan trades around Jeet Kune Do's cooldown. It deals 180 per hit and comes back in 9.5 seconds at first, 8 seconds at max level. Trade when all three casts are ready, then back off until it returns; trading without it gives the enemy fighter the upper hand.

Set up the kick angle before the fight starts. The Way of Dragon sends the target away from Chou, so the target's back must face your team. Walk around them during the lane or the opening seconds of the fight; a kick from the wrong side sends the carry to safety and ends your chance.

Use the Shunpo reset for double engages. Shunpo in with control immunity, land the third Jeet Kune Do on a hero to reset it, then Shunpo again onto the second target or out. Two dashes in one fight are what let Chou both start a fight and survive it.

Spend the kick on the carry or the diver, never the tank. A kick on the tank moves a hero who wants to be in front. A kick that sends the marksman into your team, or the assassin off your marksman, decides the fight.

Review every kick: where did the target land, and did someone follow? Kicks that sent a target toward their team or nobody followed are the fights to fix first, and they are usually decided before you press the button.

focus: Valir is a mid lane mage who controls space with fire. Every skill hit adds a stack of Ablaze (a burn of 0.6% of Max HP per second for 4 seconds), and at 3 stacks the fire detonates for 6% of the target's Max HP and a 1-second stun. Burst Fireball holds 2 charges, and hitting a hero gives a charge back at once. At this win rate, most losses come from throwing fireballs at minions while enemy heroes walk past. Aim fireballs at heroes first: each hit is damage, slow, a stack and a refund.

Your step now is counting Ablaze. Two fireballs and a Searing Torrent are three stacks, which means a stun, but the same target can only be stunned by your skills once every 7 seconds. So the stun is a timed event: land it when your team can follow, then use the next 7 seconds for damage and spacing. Searing Torrent knocks enemies to the end of its path, so it decides where the target ends up: away from your carry, or into your team.

Valir is strong in Mythical Glory+ right now (pick about 1.16%, win about 53.8%, ban about 2%, official site, past 30 days). The listed counters are Alice, Fredrinn, Balmond, Leomord and Thamuz: sustain fighters and divers who absorb or ignore his slows. He also appears on other heroes' counter lists, including Kagura's. His MPL sample is small (7 games, 5 wins), and every build had Glowing Wand and Ice Queen Wand.

At the top, Valir is a peel mage. Vengeance Flame removes all debuffs and gives 4 flames for 9 seconds; each skill during it uses a flame for 30% more base damage and an enhanced effect (Searing Torrent leaves a 4-second fire wall). Use it to stop a dive: purify the stun, torrent the diver away, and wall them off from your carry. Review fights where a diver reached your marksman while you had the ultimate: that is Valir's main job at this level.
tips: Aim fireballs at heroes. Burst Fireball holds 2 charges and recharges one every 9 seconds, but hitting an enemy hero or a Legend Creep restores a charge at once. A fireball on a hero is damage, a slow, an Ablaze stack and a refund.
Three hits stun. Each skill hit adds an Ablaze stack, and at 3 stacks the fire detonates for 6% of the target's Max HP and stuns for 1 second. Two fireballs and a torrent are your stun.
Use Searing Torrent to push enemies away. It knocks enemies hit to the end of its path. Aim it at a diver to send them away from you or your carry.
Clear waves with fireballs, then roam. Hitting a minion restores half the recharge time, so fireballs clear waves without running out. Clear, then help your team.
Mind the stun's 7-second limit. The same target can only be stunned by your skills once every 7 seconds. Land the stun when your team can follow, then spend the next 7 seconds on damage and spacing.
Decide where the torrent sends the target. The knockback goes to the end of its path, so aim from the side to push an enemy into your team, or straight to push them away from your carry.
Use the ultimate to purify. Vengeance Flame removes all debuffs and gives 40% speed that decays over 3 seconds. Use it when you are stunned or slowed during a dive.
Spend the four flames. The ultimate conjures 4 Vengeance Flames for 9 seconds; each skill uses one for 30% extra base damage and an enhanced effect. Use all four before they expire.

Check the counters. In Mythical Glory+ the official site lists Alice, Fredrinn, Balmond, Leomord and Thamuz as Valir counters. Against sustain fighters, Glowing Wand's healing reduction matters, and your job is to keep them away from your backline rather than to kill them.

Copy the pro build while you learn. All 7 MPL Season 18 Valir builds had Glowing Wand and Ice Queen Wand. Glowing Wand burns for 1% of Max HP per second and cuts shields and regen to 60%; Ice Queen Wand adds a 10% slow per skill hit, stacking to 3.

Use the enhanced torrent as a wall. During Vengeance Flame, Searing Torrent forms a fire wall at the end of its path for 4 seconds, damaging nearby enemies and slowing those it hits by 25%. Place it between the enemy and your carry.
Poke before objectives. Fireballs refund on hero hits, so a hero-hitting Valir can keep poking during the wait before the Turtle or Lord.
Peel first, damage second. A Valir who sends the diver away from his marksman wins more fights than one who dives the enemy carry.
Time the stun with your team's engage. Ping before you land the third stack, so your team's damage lands during the 1-second stun.
Keep the ultimate for the dive. Vengeance Flame's purify is your answer to a stun on you; spending it early leaves you without it.
Review fights where a diver reached your carry while you had the ultimate. That is Valir's main job, and fixing it is worth more than any build change.

focus: Badang is a fighter usually played as a roamer in pro games. Fist Break dashes with a shield and stops on the first enemy hero it hits, creating an obstacle behind them for 4 seconds. At this win rate, most losses come from using the skills without the wall. The combo is the point: Fist Break builds the wall, and Fist Wind knocks the target into it for the stun.

Your step now is the wall combo. Fist Break stops on the first hero it hits and places an obstacle behind them. Fist Wind knocks back and explodes on obstacles, and it triggers the passive's knockback (it also grants a Chivalry Fist stack on cast). So: Fist Break into the target, Fist Wind to knock them into the wall for the stun, then Fist Crack's 9 punches over 2.5 seconds, with control immunity, while they cannot leave.

Fist Crack's punches also explode on obstacles, so a target pinned against terrain takes more. Review fights where your Fist Wind knocked a target away from the wall instead of into it: at this level, that angle decides whether the pick happens.

focus: Grock is a Roaming tank who gets stronger near terrain. Your next step is using walls with each skill. Mighty Swing knocks enemies with an obstacle behind them into it, launching them airborne for extra damage. Earthen Rampart summons a wall after a brief delay and knocks enemies toward Grock, and that wall is an obstacle for Mighty Swing. Tectonic Charge stops on terrain and explodes, knocking enemies airborne for 1 second; if it misses terrain, half its cooldown comes back.

Review fights where you charged into open ground: those are where the ultimate wasted half its cooldown and the fight was lost.

focus: Aulus is a jungle fighter who gets stronger with every skill he lands. His passive, Fighting Spirit, gives 2 seconds of enhanced basic attacks after any skill damage (up to 4 seconds): longer range, faster attacks, a line hit that slows, and 30 HP back per hit. Aulus, Charge! clears slows and gives 30% speed for 5 seconds, and if no hard control hits him in the first 2 seconds, he becomes immune to control for the rest. At this win rate, most losses come from walking into a stun in those first 2 seconds. Charge in when the enemy's main stun has been used.

Your step now is chaining skills into attacks. Every skill hit adds enhanced attack time, so The Power of Axe (a fan that stuns for 0.3 seconds and slows 30%, then a recast dash smash) followed by attacks, then the recast, keeps the enhanced state running. Cleaving Axe swings four times, then a wide final slash, with 20% to 40% damage reduction and speed on each slash. Cast it in the middle of enemies, after the Charge, so you are hard to stop while it finishes.

Aulus is a top priority in Mythical Glory+: banned in about 64.8% of games, with a win rate about 54.1% when he gets through (official site, past 30 days), and played in 119 MPL Season 18 games. His listed counters are Gloo, Minsitthar, Tigreal, Lolita and Natalia: heroes with hard control that land in his first 2 seconds, or stop his engage outright. War Axe was in 118 of 119 pro builds and Queen's Wings in 106.

At the top, Aulus is a timing hero. His engage is strong once the enemy's hard control is spent, and his ultimate's damage reduction means he survives fights he starts at the right moment. Track the enemy tank's and support's key skills and enter a second after they are used. Review fights where you were stunned during the first 2 seconds of Charge: those are the ones a top Aulus avoids.
tips: Land skills to power your attacks. After dealing skill damage to any unit, Aulus gets 2 seconds of enhanced basic attacks (up to 4 seconds): more range, more attack speed, a line hit that slows, and 30 HP per hit. A skill before each burst of attacks is his whole rhythm.

Charge in after the enemy's control. Aulus, Charge! removes slows and gives 30% speed for 5 seconds, and if you take no hard control in the first 2 seconds, you become control immune for the rest. Walk into a stun in those 2 seconds and the immunity never comes.

Use The Power of Axe twice. The first cast swings a fan that stuns for 0.3 seconds and slows by 30% for 2 seconds. Recast to dash forward and smash the ground for more damage, even if the first cast missed.
Ult in the middle of enemies. Cleaving Axe swings at nearby enemies four times, then unleashes a wider slash. You gain 20% to 40% damage reduction during it, so it is safe to cast inside a fight.
Chain skills between attacks. Every skill hit adds enhanced attack time. Swing, attack, recast the dash, attack: the enhanced state stays up and each hit heals 30 HP.
Use the dash recast to chase or close distance. The Power of Axe's second cast dashes forward and works even if the first missed, so it also catches a target who walks away.
Use Charge to cross slows. Charge removes all slows on Aulus. Use it to break a slow from a mage before the fight, then enter.
Cleaving Axe gives speed on each slash. A short burst of speed with each slash lets you follow enemies who walk away during the ultimate.

Check the counters. In Mythical Glory+ the official site lists Gloo, Minsitthar, Tigreal, Lolita and Natalia as Aulus counters. Minsitthar can stop dashes, and Tigreal and Gloo have hard control that lands in your first 2 seconds. Wait for those skills before you charge.

Track the enemy's hard control. Count the tank's and support's key skills (a Tigreal ultimate, a Gloo or Lolita control skill). Enter a second after they are used, so the first 2 seconds of Charge pass clean and the control immunity comes in.

Ult when the immunity is up. Cast Cleaving Axe after Charge's first 2 seconds, so you are control immune and taking 20% to 40% less damage while the four strikes and the wide slash land. Cast earlier and a single stun can cut it short.
Enter from the side. A side entry reaches the backline and avoids the frontline's control, and the wide final slash of Cleaving Axe hits more enemies when you stand in the middle of their formation.

Review fights where you were stunned in the first 2 seconds of Charge. Those fights show which enemy skill you entered into, and learning to wait for that one skill is what separates a top Aulus from the rest.

focus: Carmilla is a Roaming support built around her ultimate, Curse of Blood. It slows enemies in an area by 50%, and after 0.8 seconds, enemies still inside take damage, are immobilized for 1 second and are linked for 5 seconds. Linked enemies share 50% of damage and 100% of control: stun one and you stun them all. At this win rate, most losses come from ulting one enemy. The link is the point: aim it at two or more, then make sure your team has control to spread through it.

Your step now is Bloodbath. It gives 70% speed that decays over 4.5 seconds while it charges, and its recast stuns the target for 0.6 seconds with damage, both scaling with the charge time (up to 100%). Charge it on the way in, then recast on the target. Crimson Flower circles you for 5 seconds, slowing each hit (up to 50%) and healing you 75 to 150 HP per hit, so stay close to enemies while it spins. Her passive steals defense from every hero you hit, so the longer you stay in, the tougher you are.

Carmilla is a top pick in Mythical Glory+ (pick about 1.79%, win about 52.9%, ban about 39.4%, official site, past 30 days) and was played in 115 MPL Season 18 games, all with the Tank emblem. The most common items were Antique Cuirass, Radiant Armor and Chastise Pauldron. Her listed counters are Chip, Popol and Kupa, Estes, Minotaur and Cyclops; Estes can heal through the shared damage, and heroes who move apart break the link.

At the top, Carmilla is a fight starter whose ultimate multiplies her team's control. Aim Curse of Blood so it catches the carry together with a frontliner, then let your tank or mage land one stun that spreads to everyone linked. Enemies break the link by moving apart, so the follow-up must come fast. Review fights where you ulted one target or where nobody followed within the 5-second link.
tips: Aim the ultimate at two or more enemies. Curse of Blood links everyone it immobilizes for 5 seconds. Linked enemies share 50% of damage and 100% of control, so a stun on one stuns all. One enemy linked is a wasted ultimate.
The ultimate has a delay. Enemies are slowed by 50% at once, and after 0.8 seconds those still inside take damage and are immobilized for 1 second. Cast it where they will still be.
Charge Bloodbath on the way in. Bloodbath gives 70% speed that decays over 4.5 seconds while it charges. The recast's damage and stun grow with the charge time, up to 100%.

Stay close while Crimson Flower spins. Two flowers circle you for 5 seconds, slowing each hit (up to 50%) and healing you 75 to 150 HP per hit (30% on minions). Walk into enemies to make the flowers hit.

Steal defense in fights. Each time you damage an enemy hero, you steal 7 to 11 Physical and Magic Defense for 5 seconds, up to 5 stacks, once per hero every 5 seconds. Hitting several heroes makes you much tougher.
Recast Bloodbath on the carry. The recast stuns the target for 0.6 seconds (at full charge). Use it on the hero who can escape or who deals the most damage.
Follow the link with control. After the ultimate, your tank's or mage's stun on one linked enemy spreads to all of them. Ping your team before you cast.
Watch for link breaks. Enemies can break the link by moving apart. Follow-up must come within those 5 seconds, before they spread out.

Check the counters. In Mythical Glory+ the official site lists Chip, Popol and Kupa, Estes, Minotaur and Cyclops as Carmilla counters. Estes's healing undoes shared damage; ult when his heal is spent.
Copy the pro build while you learn. All 115 MPL Season 18 Carmilla builds used the Tank emblem, and the most common items were Antique Cuirass, Radiant Armor and Chastise Pauldron.
Use the ultimate's cooldown wisely. Curse of Blood has a 60, 52 and 44-second cooldown. Save it for objective fights, not lane skirmishes.
Combine the ultimate with your team's area damage. Linked enemies share 50% of damage, so a mage's area skill on the group multiplies.

Catch the carry with a frontliner. Aim Curse of Blood so it immobilizes the enemy carry and their tank together; any control your team lands on the tank then also controls the carry for the full duration, and half the damage on one is shared.

Ping before you cast. Linked enemies can break the link by moving apart, so follow-up control has to come during the 1-second immobilize or right after it. Ping, wait for your team to be in range, then cast.

Keep stolen defense up. Each enemy hero gives up to one stack every 5 seconds, up to 5 stacks lasting 5 seconds. In a long fight, touch each enemy once with Crimson Flower or Bloodbath, and you stay at full stacks.
Review fights where you ulted one target or where nobody followed. Both waste a skill with a cooldown of up to 60 seconds, and both are decided before the cast, by where your team stands.

sel.intro: I'm Sel. I pull one idea at a time from the app's guides, so you can learn a little each time you open it. Tap a tip to read the full guide.

tips.t: The goal: Destroy the enemy Base. Everything else in Mobile Legends (kills, gold, buffs, Turtle, Lord) only matters because it helps you get there faster or stops the enemy from getting to yours.
The map in one picture: The Land of Dawn has three lanes (top, middle, bottom), each guarded by three turrets per team: the Outer Turret, the Inner Turret and the Inhibitor (Base) Turret.
Why turrets matter so much: A turret is permanent map control. When your Outer Turret falls, that part of the jungle becomes dangerous for your team and safe for theirs.
The six roles: Many heroes have two roles (for example Fighter/Assassin), and the in-game lane is what really matters: EXP, Mid, Gold, Jungle or Roam. Every hero page in this app shows both.

Gold priority: A simple way to think about who gets resources: Jungler and Gold Laner first, then Mid and EXP, then Roamer. The Roamer buys a Roaming item that shares gold with the team, and the team plays to make the carries strong.
Damage types: Physical damage is reduced by Physical Defense; magic damage by Magic Defense; true damage ignores both. Check each hero's damage type on its page before you choose defensive items.

Minion waves: Minions spawn from each Base and walk down all three lanes. Last-hitting them (dealing the killing blow) gives the most gold; if a minion is killed by something else while you are nearby, you get less.
Why waves matter: A wave that reaches an enemy turret makes the turret shoot minions instead of heroes, which is the safest time to hit it. A wave that crashes into your turret is gold you lose.
Retribution: Junglers carry the Retribution spell and a jungle item (Flame, Ice or Bloody Retribution), which upgrades as they farm.

Item categories: The shop has Attack, Magic, Defense, Movement (boots), Jungling and Roaming items. Most heroes build one pair of boots, one Jungling or Roaming item if they jungle or roam, and five or six main items.

Anti-heal: When an enemy heals a lot, Sea Halberd (physical), Dominance Ice (defense) and Glowing Wand (magic) are the common answers. Each item page in this app shows its exact passive from the MLBB Wiki.

Emblems: You pick one emblem set before the match. Each set gives fixed attributes, then you choose talents: standard talents and one core talent. The Basic Common set's talents can be used with any set.
Look every few seconds: The minimap shows allied vision, enemy heroes in vision, turret states and objective timers. Glance at it after every wave, every buff and every fight.

tips.h: Think in win conditions, not heroes
tips.t: Think in win conditions, not heroes: Before the draft starts, decide how your team wants to win: early skirmishes and snowball, a front-to-back late-game teamfight, split push, or pick-offs. Every pick should push that plan forward or deny the enemy theirs.
Flex picks: A flex pick is a hero who can go to two or more lanes. It hides your intention: the enemy cannot counter-pick a lane they cannot read.

tips.h: Solo queue drafting at high ranks
tips.t: Solo queue drafting at high ranks: You cannot coordinate five players, so draft to cover what is missing. If no one has picked a frontline by your turn, a tank or tanky fighter is worth more than your best assassin. Ban what you lose to, not what you dislike.

Counter the player, too: At Mythical Immortal, the person matters as much as the hero. A one-trick Fanny player gets a ban or a hard-control lineup. A hyper-aggressive Jungler gets an invade-ready lineup that punishes their first rotation.
Positioning first: Most deaths at high rank are positioning errors, not mechanics errors. Before every fight, ask: where is the enemy initiator, and am I within their engage range?

Hold your key skill: The best players hold their crowd control or escape until the enemy commits. A stun used at the start of a fight is predictable; a stun saved for the enemy assassin's dive wins the fight.
Animation and attack canceling: Many heroes can cancel the end of a basic attack animation with movement or a skill. Practice in Practice mode until the timing is automatic.
Target selection: The target you can kill is usually more valuable than the target you want to kill. In teamfights, hit what is in front of you until the backline is reachable safely.

Cooldown tracking: Track the enemy's ultimates and spells (especially Flicker, Purify, Retribution). The window right after an enemy uses Flicker is the best time to engage on them; Flicker's cooldown is listed in the Spells screen.

Tempo: Tempo is who forces the other team to react. A team with tempo arrives first at objectives, starts fights on its terms and takes free turrets. You gain tempo by clearing your wave quickly, then moving before the enemy does.

Trading objectives: When the enemy takes an objective you cannot contest, take something else on the opposite side of the map at the same time: a turret, a buff or the other Turtle. Never stand around watching them take it.

Converting a won fight: After a won fight, check the timer and the map. In order of value: Lord (late game), Inhibitor or Base turrets, Turtle, outer turrets, enemy buffs. Then reset (go back to base) together so you do not get caught one by one.
Playing from behind: Clear waves under your turret, avoid face-checking bushes, trade objectives on the side away from the enemy, and wait for the enemy to overextend.

Lord timing: The Lord is worth the most when two or three enemies are dead, or when the enemy Jungler is dead or out of position. A Lord taken while all five enemies are alive is a gamble on a single Retribution.
Buff control: Taking the enemy's Purple or Orange Buff denies their carry and speeds up yours. Only invade when your laners have pushed their waves (lane priority), or you will be collapsed on.

Where vision comes from: Allied heroes, minions, turrets and some skills reveal the map. There are no buyable wards in MLBB, so vision comes from where your heroes and minions stand and from skills that scout.
Using bushes: Bushes hide heroes. Control the bushes on the path to the next objective and around your carry. A Roamer who checks bushes first saves the carry from walking into an ambush.
Reading absence: When an enemy disappears from the minimap, count the seconds. A Jungler gone for several seconds after clearing a camp is most likely moving to the lane nearest that camp.

Pressure without vision: If you cannot see the enemy Jungler, do not push past the river on the side they were last seen. If you can see them on the opposite side, that is your window to push or invade.

The swap rule: Your standard build is a starting point. At high rank, the best players change one or two items every game. A Marksman who keeps building damage against a fed Assassin dies before the damage matters.

Who to buy it against: Heroes whose kits heal or shield heavily: Freya's ultimate heals per basic attack, Esmeralda converts shields, Uranus regenerates, Kalea heals herself and the lowest-HP ally, Masha's Feral claw strikes recover HP.
Who buys it: One player on each damage type is enough. Usually the Marksman or physical Jungler buys Sea Halberd, the Mage buys Glowing Wand, and a Tank or Fighter buys Dominance Ice.

Why it matters this patch: Freya was the most contested hero of MPL PH Season 18 (100% pick or ban presence). Her ultimate turns her basic attacks into splash damage with healing, and her damage relies on attack speed and on-hit effects.
Roaming: The Roamer buys roaming boots and picks one roaming effect: Active - Conceal, Passive - Dire Hit, Passive - Encourage, Passive - Favor (as listed in the MLBB Wiki item data).

My arrows will pierce windows into new dimensions!

I'll save you with a song!

Your code was corrupted by the Soul Blight.
Eudora's called me back to Harmonia!
Gotta regroup for the ALLSTAR celebration!

games.title: Bigetron's back-to-back title in a 23-minute Game 7
games.summary: Bigetron came back from 2-3 down and won the deciding game of the MPL ID Season 18 Grand Final against NAVI in 22:59. They won the early turtles, piled up a lead of about 14,000 gold, and finally broke a NAVI side built to win late.

essay.stakes: This was the last game of MPL Indonesia Season 18. NAVI had beaten Team Liquid ID 3-2 in the upper bracket final and led this Grand Final 3-2 after five games. Bigetron by Vitality, the defending Season 17 champions, came up from the lower bracket, where they beat Team Liquid ID 4-3 the day before. They won Game 6 to force this decider. Both teams had already earned M8 World Championship spots as the two finalists, so the game was purely for the trophy. Bigetron were going for back-to-back titles.
essay.draft:
NAVI were on blue side and Bigetron on red. Liquipedia gives five bans a side. NAVI banned Fanny, Yu Zhong, Freya, Lesley and Clint. Bigetron banned Kalea, Marcel, Masha, Belerick and Bruno. The NAVI bans went straight at what had hurt them in the series. Nnael's Fanny had won Game 6 almost on her own, and Yu Zhong and Clint were Bigetron's EXP and gold-lane answers from their lower-bracket run. On the broadcast the casters pointed out that NAVI kept banning Lesley and that Bigetron took Bruno off the board.

NAVI's lineup was Karss on Atlas in the EXP lane, Joshuaa on Paquito in the jungle, Jiizee on Lylia in mid, Zeonn on Obsidia in the gold lane and Aprho on Carmilla at roam. Bigetron answered with Shogun on Sora, Nnael on Hirara, Morenooo on Zhuxin, EMANN on Chou and Finn on Gloo. Liquipedia lists heroes, not the order they were picked, so this breakdown does not claim a pick order. The casters said EMANN's Chou was certain to go to the gold lane, which is not a normal marksman pick.

The two drafts wanted different games. NAVI's was the slower one. Lylia and Obsidia are damage that grows with items, and Atlas and Carmilla both bring teamfight ultimates (Atlas's is Fatal Links). The plan was to survive the early game and win one big fight later. The esports.id recap describes NAVI's composition as designed for the late game. Bigetron drafted to make sure that late game never came. Hirara gave Nnael an aggressive jungler. Chou in the gold lane gave them a second hero who could leave lane, dive and kick a target out of position. Zhuxin and Gloo added control, and Sora gave Shogun a fighter who could brawl in every skirmish. Bigetron's win condition was to keep fighting over objectives while NAVI's carries were still short on items, and turn every won fight into turrets.
essay.early:
The broadcast calls this map Revealing Wisps; Liquipedia leaves the map field empty for this game. The first big moment was the first turtle. According to the casters, NAVI's jungler was not there when it spawned, so NAVI could not contest it and Bigetron took it for free. Without their jungler's Retribution nearby, NAVI handed over the first objective of the game without a fight.

EMANN's Chou then did what Bigetron drafted him for. Instead of staying in the gold lane like a marksman, he rotated, and a three-man Bigetron rotation caught Zeonn's Obsidia. That is the point of a melee gold laner: if the enemy carry is lane-bound and fragile, a Chou who can walk into the jungle and kick her into his team is a constant threat. Joshuaa's Paquito struggled from here on. The casters noted him dying again and again, and he finished the game 1/5/1, the most deaths of anyone on the map. Bigetron took the outer middle turret, invaded NAVI's purple buff, and the casters credited them with control of the turtles in the opening phase.
essay.mid:
By the time the first Lord came up, the gold graph had swung hard. The casters read Bigetron's lead at around 7,300 and then 7,600 gold, and later around 10,000. Bigetron took the first Lord and pushed with it, but NAVI defended their base turrets. The casters reminded viewers that base turrets are protected until minute 12, which is why the first Lord push could not end the game even with the lead.

That is the uncomfortable middle of a game like this. Bigetron had everything except the win. NAVI's draft is built for exactly this: if they hold the high ground, every minute adds items to Lylia and Obsidia. The final numbers show how hard NAVI held on. Jiizee's Lylia ended with 37,444 hero damage and no deaths, the most damage of any player in the game, just above Nnael's 37,221. Aprho's Carmilla soaked 71,591 damage, also the most in the game.
essay.late:
The game went to 22:59, long for a decider where one side led for most of it. The casters called the Lord taken by Bigetron at around the 18-minute mark the evolved Lord. Even that push only took down one base turret, so NAVI still had a chance to find the fight their draft was built for. They never got it. Medcom's recap says Bigetron won several important teamfights, secured the fourth Lord and used it for the final assault. The esports.id recap describes the Lord being pushed through the top lane and NAVI being unable to stop it. Medcom puts the end at 23:02; Liquipedia lists 22:59.

The stat lines show how the game was won. Bigetron finished with 11 kills to NAVI's 3, 70,634 gold to 56,603, and 22,229 turret damage to NAVI's 1,583. Nnael's Hirara went 4/0/5 with 18,082 gold, the most of anyone. His final build was Immortality, Blade of Despair, Malefic Roar, Hunter Strike, War Axe and Brute Force Breastplate. Morenooo's Zhuxin went 4/0/4 and Finn's Gloo 1/0/7, so three of Bigetron's five never died. EMANN's Chou dealt 14,313 turret damage, the most on either side. His build was Brute Force Breastplate, Immortality, Rose Gold Meteor, War Axe, Malefic Roar and Endless Battle, a damage build for a hero sent to take turrets. On NAVI, Zeonn's Obsidia had 14,481 gold and a full carry build, but only 20,893 hero damage. A late-game carry who can't reach the enemy, or is caught before the fight starts, can't carry. Shogun was named Grand Final MVP, and Bigetron kept their title.
lessons: A late-game draft only works if the early game is close. NAVI's composition needed even objectives to reach its power spike. Losing the first turtle without a contest, because the jungler was elsewhere, gave Bigetron the tempo for the whole game. In ranked, if your team drafted for the late game, the first turtle and your carry's safety matter more than any early kill.

A gold laner who can roam is a draft weapon. EMANN's Chou left lane to catch Zeonn and then did the most turret damage of the game. If the enemy gold laner is a fragile marksman, a fighter or assassin in the gold lane can play the whole map instead of one lane.

Gold leads do not end games on their own. Bigetron led by about 10,000 gold and still needed an 18-minute evolved Lord and a fourth Lord to finish. Base turret protection until minute 12, plus a team that defends its high ground, buys time. Keep pressure on the side lanes and take Lords, and don't throw a lead by diving the base early.

A carry's damage only counts in the fights they reach. Lylia did the most damage in the game and still lost. If your carry is being caught before fights, play around their position first, and look for damage numbers second.

Ban to stop what the other team already showed. NAVI banned Fanny after she won Game 6, but Nnael switched to Hirara and still finished with the most gold in the game. Banning a hero does not ban the player, so in ranked, plan for the enemy jungler's second-best hero too.

games.title: Nnael's Fanny forces a Game 7
games.summary: Facing elimination at 2-3, Bigetron banned the heroes that stop Fanny, gave Nnael the hero NAVI had been banning, and won in 13:58 with 11 kills to 2.

essay.stakes: NAVI led the MPL ID Season 18 Grand Final 3-2 and needed one more win for the title. For Bigetron, the defending champions, losing this game meant losing the final. Both teams were already going to the M8 World Championship as finalists, so this game decided whether the trophy went to NAVI in six games or the series went to a Game 7.
essay.draft:
Bigetron were on blue side and NAVI on red. NAVI banned Masha, Yu Zhong, Freya, Lesley and Bruno. Bigetron banned Kalea, Paquito, Atlas, Badang and Khufra. The headline is what NAVI did not ban. The casters noted that Fanny had been banned again and again against Nnael, and this time NAVI let her through. Bigetron's bans were the other half of that plan: the casters pointed out that Badang and Khufra, the heroes that stop Fanny, were both closed. Banning Paquito also took away NAVI's preferred jungle option, and the casters said that left Joshuaa on Nolan.

Bigetron played Shogun on Sora in the EXP lane, Nnael on Fanny in the jungle, Morenooo on Yve in mid, EMANN on Brody in the gold lane and Finn on Marcel at roam. NAVI played Karss on Uranus, Joshuaa on Nolan, Jiizee on Zhuxin, Zeonn on Moskov and Aprho on Hilda. Liquipedia lists the heroes but not the pick order.

The casters' reading of NAVI's draft was that it had little hard crowd control. It relied on Hilda and Uranus to start fights, with Moskov as the late-game carry and a plan to split the map four against one with Zeonn. That is a draft that needs time and space. Bigetron's draft was built around one hero. With the heroes that stop her banned and NAVI short on control, Nnael was free to take over. Yve and Brody gave Bigetron long-range damage and turret pressure behind her, and Finn's Marcel was there to protect her.
essay.early:
The first blood showed why NAVI's draft was in trouble. Joshuaa's Nolan went into Bigetron's jungle, three Bigetron players collapsed on him, and the first kill went to Nnael. NAVI did win the early tempo in one place: Joshuaa took the first turtle quickly. Aprho's Hilda and Zeonn's Moskov also connected for a kill, the kind of play NAVI's draft wanted. But Nnael kept killing, including a solo kill, and Bigetron then stole the second turtle and killed Joshuaa with it. The outer middle turret fell. At that point the casters had Joshuaa at 0/4/0 and Nnael at 5/0/0, so the two junglers had gone in opposite directions.

This is the most important early pattern for a Fanny game. Every kill gives her more gold and level to get ahead, and an enemy jungler who keeps dying can't secure objectives against her. Joshuaa finished the game 0/5/0.
essay.mid:
Bigetron took the first Lord with no contest from NAVI, as the casters described it. The first push knocked at NAVI's defences but NAVI held their base. Bigetron only had one lane pushed deep, so they still needed the inner turrets in the middle and top lanes. Meanwhile Finn's Marcel kept Nnael safe from Hilda, the one NAVI hero built to jump on her. The casters also noted that Nnael's Fanny had reached level 15, two levels above Joshuaa.

NAVI's only way back was to drag the game late for Moskov. Zeonn's build shows he got there: Warrior Boots, Golden Staff, Wind of Nature, Corrosion Scythe, Fury Hammer and Demon Hunter Sword, the most gold on NAVI at 9,538. But a split-pushing marksman can't defend a base against five.
essay.late:
The casters said the second Lord also went to Bigetron uncontested while NAVI were a player down. Nnael added Rose Gold Meteor to survive burst. Bigetron went up the high ground through the bottom lane, where a base turret was already down, and caught Zeonn. Medcom's recap says Bigetron played much more aggressively than NAVI in this game, kept NAVI on the defensive, and closed the game with a teamfight in NAVI's base. Medcom puts the end at 14:02; Liquipedia lists 13:58.

The final numbers are lopsided. Bigetron won kills 11 to 2, gold 43,910 to 36,031 and turret damage 39,383 to 6,997. Nnael went 8/0/2 with 59,852 hero damage, the most in the game, and was named the game's MVP by Medcom. His build was Malefic Roar, Fury Hammer, Blade of the Heptaseas, Rose Gold Meteor and Sea Halberd. Morenooo's Yve added 53,388 damage without dying. EMANN's Brody did 30,215 turret damage on his own, and Finn's Marcel went 0/0/8 while soaking 45,783 damage. On NAVI's side, Karss's Uranus soaked 106,941 damage, more than anyone, but that only bought time. The casters' summary was that NAVI had no answer to Fanny: Marcel opened space and Finn neutralised Hilda's aggression, and NAVI lacked heroes that could stop her.
lessons: If you leave a comfort pick open, know exactly how you'll stop it. NAVI let Fanny through, but Bigetron had already banned Badang and Khufra. Opening a dangerous hero only works if you keep a counter for it.

Ban the counters to your own power pick. Bigetron's bans weren't aimed at NAVI's best heroes but at the heroes that could stop Fanny. In ranked draft, if you are last pick on an assassin, look at what's left that can catch you and ban it if you can.

A jungler losing their early fights loses the map. Joshuaa went 0/4/0 early and NAVI couldn't contest the second turtle or either Lord. If you're the jungler and you're behind, farm safely and give up the objective rather than dying for it.
Protect the carry, not the team. Finn's Marcel went 0/0/8 by staying with Nnael and blocking Hilda. A roamer who sticks to the snowballing hero is often worth more than one who starts every fight.

A split-push plan needs a team that can hold four against five. NAVI's 4-1 plan with Moskov left them defending without enough control. In ranked, only split push when the other four can safely hold the middle.
